SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأسماءالأرضين)#541/r2.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأسماءالأرضين)#541/r2.speaker: بعض المفسرين
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأسماءالأرضين)#541/r2.claim: Some exegetes are reported to take مصر in the verse as Egypt specifically.

ITQAN:v2p305#2/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p305#2/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p305#2/r6.anchor:
﴿ وفي ذلكم بلاء ﴾ نعمة
1512 ﴿ وفومها ﴾ الحنطة

BURSEVI:v1p117#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p117#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p117#2/r1.claim: The verse recalls an earlier Israelite offense and ingratitude, addressing their descendants as the same people because of their shared identity.
BURSEVI:v1p117#2/r1.anchor: تذكير لجناية أخرى لأسلاف بني إسرائيل وكفرانهم لنعمة الله عز وجل

BURSEVI:v1p117#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p117#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p117#2/r2.claim: In the wilderness they tired of unchanging manna and quail, remembered their former agricultural life in Egypt, and longed for familiar habits.
BURSEVI:v1p117#2/r2.anchor: حين سئموا من أكل المن والسلوى لكونهما غير مبدلين

BURSEVI:v1p117#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p117#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p117#2/r3.claim: The paired manna and quail counted as one food because eaten together; alternatively, “one” means an unvaried diet even if it has several dishes.
BURSEVI:v1p117#2/r3.anchor: وهما اثنان لأنهم كانوا يأكلون أحدهما بالآخر فيصيران طعاما واحدا

BURSEVI:v1p117#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p117#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p117#2/r4.claim: Bursevī cites al-Baghawī’s note that Arabic can use a dual form for one thing, as in the phrase about pearls and coral, which come only from salt water.
BURSEVI:v1p117#2/r4.anchor: وفي "تفسير البغوي" : والعرب تعبر عن الواحد

BURSEVI:v1p117#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p117#2/r5.speaker: قيل
BURSEVI:v1p117#2/r5.claim: An alternative explanation is that they could not bear everyone being self-sufficient, since mutual aid would disappear; they were also early adopters of servants and slaves.
BURSEVI:v1p117#2/r5.anchor: وقيل : لن نصبر على الغنى فيكون جميعنا أغنياء فلا يقدر بعضنا على الاستعانة ببعض

BURSEVI:v1p117#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p117#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p117#2/r6.claim: Fūm means wheat here because lentils belong to the same food category.
BURSEVI:v1p117#2/r6.anchor: وهو الحنطة لأن ذكر العدس يدل على أنه المراد لأنه من جنسه

BURSEVI:v1p117#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p117#2/r7.speaker: قيل
BURSEVI:v1p117#2/r7.claim: Another lexical view reads fūm as garlic because garlic and onion are paired as related foods.
BURSEVI:v1p117#2/r7.anchor: وقيل : هو الثوم لأن ذكر البصل يدل على أنه هو المراد فإنه من جنسه

BURSEVI:v1p117#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p117#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p117#2/r8.claim: Baql denotes edible greens such as mint, celery, and leek; qiththāʾ is a cucumber-like plant.
BURSEVI:v1p117#2/r8.anchor: والبقل ما تنبت الأرض من الخضر والمراد أصناف البقول التي تأكلها الناس كالنعناع والكرفس

BURSEVI:v1p117#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p117#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p117#2/r9.claim: The request asks Moses to supplicate for them; the connective “so” makes their inability to endure the diet the cause of the request.
BURSEVI:v1p117#2/r9.anchor: سله لأجلنا بدعائك إياه والفاء لسببية عدم الصبر للدعاء

BURSEVI:v1p117#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p117#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p117#2/r10.claim: In “bring forth for us,” the object is omitted, and the verb is jussive as the response to the command to supplicate.
BURSEVI:v1p117#2/r10.anchor: يظهر لنا ويوجد شيئا فالمفعول محذوف والجزم لجواب الأمر

BURSEVI:v1p117#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p117#2/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p117#2/r11.claim: The wording figuratively assigns growth to the receptive earth in place of God, the true agent; “min” is partitive and “mā” is relative.
BURSEVI:v1p117#2/r11.anchor: إسناد مجازي بإقامة القابل وهو الأرض مقام الفاعل وهو الله تعالى ومن تبعيضية وما موصولة

BURSEVI:v1p117#2/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p117#2/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p117#2/r12.claim: The “min” in “from its greens” is explanatory and functions circumstantially with the pronoun.
BURSEVI:v1p117#2/r12.anchor: من بيانية واقعة موقع الحال من الضمير

BURSEVI:v1p117#2/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p117#2/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p117#2/r13.claim: Qiththāʾ is related to qathd and resembles cucumber.
BURSEVI:v1p117#2/r13.anchor: أخو القثد وهي شيء يشبه الخيار

BURSEVI:v1p118/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p118/r1.speaker: ابن التمجيد
BURSEVI:v1p118/r1.claim: Ibn al-Tamjīd prefers reading fūm as garlic over wheat because it is mentioned with onion and lentils, which are cooked with garlic and onion.
BURSEVI:v1p118/r1.anchor: ابن التمجيد في "حواشيه" وحمله على الثوم أوفق من الحنطة

BURSEVI:v1p118/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p118/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p118/r2.claim: Lentils are a familiar seed whose measure by volume matches its weight.

BURSEVI:v1p118/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p118/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p118/r3.claim: Onion is a familiar green used to flavor cooking pots.

BURSEVI:v1p118/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p118/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p118/r4.claim: The clause beginning “He said” is a new sentence answering an implied question about what God or Moses replied.
BURSEVI:v1p118/r4.anchor: استئناف وقع جوابا عن سؤال مقدر كأنه قيل

BURSEVI:v1p118/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p118/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p118/r5.claim: The rebuke asks whether they are choosing the lower thing for themselves in exchange for what is better; “adnā” is lower in rank and worth.

BURSEVI:v1p118/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p118/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p118/r6.claim: The exchange preposition attaches to what is relinquished, and manna and quail are better for taste, ease, and other reasons than the requested produce.
BURSEVI:v1p118/r6.anchor: فإن الباء تصحب الزائل دون الآتي الحاصل وخيرية المن والسلوى في اللذاذة وسقوط المشقة

BURSEVI:v1p118/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p118/r7.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v1p118/r7.claim: Some say wheat is inferior here only in comparative value; the verse does not prove they wanted to replace manna and quail altogether, since they may have wanted alternation.
BURSEVI:v1p118/r7.anchor: قال بعضهم : الحنطة وإن كانت أعلى من المن والسلوى لكن خساستها ههنا بالنسبة إلى قيمتها

BURSEVI:v1p118/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p118/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p118/r8.claim: “Descend” means leave the wilderness if they want these foods.
BURSEVI:v1p118/r8.anchor: انحدروا وانزلوا من التيه إن كنتم تريدون هذه الأشياء

BURSEVI:v1p118/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p118/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p118/r9.claim: Miṣr means any town, not Pharaoh’s Egypt: the Israelites had been commanded to enter the Holy Land, so Egypt would not fit.
BURSEVI:v1p118/r9.anchor: وإذا وجب عليهم دخول تلك الأرض فكيف يجوز دخول مصر فرعون وهو الأظهر

BURSEVI:v1p118/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p118/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p118/r10.claim: Miṣr can mean a great town; its name is linked to cutting off open space through building, and it can be used for a town or village. It is indefinite here, so it declines.
BURSEVI:v1p118/r10.anchor: والمصر البلد العظيم من مصر الشيء بمصره

BURSEVI:v1p118/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p118/r11.speaker: قيل
BURSEVI:v1p118/r11.claim: An alternative identifies Miṣr as Pharaoh’s Egypt; its declension is explained by its medial still consonant, or by construing it as “country” rather than “city.”
BURSEVI:v1p118/r11.anchor: وقيل : أريد به مصر فرعون وإنما صرف لسكون وسطه كهند ودعد ونوح

BURSEVI:v1p118/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p118/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p118/r12.claim: The promise that they will have what they asked for explains the command to descend.
BURSEVI:v1p118/r12.anchor: تعليل للأمر بالهبوط أي : فإن لكم فيه

BURSEVI:v1p118/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p118/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p118/r13.claim: Dhilla means humiliation and maskana means poverty; the poor are called miskīn because poverty stills them and impedes movement.
BURSEVI:v1p118/r13.anchor: يسمى الفقير مسكينا لأن الفقر أسكنه وأقعده عن الحركة

BURSEVI:v1p118/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p118/r14.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p118/r14.claim: Humiliation and poverty surround and cling to them like a dome, becoming an inescapable covering.
BURSEVI:v1p118/r14.anchor: جعلتا محيطتين بهم إحاطة القبة بمن ضربت عليه وألصقتا بهم وجعلتا ضربة لازب

BURSEVI:v1p118#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p118#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p118#2/r1.claim: Their humiliation and poverty are retribution for ingratitude; the image is like plastering clay onto a wall, and even wealthy Jews seem poor.
BURSEVI:v1p118#2/r1.anchor: عنهم مجازاة لهم على كفرانهم كما يضرب الطين على الحائط

BURSEVI:v1p118#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p118#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p118#2/r2.claim: To “return bearing” God’s anger means they deserved and bound themselves to it; the Prophet’s wording “I acknowledge” illustrates the verb.
BURSEVI:v1p118#2/r2.anchor: قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم "أبوء بنعمتك علي"

BURSEVI:v1p118#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p118#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p118#2/r3.claim: God’s anger means His censure of them in this world and punishment in the next.
BURSEVI:v1p118#2/r3.anchor: وغضب الله تعالى ذمه إياهم في الدنيا وعقوبتهم في الآخرة

BURSEVI:v1p118#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p118#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p118#2/r4.claim: “That” refers to the humiliation, poverty, their bearing the anger, and the great wrath.
BURSEVI:v1p118#2/r4.anchor: ضرب الذلة والمسكنة والبوء والغضب العظيم

BURSEVI:v1p118#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p118#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p118#2/r5.claim: God’s signs include the conspicuous miracles shown through Moses, whether familiar or unfamiliar.
BURSEVI:v1p118#2/r5.anchor: الباهرة التي هي المعجزات الساطعة الظاهرة على يدي موسى عليه السلام مما عاد أو لم يعد

BURSEVI:v1p118#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p118#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p118#2/r6.claim: Their disbelief also involved rejecting the Qur’an and Muhammad, denying his description in the Torah, and rejecting Jesus and the Gospel.
BURSEVI:v1p118#2/r6.anchor: وكذبوا بالقرآن ومحمد عليه السلام وأنكروا صفته في التوراة وكفروا بعيسى والإنجيل

BURSEVI:v1p118#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p118#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p118#2/r7.claim: Shuʿayb, Zechariah, and John are named among the prophets they killed; “without right” stresses that even they did not regard the killings as justified.
BURSEVI:v1p118#2/r7.anchor: كشعيب وزكريا ويحيى عليهم السلام وفائدة التقييد مع أن قتل الأنبياء

BURSEVI:v1p118#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p118#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p118#2/r8.claim: Allowing prophets to be killed honors them and raises their rank, as with believers killed in God’s path; it is not abandonment.
BURSEVI:v1p118#2/r8.anchor: قيل ذلك كرامة لهم وزيادة في منازلهم كمثل من يقتل في سبيل الله من المؤمنين

BURSEVI:v1p118#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p118#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
BURSEVI:v1p118#2/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥasan say only prophets not commanded to fight were killed, while every prophet commanded to fight was granted victory.
BURSEVI:v1p118#2/r9.anchor: قال ابن عباس والحسن رضي الله عنهم لم يقتل قط من الأنبياء إلا من لم يؤمر بقتال وكل من أمر بقتال نصر

BURSEVI:v1p118#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p118#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p118#2/r10.claim: This account does not conflict with 40:51 or 37:171–172; alternatively, victory can mean victory through proof and disclosure of truth, which every prophet had.
BURSEVI:v1p118#2/r10.anchor: مع أنه يجوز أن يراد به النصرة بالحجة وبيان الحق وكل منهم بهذا المعنى منصور

BURSEVI:v1p118#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p118#2/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p118#2/r11.claim: A report says the Israelites killed seventy prophets in one day.
BURSEVI:v1p118#2/r11.anchor: روي أنهم قتلوا في يوم واحد سبعين نبيا

BURSEVI:v1p118#2/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p118#2/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p118#2/r12.claim: The Mathnawī couplet links foolishness with killing prophets and alludes to people calling the messengers ill omens.
BURSEVI:v1p118#2/r12.anchor: اين كار وكيا لازم آمد يقتلون الأنبيا

BURSEVI:v1p119/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p119/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p119/r1.claim: Persistent disobedience and transgression led to the previously described disbelief and prophet-killing.
BURSEVI:v1p119/r1.anchor: يتجاوزون أمري ويرتكبون محارمي أي : جر بهم العصيان

BURSEVI:v1p119/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p119/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p119/r2.claim: Repeated minor sins lead to major sins, just as persistence in small acts of obedience leads toward greater acts.
BURSEVI:v1p119/r2.anchor: فإن صغار الذنوب إذا دووم عليها أدت إلى كبارها كما أن مداومة صغار الطاعات مؤدية إلى تحري كبارها

BURSEVI:v1p119/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p119/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p119/r3.claim: Heedlessness sickens the heart and prevents it from tasting faith; as fever makes sugar taste bitter, heedlessness is lethal poison to hearts.
BURSEVI:v1p119/r3.anchor: وسقم القلب بالغفلة عن الله تعالى منعهم عن إدراك لذاذة الإيمان وحلاوته

BURSEVI:v1p119/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p119/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p119/r4.claim: Believers’ recoil from disobeying God resembles one’s recoil from poisoned food.
BURSEVI:v1p119/r4.anchor: فنفرة قلوب المؤمنين عن مخالفة الله نفرتك عن الطعام المسموم

BURSEVI:v1p119/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p119/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p119/r5.claim: In the inward reading, the servant has a will, but God’s will is better; “descend” means leaving surrender and divine governance for self-directed choice.
BURSEVI:v1p119/r5.anchor: واعلم أنمرادا وللعبد مرادا وما أراد الله خير فقوله : اهبطوا

BURSEVI:v1p119/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p119/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p119/r6.claim: Choosing and planning for oneself alongside God’s governance brings humiliation and poverty.
BURSEVI:v1p119/r6.anchor: إلى أرض التدبير والاختيار منكم لأنفسكم موصوفين بالذلة والمسكنة لاختياركم مع الله

BURSEVI:v1p119/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p119/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p119/r7.claim: This community would not have spoken like Israel because of its brighter lights and penetrating spiritual insight; it is the balanced community of 2:143.
BURSEVI:v1p119/r7.anchor: لما قالت مقال بني إسرائيل لشفوف أنوارهم ونفوذ أسرارهم

BURSEVI:v1p119/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p119/r8.speaker: التأويلات
BURSEVI:v1p119/r8.claim: The inward analogy says Israel could not endure one heavenly food because of low nature, just as the lower human self cannot be content with one spiritual nourishment from God.
BURSEVI:v1p119/r8.anchor: وفي "التأويلات" : كما أن بني إسرائيل لم يصبروا على طعام واحد

BURSEVI:v1p119/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p119/r9.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v1p119/r9.claim: The Prophet says he is unlike others because he spends the night with his Lord, who feeds and gives him drink, modeling the soul’s endurance of spiritual nourishment.
BURSEVI:v1p119/r9.anchor: كما كان يصبر نفس النبي عليه السلام ويقول

BURSEVI:v1p119/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p119/r10.speaker: التأويلات
BURSEVI:v1p119/r10.claim: The lower self asks its heart, figured as Moses, for bodily produce: animal desires and physical pleasures; the answer is to exchange the perishing for the enduring.
BURSEVI:v1p119/r10.anchor: وفي "التأويلات" : كما أن بني إسرائيل لم يصبروا على طعام واحد كان ينزل عليهم من السماء

BURSEVI:v1p119/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p119/r11.speaker: التأويلات
BURSEVI:v1p119/r11.claim: The inward Egypt is the lower body, reached by descending from the high stations of the spirit; its base demands bring beast-like degradation.
BURSEVI:v1p119/r11.anchor: وفي "التأويلات" : كما أن بني إسرائيل لم يصبروا على طعام واحد كان ينزل

BURSEVI:v1p119/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p119/r12.speaker: التأويلات
BURSEVI:v1p119/r12.claim: Inward disbelief means denying unseen inspirations and spiritual unveilings; killing prophets means nullifying divinely opened reports of the unseen and denying their secrets.
BURSEVI:v1p119/r12.anchor: وفي "التأويلات" : كما أن بني إسرائيل لم يصبروا على طعام واحد كان ينزل

BURSEVI:v1p119/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p119/r13.speaker: التأويلات
BURSEVI:v1p119/r13.claim: These losses result from disobedience and breaking the covenant of striving in worship; transgression is seeking something other than God.
BURSEVI:v1p119/r13.anchor: وفي "التأويلات" : كما أن بني إسرائيل لم يصبروا على طعام واحد كان ينزل

BURSEVI:v1p119/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p119/r14.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p119/r14.claim: The verse permits eating wholesome and pleasurable foods; the Prophet liked sweets and honey and drank cool, sweet water, while lentils and oil are foods of the righteous.
BURSEVI:v1p119/r14.anchor: ثم إن في الآية الكريمة دليلا على جواز أكل الطيبات والمطاعم المستلذات

ELMALILI:2:61/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:61/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:61/r1.claim: Israelites say they cannot endure eating one kind of food and ask Moses to pray for produce from the earth, including vegetables, cucumber, garlic, lentils, and onions.
ELMALILI:2:61/r1.anchor: biz bir türlü yemeğe artık sabredemeyeceğiz, her gün bıldırcın eti, kudret helvası yemekten bıktık usandık

ELMALILI:2:61/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:61/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:61/r2.claim: The commentary renders qiththā as cucumber and fūm as garlic in the requested list.
ELMALILI:2:61/r2.anchor: sebzelerinden, kabağından, hıyarından, sarımsağından, mercimeğinden, soğanından çıkarıversin.

ELMALILI:2:61/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:61/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:61/r3.claim: Monotony may bore human desire, but seeking variety is not itself sinful.
ELMALILI:2:61/r3.anchor: Gerçi yeknesaklığın şehevât-ı beşeriye üzerinde az çok sıkıcı bir tesiri vardır ve buna[^1] karşı tenevvü‘talebinde esasen bir masiyet yoktur.

ELMALILI:2:61/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:61/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:61/r4.claim: While making a request, they should remember past deprivation and seek increase through gratitude and an elevated spirit.
ELMALILI:2:61/r4.anchor: Fakat bunu yaparken bir taraftan o nimetin yokluğu zamanındaki[^2] ıztırâbâtı unutmamak ve diğer taraftan ulvî bir kalb ile hareket edip şükran ile izdiyâdını aramak

ELMALILI:2:61/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:61/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:61/r5.claim: They should preserve proper reverence rather than say “your Lord” where “our Lord” is due, which displays faithlessness.
ELMALILI:2:61/r5.anchor: “Rabbimiz” diyecek yerde “Rabbin” diye imansızlık eseri göstermemek îcab ederdi.

ELMALILI:2:61/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:61/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:61/r6.claim: Their request reflects a desire for civilized life, but it rests on a petty craving rather than a lofty purpose and betrays longing for their former Egyptian degradation and slavery, showing failure to value freedom.
ELMALILI:2:61/r6.anchor: bu talebinde şüphesiz ki medenî bir hayat talebi vardı, fakat bu talep yüksek bir maksad ve gaye ile değil, bıldırcın yerine soğan, sarımsak yemek için hasis bir emele ibtinâ ediyordu.

ELMALILI:2:61/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:61/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:61/r7.claim: Moses asks whether they would exchange a better blessing for an inferior thing and tells them to descend to a town, where they can obtain what they requested; this both fulfills the demand and exposes their poor choice and its outcome.
ELMALILI:2:61/r7.anchor: Bu cevap bir taraftan matlublarının is‘âfı esbâbını irâe ederek yeni bir in‘âmı, diğer taraftan da sû’-i ihtiyarlarını ve âkıbetlerinin fenâlığını ifade etmektedir.

ELMALILI:2:61/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:61/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:61/r8.claim: Misr may be a proper name or a common noun; as a proper name it is indeclinable, though declension is permitted because it has three letters and a quiescent middle letter.
ELMALILI:2:61/r8.anchor: “Mısr”, ism-i has ve ism-i cins olur. İsm-i has olduğu zaman gayr-i munsarif olur. Cer ve tenvin kabul etmez.

ELMALILI:2:61/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:61/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:61/r9.claim: One interpretation takes Misr as Egypt, making the command simply a reproach; the author notes that the same reproachful implication remains under the town interpretation.
ELMALILI:2:61/r9.anchor: Evvelki takdirde bu emir sırf bir emr-i tevbîhî olmuş olacaktır.

ELMALILI:2:61/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:61/r10.speaker: ekser-i müfessirîn
ELMALILI:2:61/r10.claim: Most commentators take Misr as a common noun meaning a town, specifically one of the towns in the Holy Land, since Israel did not return to Egypt after leaving it.
ELMALILI:2:61/r10.anchor: ekser-i[^8] müfessirîn bunu ism-i cins mânasıyla arz-ı mukaddes kasabalarından birine haml etmişlerdir.

ELMALILI:2:61/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:61/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:61/r11.claim: The wording Misr instead of qarya or balad hints that Israel preferred a humiliating condition resembling Egypt for the sake of eating onions and garlic.
ELMALILI:2:61/r11.anchor: bunun için “karye” veya “belde” denilmeyip “mısır” denilmiştir. Demek oluyor ki Benî İsrâil böyle soğan sarımsak yemek için bi’n-netîce Mısır’daki hâllerini andırır bir hâl-i zillete taraftar olmuş oldular

ELMALILI:2:61/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:61/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:61/r12.claim: Their humiliation and misery are pictured as a structure built or a stamp set upon them, leaving them under contempt, heavy taxes, poverty, and destitution.
ELMALILI:2:61/r12.anchor: ta‘bîr-i âharla üzerlerine zillet ve meskenet damgası basıldı. Hakaret altında ağır vergilere ve fakr u meskenete mahkum kaldılar

ELMALILI:2:61/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:61/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:61/r13.claim: They incurred God's anger and deserved it; their state was extinguished, their society scattered, and they became those described in al-Fātiḥa as subject to wrath.
ELMALILI:2:61/r13.anchor: ve nihâyet Allah’tan bir gazaba değdiler[^10], müstahik oldular, devletleri munkariz ve cemiyetleri perişan oldu.

ELMALILI:2:61/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:61/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:61/r14.claim: Their punishment came because they disbelieved God's manifest signs and unjustly killed prophets, including Isaiah, Zechariah, and John.
ELMALILI:2:61/r14.anchor: Hazret-i Şa‘yâ, Hazret-i Zekeriyâ, Hazret-i Yahyâ gibi enbiyâyı şehid etmişlerdi

ELMALILI:2:61/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:61/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:61/r15.claim: The added phrase “without right” emphasizes the heinousness and deliberate character of killing prophets, since it plainly violated divine judgment; it also alludes to their hostile intent against the Seal of the Prophets.
ELMALILI:2:61/r15.anchor: ayrıca tasrih buyurulması şenâ‘atlerini tansis ve bilerek yaptıklarına işaret içindir. Burada bunların Hâtemü’l-enbiyâ Efendimiz hazretlerine dahi sû’-i kasdlarına işaret buyurulmuştur.

ELMALILI:2:61/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:61/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:61/r16.claim: They made rebellion habitual and continually exceeded limits; persistence in lesser sins leads to major sins, persistence in major sins to disbelief, which enables every atrocity.
ELMALILI:2:61/r16.anchor: Hâlbuki sağîrede ısrar kebîreye, kebîrede ısrar küfre dâ‘î olur. Küfür ise her şenâ‘ati yaptırır.

ELMALILI:2:61/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:61/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:61/r17.claim: Nabī derives from nabaʾ and originally means one who brings news by revelation from God; it is equivalent to prophet, with plurals anbiyāʾ and nabiyyīn.
ELMALILI:2:61/r17.anchor: “Nebî”, “nebe’”den müştak olarak aslında نبئ’dir ki Allah teâlâ’dan vahiy ile haber getiren demektir ve tam “peygamber” mürâdifidir.

ELMALILI:2:61/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:61/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:61/r18.claim: Nafiʿ reads the word in its original form as nabiyyīn.

ELMALILI:2:61/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:61/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:61/r19.claim: Nabī is broader than rasūl—every rasūl is a nabī but not every nabī is a rasūl—although the Qur'an sometimes uses the terms synonymously.
ELMALILI:2:61/r19.anchor: “Nebî” “resul”den e‘amdır. Her resul nebîdir, fakat her nebî resul değildir. Ma‘amâfîh Kur’an’da mürâdif olarak kullanıldığı da vardır.

ELMALILI:2:61/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:61/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:61/r20.claim: After explaining the divine anger, the author transitions by asking whether any possibility of deliverance remains for them.
ELMALILI:2:61/r20.anchor: Bu gazabdan sonra acaba bunlar için hiçbir felâh imkânı yok mudur?

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r1.claim: Despite their Abrahamic religious and moral heritage, Israelites were degraded by centuries in Egypt and its idolatrous culture, settling for comfort and becoming fearful.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r1.anchor: yüzyıllar boyunca Mısır’da kaldıkları için oranın putperest kültürüyle dejenere olmuş

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r2.claim: Moses reminded them of their national dignity and ordered them toward the holy land, but they refused to enter while its strong people remained and told Moses and God to fight without them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r2.anchor: Ey Mûsâ! Onlar orada bulundukları sürece biz oraya asla giremeyeceğiz. Sen ve rabbin gidin savaşın; biz burada oturacağız

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r3.claim: To return to their homeland as an independent, honorable society, they needed fidelity to God and Moses, acceptance of his teaching, and willingness to endure material hardship.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r3.anchor: amaçlarını gerçekleştirme yolunda maddî sıkıntılara katlanmaları gerekiyordu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r4.claim: They longed for ordinary Egyptian life and vegetables, though manna, quail, and twelve springs were extraordinary divine gifts of special value; Moses rebuked their preference for the inferior.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r4.anchor: Allah tarafından özel olarak lutfedildiği için ayrı bir önem –ve belki de yüksek bir besin değeri– taşımaktaydı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r5.claim: Some listed sins occurred generations after Moses, but the verse recalls them alongside the wilderness complaint to warn Muslims and the Prophet’s Jews against repeating ancestral sins for worldly gain.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r5.anchor: hem müslümanlara hem de Hz. Peygamber dönemindeki yahudilere bir hatırlatmada bulunulmakta

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r6.claim: Nebī, plural anbiyā, denotes chosen servants who mediate between God and people by conveying divine commands and prohibitions; Turkish commonly uses the Persian-derived peygamber for both nebī and rasūl.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r6.anchor: Nebî (çoğulu enbiyâ) Allah ile kulları arasında elçilik görevi yapan, O’nun buyruk ve yasaklarını kullarına haber veren seçkin kullar için kullanılan dinî bir terimdir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r7.speaker: İslâm bilginleri
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r7.claim: One proposed etymology derives nebī from nebve or nebâve, meaning high, noble, or honorable, because prophethood and its revelation bear transcendent superiority.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r7.anchor: İslâm bilginleri nebî kelimesinin kökü ve anlamı konusunda iki farklı görüş ortaya koymuşlardır. a) Bir görüşe göre nebî, Arapça’da

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r8.speaker: İkinci görüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r8.claim: Another proposed etymology derives nebī from nebeʾ, “news,” because a prophet conveys information and knowledge from God to people.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r8.anchor: İkinci görüşe göre nebî, Arapça’da “haber” anlamına gelen nebe’ kelimesinden türetilmiş olup

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r9.claim: The etymological disagreement does not amount to a substantive disagreement over the technical definition of prophet; scholars also differ over whether nebī and rasūl mean the same or different things.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r9.anchor: Bu görüş farkı sadece kelimenin köküyle ilgili olup nebînin terim olarak tanımı konusunda ciddi bir ihtilâf olduğu anlamına gelmez.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r10.speaker: İslâm bilginleri
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r10.claim: Nearly all Islamic scholars define a prophet as a person chosen from humanity, given superior capacities, and assigned to convey the divine message to a community or all people.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r10.anchor: hemen bütün İslâm bilginleri nebînin, “Allah’ın insanlar arasından seçtiği ve sıradan insanlardan farklı bazı üstün kabiliyetlerle donattığı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r11.speaker: İslâm bilginleri
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r11.claim: Scholars agree prophethood is a bestowed divine rank, not something acquired through effort; some read the “wisdom” of 2:269 as revelation and cite it as evidence.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r11.anchor: Bütün İslâm bilginleri nübüvvetin, çalışmakla elde edilemeyen Allah vergisi (vehbî) bir mertebe olduğunu kabul ederler.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r12.speaker: Bazı bilginler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r12.claim: Some scholars interpret the wisdom in 2:269 as revelation and use it as evidence that prophethood is divinely bestowed.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r12.anchor: Bazı bilginler “Allah hikmeti dilediğine verir” (Bakara 2/269) meâlindeki âyette geçen “hikmet” kelimesini vahiy olarak açıklamış

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r13.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r13.claim: The interpretation of Ibrahim 14:11 and Quranic statements that God sends people as messengers also show that prophethood is bestowed, not earned.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r13.anchor: İbrâhim sûresinin 11. âyeti de bu anlamda yorumlanmıştır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r14.speaker: İslâm bilginleri
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r14.claim: Faith in prophets is one of Islam’s six articles of faith; scholars who group belief into three fundamentals—divinity, prophethood, and afterlife—hold that denying prophethood removes a believer in God from the religion.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r14.anchor: Allah’a iman etse bile, peygamberliği inkâr eden bir kimsenin dinden çıkmış olacağı görüşünde birleşmişlerdir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r15.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r15.speaker: İslâm bilginleri
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r15.claim: Scholars identify five defining prophetic traits: truthfulness, trustworthiness, sinlessness, keen judgment, and complete delivery of the divine message.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r15.anchor: Bunlar sıdk (doğruluk ve dürüstlük), emanet (güvenilirlik), ismet (günahsızlık), fetânet (zeki ve güçlü bir muhakeme yeteneğine sahip olma), tebliğ (ilâhî mesajı eksiksiz bildirme, duyurma) şeklinde tesbit edilmiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r16.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r16.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r16.claim: Prophets faithfully convey the truth; rare minor slips, called zalla, are corrected by revelation, and their intelligence enables them to understand and explain divine teaching accurately.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r16.anchor: nâdiren işledikleri ve “zelle” denilen küçük yanılgıları vahiy yoluyla Allah tarafından düzeltilmiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r17.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r17.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r17.claim: Islam takes a middle course by treating prophets as God’s chosen messengers and servants rather than divine beings, unlike Christian deification of Jesus.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r17.anchor: İslâm dini onları, Hıristiyanlık’ta Hz. Îsâ için yapılanın aksine, tanrılık mertebesine çıkarmamış, Allah’ın seçkin elçileri ve kulları kabul etmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r18.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r18.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r18.claim: Prophets first believe in the truths they preach and carefully apply religious, moral, and legal rulings in their own lives.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r18.anchor: peygamberler, tebliğ ettikleri ilâhî gerçeklere öncelikle kendileri inanmışlar; dinî, ahlâkî, hukukî hükümleri en titiz bir şekilde kendi hayatlarına uygulamışlardır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r19.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r19.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r19.claim: Outside their prophetic mission, prophets share ordinary human experiences such as eating, marrying, owning property, illness, and death; attributing extraordinary qualities in these matters is impermissible.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r19.anchor: yeme içme, evlenme, mal mülk edinme, hastalanma, ölme gibi beşerî durumlar bakımından diğer insanlardan farksız olup olağan üstü bir özellik taşımazlar

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r20.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r20.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r20.claim: When people leave prophetic guidance they fall into false belief, moral corruption, greed, oppression, and violence; God mercifully sends prophets to rescue humanity and show the way to happiness in both lives, with Muhammad last.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r20.anchor: çeşitli devirlerde peygamberler göndermek suretiyle insanlığı bu tür buhranlardan kurtarmış, onlara dünya ve âhirette mutlu olmalarının yollarını göstermiş; son olarak bu şerefli görevi Hz. Muhammed’e yüklemiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r21.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r21.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r21.claim: The commentary traces modern Western departure from prophecy from deism through positivism and Marxism to atheism, warning that modern capabilities magnify threats to human values and existence and demonstrate prophecy’s necessity.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r21.anchor: önce peygambersiz bir tanrı inancıyla (deizm) başlayan peygamberlik yolundan sapış, pozitivizm ve Marksizm’le giderek tam bir dinsizlik ve tanrısızlık inancına dönüşmüş

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r22.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r22.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r22.claim: Earlier lost or altered scriptures required new revelation and prophets, but the preserved Quran leaves no need for another prophet after Muhammad; the Quran is final scripture and Muhammad the seal of prophets.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r22.anchor: Hz. Muhammed’den sonra böyle bir durum söz konusu olmadığı ve Kur’an-ı Kerîm Allah tarafından geldiği şekliyle ortada olduğu için yeni bir peygamber gelmesine de ihtiyaç kalmamıştır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r23.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r23.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r23.claim: Adam was the first human and first prophet; the Quran provides no count of later prophets and names twenty-eight, while whether Luqman, Dhu al-Qarnayn, and Uzayr were prophets or saints is disputed.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:61/r23.anchor: Kur’an’da adı anılan ve haklarında bilgi verilen yirmi sekiz peygamber şunlardır

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p110/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p110/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p110/r1.claim: Abu ʿAmr kasras the pronoun mīm because its underlying connected form ended in yāʾ; after deletion, the mīm resumes that original vowel when moved.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p110/r1.anchor: ولكن كأن الأصل عنده في الوصل عليهمي، فحذف الياء استخفافا، كما حذف عاصم وابن عامر ونافع في إحدى الروايتين لذلك

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p110/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p110/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p110/r2.claim: He treats Abu ʿAmr’s kasra like the original ḍamma of Ibn Kathīr, Nāfiʿ, ʿĀṣim, and Ibn ʿĀmir, preferring an original vowel to an added one.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p110/r2.anchor: لأن الكسر في قوله: (عليهم الذلة) و (إليهم اثنين) على قوله في أنه أصل، نظير الضم في قول ابن كثير ونافع وعاصم وابن عامر

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p110/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p110/r3.speaker: سيبويه
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p110/r3.claim: Sībawayh’s vocative truncation of Rād retains its original vowel at a consonant meeting, an analogy al-Fārisī uses for Abu ʿAmr.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p110/r3.anchor: قال سيبويه : في ترخيم راد اسم رجل على قول من قال: يا حار، يا راد أقبل

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p110/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p110/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p110/r4.claim: Vowel-following is not always productive analogy: some forms are transmitted, while it is regular in رد، عض، فر and apparently in مردفين.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p110/r4.anchor: ومع ذلك فقد اطردت هذه الحركة في قول من قال: رد وعض وفر والأظهر في مردفين أنه مطرد في بابه

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p110/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p110/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p110/r5.claim: Following kasra is already accepted on the mīm of an active-participle marker even though it obscures the pattern, making it still likelier on a pronoun marker.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p110/r5.anchor: ومما يقوي تحريك هذه الميم بالكسر من جهة القياس، أنهم قد أتبعوا حركة الميم الدالة على اسم الفاعل الكسر

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p110/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p110/r6.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p110/r6.claim: Arabic allows vowel-following across an intervening consonant, as in أجوءك for أجيئك and منتن.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p110/r6.anchor: ومما يقوي إتباع الميم في الكسر الهاء، أن حركة الإتباع قد جاءت عنهم مع حجز حرف بين الحركتين

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p112/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p112/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p112/r1.claim: In منحدر, the ḍamma follows the inflectional ḍamma, as in ابنم، امرؤ، أخوك، فوك، and ذو مال.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p112/r1.anchor: منحدر تبعت الضمة فيه ضمة الإعراب، كقولهم: ابنم وامرو، وأخوك

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p112/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p112/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p112/r2.claim: أنبؤك can follow the inflectional ḍamma or the initial imperfect-prefix ḍamma, even across an intervening consonant.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p112/r2.anchor: فأما قولهم: أنبؤك، فإن شئت أتبعت ضمة العين ضمة الإعراب مثل منحدر، وإن شئت أتبعتها ضمة همزة المضارعة

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p112/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p112/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن أبي إسحاق
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p112/r3.claim: Abū ʿUthmān reports through Maḥbūb and ʿĪsā that Ibn Abī Isḥāq read بين المرء وقلبه and said رأيت مرءا وهذا مرء.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p112/r3.anchor: حدثني محبوب بن الحسن القرشي عن عيسى ، قال: كان عبد الله بن أبي إسحاق يقرأ: بين المرء وقلبه

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p112/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p112/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p112/r4.claim: The exceptional pronunciation هو يئبى does not refute the pattern because it is anomalous; يخطف has kasra to favor vowel-following.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p112/r4.anchor: فأما ما حكاه من قولهم: هو يئبى، فليس مما يعترض به لشذوذه

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p112/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p112/r5.speaker: أبو الحسن
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p112/r5.claim: Abū al-Ḥasan explains يخطف by first kasrating خ for two sukūns, then matching the prefix yāʾ to that kasra.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p112/r5.anchor: قال أبو الحسن: من قال يخطف كسر الخاء لاجتماع الساكنين ثم كسر الياء

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p112/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p112/r6.speaker: أبو الحسن
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p112/r6.claim: Abū al-Ḥasan reports from ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar that some Arabs give three-letter nouns beginning with ḍamma a heavy pronunciation.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p112/r6.anchor: أن أبا الحسن قال: روى عيسى بن عمر أن بعض العرب يثقل كل اسم أوله مضموم إذا كان على ثلاثة أحرف

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p112/r7.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p112/r7.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p112/r7.claim: Forms of فم show case-conditioned endings (فوك، فاك، فيك); ذو مال behaves similarly but ذو does not take a pronominal suffix.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p112/r7.anchor: ومن الإتباع قولهم: هذا فوك ورأيت فاك، ومررت بفيك. ومثله قولهم: ذو مال، إلا أن ذو لا يضاف إلى المضمر

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p114/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p114/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p114/r1.claim: With a first-person suffix, فم ends in yāʾ in all cases because the following pronoun imposes kasra, unlike عصاي whose weak ending does not shift with case.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p114/r1.anchor: فكذلك إذا أضافه إلى نفسه انقلبت ياء؛ لأن حركة الحرف الذي يلي الياء في جميع أحواله الكسر

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p114/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p114/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p114/r2.claim: Following works alike when the triggering vowel is inflectional or built; the distinction does not change the pattern, as ابنم shows.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p114/r2.anchor: فأما افتراق الحركتين بأن إحداهما حركة إعراب، والأخرى حركة بناء، فليس مما يوجب اختلافا فيما ذكرنا

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p114/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p114/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p114/r3.claim: The proposal that ابنم’s nūn follows an added mīm is unsound: امرؤ shows the same following without deletion, and مرء is also attested.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p114/r3.anchor: وليس هذا بمستقيم، لأنهم قد فعلوا ذلك بامرئ، ولم يحذف منه شيء

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p114/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p114/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p114/r4.claim: The contrasting forms غد and غدو show that فم’s alternating deletion and completion is not a general consequence of matching وزن.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p114/r4.anchor: على أنهم قد قالوا: غد فحذفوا، وغدو، فأتموا، ولم يفعلوا به ما فعلوا بفم

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p116/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p116/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p116/r1.claim: Vowel-following has two types: a non-inflectional vowel follows another non-inflectional vowel, as in مغيرة، منتن، يعفر، and ظلمات.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p116/r1.anchor: والحركة التي تتبع الحركة على ضربين: أحدهما: إتباع حركة ليست للإعراب حركة ليست للإعراب نحو: مغيرة، ومنتن، ويعفر، وظلمات

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p116/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p116/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p116/r2.claim: In the second type, a non-inflectional vowel follows an inflectional one, as in امرؤ، ابنم، فوك، أجوءك، and أنبؤك.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p116/r2.anchor: والآخر: إتباع حركة ليست للإعراب حركة إعراب، وذلك مثل: امرؤ، وابنم، وفوك، وأجوءك، وأنبؤك

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p116/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p116/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p116/r3.claim: The examples of فم undermine the claim that these words are inflected in two places; movement can follow either inflection or construction.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p116/r3.anchor: وما ثبت مما ذكرناه من قولهم في في يدل على فساد قول من قال: إن هذه الكلم معربة من مكانين

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p116/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p116/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p116/r4.claim: The reversed pattern cited in the grammar book is too rare to establish a rule; comparison of inflection with building is likewise only an exceptional analogy.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p116/r4.anchor: والحرف المذكور في الكتاب بعكس هذه القسمة، من النادر الذي لا حكم له

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p117/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p117/r1.speaker: حمزة
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p117/r1.claim: Ḥamza moves the mīm in عليهم، لديهم، and إليهم with ḍamma, matching the pronoun hāʾ, which he also pronounces with ḍamma.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p117/r1.anchor: فأما قول حمزة والكسائي: (عليهم الذلة)، و (من دونهم امرأتين)، فإن تحريك حمزة الميم، في: عليهم ولديهم، وإليهم، خاصة بالضم مستقيم حسن

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p117/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p117/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p117/r2.claim: Because Ḥamza gives hāʾ its underlying ḍamma, the mīm takes that original vowel rather than an added kasra; no reader with hāʾ-ḍamma kasras this mīm.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p117/r2.anchor: وذلك أنه يضم الهاء في هذه الأحرف ولا يكسرها، فإذا ضمها لم يكن في تحريك الميم إلا الضم

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p117/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p117/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p117/r3.claim: The same principle explains ذال in مذ اليوم: its original ḍamma is retained when the consonant is moved.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p117/r3.anchor: وعلى هذا قالوا: مذ اليوم، فحركوا الذال بالضم

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p117/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p117/r4.speaker: الكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p117/r4.claim: Al-Kisāʾī joins Ḥamza in ḍamma on عليهم and لديهم, though they normally kasra this hāʾ outside the relevant environments.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p117/r4.anchor: وأما موافقة الكسائي له في عليهم ولديهم، واتفاقهما على تحريك الهاء من ضمير المجرور أو المنصوب المجموع بالضم

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p117/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p117/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p117/r5.claim: Al-Kisāʾī and Ḥamza use two dialect forms, a choice that broadens and eases recitation and accords with the transmitted seven modes.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p117/r5.anchor: فوجهه أن ذلك لغة، كما أن الكسر لغة، فكأنهما أحبا أن يأخذا باللغتين جميعا

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p117/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p117/r6.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p117/r6.claim: Other readings likewise take more than one dialect form, including variants in أنعام، تكملوا، and يألتكم.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p117/r6.anchor: وكما قرئ: ولتكملوا العدة [البقرة/ 185] ولتكملوا العدة وكما قال: لا يألتكم من أعمالكم شيئا، ولا يلتكم من أعمالكم

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p117/r7.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p117/r7.speaker: النبي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p117/r7.claim: A transmitted prophetic report says the Qurʾān was revealed in seven modes, all healing and sufficient.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p117/r7.anchor: الخبر المأثور: «نزل القرآن على سبعة أحرف كلها شاف كاف»

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p117/r8.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p117/r8.speaker: نافع
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p117/r8.claim: Nāfiʿ is reported to alternate between عليهمو and عليهم, another instance of using both dialect forms.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p117/r8.anchor: ما روي عن نافع من قراءته مرة: (عليهمو) وأخرى (عليهم)

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p117/r9.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p117/r9.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p117/r9.claim: The objection that transitional movement should not trigger ḍamma on hāʾ only challenges the reading under a different analysis; it does not touch his explanation.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p117/r9.anchor: فإذا تؤول قولهما على ما قدمناه لم يدخل هذا السؤال عليه

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p120/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p120/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p120/r1.claim: Weak radicals remain deleted in forms such as رمت المرأة and لم يخف الرجل despite a vowel inserted for two sukūns; if that vowel counted, forms like لم يقولا would retain the radical.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p120/r1.anchor: فحذفوا الألف المنقلبة عن اللام لسكونها وسكون تاء التأنيث، ولما حركت التاء لالتقاء الساكنين لم يرد الألف

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p120/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p120/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p120/r2.claim: The poetic restorations أجره الرمح and ولا تهاله are too rare to outweigh the ordinary evidence against counting the transitional vowel.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p120/r2.anchor: فالقول: إن ذلك من القلة بحيث إن لم يعتبر به المعتبر كان المذهب على أن الألف يجوز أن تكون على حدها

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p120/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p120/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p120/r3.claim: The retained yāʾ in لم يكن الذين كفروا is a stronger counterexample because it is frequent and occurs in revelation.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p120/r3.anchor: فالقول: إن ذلك أوجه من الأول، من حيث كثر في الاستعمال. وجاء به التنزيل. فالاحتجاج به أقوى

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p120/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p120/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p120/r4.claim: Poetic deletion can restore an underlying form for metrical necessity, as ضننوا, although ordinary usage keeps the consonant.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p120/r4.anchor: فأما حذف الشاعر له مع تحركها بهذه الحركة كما يحذفها إذا كانت ساكنة فإن هذه الضرورة من رد الشيء إلى أصله نحو: «ضننوا»

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p121/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p121/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p121/r1.claim: In اضرب الاثنين and اكتب الاسم, the imperative lām remains kasrated because movement of the article lām for two sukūns counts like its being still.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p121/r1.anchor: فحركت اللام من افعل بالكسر لالتقاء الساكنين. ثم لما حركت لام المعرفة من الاثنين والاسم لم تسكن اللام من افعل

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p121/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p121/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p121/r2.claim: Although the article lām attaches closely and adds definiteness, it behaves like a separate element because it is not part of the word’s root, as in hesitation forms ألي.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p121/r2.anchor: فالقول: إنها قد جرت مجرى المنفصل منها لما لم تكن أصلا فيها كما كان في التذكر كذلك

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p121/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p121/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p121/r3.claim: Jussive حذف of nūn in لم يضربا and لم يضربوا shows that transitional movement is not counted like a stable vowel.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p121/r3.anchor: فحذفوا النون في هذه المواضع، كما حذفوا الألف والياء والواو السواكن إذا كن لامات، من حيث عودلن بالحركة

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p121/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p121/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p121/r4.claim: Identical consonants do not assimilate when the second is moved only for two sukūns, another sign that this movement is disregarded.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p121/r4.anchor: فلم يدغموا في الثاني إذا تحرك لالتقاء الساكنين، كما لم يدغموه قبل هذا التحريك

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p121/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p121/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p121/r5.claim: Ordinary ḍamma on wāw can permit its replacement by hamza, as in أقتت، أدؤر، and النئوور; the next argument tests transitional ḍamma.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p121/r5.anchor: أن الواوات إذا تحركت بالضم، جاز أن تبدل منها الهمزة. نحو: أقتت وأدؤر والنئوور

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p123/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p123/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p123/r1.claim: Wāw is not replaced by hamza when its ḍamma is only transitional; reports that some do so are treated as mistakes.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p123/r1.anchor: ولم يبدلوا الهمزة منها إذا تحركت بالضم لالتقاء الساكنين، كما لم يبدلوها منها إذا كانت ساكنة

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p123/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p123/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p123/r2.claim: A non-obligatory vowel behaves like a transitional one: in رمتا and غزتا, the weak radical stays deleted as in رمت المرأة.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p123/r2.anchor: وقد جعلوا ما لم يلزم من الحركات كما لم يلزم من حركة التقاء الساكنين في أن لم يعتد به

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p123/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p123/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p123/r3.claim: For the poetic form لها متنتان خظاتا, al-Fārisī prefers the account of metrical restoration over deleting the dual nūn, since such deletion occurs with relatives.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p123/r3.anchor: وليس ذلك عندنا بأوجه القولين، لأن حذف نون التثنية إنما جاء في الموصولة نحو

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p87/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p87/r1.speaker: المسيبي وقالون
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p87/r1.claim: Al-Musayyibī and Qālūn report that Nāfiʿ hamzas النبيّ forms throughout the Qurʾān except al-Aḥzāb 50 and 53, where adjacent same-type kasra hamzas meet.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p87/r1.anchor: وإنما ترك همز هذين لاجتماع همزتين مكسورتين من جنس واحد ، هذا قول المسيبي وقالون

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p87/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p87/r2.speaker: ورش عن نافع
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p87/r2.claim: Warsh reports Nāfiʿ hamzas all forms but drops the second hamza when two meet, whether alike or different, as in the two al-Aḥzāb phrases.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p87/r2.anchor: وقال ورش عن نافع: إنه كان يهمزها جميعا، إلا أنه كان يروي عن نافع: أنه كان يترك الهمزة الثانية في المتفقتين والمختلفتين

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p87/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p87/r3.speaker: الباقون
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p87/r3.claim: All remaining readers leave hamza out of these forms.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p87/r3.anchor: وكان الباقون لا يهمزون من ذلك شيئا

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p87/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p87/r4.speaker: أبو زيد
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p87/r4.claim: Abū Zayd explains نبأت from moving from one land to another, but distinguishes this travel verb from the etymology of نبي.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p87/r4.anchor: قال أبو زيد: نبأت من أرض إلى أخرى، فأنا أنبأ نبأ ونبوءا: إذا خرجت منها إلى أخرى

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p87/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p87/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p87/r5.claim: Al-Fārisī derives نبي from نبأ, news, because a prophet reports from God, rather than from the travel verb.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p87/r5.anchor: ولكن من النبأ الذي هو الخبر، كأنه المخبر عن الله سبحانه

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p87/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p87/r6.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p87/r6.claim: He rejects derivation from النباوة, or both proposed roots, because Sibawayh’s diminutive and the agreed forms تنبأ and النبيئة establish hamza as the root consonant.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p87/r6.anchor: ليس كالعضة، لأن سيبويه زعم: أنهم يقولون في تحقير النبوة: كان مسيلمة نبوته نبيئة سوء

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p87/r7.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p87/r7.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p87/r7.claim: Agreement on تنبأ مسيلمة and النبيئة shows that the root has hamza, despite both hamza and weak-letter readings in the transmitted forms.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p87/r7.anchor: أجمعوا على تنبأ، ولا على النبيئة، بل جاء فيه الأمران: الهمز وحرف اللين

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p80/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p80/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p80/r1.claim: The kasra reading of both hāʾ and mīm in عليهم reflects the hāʾ's proximity to yāʾ and the need to break the meeting of two sukūns.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p80/r1.anchor: فالحجة لمن كسرهما أنه كسر الهاء لمجاورة الياء وكسر الميم لالتقاء الساكنين

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p80/r2.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p80/r2.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p80/r2.claim: The ḍamma reading of both letters preserves their original vowels: the pronoun was originally همو before the preposition.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p80/r2.anchor: والحجة لمن ضمهما أنه لما ضم الهاء على أصل ما كانت عليه حرك الميم ايضا بالضم على الأصل لأنه كان همو

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p80/r3.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p80/r3.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p80/r3.claim: A kasra on hāʾ with ḍamma on mīm combines yāʾ proximity with the mīm's original ḍamma, needed to avoid two sukūns.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p80/r3.anchor: والحجة لمن كسر الهاء مجاورة الياء وضم الميم لأنه لم يجد بدا من حركتها فحركها بما قد كان في الأصل لها

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p80/r4.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p80/r4.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p80/r4.claim: Al-Kisāʾī matches Ḥamza here but differs in أنعمت عليهم: there mīm stays still, avoiding a shift from yāʾ to ḍamma; here hāʾ returns to its original vowel before mīm is moved.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p80/r4.anchor: فقل لما كانت الميم ساكنة كره الخروج من ياء إلى ضمة فكسر الهاء لمجاورة الياء هناك

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p80#2/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p80#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p80#2/r1.claim: The hamzated form of النبيين derives from informing or announcing, as in the cited expressions about reporting truth and naming the angels.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p80#2/r1.anchor: فالحجة لمن همز أنه أخذه من قوله

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p80#2/r2.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p80#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p80#2/r2.claim: The unhamzated form is supported by the heaviness of hamza in Arabic speech; the cited Prophetic wording and Quraysh's non-hamzating illustrate this.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p80#2/r2.anchor: والدليل عليه قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم لست نبيء الله كأنه كره الهمز لأن قريشا

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p80#2/r3.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p80#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p80#2/r3.claim: The unhamzated form may derive from nabwa, an elevated place, because the Prophet reports from the exalted realm and conveys God's message.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p80#2/r3.anchor: والثاني أنه مأخوذ من النبوة وهي ما ارتفع من الأرض وعلا لأنه أخبر عن العالم العلوي وأتى به عن الله تعالى

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p80#2/r4.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p80#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p80#2/r4.claim: Arabic often drops hamza in words whose origins contain it; the author gives النبي، الخابية، البرية، الذرية، and الروية as parallels.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p80#2/r4.anchor: والثالث أن العرب تدع الهمزة من النبي وهو من أنبأت ومن الخابية وهي من خبأت ومن البرية وهي من برأ الله الخلق

QIRAAT-ER:2:61:48#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:61:48#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:2:61:48#1/r1.claim: The ḍamma on hāʾ is a canonical vowel-harmony variant of the kasra form and does not alter meaning.
QIRAAT-ER:2:61:48#1/r1.anchor: Ḍamma on hāʾ instead of kasra — canonical variant; dialectal vowel harmony difference; no semantic change

QIRAAT-ER:2:61:48#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:61:48#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:2:61:48#2/r1.claim: The kasra on mīm is a canonical case-vowel variant of the ḍamma form, varying in pause or connection without changing meaning.
QIRAAT-ER:2:61:48#2/r1.anchor: Kasra on mīm instead of ḍamma — canonical variant; case vowel variation in pause/connection; no semantic change

QIRAAT-ER:2:61:68#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:61:68#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:2:61:68#1/r1.claim: The hamzated nabīʾīn reading derives the word from informing rather than elevation, making the etymological distinction explicit.
QIRAAT-ER:2:61:68#1/r1.anchor: explicitly from n-b-ʾ (to inform) — the hamza-form anchors the etymology to

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p47/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p47/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p47/r1.claim: The Israelites tired of their single food and remembered their former life, so they asked Moses for produce from the earth.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p47/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ لن نصبر على طعام واحد ﴾ قال ملو طعامهم وذكروا عيشهم الذي كانوا فيه

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p47/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p47/r2.speaker: قتادة والحسن
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p47/r2.anchor: قال معمر وقال قتادة والحسن الفوم الخبز

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p47/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p47/r3.speaker: قتادة والحسن
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p47/r3.claim: The humiliation imposed on them means that they pay the poll tax by hand while subdued.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p47/r3.anchor: عن الحسن وقتادة في قوله ﴿ وضربت عليهم الذلة ﴾ قالا يعطون الجزية عن يد وهم صاغرون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p353/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p353/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p353/r10.claim: Ṭaʿām means whatever is eaten, analogously to ʿaṭāʾ for whatever is given, and is a generic noun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p353/r10.anchor: الطعام: اسم لما يطعم، كالعطاء، اسم لما يعطى، وهو جنس.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p353/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p353/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p353/r11.claim: Wāḥid means indivisible or something to which no second is added; waḥada/yahidu means to be alone.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p353/r11.anchor: الواحد: هو الذي لا يتبعض، والذي لا يضم إليه ثان. يقال: وحد يحد وحدا وحدة إذا انفرد.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p353/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p353/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p353/r12.claim: Duʿāʾ is calling aloud by the name of the person invoked, from daʿā/yadʿū.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p353/r12.anchor: الدعاء: التصويت باسم المدعو على سبيل النداء، والفعل منه دعا يدعو دعاء.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p353/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p353/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p353/r13.claim: The hamza in inbāt is causative: the word means bringing out something whose nature is to grow.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p353/r13.anchor: الإنبات: الهمزة فيه للنقل، وهو: الإخراج لما شأنه النمو.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p353/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p353/r14.speaker: ابن دريد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p353/r14.claim: Baql is a genus covering fresh growth eaten by people and animals; the land verbs mean that the land has become vegetated, and Ibn Durayd connects al-bāqillāʾ to it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p353/r14.anchor: البقل: جنس يندرج فيه النبات الرطب مما يأكله الناس والبهائم، يقال منه بقلت الأرض وأبقلت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p353/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p353/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p353/r15.claim: Qithāʾ is a generic noun whose singular is qithāʾa, with qāf either ḍamma or kasra; maqthaʾa means land rich in it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p353/r15.anchor: القثاء: اسم جنس واحده قثاءة، بضم القاف وكسرها، وهو هذا المعروف.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p353/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p353/r16.speaker: الخليل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p353/r16.anchor: وقال الخليل: هو الخيار، ويقال: أرض مقثأة: أي كثيرة القثاء.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r1.claim: Al-Ṣalt’s verse groups fūm with onion among the people’s provisions, supporting the reported garlic interpretation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r1.anchor: كانت منازلهم إذ ذاك ظاهرة ... فيها القراديس والفومان والبصل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r2.speaker: الصلت
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r2.claim: Al-Ṣalt’s verse cites fūm and onion among the people’s provisions, supporting the garlic reading.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r2.anchor:
وأنشد مؤرج لحسان:
وأنتم أناس لئام الأصول ... طعامكم الفول والحوقل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r3.speaker: مؤرج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r3.claim: Muʾarrij’s quotation of Ḥassān’s verse glosses its food words as fūm and onion.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r3.anchor: وأنشد مؤرج لحسان: وأنتم أناس لئام الأصول ... طعامكم الفول والحوقل يعني: الفوم والبصل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r4.claim: Neither consonant substitution is productive: thāʾ may become fāʾ and fāʾ may become thāʾ, as in athāfī/athāthī.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r4.anchor: وهذا كما أبدلوا بالفاء الثاء، قالوا في الأثافي: الأثاثي، وكلا البدلين لا ينقاس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r5.speaker: أبو مالك وجماعة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r5.claim: Abū Mālik and a group identify fūm as wheat; the cited Uḥayḥa ibn al-Jallāḥ poem speaks of cultivating it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r5.anchor: وقال أبو مالك وجماعة: الفوم: الحنطة، ومنه قول أحيحة بن الجلاح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r6.speaker: المبرد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r6.claim: The wheat meaning is identified as Egyptian usage and is al-Mubarrad’s preferred interpretation; al-Farrāʾ calls it an ancient dialect.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r6.anchor: قيل: وهي لغة مصر، وهو اختيار المبرد. وقال الفراء: وهي لغة قديمة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r7.speaker: ابن قتيبة، والزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r7.claim: Ibn Qutayba and al-Zajjāj say fūm means edible grains.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r7.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة والزجاج: هي الحبوب التي توكل.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r8.speaker: أبو عبيدة، وابن دريد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r8.claim: Abū ʿUbayda and Ibn Durayd define fūm as an ear of grain; Abū ʿUbayda specifies that this is the Asad dialect.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r8.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة وابن دريد: هي السنبلة، زاد أبو عبيدة بلغة أسد.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r9.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r9.claim: Other reported definitions make fūm the grains used for baking or bread itself.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r9.anchor: وقيل: الحبوب التي تخبز. وقيل: الخبز، تقول العرب: فوموا لنا، أي اخبزوا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r10.speaker: ابن قتيبة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r10.claim: Ibn Qutayba chooses the bread interpretation, supported by the cited poem using fūm as a verb for baking.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r10.anchor: واختاره ابن قتيبة قال: تلتقم الفالح لم يفوم ... تقمما زاد على التقمم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r11.speaker: قطرب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r11.claim: Quṭrub gives fūm three senses: an onion cluster, a large piece of meat, or a large mouthful.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r11.anchor: وقال قطرب: الفوم: كل عقدة في البصل، وكل قطعة عظيمة في اللحم، وكل لقمة كبيرة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r12.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r12.claim: Another view identifies fūm as chickpea in a Syrian dialect; its seller is called fāmī, a nisba form from fūmī, like shahli and dahri.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r12.anchor: وقيل: إنه الحمص، وهي لغة شامية، ويقال لبائعه: فامي، مغير عن فومي للنسب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r13.claim: ʿAdas is the familiar lentil; ʿAdas is also a proper name and a command used to urge a mule.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r13.anchor: العدس: معروف، وعدس وعدس من الأسماء الأعلام، وعدس: زجر للبغل.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r15.claim: Adnā may be the elative of dunūw, ‘nearness,’ from danā/yadnū.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r15.anchor: أدنى: أفعل التفضيل من الدنو، وهو القرب، يقال: منه دنا يدنو دنوا.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r16.speaker: الأخفش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r16.claim: ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān al-Akhfash derives adnā from danāʾa, baseness or poor quality, with hamza lightened to alif.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r16.anchor: وقال علي بن سليمان الأخفش: هو أفعل من الدناءة، وهي: الخسة والرداءة، خففت الهمزة بإبدالها ألفا.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r17.speaker: أبو زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r17.claim: Abū Zayd records the hamzated forms danuʾa/yadnaʾu and danāʾa/danāʾ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r17.anchor: وقال أبو زيد في المهموز: دنؤ الرجل، يدنأ دناءة ودناء، ودنأ يدنأ.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r18.speaker: غيره
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r18.claim: Another grammarian derives adnā from dūn, ‘lower in rank,’ as a transformed form of adwan, like awlā from wayl.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r18.anchor: وقال غيره: هو أفعل من الدون، أي أحط في المنزلة، وأصله أدون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r19.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r19.claim: Miṣr means a city and may derive from milking a sheep completely, drawing everything from its udder.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r19.anchor: المصر: البلد، مشتق من مصرت الشاة، أمصرها مصرا: حلبت كل شيء في ضرعها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r20.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r20.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r20.claim: Miṣr can instead mean a boundary between two lands; Hajar writes bimuṣawrihā for its borders, and the poem depicts the sun as a boundary between day and night.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p354/r20.anchor: وقيل المصر: الحد بين الأرضين، وهجر يكتبون: اشترى الدار بمصورها: أي بحدودها.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p356/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p356/r11.speaker: غيره
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p356/r11.claim: Another account says they tired of manna and quail, were told to descend to a city, and first encountered Jericho.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p356/r11.anchor: وقال غيره: ملوا المن والسلوى، فقيل لهم: اهبطوا مصرا، وكان أول ما لقوا أريحا.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p373/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p373/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p373/r7.claim: The Israelites were weary of the wilderness and repetitive food, distant from their familiar land and habits; they expressed impatience and asked Moses to petition God for them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p373/r7.anchor: وإذ قلتم يا موسى لن نصبر على طعام واحد: لما سئموا من الإقامة في التيه، والمواظبة على مأكول واحد،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p373/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p373/r8.speaker: أكثر أهل الظاهر من المفسرين
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p373/r8.claim: Most outward commentators regard the request as sinful because they disliked the manna and quail, Moses called their requested food inferior, and his question rebuked them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p373/r8.anchor: وأكثر أهل الظاهر من المفسرين على أن هذا السؤال كان معصية، قالوا: لأنهم كرهوا إنزال المن والسلوى،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p373/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p373/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p373/r9.claim: Abū Ḥayyān replies that saying they could not endure one food shows a desire for other foods, not necessarily dissatisfaction with what God provided; a rebuke may concern forfeiting worldly or afterlife benefit.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p373/r9.anchor: والجواب، أن قولهم: لن نصبر على طعام واحد لا يدل على عدم الرضا به فقط، بل اشتهوا أشياء أخر.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374/r1.claim: Their request was permissible: the earlier eat-and-drink command was permission, so people allowed different foods may reasonably ask for another kind directly or through a messenger.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374/r1.anchor: وإنما كان سؤالا مباحا، والدليل عليه أن قوله: كلوا واشربوا من قبل هذه الآية، عند إنزال المن وتفجير العين ليس بإيجاب بل هو إباحة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374/r2.claim: They asked Moses because a prophet’s prayer is more likely to be answered; they had eaten the same food for forty years, were unused to it, and preferred familiar foods even when inferior.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374/r2.anchor: ولما كان سؤال النبي أقرب للإجابة، سألوه عن ذلك، ولأن النوع الواحد أربعين سنة يمل ويشتهى إذ ذاك غيره،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374/r3.claim: They may have sought other foods to leave the wilderness, where those foods were unavailable; variety also improves appetite and digestion compared with a single repeated food.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374/r3.anchor: ولأن ذلك يكون سببا لانتقالهم عن التيه الذي ملوه، لأن تلك الأطعمة لا توجد فيه،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374/r4.claim: Because replacing one food kind with another is a reasonable aim and the Qurʾān does not say they were forbidden to ask, the request cannot be treated as sinful.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374/r4.anchor: فثبت بهذا أن تبديل نوع بنوع يصلح أن يكون مقصودا للعقلاء، وثبت أنه ليس في القرآن ما يدل على أنهم كانوا ممنوعين عنه،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374/r5.claim: The response, descend to a town and you will have what you asked, confirms that the request was granted; granting a sinful request would be impermissible for prophets.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374/r5.anchor: ومما يؤكد ذلك قوله: اهبطوا مصرا فإن لكم ما سألتم هو كالإجابة لما طلبوا.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains one food as the unchanged manna and quail, which they called one because it did not vary from day to day.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374/r6.anchor: لأنهم أرادوا بالواحد ما لا يختلف ولا يتبدل، ولو كان على مائدة الرجل ألوان عديدة يداوم عليها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374/r7.claim: Another explanation is that manna and quail were one class of luxurious fare, while the Israelites as agricultural people wanted familiar varied crops and vegetables.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374/r7.anchor: ويجوز أن يريدوا أنهما ضرب واحد لأنهما معا من طعام أهل التلذذ والسرف، ونحن قوم فلاحة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r1.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r1.claim: One explanation follows the singular grammatical form of ṭaʿām, not the fact that it refers to two foods.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r1.anchor: أعاد على لفظ الطعام من حيث أنه مفرد لا على معناه.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd says the Israelites mixed manna and quail, making them like one color that combines several things.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r2.anchor: وقيل: كانوا يأكلون المن والسلوى مختلطين، فيصير بمنزلة اللون الذي يجمع أشياء ويسمى لونا واحدا، قاله ابن زيد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r3.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r3.claim: Another explanation says they received manna alone for a period, became tired of it, and then received quail alone and tired of that.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r3.anchor: وقيل: كان طعامهم يأتيهم بصفة الوحدة، نزل عليهم المن فأكلوا منه مدة حتى سئموه وملوه،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r4.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r4.claim: Some take the one food to mean quail, since manna was a drink or sweet accompaniment and only quail counted as food to them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r4.anchor: وقيل: أرادوا بالطعام الواحد السلوى، لأن المن كان شرابا، أو شيئا يتحلون به،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r5.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r5.claim: Others compare calling two foods one to calling one source two, as in the verse about pearl and coral coming from two seas although they come only from the salty sea.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r5.anchor: وقيل: عبر عنهما بالواحد، كما عبر بالاثنين عن الواحد نحو: يخرج منهما اللؤلؤ والمرجان ،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r6.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r6.claim: Another view says they spoke while only one of the two foods was being sent down.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r6.anchor: وقيل: قالوا ذلك عند نزول أحدهما.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r7.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r7.claim: Another interpretation says they meant they could not endure everyone being wealthy and no one needing to serve another; the one food represents their common status in the wilderness before social differences returned.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r7.anchor: وقيل: معناه لن نصبر على أننا كلنا أغنياء، فلا يستعين بعضنا ببعض،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r8.claim: The author counts nine reported explanations for one food, including the two explanations attributed to al-Zamakhsharī on the preceding page.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r8.anchor: فهذه تسعة أقوال في معنى قوله: على طعام واحد.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r9.claim: Fa-dʿu lanā rabbaka means ask your Lord for us; the object of the prayer is omitted and understood as asking Him to produce the requested foods.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r9.anchor: فادع لنا ربك: معناه: اسأله لنا، ومتعلق الدعاء محذوف، أي ادع لنا ربك بأن يخرج كذا وكذا.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r10.speaker: بنو عامر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r10.claim: The Banū ʿĀmir dialect pronounces the command fa-dʿi with kasra on the ʿayn, treating daʿā as a weak verb like ramā-yarmī.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r10.anchor: ولغة بني عامر: فادع بكسر العين، جعلوا دعا من ذوات الياء، كرمى يرمي،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r11.claim: The Israelites asked Moses to pray because a prophet’s prayer was more likely to be answered; saying your Lord reflects his special closeness through conversation and revelation of the Torah.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r11.anchor: وإنما سألوا من موسى أن يدعو لهم بما اقترحوه ولم يدعوا هم، لأن إجابة الأنبياء أقرب من إجابة غيرهم،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r12.claim: They said your Lord because God had specially favored Moses through intimate speech and giving him the Torah, so they hoped He would answer Moses’s prayer for them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r12.anchor: ولذلك قالوا: ربك، ولم يقولوا: ربنا، لأن في ذلك من الاختصاص به ما ليس فيهم من مناجاته وتكليمه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r13.claim: Yukh r ij is jussive as the response to the command udʿu, parallel to the response in the verse about fulfilling God’s covenant.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r13.anchor: يخرج لنا: جزمه على جواب الأمر الذي هو ادع، وقد مر نظيره في أوفوا بعهدي أوف بعهدكم .

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r14.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r14.claim: Another grammatical analysis supplies an omitted command, ask Him to bring the foods forth, with yukh r ij responding to that command.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r14.anchor: وقيل: ثم محذوف تقديره: وقل له أخرج فيخرج، مجزوم على جواب هذا الأمر الذي هو أخرج.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r15.speaker: بعضهم
