ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r15.claim: Some say yukh r ij is jussive under an unexpressed lām of command; Basran grammarians do not allow this analysis.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r15.anchor: وقيل: جزم يخرج بلام مضمرة، وهي لام الطلب، أي ليخرج، وهذا عند البصريين لا يجوز.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r16.speaker: سيبويه
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r16.claim: Sībawayh takes min in مما تنبت الأرض as partitive, with an omitted object of yukh r ij meaning something edible from what the earth grows.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r16.anchor: مما تنبت الأرض: مفعول يخرج محذوف ومن تبعيضية: أي مأكولا مما تنبت، هذا على مذهب سيبويه.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r17.speaker: الأخفش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r17.claim: Al-Akhfash takes min as redundant and mā as a relative pronoun with an omitted object pronoun, a deletion that meets the required conditions.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r17.anchor: وقال الأخفش: من زائدة، التقدير: ما تنبت، وما موصولة، والعائد محذوف تقديره، تنبته،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r18.speaker: بعضهم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r18.claim: Some take mā as a verbal noun, meaning from the earth’s growing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r18.anchor: وأجاز بعضهم أن تكون ما مصدرية تقديره: من إنبات الأرض.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r19.speaker: أبو البقاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r19.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ rejects the verbal-noun analysis because an omitted concrete object cannot be described by a verbal noun; saying the earth grows is figurative, since God causes growth and the earth only receives it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p374#2/r19.anchor: قال أبو البقاء: لا يجوز ذلك لأن المفعول المقدر لا يوصف بالإنبات، لأن الإنبات مصدر،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p375/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p375/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p375/r1.claim: The phrase من بقلها is an appositive to مما تنبت الأرض with the preposition repeated, a fluent construction.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p375/r1.anchor: من بقلها: هذا بدل من قوله: مما تنبت الأرض، على إعادة حرف الجر، وهو فصيح في الكلام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p375/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p375/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p375/r2.claim: Both occurrences of من are partitive and attach to يخرج, either directly or through an estimated repeated verb; the latter analysis is standard.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p375/r2.anchor: فمن على هذا التقدير تبعيضية، كهي في مما تنبت، ويتعلق بيخرج، إما الأولى، وإما أخرى مقدرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p375/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p375/r3.speaker: أبو البقاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p375/r3.claim: Abu al-Baqa allows من بقلها to explain the kind and treats it as an accusative circumstantial phrase from an omitted pronoun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p375/r3.anchor: فقال أبو البقاء: موضعها نصب على الحال من الضمير المحذوف تقديره: مما تنبته الأرض

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p375/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p375/r4.speaker: المهدوي وابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p375/r4.claim: Al-Mahdawi and Ibn Atiyya call من بقلها an appositive even though they take the two prepositions to have different senses.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p375/r4.anchor: وأما المهدوي، وابن عطية فزعما مع قولهما: إن من في من بقلها بدل من قوله: مما تنبت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p375/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p375/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p375/r5.claim: The appositive analysis fails if the first من is partitive but the second is explanatory, since the two particles then differ in meaning.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p375/r5.anchor: فقد اختلف مدلول الحرفين، واختلاف ذلك كاختلاف الحرفين، فلا يجوز البدل إلا إن ذهب ذاهب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p375/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p375/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p375/r6.claim: He prefers taking both particles as partitive; his school rejects the explanatory sense of من here and reinterprets its evidence.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p375/r6.anchor: والمختار ما قدمناه من كون من في الموضعين للتبعيض، وأما أن تكون لبيان الجنس، فقد أباه أصحابنا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p375/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p375/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p375/r7.claim: The greens mean choice vegetables people eat, such as mint, celery, and leek.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p375/r7.anchor: والمراد بالبقل هنا: أطايب البقول التي يأكلها الناس، كالنعناع، والكرفس، والكراث، وأشباهها، قاله الزمخشري

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p375/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p375/r8.speaker: يحيى بن وثاب وطلحة بن مصرف
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p375/r8.claim: They read وقثائها with a ḍamma on qāf, which is an established dialect form.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p375/r8.anchor: وقرأ يحيى بن وثاب وطلحة بن مصرف وغيرهما: وقثائها بضم القاف، وقد تقدم أنها لغة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p375/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p375/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p375/r9.claim: One interpretation takes فومها as garlic; Ibn Masud's ثومها reading supports it and fits the neighboring foods.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p375/r9.anchor: أحدها: أنه الثوم، وبينته قراءة ابن مسعود: وثومها بالثاء، وهو المناسب للبقل والعدس والبصل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p375/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p375/r10.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة والسدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p375/r10.anchor: الثاني: قاله ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة والسدي: أنه الحنطة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p375/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p375/r11.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p375/r11.claim: Another interpretation takes فومها to mean all grains.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p375/r11.anchor: الثالث: أنه الحبوب كلها. الرابع: أنه الخبز

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p375/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p375/r12.speaker: مجاهد وابن عطاء وابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p375/r12.anchor: الرابع: أنه الخبز، قاله مجاهد وابن عطاء وابن زيد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p375/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p375/r13.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p375/r13.claim: Another interpretation takes فومها to mean chickpeas.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p375/r13.anchor: الخامس: أنه الحمص. السادس: أنه السنبلة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p375/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p375/r14.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p375/r14.claim: A final interpretation takes فومها to mean a grain ear or spike.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p376/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p376/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p376/r1.claim: The listed foods span hot, cold, moist, and dry qualities: greens vary, cucumber is cold and moist, garlic hot and dry, lentils cold and dry, and onion hot and moist unless cooked.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p376/r1.anchor: وثانيا القثاء، وهو بارد رطب. وثالثا: الثوم، وهو حار يابس. ورابعا: العدس، وهو بارد يابس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p376/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p376/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p376/r2.claim: This sequence of five foods follows their differing temperamental qualities.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p376/r2.anchor: فعلى هذا جاء ترتيب ذكر هذه الخمسة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p376/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p376/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p376/r3.claim: The pronoun in قال most naturally refers to Moses.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p376/r3.anchor: الضمير في قال ظاهر عوده على موسى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p376/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p376/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p376/r4.claim: The pronoun could instead refer to God, supported by the ensuing command and promise.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p376/r4.anchor: ويحتمل عوده على الرب تعالى، ويؤيده اهبطوا مصرا فإن لكم ما سألتم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p376/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p376/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p376/r5.claim: The interrogative hamza in أتستبدلون expresses denial, and istibdāl means taking something in exchange.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p376/r5.anchor: والهمزة في أتستبدلون للإنكار، والاستبدال: الاعتياض

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p376/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p376/r6.speaker: أبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p376/r6.claim: Ubayy reads أتبدلون; the wording is figurative because God alone effects the change, but their request makes them seem to change it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p376/r6.anchor: وقرأ أبي: أتبدلون، وهو مجاز لأن التبديل ليس لهم إنما ذلك إلى الله تعالى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p376/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p376/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p376/r7.claim: In the construction, الذي is the object and denotes what is gained, while the item introduced by باء is what is given up.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p376/r7.anchor: والذي: مفعول أتستبدلون، وهو الحاصل، والذي دخلت عليه الباء هو الزائل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p376/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p376/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p376/r8.claim: On the Basran analysis, هو أدنى is the relative clause and أدنى its predicate; the comparison phrase من ذلك الطعام الواحد is omitted because the comparative is predicative and its counterpart follows.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p376/r8.anchor: هو أدنى: صلة للذي، وهو هنا واجب الإثبات على مذهب البصريين، إذ لا طول في الصلة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p376/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p376/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p376/r9.claim: الذي is singular because it points back to the food and to ما in مما تنبت; agreement with the appositive would instead require a feminine plural.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p376/r9.anchor: وأفرد: الذي هو أدنى لأنه أحال به على المأكول الذي هو مما تنبت الأرض، وعلى ما من قوله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p376/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p376/r10.speaker: زهير الفرقبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p376/r10.claim: Zuhayr al-Farqabi, also called Zuhayr al-Kisa'i, reads أدنأ with hamza.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p376/r10.anchor: وقرأ زهير الفرقبي، ويقال له زهير الكسائي: أدنأ بالهمز

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p377/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p377/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p377/r1.claim: A commentator mistakenly split Zuhayr al-Kisa'i into two people when attributing the anomalous reading; Zuhayr al-Kisa'i and al-Farqabi are one man.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p377/r1.anchor: فظن أن هذه قراءة الكسائي، وجعل زهيرا والكسائي شخصين، وإنما هو زهير الكسائي يعرف بذلك، وبالفرقبي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p377/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p377/r2.speaker: الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p377/r2.claim: The first explanation measures superiority by value: vegetables are of little worth beside the more valuable manna and quails.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p377/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج: تفاضل الأشياء بالقيم، وهذه البقول لا خطر فيها ولا علو قيمة، والمن والسلوى هما أعلا قيمة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p377/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p377/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p377/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari chooses the value reading, glossing أدنى as lower in rank and less in worth; nearness can figuratively mean small value.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p377/r3.anchor: واختار هذا الزمخشري، قال: أقرب منزلة وأهون مقدارا، والدنو والقرب يعبر بهما عن قلة المقدار

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p377/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p377/r4.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p377/r4.claim: A second explanation says manna and quails were God's gift and commanded food, so continuing to obey and thank Him earned reward in the afterlife, unlike the requested food.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p377/r4.anchor: الثاني: أن المن والسلوى هو الذي من الله به وأمرهم بأكله، وفي استدامة ما أمر الله به وشكر نعمته أجر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p377/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p377/r5.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p377/r5.claim: A third explanation grounds the comparison in taste and pleasure: manna and quails are better tasting than the vegetables requested.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p377/r5.anchor: الثالث: أن التفضيل يقع من جهة الطيب واللذة، والمن والسلوى لا شك أنهما أطيب من البقول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p377/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p377/r6.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p377/r6.claim: A fourth explanation values freedom from toil: manna and quails came without labor, while crops required cultivation and care.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p377/r6.anchor: الرابع: أن المن والسلوى لا كلفة في تحصيله ولا تعب ولا مشقة، والبقول لا تحصل إلا بعد مشقة الحرث

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p377/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p377/r7.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p377/r7.claim: A fifth explanation values lawful purity: manna and quails came from God free of the defects, usurpation, unlawful elements, and doubts that can affect crops.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p377/r7.anchor: الخامس: أن المن والسلوى لا شك في حله وخلوصه لنزوله من عند الله، والحبوب والأرض يتخللها العيوب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p377/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p377/r8.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p377/r8.claim: A sixth explanation says manna and quails are superior in the kind of nourishment and benefit they provide.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p377/r8.anchor: السادس: أن المن والسلوى يفضلان ما سألوه من جنس الغذاء ونفعه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p377/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p377/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p377/r9.claim: The six explanations locate superiority in value, obedience and reward, pleasure, effort, lawfulness, or the kind of food.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p377/r9.anchor: وملخص هذه الأقوال: هل الأدنوية والخيرية بالنسبة إلى القيمة، أو امتثال الأمر وما يترتب عليه، أو اللذة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p377/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p377/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p377/r10.claim: Zuhayr's hamzated reading derives أدنأ from lowliness; the unhamzated form may also have originated with hamza and been softened.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p377/r10.anchor: وأما قراءة زهير فهي من الدناءة. وقد تقدم أن أدنى غير المهموز قيل إن أصلها الهمز فسهل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p377/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p377/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p377/r11.claim: If أدنى arose by metathesis from أدون, both forms mean lowliness and make a better contrast with خير; if it means nearer, its opposite is farther.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p377/r11.anchor: ومن قال بالقلب وإن أصله أدون، فالدناءة والدون راجعان إلى معنى واحد، وهو الخسة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p377/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p377/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p377/r12.claim: The omitted comparison after خير is منه, referring back to الذي هو أدنى; both relative clauses are nominal to express unbounded states, while the verbal clause مما تنبت suits recurring growth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p377/r12.anchor: وحذف من ومعمولها بعد قوله: هو خير، لما ذكرناه في قوله: هو أدنى، من وقوع أفعل التفضيل خبرا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p378/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p378/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p378/r1.claim: If Moses said أتستبدلون, the narrative omits that he prayed and God answered before the command هبطوا.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p378/r1.anchor: في الكلام حذف على تقدير أن القائل: أتستبدلون هو موسى، وتقدير المحذوف، فدعا موسى ربه فأجابه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p378/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p378/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p378/r2.claim: هبطوا مصرا can mean settle in a city; هبط منه means leave it, as though a person arriving in a town descends upon it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p378/r2.anchor: ويقال: هبط الوادي: حل به، وهبط منه: خرج، وكأن القادم على بلد ينصب عليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p378/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p378/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p378/r3.claim: A reading with ḍamma on the bāʾ in اهبطوا is another dialect form; kasra is more eloquent.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p378/r3.anchor: وقرىء اهبطوا، بضم الباء، وهما لغتان، والأفصح الكسر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p378/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p378/r4.speaker: الحسن وطلحة والأعمش وأبان بن تغلب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p378/r4.claim: They read مصر without tanwin, as also written in the codices of Ubayy, Ibn Masud, and some Uthmanic copies; most readers give it tanwin.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p378/r4.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وطلحة والأعمش وأبان بن تغلب: بغير تنوين، وبين كذلك في مصحف أبي بن كعب، ومصحف عبد الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p378/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p378/r5.speaker: قتادة والسدي ومجاهد وابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p378/r5.claim: With tanwin, مصر can mean any unspecified city, supported by the command to enter a town, later settlement in Syria, and the need for cities to obtain the foods requested.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p378/r5.anchor: وبأنهم سكنوا الشام بعد التيه، وبأن ما سألوه من البقل وغيره لا يكون إلا في الأمصار، وهذا قول قتادة والسدي ومجاهد وابن زيد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p378/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p378/r6.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p378/r6.claim: The tanwin may still indicate an unspecified city, specifically one among the cities of the Holy Land, as supported by the command to enter the Holy Land.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p378/r6.anchor: وقيل: هو مصر غير معين لكنه من أمصار الأرض المقدسة، بدليل: ادخلوا الأرض المقدسة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p378/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p378/r7.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p378/r7.claim: An indefinite مصر may refer specifically to Pharaoh's Egypt, using an indefinite noun for a known person or place, as in asking for a man while meaning Zayd.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p378/r7.anchor: وقيل: أراد بقوله: مصرا وإن كان غير معين مصر فرعون، وهو من إطلاق النكرة، ويراد بها المعين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p378/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p378/r8.speaker: مالك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p378/r8.claim: Malik identified the place as Egypt, the speaker's town where Pharaoh lived, in a report transmitted by Ashhab.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p378/r8.anchor: قال أشهب، قال لي مالك: هي مصر قريتك مسكن فرعون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p378/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p378/r9.speaker: المعربون والمفسرون
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p378/r9.claim: Some grammarians and exegetes allow the tanned مصر to be a proper name, explaining its declension by its lightness or by treating it as a place noun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p378/r9.anchor: وأجاز من وقفنا على كلامه من المعربين والمفسرين أن تكون مصر هذه المنونة هي الاسم العلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p378/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p378/r10.speaker: الأخفش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p378/r10.claim: Al-Akhfash explains declension despite proper-name and feminine status by the word's lightness from a still middle consonant.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p378/r10.anchor: كما صرف هند ودعد لمعادلة أحد السببين، لخفة الاسم لسكون وسطه، قاله الأخفش

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p378/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p378/r11.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p378/r11.claim: Al-Zamakhshari compares مصر, when treated as a proper name, to Nuh and Lut, which are declined despite foreignness because they are short with a still middle consonant.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p378/r11.anchor: وشبهه الزمخشري في منع الصرف، وهو علم بنوح ولوط حيث صرفا، وإن كان فيهما العلمية والعجمة لخفة الاسم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p379/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p379/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p379/r1.claim: Abu Hayyan says foreignness only blocks declension in names longer than three letters, so a three-letter name with a still middle consonant is declined.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p379/r1.anchor: وبخلاف نوح، فإن العجمة لم تعتبر إلا في غير الثلاثي الساكن الوسط

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p379/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p379/r2.speaker: عيسى بن عمر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p379/r2.claim: Isa ibn Umar allowed مصر to be diptote by analogy with Hind, but this is unattested from Arabs except in the declined form, so the author rejects the analogy.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p379/r2.anchor: وقد أجاز عيسى بن عمر منع صرفه قياسا على هند، ولم يسمع ذلك من العرب إلا مصروفا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p379/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p379/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p379/r3.claim: The proposed diptote form rests on analogy to a disputed case and conflicts with Arabic usage, so it must be discarded.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p379/r3.anchor: فهو قياس على مختلف فيه مخالف لنطق العرب، فوجب اطراحه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p379/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p379/r4.speaker: الحسن بن بحر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p379/r4.claim: Hasan ibn Bahr says مصر means Jerusalem: although indefinite in form, it refers to a specific place.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p379/r4.anchor: وقال الحسن بن بحر: المراد بقوله مصرا، البيت المقدس، يعني أن اللفظ، وإن كان نكرة، فالمراد به معين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p379/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p379/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p379/r5.claim: The un-tanwined reading مصر means the proper name of Pharaoh's land.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p379/r5.anchor: وأما من قرأ مصر بغير تنوين، فالمراد مصر العلم، وهي دار فرعون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p379/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p379/r6.speaker: بعض الناس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p379/r6.claim: Some reject Pharaoh's Egypt because the Israelites left it, refused to fight the giants in the Holy Land, wandered for forty years and died, while their descendants entered Syria and later returned to Jerusalem; no exegete or historian says the wanderers went to Egypt.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p379/r6.anchor: واستبعد بعض الناس قول من قال: إنها مصر فرعون، قال: لأنهم من مصر خرجوا، وأمروا بالهبوط إلى الأرض المقدسة لقتال الجبارين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p379/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p379/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p379/r7.claim: He summarizes four tanwin interpretations: an unspecified city anywhere, an unspecified Syrian city, Jerusalem as a specific place, or Pharaoh's Egypt.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p379/r7.anchor: فتلخص من قراءة التنوين: أن يكون المراد مصرا غير معين لا من الشام ولا من غيره، أو مصرا غير معين من أمصار الشام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p379/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p379/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p379/r8.claim: فإن لكم ما سألتم answers the imperative like a jussive clause; grammarians dispute whether اهبطوا implies a conditional or has an omitted condition.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p379/r8.anchor: هذه الجملة جواب للأمر، كما يجاب بالفعل المجزوم، ويجري فيه الخلاف الجاري فيه: هل ضمن اهبطوا مصرا معنى أن تهبطوا أو أضمر الشرط

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p379/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p379/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p379/r9.claim: The construction omits both a locative link, فيها, and the pronoun in سألتموه, with the conditions for ellipsis satisfied.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p379/r9.anchor: وفي ذلك محذوفان: أحدهما: ما يربط هذه الجملة بما قبلها، وتقديره: فإن لكم فيها ما سألتم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p379/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p379/r10.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي ويحيى بن وثاب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p379/r10.claim: They read سألتم with a kasra on the initial sīn, a form produced by overlap between two verb patterns for سأل.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p379/r10.anchor: وقرأ إبراهيم النخعي ويحيى بن وثاب: سألتم: بكسر السين، وهذا من تداخل اللغات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p379/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p379/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p379/r11.claim: The verb has a hamza-root pattern and a wāw-root pattern; يتساولان, analogous to يتجاوبان, supports the latter.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p379/r11.anchor: ويدل على أنه من الواو، وقولهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p380/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p380/r1.speaker: شاعر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p380/r1.claim: The cited poetic form سأيلتهم is analyzed as the hamzated ساءلتهم with a yāʾ substitution; the poet combines the substitute with the hamza it replaces under metrical pressure.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p380/r1.anchor: الأصل ساءلتهم، والمعروف إبدال الهمزة ياء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p380/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p380/r2.speaker: ابن جني
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p380/r2.claim: Ibn Jinni offers another account: hamza in سألتم became yāʾ as in a cited line, then the sīn was kasrated before yāʾ and the speaker restored hamza.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p380/r2.anchor: وقال ابن جني: يحتمل أن يكون إبدال الهمزة في سألتم ياء، كما أبدلت ألفا في قوله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p380/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p380/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p380/r3.claim: The request refers to the vegetables and grains they chose over manna and quails.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p380/r3.anchor: والمعنى: ما سألتم من البقول والحبوب التي اخترتموها على المن والسلوى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p380/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p380/r4.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p380/r4.claim: Another interpretation takes the request to mean their reliance on managing their own livelihoods and food supplies.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p380/r4.anchor: وقيل: ما سألتم من اتكالكم على تدبير أنفسكم في مصالح معاشكم وأحوال أقواتكم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p381/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p381/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p381/r1.claim: If باء means return, its preposition marks accompanying state; if it means deserve, the preposition completes the verb; if it means settle or become equal, it is locative, with different attachment analyses.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p381/r1.anchor: فعلى من قال: باء: رجع، تكون الباء للحال، أي مصحوبين بغضب، ومن قال: استحق، فالباء صلة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p381/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p381/r2.speaker: الأخفش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p381/r2.claim: Al-Akhfash takes the preposition as causal and attached to باء, with an omitted object: they deserved punishment because God was angry with them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p381/r2.anchor: وزعم الأخفش أن الباء في قوله بغضب للسبب، فعلى هذا تتعلق بباء، ويكون مفعول باء محذوفا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p381/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p381/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p381/r3.claim: The verb باء is used with good outcomes as well as evil ones, contrary to the claim that it occurs only for evil.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p381/r3.anchor: وباء يستعمل في الخير: لنبوئنهم من الجنة غرفا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p381/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p381/r4.speaker: بعض الناس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p381/r4.claim: Some claim باء is used only in evil contexts.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p381/r4.anchor: وقال بعض الناس: باء لا تجيء إلا في الشر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p381/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p381/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p381/r5.claim: A Prophetic supplication uses باء for both a blessing and a sin, confirming the two usages.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p381/r5.anchor: في الحديث: «أبوء بنعمتك علي وأبوء بذنبي»

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p381/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p381/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p381/r6.claim: Wrath here can mean the worldly calamities and punishments that befell them or punishment awaiting them in the afterlife.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p381/r6.anchor: والغضب هنا ما حل بهم من البلاء والنقم في الدنيا، أو ما يحل بهم من العذاب في الآخرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p381/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p381/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p381/r7.claim: باءوا may carry a present-tense sense, as in other expressions where an impending event is stated in the past tense.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p381/r7.anchor: ويكون باؤوا في معنى يبوؤون، نحو

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p381/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p381/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p381/r8.claim: من الله may attach to باءوا if باء means return, suggesting they turned away from God through disobedience; alternatively it adjectivally describes غضب, the clearer analysis with the meanings deserve or settle.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p381/r8.anchor: من الله يحتمل أن يكون متعلقا بباءوا إذا كان باء بمعنى رجع، وكأنهم كانوا مقبلين على الله تعالى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p381/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p381/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p381/r9.claim: Describing the wrath as being from God magnifies and exalts its seriousness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p381/r9.anchor: وفي وصف الغضب بكونه من الله تعظيم للغضب، وتفخيم لشأنه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p381/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p381/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p381/r10.claim: ذلك may point to the punishment of wrath, or to the blow of humiliation and poverty.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p381/r10.anchor: والضرب وهو مبتدأ، والجار والمجرور بعده خبر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p381/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p381/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p381/r11.claim: In ذلك بأنهم, ذلك is the subject, the following prepositional phrase its predicate, and باء marks cause: this happened because they disbelieved and killed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p381/r11.anchor: والضرب وهو مبتدأ، والجار والمجرور بعده خبر، والباء للسبب، أي ذلك كائن بكفرهم وقتلهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p381/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p381/r12.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p381/r12.claim: God's signs may mean Moses's nine miracles and others, the Torah, selected Torah passages, the Qur'an, or all signs revealed to the messengers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p381/r12.anchor: الآيات المعجزات التسع وغيرها التي أتى بها موسى، أو التوراة، أو آيات منها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p381/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p381/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p381/r13.claim: The signs are attributed to God because they originate from Him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p381/r13.anchor: وإضافة الآيات إلى الله لأنها من عنده تعالى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p381/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p381/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p381/r14.claim: The prophets they killed included John, Isaiah, and Zechariah.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p381/r14.anchor: ويقتلون النبيين: قتلوا يحيى وشعيا وزكريا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p382/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p382/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p382/r1.claim: A report from Ibn Masud says the Israelites killed seventy prophets; another version says three hundred in the morning, with killings openly active by evening.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p382/r1.anchor: وروي عن ابن مسعود قتل بنو إسرائيل سبعين نبيا، وفي رواية ثلاثمائة نبي في أول النهار

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p382/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p382/r2.speaker: علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p382/r2.claim: Ali's doubled-consonant reading يقتّلون intensifies the sense of repeated killing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p382/r2.anchor: وعلى هذا يتوجه قراءة من قرأ: يقتلون بالتشديد لظهور المبالغة في القتل، وهي قراءة علي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p382/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p382/r3.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p382/r3.claim: Hasan reads وتقتلون with second-person address, an instance of turning to address; another report gives the common third-person reading.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p382/r3.anchor: وقرأ الحسن: وتقتلون بالتاء، فيكون ذلك من الالتفات. وروي عنه بالياء كالجماعة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p382/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p382/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p382/r4.claim: When definite, النبيين and الأنبياء do not differ in meaning; without the article, the sound plural suggests few and the broken plural suggests many.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p382/r4.anchor: ولا فرق في الدلالة بين النبيين والأنبياء، لأن الجمعين إذا دخلت عليهما ال تساويا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p382/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p382/r5.speaker: نافع
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p382/r5.claim: Nafi hamzates forms of نبي; Qalun replaces and assimilates the hamza in two connected readings in al-Ahzab, while most readers omit hamza.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p382/r5.anchor: وقرأ نافع: بهمز النبيين والنبيء والأنبياء والنبوءة، إلا أن قالون أبدل وأدغم في الأحزاب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p382/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p382/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p382/r6.claim: بغير الحق attaches to وتقتلون and is either a circumstantial phrase or a qualifier of an omitted verbal noun; both analyses are emphatic.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p382/r6.anchor: بغير الحق: متعلق بقوله: وتقتلون، وهو في موضع نصب على الحال من الضمير في تقتلون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p382/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p382/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p382/r7.claim: The wording does not imply any prophets were killed justly: prophets cannot deserve execution; the qualification shames and condemns the killers, who claimed no justified basis even by their own standard.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p382/r7.anchor: ولم يرد هذا على أن قتل النبيين ينقسم إلى قتل بحق وقتل بغير حق، بل ما وقع من قتلهم إنما وقع بغير حق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p382/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p382/r8.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p382/r8.claim: Another explanation treats the phrase as emphatic because no prophet ever brought anything warranting death; those killed were hated, and their killing raised their rank.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p382/r8.anchor: وقيل: جاء ذلك على سبيل التأكيد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p382/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p382/r9.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p382/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas and others say prophets not commanded to fight were killed, while every prophet commanded to fight was victorious.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p382/r9.anchor: قال ابن عباس وغيره: لم يقتل نبي قط من الأنبياء إلا من لم يؤمر بقتال، وكل من أمر بقتال نصر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r1.claim: One explanation takes definite الحق as an allusion to the established rule in the Prophetic hadith that Muslim blood is protected except in three cases.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r1.anchor: لا يحل دم امرئ مسلم إلا بإحدى ثلاث

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r2.claim: The definite wording can instead emphasize totality: no right existed, whether recognized by Muslims or anyone else.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r2.anchor: وأما المنكر فالمراد به تأكيد العموم، أي لم يكن هناك حق لا ما يعرفه المسلمون ولا غيره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r3.claim: The second ذلك may repeat the earlier reference to punishment, or point to disbelief and killing; on the latter reading it is neither repetition nor emphasis.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r3.anchor: ذلك: رد على الأول وتكرير له، فأشير به لما أشير بذلك الأول، ويجوز أن تكون إشارة إلى الكفر والقتل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r4.claim: Prior disobedience and transgression emboldened them to reject signs and kill prophets, since sins pave the way to disbelief.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r4.anchor: إنما هو تقدم عصيانهم واعتدائهم، فجسرهم هذا على ذلك، إذ المعاصي بريد الكفر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r5.claim: The cited verses describe deeds darkening hearts and connect the claim that hearts are veiled to God's curse and their disbelief.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r5.anchor: بل ران على قلوبهم ما كانوا يكسبون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r6.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r6.claim: Transgression is crossing God's boundary from what is right into falsehood.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r6.anchor: وقد فسر الاعتداء هنا أنه تجاوزهم ما حد الله لهم من الحق إلى الباطل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r7.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r7.claim: Another explanation takes transgression as persistence in disobedience and killing prophets.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r7.anchor: وقيل: التمادي على المخالفة وقتل الأنبياء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r8.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r8.claim: Another interpretation maps disobedience to breaking the covenant and transgression to killing many prophets.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r8.anchor: وقيل: العصيان بنقض العهد والاعتداء بكثرة قتل الأنبياء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r9.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r9.claim: Another gloss describes transgression as long-lasting disobedience and persistence in it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r9.anchor: وقيل: الاعتداء بسبب المخالفة والإقامة على ذلك الزمن الطويل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r10.speaker: أبو هريرة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r10.claim: A Prophetic report through Abu Hurayra says the Israelites split five hundred years after Moses when children of captives multiplied, and split again a hundred years after Jesus.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r10.anchor: أثر عن أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r11.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r11.claim: Another explanation identifies the transgression as their violation of the Sabbath prohibition.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r11.anchor: وقيل: هو الاعتداء في السبت، قال تعالى: وقلنا لهم لا تعدوا في السبت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r12.claim: ما in بما عصوا is a verbal noun marker, so the phrase means because of their disobedience.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r12.anchor: وما: في قوله بما عصوا مصدرية، أي ذلك بعصيانهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r13.claim: اعتداء is not coordinated with عصيان to preserve the verse endings and suggest transgression had become their habitual, continual act.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r13.anchor: ولم يعطف الاعتداء على العصيان لئلا يفوت تناسب مقاطع الآي، وليدل على أن الاعتداء صار كالشيء الصادر منهم دائما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r14.speaker: صاحب المنتخب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r14.claim: The punishment is explained by causes ordered by gravity: first disbelief in God's signs, then killing prophets, then lesser sins and transgression.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r14.anchor: فبدأ بأعظم الأسباب في ذلك، وهو كفرهم بآيات الله. ثم ثنى بما يتلو ذلك في العظم وهو قتل الأنبياء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r15.claim: The first causal clause explains humiliation and wrath; the second points to disbelief and killing, mapping the two punishments to those two causes as a balanced luff-and-nashr and avoiding redundancy.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p383/r15.anchor: قال معنى هذا صاحب المنتخب، ويظهر أن قوله ذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p384/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p384/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p384/r3.claim: They wearied of the provision and asked Moses to intercede for familiar foods; he rebuked them for trading precious, effortless manna and quails for laborious, harmful foods that stole worship time and impaired body and perception.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p384/r3.anchor: ثم ذكر تعالى تبرمهم من الرزق الذي امتن به عليهم، فلجوا في طلب ما كان مألوفهم إلى نبيهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p384#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p384#2/r1.speaker: الخليل بن أحمد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p384#2/r1.claim: Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad subsisted on barley flour and fresh water, yet had an exceptionally bright mind and strong body, campaigning one year and making pilgrimage the next.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p384#2/r1.anchor: كان الخليل بن أحمد، رحمه الله، يستف دقيق الشعير، ويشرب عليه الماء العذب، وكان ذهنه أشرق أذهان أهل زمانه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p384#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p384#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p384#2/r2.claim: The Israelites were then told to settle where their request could be met and descend to the source of the foods they wanted.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p384#2/r2.anchor: ثم أمروا بالحلول فيما فيه مطلبهم والهبوط إلى معدن ما سألوه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p384#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p384#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p384#2/r3.claim: Their humiliation, poverty, and wrath resulted from rejecting miraculous signs that should have led to faith and killing prophets whose guidance brings worldly honor and salvation; earlier disobedience and transgression led to those acts.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p384#2/r3.anchor: وأن ذلك متسبب عن كفرهم بالآيات التي هي سبب الإيمان، لما احتوت عليه من الخوارق التي أعجزت الإنس والجان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p384#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p384#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p384#2/r4.claim: The poet's lines illustrate how small beginnings can stir great consequences, fitting the claim that earlier disobedience grew into disbelief and murder.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p384#2/r4.anchor: إن الأمور صغيرها ... مما يهيج له العظيم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p384#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p384#2/r5.speaker: شاعر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p384#2/r5.claim: A second poetic line says people may underestimate evil even as it grows.

QASHANI:2:61/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:61/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:61/r1.claim: The Israelites’ one food is spiritual nourishment through knowledge, gnosis, and wisdom.
QASHANI:2:61/r1.anchor: الغذاء الروحاني من العلم والمعرفة والحكمة

QASHANI:2:61/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:61/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:61/r2.claim: Their request to Moses means asking God to permit the soul’s base desires, low pleasures, stale amusements, and other ego-centered satisfactions.
QASHANI:2:61/r2.anchor: يرخص لنا فيما تنبته أرض نفوسنا من الشهوات الخبيثة واللذات الخسيسة

QASHANI:2:61/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:61/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:61/r3.claim: Egypt signifies the city of the body; humiliation is the condition following pursuit of desires and greed for possessions, while misery means lasting need and dwelling in the lower realm.
QASHANI:2:61/r3.anchor: اهبطوا مصرا } أي: مدينة البدن { فإن لكم } فيها { ما سألتم وضربت عليهم الذلة

QASHANI:2:61/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:61/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:61/r4.claim: Incurring divine wrath signifies deserving distance from and expulsion by God; their downfall follows from being veiled from His signs and manifestations.
QASHANI:2:61/r4.anchor: باحتجابهم عن آيات الله وتجلياته، والباقي ظاهر

QASHANI:2:61/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:61/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:61/r5.claim: On a second inward reading, killing the prophets means attacking the heart’s prophets without a sound warrant, through falsehood, disobedience to heart and intellect, and transgression against their guidance.
QASHANI:2:61/r5.anchor: وبقتلهم أنبياء القلوب بغير أمر ثابت لهم عليهم يتوجه به ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r1.claim: The request is included in the account of blessings: God grants what they asked for by ordering them down to a town, although their ingratitude deserved wrath.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r1.anchor: الظاهر أنه داخل في تعداد النعم وتفصيلها

ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r2.claim: Their declaration that they could not endure one food signals aversion to the manna and quails and failure to thank God for an effortless provision.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r2.anchor: فإنه يدل على كراهيتم إياه إذ الصبر حبس النفس في المضيق

ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r3.claim: The episode resembles their earlier resistance after hearing God's speech, followed by their destruction and then the gift of life.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r3.anchor: حيث عاندوا بعد سماع الكلام وأهلكوا ثم أفاض عليهم نعمة الحياة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r4.speaker: الرازي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r4.claim: Al-Razi argues that the request could not be sinful because God answered it, since answering a sinful request would itself be sinful and prophets cannot do that.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r4.anchor: ما قال الإمام الرازي لو كان سؤالهم معصية لما أجابهم لأن الإجابة إلى المعصية معصية

ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r5.claim: The author endorses al-Salikuti's judgment that al-Razi's inference is weak: granting the request does not make their ungrateful demand virtuous.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r5.anchor: قال مولانا الساليكوتي ومن هذا ظهر ضعف ما قال الإمام الرازي

ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r6.claim: One food can mean a single, unchanging regimen, even if it consists of the two foods manna and quails.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r6.anchor: بإعتبار كونه على نهج واحد كما يقال :

ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r7.claim: Another explanation is that the Israelites sought familiar agricultural produce because manna and quails were luxurious foods unlike their usual fare.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r7.anchor: من طعام أهل التلذذ والسرف وكأن القوم كانوا فلاحة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r8.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r8.claim: A reported explanation says they cooked manna and quails together, making one dish.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r8.anchor: إنهم كانوا يطبخونهما معا فيصير طعاما واحدا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r9.claim: The author calls it a weak account that the request preceded the descent of the quails.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r9.anchor: والقول بأن هذا القول كان قبل نزول

ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r10.claim: It is even less plausible that “one food” meant only quails because manna was a drink or sweetener and therefore supposedly did not count as another food.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r10.anchor: وأهون منه القول بأنهم أرادوا بالطعام الواحد

ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r11.claim: The proposal that a singular “one” stands for two foods is still less plausible; the cited comparison uses a dual expression for pearls that come from only one sea.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r11.anchor: وإلا نزل القول بأنه عبر بالواحد عن الإثنين كما عبر بالإثنين عن الواحد

ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r12.claim: The phrase asks Moses to pray on their behalf for the listed produce; the conjunction marks their impatience as the reason for asking.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r12.anchor: فأدع لنا ربك أي سله لأجلنا بدعائك إياه بأن يخرج لنا كذا وكذا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r13.speaker: بنو عامر
ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r13.claim: Banu ʿAmir read the imperative with kasra on its final letter, treating دعا like the defective verb رمى.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r13.anchor: ولغة بني عامر ( فأدع ) بكسر العين

ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r14.claim: They asked Moses to pray because prophetic prayers are more likely to be answered; more generally, one person's prayer for another is especially apt to be answered.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r14.anchor: لأن دعاء الأنبياء عليهم الصلاة والسلام أقرب للإجابة من دعاء غيرهم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r15.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r15.claim: The Prophet asked ʿUmar to include him among those for whom he prayed.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r15.anchor: لهذا قال صلى الله عليه وسلم لعمر رضي الله تعالى عنه : أشركنا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r16.speaker: الأثر
ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r16.claim: A transmitted saying urges prayer through tongues that have not disobeyed God, understood here as other people's tongues.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r16.anchor: وفي الأثر أدعوني بألسنة لم تعصوني فيها وحملت على ألسنة الغير

ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r17.claim: Calling God “Lord” prepares the grounds for the prayer's acceptance.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r17.anchor: والتعرض لعنوان الربوبية لتمهيد مبادي الإجابة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r18.claim: They say “your Lord” because Moses had a special intimacy with God through His favor, direct speech, and the Torah, as if asking him to pray to the benefactor who favored him.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p273/r18.anchor: لأن في ذلك من الإختصاص به ما ليس فيهم من مناجاته وتكليمه وإيتائه التوراة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r1.claim: Here “bring forth” is a figurative consequence of literal extraction: it means producing by creation, not merely revealing what was hidden.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r1.anchor: المراد بالإخراج المعنى المجازي اللازم للمعنى الحقيقي وهو الإظهار بطريق الإيجاد

ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r2.claim: The literal reading would require the earth to be an extractor and make the statement nonsensical.

ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r3.claim: The verb يخرج is jussive as the response to the imperative; Basran grammarians do not allow explaining its jussive with an omitted لام الطلب.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r3.anchor: مجزوم لأنه جواب الأمر وجزمه بلام الطلب محذوفة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r4.claim: The first من is partitive: they ask for some of what the earth grows, specifically some edible produce.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r4.anchor: الأولى تبعيضية أي مأكولا بعض ما

ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r5.speaker: الأخفش
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r5.claim: Al-Akhfash treats the first من as extra, a parsing the author rejects.

ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r6.claim: ما is a relative pronoun with its object omitted; Abu al-Baqa rejects taking it as a verbal noun because the implied referent would be a substance.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r6.anchor: والعائد محذوف أي تنبته وجعلها مصدرية لم يجوزه أبو البقاء

ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r7.claim: Attributing growth to the earth is figurative, treating the receptacle as the agent; God placed the receptive capacity in the clay layer of the earth.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r7.anchor: مجاز من باب النسبة إلى القاب وقد أودع الله تعالى في الطبقة الطينية

ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r8.claim: Locating the receptive power in the seed rather than the soil could lead to the claim that seeds have existed eternally as a kind.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r8.anchor: وكون القوة القابلة مودعة في الحب دون التراب ربما يفضي إلى القول بقدم الحب بالنوع

ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r9.claim: The second من may be explanatory, with the phrase functioning as a circumstantial expression meaning “being among the greens.”
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r9.anchor: فالظرف مستقر واقع موقع الحال اي كائنا من

ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r10.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r10.claim: Abu Hayyan instead takes the second من as partitive, in apposition to ما, with the phrase attached directly to يخرج.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r10.anchor: وقال أبو حيان : تبعيضية واقعة موقع البدل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r11.speaker: الساليكوتي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r11.claim: Al-Salikuti says both parsings imply that they sought only some of the listed items; treating the second من as explanatory alongside the first partitive would lose that meaning and suggest all items.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r11.anchor: كما قال الساليكوتي يفيد أن المطلوب إخراج بعض هؤلاء

ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r12.speaker: المولى عصام الدين
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r12.claim: Mawla ʿIsam al-Din's explanatory parsing would leave the wording implying that all listed plants were requested, since there is no prior specification.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r12.anchor: المولى عصام الدينل خلا الكلام عن الإفادة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r13.claim: Baql is a generic term for fresh plants eaten by people or animals; here it means edible herbs and greens.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r13.anchor: والبقل جنس يندرج فيه النبات الرطب مما يأكله الناس والأنعام والمراد به هنا أطابيب البقول

ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r14.claim: The familiar qiththa is identified as cucumber; al-Khalil also says it means cucumber.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r14.anchor: والقثاء هو هذا المعروف وقال الخليل : هو الخيار

ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r15.speaker: يحيى بن وثاب وغيره
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r15.claim: Yahya ibn Waththab and others read قثاء with damma on qaf, a dialect form.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r15.anchor: وقرأ يحيى إبن وثاب وغيرهبضم القاف وهو لغة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r16.speaker: الزجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r16.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the language authorities agree that الفوم means wheat and other grains used for baking.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r16.anchor: قال الزجاج : لا خلاف عند أهل اللغة أنا لقوما

ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r17.speaker: الكسائي وجماعة
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r17.claim: Al-Kisaʾi and a group identify الفوم as garlic; the text explains the reading through substitution of ثاء for فاء.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r17.anchor: وقال الكسائي وجماعة : هو الثوم وقد أدل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r18.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r18.claim: Ibn Masʿud's reading as garlic fits its pairing with onion and lentils, and the author's teacher inclines to that reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r18.anchor: قرأ إبن مسعود رضي الله تعالى عنه ونفس شيخنا عليه الرحمة إليه تميل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r19.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r19.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas is quoted as identifying الفوم with bread; the author says this can be understood as a word also applied to bread, though bread is unlikely here because it grows neither from earth nor alongside greens.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r19.anchor: وما في المعالم عن إبن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما منا لقوما لخبز يمكن توجيهه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r20.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r20.claim: One rationale for the sequence is its balance of hot, cold, moist, and dry qualities: greens encompass varieties, followed by cucumber, garlic, lentils, and onion.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r20.anchor: وجه ترتيب النظم أنه ذكر أولا ما هو جامع للحرارة والبرودة والرطوبة واليبوسة وهو البقل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r21.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r21.claim: Another rationale is that the list starts with food eaten without fire, then gives foods that should be cooked; onion may become cold and moist after cooking according to some.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274/r21.anchor: ذكر أولا ما يؤكل من غير علاج نار

ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r1.claim: The question أتستبدلون is a fresh sentence answering the implied question of what Moses or God said.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r1.anchor: إستئناف وقع جوابا عن سؤال مقدر كأنه قيل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r2.claim: The speaker may be God speaking through Moses, which suits the surrounding enumeration of blessings, or Moses himself, which better fits the discourse sequence.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r2.anchor: والقائل إما الله تعالى على لسان موسى عليه السلام ويرجحه كون المقام مقام تعداد النعم أو موسى نفسه وهو الأنسب بسياق النظم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r3.claim: The interrogative rebukes them, and الاستبدال means exchanging one thing for another.

ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r4.claim: Although inability to endure one food might imply wanting an addition, their aversion and ingratitude imply a wish to remove the blessing and replace it.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r4.anchor: يدل على كراهتم ذلك الطعام وعدم الشكر على النعمة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r5.claim: A reported view says they explicitly sought replacement, and the reply signals that receiving the requested food would mean losing manna and quails rather than combining the foods.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r5.anchor: إنهم طلبوا ذلك وخطابهم بهذا إشارة إلى أنه تعالى إذا أعطاهم ما سألوا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r6.claim: The explanation that the exchange takes place in the stomach is dismissed.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r6.anchor: الإستبدال في المعدة وهو كما ترى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r7.speaker: أبي بن كعب
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r7.claim: Ubayy read أتبدلون; this is figurative because God effects the change, but their request causes it, so they are described as exchangers.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ أبي أتبدلون وهو مجاز لأن التبديل ليس لهم إنما ذلك إلى الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r8.claim: The object is the thing they would obtain, while the noun with باء denotes what would be relinquished; أدنى qualifies the latter.

ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r9.claim: أدنى may derive from nearness or be inverted from دون, meaning inferior; on the first derivation, nearness is metaphorically used for low worth, as distance is used for honor.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r9.anchor: إما من الدنو أو مقلوب من الدون وهو على الثاني ظاهر

ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r10.speaker: زهير والكسائي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r10.claim: Zuhayr and al-Kisaʾi read أدنا with hamza, supporting derivation from الدناءة with hamza changed into alif.

ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r11.claim: The better food is manna and quails; its superiority lies in greater value, taste, benefit, ease of acquisition, and freedom from doubt about its lawfulness.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r11.anchor: ومعنى خيرية هذا المأكول بالنسبة إلى ذلك غلاء قيمته وطيب لذته

ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r12.claim: أهبطوا مصرا is a separate reported sentence; it is unjoined because the first is declarative and the second is not, and because descending explains how they could exchange foods.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r12.anchor: جملة محكية بالقول كالأولى وإنما لم يعطف إحداهما على الأخرى في المحكى لأن الأولى خبر معنى وهذه ليست كذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r13.claim: If both sentences are spoken by the same speaker, their separation has the stated grammatical rationale; if Moses and God speak them separately, the lack of conjunction is self-explanatory.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r13.anchor: هذا إذا جعل الجملتان من كلام الله تعالى أو كلام موسى وإن جعل إحداهما من موسى والأخرى من الله تعالى فوجه الفصل ظاهر

ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r14.claim: The pause after خبر is sufficient under the same-speaker analysis and complete under the two-speaker analysis.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r14.anchor: والوقف على خبر كاف على الأول وتام على الثاني

ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r15.claim: Descent may be spatial, if the wilderness is higher than the town, or a descent in rank; the contextual sense is the latter.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r15.anchor: وأن يكون رتبيا وهو الأنسب بالمقام

ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r16.claim: A reading has أهبطوا with damma on both hamza and ba.

ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r17.claim: مصر means a great town and originally denotes a boundary between two things; a quoted poetic line uses it for the boundary dividing day and night.

ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r18.claim: Deriving the town name from milking every drop from a sheep is far-fetched.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r18.anchor: وأخذه من مصرت الشاة أمصرها إذا حلبت كل شيء في ضرعها بعيد

ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r19.speaker: أشهب عن مالك
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r19.claim: Ashhab relates that Malik identified the place as Egypt, his town, where Pharaoh lived, making مصر a proper name.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r19.anchor: وحكى عن أشهب أنه قال : قال لي مالك : هي مصر قريتك

ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r20.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r20.claim: Place names can be masculine when considered as places and feminine when considered as lands; if مصر is a feminine town name it takes tanwin because its middle consonant is still.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r20.anchor: وأسماء المواضع قد تعتبر من حيث المكانية فتذكر وقد تعتبر من حيث الأرضية فتؤنث

ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r21.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r21.claim: The claim that مصر is a proper name is supported by Ibn Masʿud's codex spelling it without alif after ra, but opposed by the Qur'anic tanwin and by the command to enter the holy land, understood as Syria, which implies they were confined to the wilderness.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r21.anchor: ويؤيد ما قاله الإمام مالك رضي الله تعالى عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r22.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r22.claim: Some derive مصر from the Arabicized Misraim, a son of Noah who first laid out the city; Arabicization permits declension because foreignness no longer governs the form.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p274#2/r22.anchor: ومن اناس من جعل ( مصر ) معرب

ALUSI-FULL:v1p275/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p275/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p275/r1.claim: “You will have what you asked” explains the order to descend; al-Bahr instead calls it an answer to the imperative, which can be answered by a clause, with an implied link and pronoun: “therein” and “what you asked for.”
ALUSI-FULL:v1p275/r1.anchor: فإن لكم ما سألتم تعليل للأمر بالهبوط وفي البحر أنها جواب للأمر

ALUSI-FULL:v1p275/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p275/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p275/r2.claim: Calling the requested items simply ما avoids naming them directly as a sign of disdain.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p275/r2.anchor: والتعبير عن الأشياء المسئولة ب ( ما )

ALUSI-FULL:v1p275/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p275/r3.speaker: النخعي ويحيى
ALUSI-FULL:v1p275/r3.claim: Al-Nakhaʿi and Yahya read سألتم with kasra on the first letter.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p275/r3.anchor: وقرأ النخعي ويحيى ( سألتم ) بكسر السين

ALUSI-FULL:v1p275/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p275/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p275/r4.claim: The image of humiliation being laid over them evokes either a tent or dome set over people or clay plastered onto a wall; the metaphor conveys encompassing, adherence, and humiliation.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p275/r4.anchor: أي جعل ذلك محيطا بهم إحاطة القبة بمن ضربت عليه أو ألصق بهم من ضرب الطين على الحائط

ALUSI-FULL:v1p275/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p275/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p275/r5.claim: The image alludes to their poll tax paid in submission, distinctive clothing that identifies them as Jews, ingrained miserliness and inner poverty, and their habit of displaying hardship to avoid increased tax.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p275/r5.anchor: وذلك بما ضرب عليهم من الجزية التي يؤدونها عن يد وهم صاغرون وبما ألزموه من إظهار الزي

ALUSI-FULL:v1p275/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p275/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p275/r6.claim: Their humiliation is retribution for ingratitude toward the blessing, linking this punishment to the preceding account; the third-person pronoun includes all Jews through later generations and is not an instance of iltifat.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p275/r6.anchor: وهذا الضرب مجازاة لهم على كفران تلك النعمة وبهذا أرتبطت الآية بما قبلها

ALUSI-FULL:v1p275/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p275/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p275/r7.claim: باءوا may mean they settled into worldly trials, afterlife punishment, or hardships in both worlds; it may also mean that wrath came upon them, so no object of “return” is needed.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p275/r7.anchor: أي نزلوا وتمكنوا بما حل بهم من البلاء والنقم في الدنيا أو بما تحقق لهم من العذاب في العقبى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p275/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p275/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p275/r8.claim: Other interpretations say they became fitting for wrath or deserved punishment; the author calls the latter account far-fetched.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p275/r8.anchor: أو صاروا أحقاء به أو استحقوا العذاب بسببه وهو بعيد

ALUSI-FULL:v1p275/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p275/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p275/r9.claim: The root باء first denotes equality of parts and then any equivalence or matching, as in saying someone is another's equal and in cited idioms and a prophetic warning.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p275/r9.anchor: واصل البواء بالفتح والضم مساواة الأجزاء ثم أستعمل في كل مساواة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p275/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p275/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p275/r10.claim: Describing the wrath as coming from God heightens and magnifies its severity.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p275/r10.anchor: وفي وصف الغضب بكونه من الله تعالى تعظيم لشأنه بعد تعظيم وتفخيم بعد تفخيم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p276/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p276/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p276/r1.claim: The demonstrative refers to the preceding humiliation, poverty, and wrath; its distance may reflect the intervening material, their surprising punishment despite being People of the Book, or the enormity of these deeds.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p276/r1.anchor: أشار بذلك إلى ما سبق من ضرب الذلة والمسكنة والبوء بالغضب العظيم وإنما بعده لبعد بعضه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p276/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p276/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p276/r2.claim: The causal باء introduces an interpreted verbal noun; the nominal wording highlights repeated disbelief and killing over time or vividly recalls their ugly acts.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p276/r2.anchor: والباء للسببية وهي داخلة على المصدر المؤل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p276/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p276/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p276/r3.claim: The signs may mean miracles generally, Moses's nine signs, those nine and other miracles, revealed scriptural signs generally, the Torah or some of its verses, verses describing Muhammad, the stoning passages, or the Qur'an.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p276/r3.anchor: إما المعجزات مطلقا أو التسع التي أتى بها موسى عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v1p276/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p276/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p276/r4.claim: Attributing the signs to God intensifies the condemnation; disbelief is mentioned first because it is the gravest offense, then prophet-killing as its consequence or source.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p276/r4.anchor: وفي إضافة الآيات إلى أسمه تعالى زيادة تشنيع عليهم وبدا سبحانه بكفرهم بآياته لأنه أعظم كل عظيم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p276/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p276/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p276/r5.claim: The indefinite plural النبيين appears fewer than الأنبياء, while the two forms are equivalent when definite, so the report that they killed three hundred prophets in one morning does not contradict the wording.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p276/r5.anchor: وأتى بالنبيين الظاهر في القلة دون الأنبياء الظاهر في الكثرة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p276/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p276/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p276/r6.claim: One explanation of “without right” is that they knew the murders were unjust: worldly desire, caprice, and excess drove them; on this reading the definite article points to a known right.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p276/r6.anchor: للإيذان بأن ذلك بغير الحق عندهم إذ لم يكن أحد معتقدا حقية قتل أحد منهم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p276/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p276/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p276/r7.claim: A more apparent reading takes الحق generically, meaning no right at all; the parallel wording in 3:112 supports this and means the killings were unjust even in their own view.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p276/r7.anchor: الأظهر أنها للجنس والمراد بغير حق أصلا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p276/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p276/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p276/r8.claim: The phrase may simply expose the escalating ugliness of their conduct—killing a prophet, killing a group, and doing so without right—which best fits the ordinary sense of prohibition regardless of the killer's beliefs.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p276/r8.anchor: إظهار معايب صنيعهم فإنه قتل النبي ثم جماعة منهم ثم كونه بغير الحق

ALUSI-FULL:v1p276/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p276/r9.speaker: بعض المتأخرين
ALUSI-FULL:v1p276/r9.claim: A later scholar says the qualifier is useful if غير means “for a cause other than the truth”: they killed prophets for falsehood and to defend it.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p276/r9.anchor: قال بعض المتأخرين : هذا كله إذا كان الغير بمعنى النفي

ALUSI-FULL:v1p276/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p276/r10.speaker: القفال
ALUSI-FULL:v1p276/r10.claim: Al-Qaffal says they claimed prophets were liars and their miracles deceptions, and killed them for this reason and to suppress what they regarded as truth.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p276/r10.anchor: ما قاله القفال : من إنهم كانوا يقولون

ALUSI-FULL:v1p276/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p276/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p276/r11.claim: That false accusation explains many cases, but Isaiah, John, and Zechariah were killed for other reasons: Isaiah rebuked factional violence after a king's death, John was killed over a woman, and Zechariah was sawn in two inside a tree while fleeing the king.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p276/r11.anchor: ولعل ذلك غالب أحوالهم وإلا فشعياء ويحيى وزكريا عليهم السلام لم يقتلوا لذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v1p276/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p276/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p276/r12.claim: The apparent syntax makes بغير الحق a contested modifier governed by both disbelief and killing; al-Bahr attaches it to the nearby killing alone.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p276/r12.anchor: ثم الظاهر أن الجار والمجرور مما تنازع فيه الكفر والقتل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r1.claim: An atheist alleges a contradiction between Israelite prophet-killing and God's promise to help His messengers.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r1.anchor: تناقضا وأجيب بأن المقتولين من الأنبياء والموعود بنصرهم الرسل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r2.claim: One reply distinguishes the prophets who were killed from the messengers promised help.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r2.anchor: وأجيب بأن المقتولين من الأنبياء والموعود بنصرهم الرسل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r3.claim: The distinction fails because 2:87 also says that some messengers were killed.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r3.anchor: يدل على أن المقتول رسل أيضا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas is reported to say that God decreed that seventy thousand people would be killed for each prophet and thirty-five thousand for each caliph; the author finds this answer unsound.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r4.anchor: كما روى عن إبن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما أن الله تعالى قدر أن يقتل بكل نبي سبعين ألفا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r5.speaker: بعض المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r5.claim: The preferred answer limits the promised messengers to those commanded to fight; their exposure to death is not incompatible with divine wisdom.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r5.anchor: فالأحسن أن المراد بالرسل المأمورون بالقتال كما أجاب به بعض المحققين

ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r6.speaker: علي والحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r6.claim: ʿAli and, in one report, al-Hasan read يقتلون with a doubled qaf.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r6.anchor: وقرأ علي رضي الله تعالى عنه : يقتلون بالتشديد

ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r7.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r7.claim: In another reading, al-Hasan uses second-person تقتلون, creating a shift in address.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r7.anchor: وتقتلون بالتاء فيكون ذلك من الالتفات

ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r8.speaker: نافع
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r8.claim: Nafiʿ reads النبيين with hamza, as he does النبي and النبوة.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r8.anchor: وقرأ نافع بهمز النبيين وكذا النبي والنبوة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r9.claim: A man addressed the Prophet as نبيء الله with hamza; the Prophet replied that he was نبي الله without hamza.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r9.anchor: بما روى أن رجلا قال للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يانبي الله بالهمز فقال لست بنبيء الله

ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r10.speaker: أبو زيد
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r10.claim: Abu Zayd traces نبأت to leaving the earth; the objection may have been to the ambiguity of “expelled by God,” not to the reading itself, and a prophet's use is not automatically permitted for people.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r10.anchor: بأن أبا زيد حكى نبأت من الأرض إذا خرجت منها فمنع لوهم أن معناه ياطريد الله

ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r11.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r11.claim: Another explanation confines the prohibition to early Islam, when Jewish subterfuge was prevalent, as with replacing راعنا by انظرنا.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r11.anchor: وقيل : إن النهي كان خاصا في صدر الإسلام

ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r12.claim: The plural نبيين is challenged because a passive participle is not normally given the sound masculine plural; a reply says the word is active, or that its original sense has faded so the common meaning permits the plural.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r12.anchor: جمع النبي على نبيين وهو فعيل بمعنى مفعول

ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r13.claim: The final ذلك points back to disbelief and prophet-killing as causes of the earlier punishments; a singular demonstrative can gather several matters by treating them as one mentioned event.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r13.anchor: إشارة إلى الكفر والقتل الواقعين سببا لما تقدم وجازت الإشارة بالمفرد إلى متعدد للتأويل بالمذكور

ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r14.claim: The following phrase gives the cause behind their disbelief and killings: earlier disobedience and transgression lead one sin to another, with the first cause emphasized because it might seem unexpected.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r14.anchor: وما بعدها سبب للسبب والمعنى إن الذي حملهم على الكفر بآيات الله تعالى وقتلهم الأنبياء إنما هو تقدم عصيانهم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r15.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r15.claim: A reported alternative takes the causal باء to mean “with,” and links the demonstrative to the earlier punishment; it omits a conjunction to show that each wrongdoing independently deserves punishment.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r15.anchor: وقيل : الباء بمعنى مع وقيل : الإشارة بذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r16.claim: The author rejects that alternative as repetitious and as losing the earlier subtle causal relation; it also leaves the demonstrative without a clear purpose.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r16.anchor: وضعف هذا الوجه بأن التكرار خلاف الأصل مع فوات معنى لطيف حصل بالأول

ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r17.claim: The spiritual lesson is that they refused God's decree, gratitude, and patience; tyranny and abasement took hold, worldly love filled their hearts, and they fell from their high station.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r17.anchor: وحظ العارف من هذه الآيات الإعتبار بحال هؤلاء الذين لم يرضوا بالقضاء ولم يشكروا على النعماء ولم يصبروا على البلواء

ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r18.claim: In the mystical reading, the one food is wisdom and knowledge, while earthly growth symbolizes vile desires and low pleasures arising from the base self in the body's Egypt; tasting them brings humiliation, poverty, and ruin.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r18.anchor: الطعام الواحد هو الغذاء الروحاني من الحكمة والمعرفة وما تنبته الأرض هو الشهوات الخبيثة واللذات الخسيسة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r19.claim: The mystical cause of this demand is veiling from divine signs, darkening hearts through sin, and heedlessness of the Beloved that replaces the sought goal with other things; the author asks for well-being.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p277/r19.anchor: وسبب طلب ذلك الإحتجاب عن آيات الله تعالى وتجلياته وتسويد القلوب بدرن الذنوب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r1.claim: The Israelites grew weary of eating manna and quail.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r1.anchor: وذلك أنهم أجمعوا وسئموا من أكل المن والسلوى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r2.claim: Although manna and quail are two foods, Arabs may refer to two as one and one as two; the pearl-and-coral verse is an example, though only the salt sea produces them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r2.anchor: وإنما قال {على طعام واحد} وهما اثنان لأن العرب تعبر عن الاثنين بلفظ الواحد كما تعبر عن الواحد بلفظ الاثنين،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r3.claim: Another view is that they ate one food together with the other, making them a single meal.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r3.anchor: وقيل: كانوا يأكلون أحدهما بالآخر فكانا كطعام واحد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r4.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r4.claim: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam says they kneaded manna with quail, making one food.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r4.anchor: وقال عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم: كانوا يعجنون المن بالسلوى فيصيران واحدا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r5.claim: “Ask for us” means ask God on our behalf.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says fūm means bread.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r8.speaker: القتيبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r8.claim: Al-Qutaybi says fūm means all edible grains.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r8.anchor: وقال القتيبي رحمه الله تعالى: الحبوب التي تؤكل كلها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r10.claim: One explanation makes wheat lower in value than manna and quail even though it is better; another says it is lower because it is ordinarily easier to obtain.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r10.anchor: وجعل الحنطة أدنى في القيمة وإن كان هي خيرا من المن والسلوى، أو أراد أنها أسهل وجودا على العادة،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r11.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r11.claim: “Better” may refer to God's choice for them as superior to their own choice.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r11.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الخير راجعا إلى اختيار الله لهم واختيارهم لأنفسهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r12.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r12.claim: “Go down to a city” means descend to one of the towns if they insist on these foods.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r12.anchor: يعني: فإن أبيتم إلا ذلك فانزلوا مصرا من الأمصار

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r13.speaker: الضحاك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r13.claim: Al-Dahhak identifies the city as the Egypt of Moses and Pharaoh; al-Baghawi prefers the generic meaning because the proper name Egypt would not take tanwīn.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r13.anchor: وقال الضحاك: هو مصر موسى وفرعون، والأول أصح، لأنه لو أراده لم يصرفه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r14.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r14.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r14.claim: What they requested means the plants of the earth.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r15.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r15.speaker: author
