BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r15.claim: “Was imposed upon them” means it was made binding on them.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r16.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r16.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r16.claim: One view interprets humiliation as the jizya tax.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r17.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r17.speaker: عطاء بن السائب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r17.claim: ʿAta ibn al-Saʾib explains humiliation as the Jewish kistīj, zunnār, and distinctive clothing.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r17.anchor: وقال عطاء بن السائب: هو الكستيج والزنار وزي اليهودية

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r18.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r18.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r18.claim: “Maskanah” means poverty; a poor person is so named because poverty stills and immobilizes him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r18.anchor: {والمسكنة} الفقر، سمي الفقير مسكينا لأن الفقر أسكنه وأقعده عن الحركة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r19.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r19.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r19.claim: Even wealthy Jews appear poor, and one view identifies humiliation as poverty of the heart; the Jews are described as especially abject and greedy for wealth among religious communities.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p100#2/r19.anchor: فترى اليهود وإن كانوا مياسير كأنهم فقراء، وقيل: الذلة هي فقر القلب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p101/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p101/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p101/r1.claim: “Bāʾū” means they returned, and the expression is used only of an evil thing.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p101/r1.anchor: {وباءوا بغضب من الله} رجعوا ولا يقال: "باءوا إلا بشر"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p101/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p101/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p101/r2.claim: Abu ʿUbayda says “bāʾū” means they bore and acknowledged the wrath, as in the prayer “I acknowledge Your favor and my sin.”
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p101/r2.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: احتملوا وأقروا به، ومنه الدعاء: أبوء {لك} (1) بنعمتك علي وأبوء بذنبي،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p101/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p101/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p101/r3.claim: “That” refers to the wrath just mentioned.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p101/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p101/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p101/r4.claim: The signs they disbelieved in included Muhammad's description, the Torah's stoning verse, the Gospel, and the Qurʾan.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p101/r4.anchor: بصفة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وآية الرجم في التوراة ويكفرون بالإنجيل والقرآن

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p101/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p101/r5.speaker: نافع
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p101/r5.claim: Nafiʿ alone pronounces the hamza in “nabī” and its related forms, giving the sense of one who announces.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p101/r5.anchor: {ويقتلون النبيين} تفرد نافع بهمز النبي وبابه، فيكون معناه المخبر من أنبأ ينبئ،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p101/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p101/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p101/r6.claim: The familiar reading omits the hamza; one explanation is that it was dropped for ease because the word is used frequently.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p101/r6.anchor: والقراءة المعروفة ترك الهمزة، وله وجهان: أحدهما هو أيضا من الإنباء، تركت الهمزة فيه تخفيفا لكثرة الاستعمال،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p101/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p101/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p101/r7.claim: Another derivation takes “nabī” to mean elevated, from a high place, with the word retaining its original form.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p101/r7.anchor: والثاني هو بمعنى الرفيع مأخوذ من النبوة وهي المكان المرتفع

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p101/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p101/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p101/r9.claim: Although killing prophets is always wrongful, “without right” describes the killing, as “judge with truth” describes judgment without implying that judgment divides into just and unjust kinds.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p101/r9.anchor: فإن قيل: فلم قال: بغير الحق وقتل النبيين لا يكون إلا بغير الحق؟ قيل ذكره وصفا للقتل،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p101/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p101/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p101/r10.claim: A report says the Jews killed seventy prophets in the morning and set up a marketplace to kill them again in the evening.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p101/r10.anchor: ويروى أن اليهود قتلت سبعين نبيا في أول النهار وقامت سوق بقتلهم في آخر النهار

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p101/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p101/r11.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p101/r11.claim: Their disobedience means they exceeded God's commands and committed His prohibitions.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r1.claim: The single food they could no longer bear was manna and quails from the wilderness.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r1.anchor: يريدون به ما رزقوا في التيه من المن والسلوى.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r2.claim: Its oneness means it did not vary or change, as in the expression that an emir's table has one food because its colors do not change.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r2.anchor: وبوحدته أنه لا يختلف ولا يتبدل، كقولهم طعام مائدة الأمير واحد يريدون أنه لا تتغير ألوانه

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r3.claim: Alternatively, it was one kind of food; though it suited people of luxury, the Israelites were farmers who longed for familiar fare.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r3.anchor: أو ضرب واحد، لأنهما طعام أهل التلذذ وهم كانوا فلاحة فنزعوا إلى عكرهم واشتهوا ما ألفوه.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r4.claim: They ask Moses to petition his Lord on their behalf.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r4.anchor: { فادع لنا ربك } سله لنا بدعائك إياه

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r5.claim: Yukhrij means to bring forth or make exist; its jussive form answers the petition because prayer causes the response.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r5.anchor: يظهر ويوجد، وجزمه بأنه جواب فادع فإن دعوته سبب الإجابة.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r6.claim: The phrase about what the earth grows uses figurative attribution, putting the recipient in the agent's place, and min is partitive.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r6.anchor: من الإسناد المجازي، وإقامة القابل مقام الفاعل، ومن للتبعيض.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r7.claim: The listed crops explain the preceding phrase as a circumstantial clarification; another analysis treats them as an appositive with the preposition repeated.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r7.anchor: تفسير وبيان وقع موقع الحال، وقيل بدل بإعادة الجار.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r8.claim: Baql means plants grown by the earth; here it refers to the choicest edible greens.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r8.anchor: والبقل ما أنبتته الأرض من الخضر والمراد به أطايبه التي تؤكل

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r9.claim: Fūm means wheat, and can also mean bread, as in the phrase ‘bring us bread’; another view takes it to mean garlic.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r9.anchor: والفوم الحنطة ويقال للخبز ومنه فوموا لنا، وقيل الثوم

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r10.claim: A reading pronounces qiththā with ḍamma, a dialectal form.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r10.anchor: وقرىء قثائها بالضم، وهو لغة فيه.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r11.claim: The speaker of ‘he said’ may be God or Moses.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r11.anchor: { قال } أي الله، أو موسى عليه السلام.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r12.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r12.claim: Adnā means nearer in rank and lower in worth; spatial nearness is metaphorically used for baseness and distance for honor.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r12.anchor: أقرب منزلة وأدون قدرا. وأصل الدنو القرب في المكان فاستعير للخسة كما استعير البعد للشرف والرفعة

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r13.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r13.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r13.claim: A reading has adnaʾ, derived from lowliness.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r14.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r14.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r14.claim: The better food means manna and quails, superior in pleasure, benefit, and freedom from the need to work for food.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r14.anchor: يريد به المن والسلوى فإنه خير في اللذة والنفع وعدم الحاجة إلى السعي.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r15.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r15.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r15.claim: Ihbiṭū miṣran means descend from the wilderness to it; the verb describes entering a valley or leaving a higher place.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r15.anchor: انحدروا إليه من التيه، يقال هبط الوادي إذا نزل به، وهبط منه إذا خرج منه

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r16.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r16.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r16.claim: Miṣr can mean a great city; the word originally denotes a boundary between two things.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r16.anchor: والمصر البلد العظيم وأصله الحد بين الشيئين

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r17.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r17.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r17.claim: A reported interpretation takes Miṣr as Egypt; its treatment as a proper name is supported by nonnunation in Ibn Masʿūd's codex.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r17.anchor: وقيل أراد به العلم، وإنما صرفه لسكون وسطه أو على تأويل البلد، ويؤيده أنه غير منون في مصحف ابن مسعود.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r18.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r18.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r18.claim: Another account derives the name from Miṣrātim and says it was Arabized.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r19.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r19.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r19.claim: Humiliation and poverty enveloped or clung to them like a canopy or plaster on a wall, as requital for ingratitude.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r19.anchor: أحيطت بهم إحاطة القبة بمن ضربت عليه، أو ألصقت بهم، من ضرب الطين على الحائط، مجازاة لهم على كفران النعمة.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r20.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r20.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r20.claim: Jews are generally humiliated and poor, either actually or by affectation for fear of increased jizya.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r20.anchor: واليهود في غالب الأمر أذلاء مساكين، إما على الحقيقة أو على التكلف مخافة أن تضاعف جزيتهم.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r21.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r21.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r21.claim: Bāʾū means they returned carrying anger or became deserving of God's anger; the idiom means someone is liable to be killed for another, and its root connotes equality.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r21.anchor: رجعوا به، أو صاروا أحقاء بغضبه، من باء فلان بفلان إذا كان حقيقا بأن يقتل به، وأصل البوء المساواة.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r22.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r22.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r22.claim: The demonstrative points back to the humiliation, poverty, and incurring of anger.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r22.anchor: إشارة إلى ما سبق من ضرب الذلة والمسكنة والبوء بالغضب.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r23.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r23.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r23.claim: God's signs may mean miracles they experienced: the sea split, clouds shaded them, manna and quails descended, and springs burst from stone.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r23.anchor: بسبب كفرهم بالمعجزات، التي من جملتها ما عد عليهم من فلق البحر، وإظلال الغمام، وإنزال المن والسلوى، وانفجار العيون من الحجر.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r24.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r24.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r24.claim: Alternatively, the signs are revealed scriptures, including the Gospel, Qurʾān, stoning verse, and the Torah's description of Muhammad.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r24.anchor: أو بالكتب المنزلة: كالإنجيل، والفرقان، وآية الرجم والتي فيها نعت محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم من التوراة

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r25.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r25.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r25.claim: They killed Isaiah, Zechariah, John, and others without grounds even by their own standards; desire and worldly love drove them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r25.anchor: وقتلهم الأنبياء فإنهم قتلوا شعياء وزكريا ويحيى وغيرهم بغير الحق عندهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r26.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r26.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r26.claim: Their disobedience, persistence, and transgression led them into disbelief in signs and killing prophets.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61/r26.anchor: أي: جرهم العصيان والتمادي والاعتداء فيه إلى الكفر بالآيات، وقتل النبيين.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61#2/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61#2/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61#2/r1.claim: Minor sins lead to major sins, just as minor acts of obedience lead toward greater acts.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61#2/r1.anchor: فإن صغار الذنوب سبب يؤدي إلى ارتكاب كبارها، كما أن صغار الطاعات أسباب مؤدية إلى تحري كبارها.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61#2/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61#2/r2.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61#2/r2.claim: The repeated demonstrative stresses that their punishment resulted both from disbelief and killing and from their sins and transgression.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61#2/r2.anchor: وقيل كرر الإشارة للدلالة على أن ما لحقهم كما هو بسبب الكفر، والقتل فهو بسبب ارتكابهم المعاصي واعتدائهم حدود الله تعالى.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61#2/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61#2/r3.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61#2/r3.claim: Alternatively, the demonstrative refers to disbelief and killing, with bāʾ meaning ‘along with’; a singular demonstrative can cover multiple matters under a contextual singular expression or ellipsis.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61#2/r3.anchor: وقيل الإشارة إلى الكفر والقتل، والباء بمعنى مع وإنما جوزت الإشارة بالمفرد إلى شيئين فصاعدا على تأويل ما ذكر، أو تقدم للاختصار

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61#2/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61#2/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61#2/r4.claim: Rubaʾ's description of a cow uses a singular pronoun for multiple marks, illustrating that demonstratives and pronouns are not strictly marked for real number or gender; alladhī can likewise mean plural.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:61#2/r4.anchor: ونظيره في الضمير قول رؤبة يصف بقرة: فيها خطوط من سواد وبلق كأنه في الجلد توليع البهق والذي حسن ذلك أن تثنية المضمرات والمبهمات وجمعها وتأنيثها ليست على الحقيقة، ولذلك جاء الذي بمعنى الجمع.

SULAMI:v1p61/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p61/r1.speaker: قيل
SULAMI:v1p61/r1.claim: People fall into two groups: those freed from self-direction and content with God's decree keep increasing, while those left to their own choices remain tossed about until they perish.
SULAMI:v1p61/r1.anchor: قيل : الناس فيه رجلان : رجل أزيل عنه تدبيره مستريح في ميدان الرضا راض بأحكام القضاء فيه ساء أم سر فهو في الزيادة أبدا

SULAMI:v1p61/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p61/r2.speaker: author
SULAMI:v1p61/r2.claim: The rebuke means they exchanged God's primordial choice for them for disobedient asking and desire; God's word does not change.
SULAMI:v1p61/r2.anchor: معناه : أتعارضون حسن اختياري لكم في الأزل بمخالفة الدعاء والسؤال ﴿ ما يبدل القول لدي ﴾ .

SULAMI:v1p61/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p61/r3.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p61/r3.claim: Al-Wasiti says they abandoned manna and quails, which came without effort, for food that suited their appetites and ordinary nature.
SULAMI:v1p61/r3.anchor: قال الواسطي في هذه الآية : ما يتولاه من المن والسلوى من غير كلفة لهم ، فتبع القوم شهوة نفوسهم وما يليق بطبائعهم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p147/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147/r1.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147/r1.claim: Al-Harali says prohibitions imply that people may violate them and commands that they may obey, since commands and bans display the distinction between the obedient and disobedient rather than compel what nature already does.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147/r1.anchor: قال الحرالي : وفيه إشعار بوقوع ذلك منهم , لأن في كل نهي إشعارا بمخالفته , إلا ما شاء الله

BIQAI-FULL:v1p147/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147/r2.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147/r2.claim: Al-Harali says their disobedience brought the humiliation God announced, and that corrupting the God-created bodies of human beings is an especially grave form of corruption.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147/r2.anchor: فكان منهم لذلك من العثي ما أوجب ما أخبر به الحق عنهم من الهوان

BIQAI-FULL:v1p147/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147/r3.claim: Israel denied the great gifts of manna, quail, and water by growing dissatisfied and requesting other food; their wilderness wandering was near at hand.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147/r3.anchor: ولما امتن عليهم بهذه النعمة العظمة من أكل المن والسلوى وشرب هذا الماء الرباني بين أنهم كفروها بالتضجر منها وطلب غيرها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p147/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147/r4.claim: Their address to Moses by his personal name shows a lack of deference.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147/r4.anchor: يا موسى } منادين له باسمه من غير تعظيم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p147/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147/r5.claim: لن نصبر means they would not endure the food for long.

BIQAI-FULL:v1p147/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147/r6.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147/r6.claim: Al-Harali defines food as what sustains the eater and becomes part of him, linking the word to the command to look at one's food.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147/r6.anchor: قال الحرالي : الطعام ما يقوت المتطعم ويصير جزاء منه { فلينظر الإنسان إلى طعامه * } [ عبس : 24 ] الآية - انتهى

BIQAI-FULL:v1p147/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147/r7.claim: Their complaint about one food means they did not want to remain with an unchanging provision, even though it was varied, noble, and effortless.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147/r7.anchor: { واحد } أي لا يتبدل وإن كان متعددا وإن كان شريفا لا تعب فيه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p147/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147/r8.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147/r8.claim: Al-Harali defines supplication as a humble, needy call requesting what necessity demands from the one who can provide it, unlike a command from a higher authority who does not need its object.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147/r8.anchor: قال الحرالي : من الدعاء وهو نداء لاقتضاء غلبة لما تدعو الحاجة إليه من القائم على الداعي بتذلل وافتقار

BIQAI-FULL:v1p147/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147/r9.claim: They attribute the title Lord to Moses rather than themselves despite God's repeated manifestation to them as benefactor.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147/r9.anchor: مضيفين لهذا الاسم إليه دون أنفسكم مع كثرة تجليه لكم بهذا الوصف الناظر إلى الإحسان

BIQAI-FULL:v1p147/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147/r10.claim: Their request that God bring food is made even if Moses himself is not attending to that matter.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147/r10.anchor: { يخرج لنا } أي وإن كنت أنت غير ملتفت إلى ذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v1p147/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147/r11.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147/r11.claim: Al-Harali glosses the earth's producing as nourishment and growth.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147/r11.anchor: من الإنبات وهو التغذية والتنمية - قاله الحرالي

BIQAI-FULL:v1p147/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147/r12.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147/r12.claim: Al-Harali says baql is the growth of the earth that supplements fatty foods; the author first identifies it as greens.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147/r12.anchor: قال الحرالي : البقل ما يكثر به الأدم , والأدم الأشياء الدسمة فما يصلح معها من نجم الأرض فهو بقل - انتهى

BIQAI-FULL:v1p147/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147/r13.claim: The author identifies fūm as wheat, while Al-Harali explains it as grain used for baking bread.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147/r13.anchor: { وقثائها وفومها } أي الحنطة . وقال الحرالي : يقال هو الحب الذي يخبز - انتهى

BIQAI-FULL:v1p147/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147/r14.claim: Moses' question rebukes them for exchanging what is lower in rank for what is better.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147/r14.anchor: { أتستبدلون } أي أتأخذون { الذي هو أدنى } أي منزلة { بالذي هو خير } أي بدله

BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r1.claim: The author notes that b-d-l has many constructions: the two things exchanged may be mentioned or omitted, the preposition may mark what is relinquished or received, and the verb may take one or two objects with differing senses.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r1.anchor: فالباء داخلة هنا على المتروك وهذه المادة أعني الباء والدال المهملة واللام بهذا الترتيب لها استعمالات كثيرة يختلف معناها معها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r2.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r2.claim: Al-Harali defines a miṣr as a substantial town where people coordinate worldly affairs and which gathers the kinds of goods Israel requested; smaller places do not have all of them.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r2.anchor: قال الحرالي : المصر هو البلد الجامع لما يتعاون عليه من أمور الدنيا الذي يجمع هذه المطالب التي طلبوها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r3.claim: Egypt's name suits its gathering of worldly needs and unusual water; even if it came from a man's name, that coincidence reflects God's knowledge and wisdom over all its details.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r3.anchor: فالوفاق في حكمه الله , لأن كل دقيق وجليل فيها جار بعلم الله وحكمته

BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r4.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r4.claim: Al-Harali defines asking as seeking what need calls for and what suffices, and says the requested goods are found in cities where God has established worldly wisdom, not in the wilderness.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r4.anchor: والسؤال قال الحرالي طلب ما تدعو إليه الحاجة وتقع به الكفاية , قال : وذكر تعالى أن مطلبهم إنما يجدونه في الأمصار

BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r5.claim: In the city they will get what they requested, while manna and quail will cease.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r5.anchor: { فإن لكم } أي فيه { ما سألتم } وينقطع عنكم المن والسلوى

BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r6.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r6.claim: Al-Harali says cities rarely exhibit extraordinary breaks in ordinary order; ascetics therefore seek travel and withdrawal from inhabited places to experience provision by God's word without the burden of His established order.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r6.anchor: وقل ما تنخرق في الأمصار والقرى , لما في هذه الآية مضمونة , ولذلك حرص السالكون على السياحة والانقطاع عن العمائر

BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r7.claim: The narrative telescopes events from Moses and Joshua through Israel's later decline, aggression, and killing of prophets, presenting worldly authority and wealth as the reason for preferring the present life.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r7.anchor: ولما نظم سبحانه بنبأ موسى عليه السلام ما كان من نبأهم مع يوشع عليه السلام بعده نظم في هذه الآية بخطاب موسى عليه السلام ما كان منهم بعد يوشع عليه السلام إلى آخر اختلال أمرهم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r8.claim: The history warns this Muslim community against following the People of the Book; the next comprehensive verse begins with the believers among this community before treating the other religious communities.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r8.anchor: وفي طيه أشد التحذير لهذه الأمة في اتباعهم لسنن أهل الكتاب في مثل أحوالهم ؛ ولذلك انتظم بها الآية الجامعة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r9.claim: Humiliation is pictured as a covering that surrounds Israel on every side, and the word denotes inward smallness under domination.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r9.anchor: { وضربت عليهم الذلة } ملازمة لهم محيطة بهم من جميع الجوانب كما يحيط البيت المضروب على الإنسان به , وهي اسم من الذل وهو صغار في النفس عن قهر وغلبة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r10.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r10.claim: Al-Harali reads the conjunction as signaling many omitted intervening events: Israel was placed where it had lowered itself, and enemies then subdued and humiliated those who remained.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r10.anchor: قال الحرالي : وفي عطفه إفهام لمجاوزة أنباء عديدة غايتها في الظهور ما عطف عليها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r11.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r11.claim: Al-Harali defines maskanah as outwardly visible lowliness or submission, shown in stillness and a slackening of movement.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r11.anchor: قال الحرالي : وهي ظهور معنى الذل أو التذلل على ظاهر الهيئة والصورة سكونا وانكفاف حراك - انتهى

BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r12.claim: Bāʾū means they returned, and they deserved the anger; the phrase can mean being liable to be killed in equivalence for another's killing.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r12.anchor: { وباؤوا } أي رجعوا وكانوا أحقاء { بغضب } من باء فلان بفلان إذا كان حقيقا بأن يقتل به لمساواته له

BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r13.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r13.claim: Al-Harali glosses their return with anger as a powerful ruler's resolve to exact vengeance for defiance.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r13.anchor: قال الحرالي : معناه إجماع القاهر على الانتقام في حق مراغمة - انتهى

BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r14.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r14.claim: Al-Harali warns Muslims against imitating Israel by trading higher, wholesome provision received freely for lower forbidden or doubtful worldly gains.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r14.anchor: قال الحرالي : وفيه تهديد لهذه الأمة بما غلب على أهل الدنيا منهم من مثل أحوالهم باستبدال الأدنى في المعنى من الحرام والمتشابه بالأعلى من الطيب

BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r15.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r15.claim: Al-Harali says anger falls on one who defies the Majestic through disobedience, so the text next states their deeds.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r15.anchor: قال الحرالي : ولما كان الغضب إنما يكون على من راغم الجليل في معصيته

BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r16.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r16.claim: The word dhālika may refer either to the anger and punishment they suffered or to their intense concern for livelihood and desires in this base fashion.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r16.anchor: ويجوز أن يرجع إلى اهتمامهم بأمر معاشهم وعنايتهم بأحوال شهواتهم على هذا النحو الأخس الأدنى

BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r17.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r17.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r17.claim: Kānū depicts a settled natural disposition; yakfurūna describes continuing, renewed concealment of assent and belief in God's signs, misleading those unaware of them.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r17.anchor: أي بسبب أنهم { كانوا } أي جبلة وطبعا { يكفرون } أي مجددين مستمرين { بآيات الله } أي يسترون إذعانهم وتصديقهم بسبب آيات الله

BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r18.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r18.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r18.claim: Al-Harali ranks denial of God's signs as farthest from faith and nearer than denial of God, since the former rejects manifest evidence while the latter rejects the unseen.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p147#2/r18.anchor: قال الحرالي : والكفر بالآيات أبعد الرتب من الإيمان , لأنه أدنى من الكفر بالله , لأن الكفر بالله كفر بغيب

BIQAI-FULL:v1p149/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p149/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p149/r1.claim: The author links denial of God's signs to the Qur'anic description of such deniers as companions of ill fortune.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p149/r1.anchor: { والذين كفروا بآياتنا هم أصحاب المشئمة * } ) 77 [ البلد : 19 ] انتهى .

BIQAI-FULL:v1p149/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p149/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p149/r2.claim: The author's description treats killing prophets as a settled disposition and habit.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p149/r2.anchor: { ويقتلون النبيين } أي كان ذلك جبلة لهم وطبعا

BIQAI-FULL:v1p149/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p149/r3.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p149/r3.claim: Al-Harali derives nabīʾ from nabaʾ, informing of an unseen matter the reporter could not know unaided.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p149/r3.anchor: قال الحرالي : وهذا جمع نبيء وهو من النبأ وهو الإخبار عن غيب عجز عنه المخبر به من حيث أخبر - انتهى

BIQAI-FULL:v1p149/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p149/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p149/r4.claim: Because a prophet is protected in religion and worldly life, killing him is never truly justified; the phrase stresses the absence of fully clear right, even if killers claim a pretext such as suspecting false prophethood.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p149/r4.anchor: ولما كان النبي معصوما دينا ودنيا قال { بغير الحق } أي الكامل تنبيها على أن قتله لا يقع إلا كذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v1p149/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p149/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p149/r5.claim: The blame concerns shedding blood without complete clarity, consistent with the prohibition against killing a protected person except by right.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p149/r5.anchor: فالذم على الإقدام على إراقة الدم بدون الوضوح التام وفاقا لنهي .

BIQAI-FULL:v1p149/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p149/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p149/r6.claim: A claimed suspicion, such as believing someone falsely claimed prophethood, does not excuse killing without certainty.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p149/r6.anchor: لكن هذا لا ينفي أن يكون ثم شبهة كظن التنبؤ

BIQAI-FULL:v1p149#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p149#2/r1.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p149#2/r1.claim: Al-Harali defines disobedience as violating a command.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p149#2/r1.anchor: قال الحرالي : وهو مخالفة الأمر - انتهى

BIQAI-FULL:v1p149#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p149#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p149#2/r2.claim: Their transgression was an ingrained habit that continued and emboldened them to commit grave acts.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p149#2/r2.anchor: وكانوا } أي جبلة وغريزة { يعتدون } أي يتجاوزون الحدود على سبيل التجدد والاستمرار

BIQAI-FULL:v1p149#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p149#2/r3.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p149#2/r3.claim: Al-Harali defines transgression as deliberately crossing a limit without excuse, because the person had been given latitude and the boundary was set.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p149#2/r3.anchor: قال الحرالي : وهو أي الاعتداء تكلف العداء , والعداء مجاوزة الحد , فيما يفسح فيه إلى حد لا عذر لمجاوزه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p149#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p149#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p149#2/r4.claim: The Qur'anic sequence of Israel's stories is not chronological; the author says the Torah's important correspondences explain its arrangement.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p149#2/r4.anchor: وقد جاء نظم هذه الآيات من قصصهم على غير ترتيبها في الوجود , وفي التوراة لما ذكرت من هذه المناسبات العظيمة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p149#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p149#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p149#2/r5.claim: The author says he consulted a current ninth-century Jewish copy of the Torah's fourth book, in an Arabic translation marked with reading times, and compared it with the meaning alongside a Jewish reader.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p149#2/r5.anchor: في النسخ الموجودة بين أظهر اليهود الآن في هذا القرن التاسع فيما قرأته في نسخة مترجمة بالعربية وخطها كذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v1p149#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p149#2/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p149#2/r6.claim: The Torah itinerary places Israel's departure from Rameses, also called Ain Shams in a variant, on the fifteenth of Nisan after Passover, with a variant dating it one day after Passover; Egyptians were burying their firstborn as Israel left armed.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p149#2/r6.anchor: ظعنوا من رعمسيس - وفي نسخة : من عين شمس - في خمسة عشر يوما من الشهر الأول من غد الفصح - وفي نسخة : بعد الفصح بيوم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p149#2/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p149#2/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p149#2/r7.claim: The cited Torah says Egypt was occupied with burying its slain firstborn and that the Lord had taken vengeance on the Egyptians' gods as Israel departed.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p149#2/r7.anchor: كانوا مشاغيل بدفن الأبكار الذين قتلهم الرب , وبما انتقم الرب من آلهتهم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p150/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p150/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p150/r1.claim: The Torah itinerary continues along the Red Sea coast, with variant names for the sea and several wilderness encampments through Rithmah.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p150/r1.anchor: على البحر الأحمر - وظعنوا من شاطئ بحر سوف - وفي نسخة : من البحر الأحمر - وفي أخرى : بحر القلزم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p150/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p150/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p150/r2.claim: At Rephidim there was no drinking water; the itinerary gives a variant name for the station.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p150/r2.anchor: ولم يكن هناك ماء يشرب الشعب وظعنوا من رفيدين - وفي نسخة : رفيديم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p150/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p150/r3.speaker: موسى
BIQAI-FULL:v1p150/r3.claim: Moses commands Israel to remember its liberation from Egyptian slavery through the annual festival of unleavened bread, observed for seven days, and to teach its meaning to their children.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p150/r3.anchor: قال موسى للشعب : اذكروا هذا اليوم الذي خرجتم فيه من مصر من العبودية والرق

BIQAI-FULL:v1p150/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p150/r4.speaker: موسى
BIQAI-FULL:v1p150/r4.claim: Moses says the observance is a sign and memorial because God brought Israel out with a mighty hand, and it should be kept year after year.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p150/r4.anchor: وتعلمون أبناءكم في ذلك اليوم وتقولون لهم إن الله فعل بنا هذا الفعل إذ أخرجنا من أرض مصر

BIQAI-FULL:v1p150/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p150/r5.speaker: موسى
BIQAI-FULL:v1p150/r5.claim: The Torah passage commands consecrating every firstborn male animal to God, redeeming it with a lamb or slaughtering it, and redeeming each firstborn son.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p150/r5.anchor: فميز كل ذكر بفتح الرحم للرب وكل ذكر من البهائم التي تكون لك يفتح الرحم يكون خاصة للرب

BIQAI-FULL:v1p150/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p150/r6.speaker: موسى
BIQAI-FULL:v1p150/r6.claim: When a child asks why the rite is performed, the parent is to recount that God brought Israel out of bondage and killed Egypt's firstborn, explaining the sacrifice and redemption of Israel's own firstborn.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p150/r6.anchor: فإذا سألك ابنك غدا وقال لك : ما هذا العمل ؟ فقل : إن الرب أخرجنا من أرض مصر من العبودية والرق

BIQAI-FULL:v1p151/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p151/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p151/r1.claim: The Torah says God avoided the nearby Palestine road lest Israel see battle and flee back to Egypt, leading them through the Sea of Reeds wilderness instead.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p151/r1.anchor: لم يرسلهم الله تعالى في طريق أرض فلسطين , لأنه كان قريبا ولأن الله قال : لعل الشعب إذا ما عاينوا القتال أن يخافوا

BIQAI-FULL:v1p151/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p151/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p151/r2.claim: Israel left armed, while Moses carried Joseph's bones because Joseph had made Israel swear to take them when God remembered and brought them out.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p151/r2.anchor: وخرج بنو إسرائيل من أرض مصر وهم متسلحون , وحمل موسى عليه السلام عظام يوسف عليه السلام معه , لأنه أقسم على بني إسرائيل بأيمان

BIQAI-FULL:v1p151/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p151/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p151/r3.claim: God led them by a cloud pillar in daylight and a fire pillar at night for shade and light, and neither pillar left the people.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p151/r3.anchor: وكان الرب يسير أمامهم بالنهار في عمود السحاب ليسكنهم في الطريق وبالليل في عمود نار ليضيء لهم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p151/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p151/r4.speaker: الرب
BIQAI-FULL:v1p151/r4.claim: God tells Moses to camp by the sea so Pharaoh will think Israel is lost, then says He will harden Pharaoh's heart, gain glory through him and his army, and teach Egypt that He is Lord.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p151/r4.anchor: وكلم الرب موسى وقال له : قل لآل إسرائيل أن يرجعوا فينزلوا على شاطئ الخندق

BIQAI-FULL:v1p151/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p151/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p151/r5.claim: Pharaoh regrets releasing Israel and pursues with six hundred thousand chosen riders and Egyptian forces; Israel sees the pursuers and panics.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p151/r5.anchor: وظعن في ستمائة ألف راكب مختارة وجميع مواكب المصريين أيضا والرجال - وفي نسخة : والقواد - على جميعها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p151/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p151/r6.speaker: بنو إسرائيل
BIQAI-FULL:v1p151/r6.claim: Israel cries to Moses that Egypt had enough graves and that slavery there would have been better than dying in the wilderness.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p151/r6.anchor: ألقلة القبور بمصر أخرجتنا لنموت في البرية ؟ لم فعلت بنا هذا الفعل وأخرجتنا من مصر ؟

BIQAI-FULL:v1p151/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p151/r7.speaker: موسى
BIQAI-FULL:v1p151/r7.claim: Moses tells the people not to fear: they will witness God's deliverance, will not see the Egyptians again, and God will fight for them while they remain calm.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p151/r7.anchor: فقال موسى للشعب : لا خوف عليكم ! انتظروا فأبصروا خلاص الرب إياكم في هذا اليوم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p151/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p151/r8.speaker: الرب
BIQAI-FULL:v1p151/r8.claim: God tells Moses to command Israel to move and to lift and strike the sea so the people can cross dry; He will harden Egypt and gain glory through Pharaoh's forces.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p151/r8.anchor: فقال : مر بني إسرائيل أن يظعنوا وأنت فارفع عصاك واضرب ماء البحر , فيسير آل إسرائيل في البحر في اليبس

BIQAI-FULL:v1p151/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p151/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p151/r9.claim: The divine pillar moves behind Israel between their camp and Egypt's, with darkness for the Egyptians and light for Israel, preventing approach throughout the night.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p151/r9.anchor: فاحتمل السحاب الذي كان أمامهم فوقف خلفهم ودخل بين عسكر المصريين ومحلة بني إسرائيل

BIQAI-FULL:v1p152/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p152/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p152/r1.claim: The Lord drives the sea back with a hot wind all night, leaving dry ground and walls of water on both sides as Israel crosses.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p152/r1.anchor: فزجر الرب البحر بريح سموم - وفي نسخة : قبول عاصف - أليل أجمع , فصير ماء البحر في اليبس , وانقسم الماء

BIQAI-FULL:v1p152/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p152/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p152/r2.claim: Egypt's chariots and horses pursue Israel into the sea; at dawn God terrifies the army and disables its chariots, prompting the Egyptians to recognize that the Lord fights for Israel.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p152/r2.anchor: فلما كان عند حريم الغداة تراءى الرب لعسكر المصريين في عمود نار ومزنة غمامة , فأرجف عسكر المصريين وأفتنه وربط مواكبهم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p152/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p152/r3.speaker: الرب
BIQAI-FULL:v1p152/r3.claim: God commands Moses to stretch his hand over the sea; the waters return and drown Pharaoh's forces, with no survivor.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p152/r3.anchor: فقال الرب لموسى : ابسط يدك على المهرقان فتؤول المياه على المصريين فتطفح على مواكبهم وفرسانهم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p152/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p152/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p152/r4.claim: Israel is saved, sees the dead Egyptians and God's great act against them, then fears God and believes and trusts the words of Moses.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p152/r4.anchor: فخلص آل إسرائيل في ذلك اليوم من أيدي المصريين , فنظر بنو إسرائيل إلى المصريين موتى على شاطئ المهرقان

BIQAI-FULL:v1p152/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p152/r5.speaker: موسى وبنو إسرائيل
BIQAI-FULL:v1p152/r5.claim: Moses and Israel sing praise to God as the glorious, eternal warrior who drowned Pharaoh's army; their song describes divine power, rescue, and kingship forever.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p152/r5.anchor: حينئذ سبح موسى وبنو إسرائيل بهذا التسبيح وقالوا : نسبح الرب ذا الجلال الذي تعالى على المواكب وغرق فرسانها في البحر المنيع

BIQAI-FULL:v1p152/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p152/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p152/r6.claim: The song says surrounding peoples trembled, Israel was led toward the sacred mountain, and God would reign forever; afterward they traveled three days through Shur without water and grumbled at bitter Marah.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p152/r6.anchor: وظعن موسى ببني إسرائيل من بحر سوف , فخرجوا حتى انتهوا إلى برية أسود , ثم ساروا في البرية مسيرة ثلاثة أيام فلم يجدوا هناك ماء

BIQAI-FULL:v1p153/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p153/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p153/r3.claim: They reached the wilderness of Sin between Elim and Sinai on the fifteenth day of the second month after leaving Egypt.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p153/r3.anchor: فأتوا برية سينين التي بين آليم وسينين في خمسة عشر من الشهر الثاني

BIQAI-FULL:v1p153/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p153/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p153/r4.claim: The Israelites grumbled against Moses and Aaron, longing for Egypt's meat and bread and accusing them of bringing the people into the wilderness to die of hunger.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p153/r4.anchor: كنا نحب أن نتوفى في أرض مصر إذ كنا جلوسا بين أيدينا مراجل اللحم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p153/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p153/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p153/r5.claim: God promised bread from heaven and daily gathering as a test of whether Israel would keep his commands.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p153/r5.anchor: ها أنا ذا مهبط لكم الخبز من السماء فليخرج الشعب فليلتقطوا طعام يوم بيوم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p153/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p153/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p153/r6.claim: God commanded a double collection on the sixth day.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p153/r6.anchor: فإذا كان اليوم السادس فليعدوا فضلا على ما يأتون به وليكن ذلك ضعف ما يلتقطون في كل يوم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p153/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p153/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p153/r7.claim: Moses and Aaron told the people that God had brought them from Egypt and that they would see his glory the next morning; their complaint had reached him.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p153/r7.anchor: تعلمون أن الرب أخرجكم من أرض مصر وبالغداة تعاينون مجد الرب

BIQAI-FULL:v1p153/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p153/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p153/r8.claim: Moses said God would give meat in the evening and bread in the morning, and that the people's complaint was against God rather than his messengers.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p153/r8.anchor: وليس إنما تتذمرون علينا بل على الرب

BIQAI-FULL:v1p153/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p153/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p153/r9.claim: Aaron brought the congregation near; God's glory appeared in a cloud, and God said he had heard their grumbling.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p153/r9.anchor: فلما قال هارون ذلك لجميع جماعة بني إسرائيل التفتوا فإذا مجد الرب قد اعتلن في السحاب

BIQAI-FULL:v1p153/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p153/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p153/r10.claim: God promised evening meat and morning bread so Israel would know that he was their Lord.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p153/r10.anchor: عند مغارب الشمس تأكلون اللحم وبالغداة شرقا تشبعون من الخبز فتعلمون أني أنا الرب إلهكم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p153/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p153/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p153/r11.claim: Quail covered the camp at evening, and morning dew surrounded it before manna appeared.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p153/r11.anchor: فلما كان عند الأصيل صعدت السماني فتغشت العسكر , وكان بالغداة ضبابة تقطر المن فأحاطت بالعسكر

BIQAI-FULL:v1p153/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p153/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p153/r12.claim: The manna appeared as flaky material on the ground, resembling frost.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p153/r12.anchor: فإذا على وجه الأرض دقيق يتقشر وكان شبه صفائح الجليد على الأرض

BIQAI-FULL:v1p153/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p153/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p153/r13.claim: Moses identified the manna as God's bread and instructed each person to gather one measure according to need for every member of the household.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p153/r13.anchor: ليلتقط المرء منه على قدر قوته مكيالا لكل نفس على عدد رؤوسكم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p153/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p153/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p153/r14.claim: Although some gathered much and others little, the measured amounts left no surplus for the first or shortage for the latter.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p153/r14.anchor: فلم يفضل الذي أخذ الكثير والذي أخذ القليل لم يعدمه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p154/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p154/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p154/r1.claim: Some disobeyed Moses by keeping manna overnight; it became wormy and foul, angering Moses.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p154/r1.anchor: فلم يطيعوا موسى فأفضل رهط منهم للغد , فدب فيه الدود وأنتن

BIQAI-FULL:v1p154/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p154/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p154/r2.claim: Manna was gathered each morning and melted when the sun grew hot.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p154/r2.anchor: وكان إذا حميت عليه الشمس يميع

BIQAI-FULL:v1p154/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p154/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p154/r3.claim: On the sixth day each person gathered two measures; Moses explained that the next day was a holy Sabbath of rest.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p154/r3.anchor: فلما كان اليوم السادس التقطوا من الخبز ضعفي ما كانوا يتناولون كل رجل مكيالين

BIQAI-FULL:v1p154/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p154/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p154/r4.claim: The people were to bake and cook what they needed and keep the remainder cold for the following day.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p154/r4.anchor: وكل ما أردتم أن تختبزوه فاخبزوه واطبخوا ما أردتم طبخه واحتفظوا بما تفضلون باردا للغد

BIQAI-FULL:v1p154/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p154/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p154/r5.claim: The saved manna did not spoil; Moses said to eat it on the Sabbath, when none could be gathered in the field, and to gather on the other six days.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p154/r5.anchor: فلم ينتن ولم يدب فيه الدود فقال لهم موسى : كلوه يومكم هذا

BIQAI-FULL:v1p154/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p154/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p154/r6.claim: Some went out to gather on the seventh day but found none; God rebuked their refusal to accept his commands, and the people rested.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p154/r6.anchor: حتى متى يأبوا أن يقبلوا وصاياي وسنني

BIQAI-FULL:v1p154/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p154/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p154/r7.claim: Israel called the food manna; it resembled a coriander seed and tasted like honey.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p154/r7.anchor: فسماه بنو إسرائيل المن وهو كحبة الكزبرة وطعمه كشهد العسل

BIQAI-FULL:v1p154/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p154/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p154/r8.claim: The fourth book describes manna as coriander-like and white like the mahā, then ground, pounded, cooked into a dish, and tasting like oil-kneaded bread.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p154/r8.anchor: والمن كان يشبه حبة الكزبرة وكان منظره أبيض كالمها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p154/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p154/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p154/r9.claim: Israel ate manna for forty years, until reaching inhabited territory and Canaan.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p154/r9.anchor: فأكل بنو إسرائيل المن أربعين سنة ولم يزالوا يأكلون المن

BIQAI-FULL:v1p154/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p154/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p154/r10.claim: The measure is glossed as ten jarīb, that is, ten waybas.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p154/r10.anchor: وكان ذلك المكيال عشر جريب أي عشر ويبة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p161/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p161/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p161/r1.claim: Al-Biqāʿī cites the Torah's wilderness account: the tabernacle was Israel's qibla, with cloud and night fire signaling when to camp or travel and shading them from the sun.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p161/r1.anchor: فقد علم من هذا ومما قبله من أن كلا يصلي على باب خيمته أن قبلتهم وهم في التيه قبة الزمان

BIQAI-FULL:v1p162/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p162/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p162/r1.claim: This segment completes the wilderness narrative: silver horns summoned Israel to the meeting tent and called commanders with one blast; the ark went ahead and the cloud shaded travelers from the sun.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p162/r1.anchor: اتخذ قرنين من قضة يكونان عند حضور الجماعة وارتحال العسكر يهتف بهما الكهنة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p162/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p162/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p162/r2.claim: When the people grumbled, fire from God burned the camp's outskirts; Moses prayed and it subsided, so the place was named Burning.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p162/r2.anchor: اشتعلت فيهم نار من قبل الرب , فأحرقت الذي في أطراف العسكر وحوله , وضج الشعب على موسى فصلى موسى أمام الرب وخمدت النار

BIQAI-FULL:v1p162/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p162/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p162/r3.claim: A mixed crowd craved meat and recalled Egypt's fish, cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions, and garlic; they complained that only manna remained to eat.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p162/r3.anchor: اشتهى الخلط الذين كانوا فيهم من الشعوب شهوة وأقبلوا على بني إسرائيل

BIQAI-FULL:v1p162/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p162/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p162/r4.claim: Moses said he could not carry the whole nation alone and asked God to kill him rather than let him see further harm.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p162/r4.anchor: لست أقدر أحتمل هذه الأمة كلها وحدي , لأنها أقوى مني , إن كان فعلك هذا بي فاقتلني قتلا

BIQAI-FULL:v1p162/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p162/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p162/r5.claim: God appointed seventy elders and shared Moses' spirit with them; a wind brought quail, then a severe plague struck the people while they ate, naming the site Graves of Lust.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p162/r5.anchor: وأخذ من الروح الذي عليه وصيره على السبعين , ودخل موسى العسكر هو وأشياخ بني إسرائيل , وهبت ريح من قبل الرب وأصعدت السلوى

BIQAI-FULL:v1p162/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p162/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p162/r6.claim: After the quail plague, the people left Graves of Lust, reached Hazeroth, and remained there seven days.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p162/r6.anchor: وارتحل الشعب من قبور الشهوة فأتوا حصروث ونزلوها , وذكر أنهم مكثوا هنالك سبعة أيام

DURR-FULL:v1p176/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p176/r1.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v1p176/r1.claim: The Israelites wanted to exchange manna and quail for the greens and foods they listed.
DURR-FULL:v1p176/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {وإذ قلتم يا موسى لن نصبر على طعام واحد} قال: المن والسلوى استبدلوا به البقل وما ذكر معه

DURR-FULL:v1p176/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p176/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v1p176/r2.claim: Qatada says they had tired of their wilderness food and recalled the life they had before, prompting their request to Moses.
DURR-FULL:v1p176/r2.anchor: عن قتادة قالوا: ملوا طعامهم في البرية وذكروا عيشهم الذي كانوا فيه قبل ذلك فقالوا {ادع لنا ربك}

DURR-FULL:v1p176/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p176/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p176/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses fum as bread, with another wording identifying it as wheat in the Banu Hashim dialect.
DURR-FULL:v1p176/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {وفومها} قال: الخبز وفي لفظ: البر وفي لفظ: الحنطة بلسان بني هاشم

DURR-FULL:v1p176/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p176/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p176/r4.claim: In another report to Nafi b. al-Azraq, Ibn Abbas says fum means wheat and cites a line by Ahihah b. al-Jallah as Arabic evidence.
DURR-FULL:v1p176/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن نافع بن الأزرق قال له: أخبرني عن قوله تعالى {وفومها} قال: الحنطة

DURR-FULL:v1p176/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p176/r5.speaker: أحيحة بن الجلاح
DURR-FULL:v1p176/r5.claim: Ahihah b. al-Jallah's verse is cited to establish Arabic use of fum for wheat.
DURR-FULL:v1p176/r5.anchor: أما سمعت أحيحة بن الجلاح وهو يقول: قد كنت أغنى الناس شخصا واحدا ورد المدينة عن زراعة فوم

DURR-FULL:v1p176/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p176/r6.speaker: مجاهد وعطاء
DURR-FULL:v1p176/r6.claim: Mujahid and Ata identify fum as bread.
DURR-FULL:v1p176/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد وعطاء في قوله {وفومها} قالا: الخبز

DURR-FULL:v1p176/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p176/r7.speaker: الحسن وأبو مالك
DURR-FULL:v1p176/r7.claim: Hasan and Abu Malik also give bread as a meaning of fum.
DURR-FULL:v1p176/r7.anchor: عن الحسن وأبي مالك في قوله {وفومها} قالا: الخبز

DURR-FULL:v1p176/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p176/r8.speaker: الحسن وأبو مالك
DURR-FULL:v1p176/r8.claim: A separate wording from Hasan and Abu Malik takes fum to mean wheat.
DURR-FULL:v1p176/r8.anchor: عن الحسن وأبي مالك في قوله {وفومها} قالا: الحنظة

DURR-FULL:v1p176/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p176/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p176/r9.claim: Another Ibn Abbas report interprets fum as garlic.
DURR-FULL:v1p176/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: الفوم الثوم

DURR-FULL:v1p176/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p176/r10.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
DURR-FULL:v1p176/r10.claim: Al-Rabi b. Anas says fum is garlic and notes a reading with thum instead.
DURR-FULL:v1p176/r10.anchor: عن الربيع بن أنس قال: الفوم الثوم - وفي بعض القراءة وثومها

DURR-FULL:v1p176/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p176/r11.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v1p176/r11.claim: Ibn Masud recited the word as thum rather than fum.
DURR-FULL:v1p176/r11.anchor: عن ابن مسعود: أنه قرأ وثومها

DURR-FULL:v1p176/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p176/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p176/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas says he follows Zayd's recitation but adopts about fourteen letters from Ibn Masud's reading, including this phrase.
DURR-FULL:v1p176/r12.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قرائتي قراءة زيد وأنا آخذ ببضعة عشر حرفا من قراءة ابن مسعود هذا أحدها

DURR-FULL:v1p176/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p176/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p176/r13.claim: In another exchange, Ibn Abbas says fum means wheat; he tells Nafi that the Ibn Masud reading means the foul thing and cites poems by Abu Mihjan and Umayya b. Abi al-Salt as evidence.
DURR-FULL:v1p176/r13.anchor: عن ابن عباس إن نافع بن الأزرق قال له: أخبرني عن قوله عز وجل {وفومها} قال: الفوم الحنطة

DURR-FULL:v1p176/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p176/r14.speaker: أبو محجن الثقفي
DURR-FULL:v1p176/r14.claim: Abu Mihjan al-Thaqafi's line is cited as evidence for Arabic use of fum for wheat.
DURR-FULL:v1p176/r14.anchor: أما سمعت أبا محجن الثقفي وهو يقول: قد كنت أحسبني كأغنى واحد قدم المدينة عن زراعة فوم

DURR-FULL:v1p176/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p176/r15.speaker: أمية بن أبي الصلت
DURR-FULL:v1p176/r15.claim: Umayya b. Abi al-Salt uses fum in poetry while describing their former homes, gardens, and onions.
DURR-FULL:v1p176/r15.anchor: قال أمية ابن أبي الصلت: كانت منازلهم إذ ذاك ظاهرة فيها الفراديس والفومات والبصل

DURR-FULL:v1p176/r16.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p176/r16.speaker: أمية بن أبي الصلت
DURR-FULL:v1p176/r16.claim: A second line by Umayya b. Abi al-Salt uses fum for healthy wheat against the image of rain and hail on the ground.
DURR-FULL:v1p176/r16.anchor: وقال أمية ابن الصلت أيضا: أنفي الدياس من الفوم الصحيح كما أنفي من الأرض صوب الوابل البرد

DURR-FULL:v1p176/r17.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p176/r17.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v1p176/r17.claim: Mujahid glosses adna as worse or inferior.
DURR-FULL:v1p176/r17.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {أتستبدلون الذي هو أدنى} قال: أردأ

DURR-FULL:v1p178/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p178/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p178/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the command means to descend to one of the cities.
DURR-FULL:v1p178/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {اهبطوا مصرا} قال: مصرا من الأمصار

DURR-FULL:v1p178/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p178/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v1p178/r2.claim: Qatada likewise takes misran to mean a city among cities.
DURR-FULL:v1p178/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {اهبطوا مصرا} يقول: مصرا من الأمصار

DURR-FULL:v1p178/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p178/r3.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR-FULL:v1p178/r3.claim: Abu al-Aliya interprets the place as Pharaoh's Egypt.
DURR-FULL:v1p178/r3.anchor: عن أبي العالية في قوله {اهبطوا مصرا} قال: يعني به مصر فرعون

DURR-FULL:v1p178/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p178/r4.speaker: الأعمش
DURR-FULL:v1p178/r4.claim: Al-Aʿmash read misra without nunation and identified it as Egypt governed by Salih b. Ali.
DURR-FULL:v1p178/r4.anchor: عن الأعمش أنه كان يقرأ {اهبطوا مصرا} بلا تنوين ويقول: هي مصر التي عليها صالح بن علي

DURR-FULL:v1p178/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p178/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p178/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies those struck with humiliation and poverty as the people who pay jizya.
DURR-FULL:v1p178/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {وضربت عليهم الذلة والمسكنة} قال: هم أصحاب الجزية

DURR-FULL:v1p178/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p178/r6.speaker: قتادة والحسن
DURR-FULL:v1p178/r6.claim: Qatada and Hasan say they pay the jizya by hand while subdued.
DURR-FULL:v1p178/r6.anchor: عن قتادة والحسن {وضربت عليهم الذلة والمسكنة} قال: يعطون الجزية عن يد وهم صاغرون

DURR-FULL:v1p178/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p178/r7.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR-FULL:v1p178/r7.claim: Abu al-Aliya glosses miskena as poverty.
DURR-FULL:v1p178/r7.anchor: عن أبي العالية في قوله {والمسكنة} قال: الفاقة

DURR-FULL:v1p178/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p178/r8.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v1p178/r8.claim: Al-Dahhak says they incurred and deserved God's anger.
DURR-FULL:v1p178/r8.anchor: عن الضحاك في قوله {وباؤوا بغضب من الله} قال: استحقوا الغضب من الله

DURR-FULL:v1p178/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p178/r9.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v1p178/r9.claim: Qatada glosses ba'u as turning back or returning.
DURR-FULL:v1p178/r9.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {وباؤوا} قال: انقلبوا

DURR-FULL:v1p178/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p178/r10.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v1p178/r10.claim: Ibn Masud says Israelites killed three hundred prophets in a day and sold vegetables in the market by evening.
DURR-FULL:v1p178/r10.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال: كانت بنو إسرائيل في اليوم تقتل ثلاثمائة نبي ثم يقيمون سوق بقلهم في آخر النهار

DURR-FULL:v1p178/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p178/r11.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v1p178/r11.claim: The Prophet says the most severely punished at Resurrection include a killer of a prophet or someone killed by a prophet, a leader of misguidance, and an image maker.
DURR-FULL:v1p178/r11.anchor: عن ابن مسعود أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال أشد الناس عذابا يوم القيامة رجل قتل نبيا أو قتله نبي وإمام ضلالة

DURR-FULL:v1p178/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p178/r12.speaker: أبو ذر
DURR-FULL:v1p178/r12.claim: Abu Dharr reports that when a Bedouin called the Prophet nabīʾ Allah, he corrected the form and said he was nabī Allah.
DURR-FULL:v1p178/r12.anchor: عن أبي ذر قال جاء اعرابي إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: يا نبيء الله قال: لست بنبيء الله ولكنني نبي الله

DURR-FULL:v1p178/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p178/r13.speaker: الحاكم
DURR-FULL:v1p178/r13.claim: Al-Hakim authenticated the report about the Prophet's distinction between nabīʾ and nabī.
DURR-FULL:v1p178/r13.anchor: وأخرج الحاكم وصححه وتعقبه الذهبي عن أبي ذر قال جاء اعرابي إلى رسول الله

DURR-FULL:v1p178/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p178/r14.speaker: الذهبي
DURR-FULL:v1p178/r14.claim: Al-Dhahabi rejects the Abu Dharr report as munkar and unsound.

DURR-FULL:v1p178/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p178/r15.speaker: حمران بن أعين
DURR-FULL:v1p178/r15.claim: Hamran b. Aʿyan separately reports a Bedouin's address as nabīʾ Allah and the Prophet's correction to nabī Allah.
DURR-FULL:v1p178/r15.anchor: عن حمران بن أعين أن رجلا من أهل البادية أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: السلام عليك يا نبيء الله

DURR-FULL:v1p178/r16.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p178/r16.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v1p178/r16.claim: Ibn Umar says the Prophet, Abu Bakr, Umar, and the caliphs did not use the hamza in nabī; he calls hamza a later innovation.
DURR-FULL:v1p178/r16.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال ما همز رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ولا أبو بكر ولا عمر ولا الخلفاء وإنما الهمز بدعة من بعدهم

AKHFASH:v1p105/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p105/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p105/r1.claim: The first من is partitive: the earth produces some unspecified amount of its plants, with the word “something” left unexpressed.
AKHFASH:v1p105/r1.anchor: أما قوله {يخرج لنا مما تنبت الأرض من بقلها وقثآئها} فدخلت فيه (من) كنحو ما تقول في الكلام: "أهل البصرة يأكلون من البر والشعير"

AKHFASH:v1p105/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p105/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p105/r2.claim: Alternatively, من can be treated as extra, as in “I saw no one” or “did a man come to you?”
AKHFASH:v1p105/r2.anchor: وان شئت [44ب] جعلته على قولك: "ما رأيت من أحد" تريد: "ما رأيت أحدا" و"هل جاءك من رجل"

AKHFASH:v1p105/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p105/r3.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p105/r3.claim: The added من is not confined to negation and questions: it appears in the cited verse and in ordinary expressions such as “Zayd is among the best.”
AKHFASH:v1p105/r3.anchor: فقد جاء في غير ذلك، قال {ويكفر عنكم من سيئاتكم} فهذا ليس باستفهام ولا نفي.

AKHFASH:v1p105/r4.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p105/r4.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p105/r4.claim: Common idioms omit an understood noun: “Do you want …?” means “Do you have a need for …?”, and “no harm on you” is similarly elliptical.
AKHFASH:v1p105/r4.anchor: ونظيره قولهم: "هل لك في كذا وكذا" ولا يقولون: "حاجة، و: لا عليك" يريدون: لا بأس عليك*.

AKHFASH:v1p105/r5.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p105/r5.speaker: بعض الناس
AKHFASH:v1p105/r5.claim: Some claimed that مصر in both this verse and the Joseph passage means the specific country of Egypt.
AKHFASH:v1p105/r5.anchor: فزعم بعض الناس انه يعني فيهما جميعا "مصر" بعينها،

AKHFASH:v1p105/r6.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p105/r6.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p105/r6.claim: Feminine names such as هند and جمل may be declined or left without declension, depending on Arab usage.
AKHFASH:v1p105/r6.anchor: ما كان من اسم مؤنث على هذا النحو

AKHFASH:v1p105/r7.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p105/r7.speaker: بعضهم
AKHFASH:v1p105/r7.claim: Some distinguish the two occurrences: مصر in Joseph is the named Egypt, while مصر here means any city among cities.
AKHFASH:v1p105/r7.anchor: وقال بعضهم: "أما التي في "يوسف" فيعني بها "مصر" بعينها، والتي في "البقرة" يعني بها مصرا من الأمصار.

AKHFASH:v1p105/r8.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p105/r8.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p105/r8.claim: باءوا بغضب means they returned bearing it or that it came upon them; the verb is also used in باء بذنبه.
AKHFASH:v1p105/r8.anchor: وأما قوله {وبآءو بغضب من الله} يقول: "رجعوا به" اي صار عليهم، وتقول "باء بذنبه يبوء بوءا".

AKHFASH:v1p105/r9.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p105/r9.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p105/r9.claim: Both النبيين and الأنبياء are forms used by Arab speakers for the plural of prophet.
AKHFASH:v1p105/r9.anchor: أما قوله {ويقتلون النبيين بغير الحق} [و] {ويقتلون الأنبيآء} كل ذلك [45ء] جماعة العرب تقوله.

AKHFASH:v1p108/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p108/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p108/r1.claim: In بما عصوا, ما عصوا functions as a noun meaning “their disobedience.”
AKHFASH:v1p108/r1.anchor: واما قوله {بما عصوا} [ف] جعله اسما هنا كالعصيان يريد: بعصيانهم، فجعل "ما" و"عصوا" اسما.

IBNABIHATIM:v1p122#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p122#2/r1.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNABIHATIM:v1p122#2/r1.claim: The Israelites had quails for food and manna for drink, and said they could not endure that single fare.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p122#2/r1.anchor: عن أبي العالية قوله : لن نصبر على طعام واحد قال كان طعامهم السلوى وشرابهم المن ، فسالوا ما ذكروا .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p122#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p122#2/r2.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v1p122#2/r2.claim: Al-Suddi says they became sated or weary of that food and said they could not endure one fare.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p122#2/r2.anchor: عن السدى قال : فاجمعوا ذلك وقالوا : ياموسى لن نصبر على طعام واحد .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p122#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p122#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNABIHATIM:v1p122#2/r3.claim: The transmitters explain their phrase as being sated or disliking the food.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p122#2/r3.anchor: قال عمرو بن حماد : اجمعوا يعني : بشموا قال أبو زرعة : فاجمعوا : اي كرهوه .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p122#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p122#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v1p122#2/r4.claim: Qatada says they tired of their food and recalled the life they had before.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p122#2/r4.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله : لن نصبر لك على طعام واحد قال : ملوا طعامهم ، وذكروا عيشهم الذي كانوا فيه قبل ذلك .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p122#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p122#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v1p122#2/r5.claim: When they reached Syria and missed their former foods, they asked Moses to seek vegetables from the earth for them.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p122#2/r5.anchor: قال قتادة انهم لما قدموا الشام فقدوا اطعمتهم التي كانوا ياكلونها فقالوا : فادع لنا ربك يخرج لنا مما تنبت الأرض من بقلها

IBNABIHATIM:v1p122#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p122#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p122#2/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses fūm as bread, and on another occasion as wheat.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p122#2/r6.anchor: عن عكرمة عن ابن عباس : وفومهاالخبز . قال مرة : البر .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p122#2/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p122#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p122#2/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas explains fūm as wheat and cites Uhayha ibn al-Halah's verse as lexical evidence for the word.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p122#2/r7.anchor: قد كنت اغنى الناس شخصا واحداورد المدينة عن زراعة فوم

IBNABIHATIM:v1p122#2/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p122#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNABIHATIM:v1p122#2/r8.claim: The author says Mujahid, al-Hasan, Abu Malik, Ikrima, Ata, al-Suddi, and Qatada likewise interpret fūm as wheat, while others differ.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p122#2/r8.anchor: وروى مجاهد ، والحسن ، وابي مالك ، وعكرمة ، وعطاء بن أبي رباح ، والسدى ، وقتادة نحو ذلك . وخالفهم اخرون .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p122#2/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p122#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p122#2/r9.claim: A report through al-Hasan attributes to Ibn Abbas the alternative reading of fūm as garlic.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p122#2/r9.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله : وفومها قال : قال ابن عباس : الثوم .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p122#2/r10.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p122#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNABIHATIM:v1p122#2/r10.claim: The author says Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Rabi', and al-Dahhak also gave the garlic interpretation.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p122#2/r10.anchor: وروى عن سعيد بن جبير والربيع والضحاك نحو ذلك .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p122#2/r11.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p122#2/r11.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v1p122#2/r11.claim: Al-Hasan says they were ungrateful, recalled their former life, and requested the vegetables and foods they used to eat.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p122#2/r11.anchor: عن الحسن قال : فبطروا ذلك ولم يصبروا عليه وذكروا عيشهم الذي كانوا يعيشون فيه ، وكانوا قوما اهل اعداس وبصل وبقول وفوم

IBNABIHATIM:v1p124/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p124/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v1p124/r1.claim: Qatada interprets “lower” as worse; al-Hasan gave the same interpretation.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p124/r1.anchor: عن قتادة : اتستبدلون الذي هو ادنى - الذي هو شر - بالذي هو خير . وروى عن الحسن نحو ذلك .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p124/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p124/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p124/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says “a town” means any one of the cities; al-Suddi, Qatada, and al-Rabi' agree.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p124/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : اهبطوا مصرا قال : مصرا من الامصار وروى عن السدى وقتادة والربيع بن انس نحو ذلك .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p124/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p124/r3.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNABIHATIM:v1p124/r3.claim: Al-Aliyah interprets the destination as Pharaoh's Egypt.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p124/r3.anchor: عن أبي العالية قال : يعني به مصر فرعون .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p124/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p124/r4.speaker: الأعمش
IBNABIHATIM:v1p124/r4.claim: Al-A'mash identifies it as Egypt, then governed by Salih ibn Ali.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p124/r4.anchor: عن الاعمش قال : هي مصر التي عليها صالح بن علي ، وكان يومئذ عليها .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p124/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p124/r5.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v1p124/r5.claim: Al-Suddi says that after leaving the wilderness, the manna and quails were withdrawn and the Israelites ate vegetables.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p124/r5.anchor: عن السدى : اهبطوا مصرا فان لكم ما سالتم فلما خرجوا من التيه رفع المن والسلوى واكلوا البقول .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p124/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p124/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p124/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies those under abasement and poverty as people subject to levies; the author clarifies that these are jizya payers.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p124/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : وضربت عليهم الذلة والمسكنة قال هم اصحاب القبالات ، كفروا بالله العظيم - قال أبو محمد : يعني باصحاب القبالات اصحاب الجزية .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p124/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p124/r7.speaker: الحسن، قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v1p124/r7.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada explain abasement as paying the jizya while subdued.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p124/r7.anchor: عن الحسن وقتادة في قوله : وضربت عليهم الذلة قالا : يعطون الجزية عن يد وهم صاغرون .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p124/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p124/r8.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v1p124/r8.anchor: عن الضحاك قوله : وضربت عليهم الذلة قال : الذل .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p124/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p124/r9.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v1p124/r9.claim: Al-Hasan says this ummah overtook them, and even the Magians collected jizya from them.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p124/r9.anchor: عن الحسن : وضربت عليهم الذلة قال : ادركتهم هذه الامة ، وان المجوس لتجبيهم الجزية .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p124/r10.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p124/r10.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v1p124/r10.claim: Al-Hasan says God humiliated them, left them without protection, and placed them under the Muslims' feet.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p124/r10.anchor: سالت الحسن عن قوله : وضربت عليهم الذلة قال : اذلهم الله فلا منعة لهم ، وجعلهم الله تحت اقدام المسلمين .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p125/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p125/r1.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNABIHATIM:v1p125/r1.claim: Al-Aliyah explains poverty as indigence; al-Suddi and al-Rabi' gave the same explanation.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p125/r1.anchor: عن أبي العالية في قوله : وضربت عليهم الذلة والمسكنة قال : المسكنة الفاقة . وروى عن السدى والربيع نحو ذلك .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p125/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p125/r2.speaker: عطية
IBNABIHATIM:v1p125/r2.claim: Atiyya interprets poverty as a tax or land levy.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p125/r2.anchor: عن عطية : وضربت عليهم الذلة والمسكنة قال : الخراج .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p125/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p125/r3.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v1p125/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak explains poverty as the jizya.

IBNABIHATIM:v1p125/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p125/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v1p125/r4.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr explains incurring God's anger as deserving His displeasure.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p125/r4.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قول الله : وباءوا بغضب من الله يقول استوجبوا سخطا .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p125/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p125/r5.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p125/r5.claim: Al-Rabi' says God's anger came upon them; al-Dahhak gave a similar account.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p125/r5.anchor: عن الربيع بن انس وباءوا بغضب من اللهفحدث عليهم من الله غضب . وروي عن الضحاك نحو ذلك .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p125/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p125/r6.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNABIHATIM:v1p125/r6.claim: Ibn Mas'ud reports that the Israelites killed three hundred prophets in a day and continued killing them through the evening.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p125/r6.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال : كانت بنو اسرائيل في اليوم تقتل ثلاثمائة نبي ثم تقوم بقلهم من اخر النهار .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p125/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p125/r7.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v1p125/r7.claim: Qatada warns them to avoid disobedience and aggression, the causes of earlier peoples' destruction.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p125/r7.anchor: عن قتادة ذلك بما عصوا وكانوا يعتدون اجتنبوا المعصية والعدوان فان بهما هلك من هلك قبلك من الناس .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p519/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p519/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p519/r5.claim: The command ‘go down to a town’ is a comparable case where the intended relation is clear without inventing an implicit condition.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p519/r5.anchor: ومنه قوله تعالى الآتي : { اهبطوا مصرا }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p520/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p520/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p520/r1.claim: This sentence continues the preceding pattern of recounting God's favors, whether pure favors or favors mixed with ingratitude and subsequent pardon, so its content should also be a favor.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p520/r1.anchor: فالظاهر أن يكون مضمون هذه الجملة نعمة أيضا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p520/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p520/r2.speaker: الفخر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p520/r2.claim: Al-Fakhr's reading treats ‘go down to Egypt, and you will have what you asked’ as God's answer and therefore a favor, even though it is conditional on entering a town.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p520/r2.anchor: فيؤخذ من كلام الفخر أن قوله تعالى : { اهبطوا مصرا فإن لكم ما سألتم } هو كالإجابة لما طلبوه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p520/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p520/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p520/r3.claim: The author finds al-Fakhr's proposed favor very remote because the text never establishes that they actually received the food they requested.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p520/r3.anchor: ولا يخفى أنه بعيدجدا لأن إعطاءهم ما سألوه لم يثبت وقوعه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p520/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p520/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p520/r4.claim: A reading transmitted through al-Fakhr and explained by ʿAbd al-Ḥakīm says asking to replace manna and quail was sinful ingratitude: ‘patience’ implies dislike, and the rebuke confirms it; the favor was pardon and the concession to go down.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p520/r4.anchor: ويؤخذ من كلام المفسرين الذي صدر الفخر بنقله ووجهه عبد الحكيم أن سؤالهم تعويض المن والسلوى بالبقل ونحوه معصية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p520/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p520/r5.speaker: الفخر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p520/r5.claim: Al-Fakhr holds that requesting another blessing for a known purpose is not itself disobedience.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p520/r5.anchor: لأن طلب الانتقال من نعمة لغيرها لغرض معروف لا يعد معصية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p520/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p520/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p520/r6.claim: The author rejects the sin-and-pardon interpretation as weak: ‘go down’ grants no favor, and the request gives no evidence of sin, since asking to move from one favor to another for a familiar purpose is not disobedience.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p520/r6.anchor: ولا يخفى أن هذا بعيد إذ ليس في قوله { اهبطوا } إنعام عليهم ولا في سؤالهم ما يدل على أنهم عصوا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p521/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p521/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p521/r1.claim: The episode shifts from favors to Israel's poor choice of appetite, which may still be lawful, but their words show discourtesy toward Moses and the benefactor: ‘we cannot endure’ casts the given food as hateful.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p521/r1.anchor: مع ما في صيغة طلبهم من الجفاء وقلة الأدب مع الرسول ومع المنعم إذ قالوا : { لن نصبر }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p521/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p521/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p521/r2.claim: The author reads lan as extending negation throughout every time of ‘endure’: they announce they will no longer eat manna and quail, pressuring Moses to ask at once and implying they have made acceptance impossible.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p521/r2.anchor: فإن ( لن ) تدل على استغراق النفي لأزمنة فعل { نصبر } من أولها إلى آخرها وهو معنى التأبيد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p521/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p521/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p521/r3.claim: God's answer withdraws special care: instead of providing food, water, and shade as before, He orders them to go to a town and procure their own, a disciplinary rebuke for their attitude rather than punishment for a sinful request.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p521/r3.anchor: فكان جواب الله لهم في هذه الطلبة أن قطع عنايته بهم وأهملهم ووكلهم إلى نفوسهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p521/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p521/r4.speaker: ابن عطاء الله
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p521/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAṭāʾ Allāh warns that a seeker may misread delayed punishment as approval; God may quietly withdraw spiritual provision or leave the seeker to personal desires, placing the person at a distance without awareness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p521/r4.anchor: من جهل المريد أن يسيء الأدب فتؤخر العقوبة عنه فيقول لو كان في هذا إساءة لعوقبت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p521/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p521/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p521/r5.claim: Worldly deprivation and loss of spiritual gifts are not consequences of a legal sin under divine command; they resemble causal ordering in the world's system. Only afterlife punishment proves the act was sinful, resolving the interpretive difficulty.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p521/r5.anchor: ولكنها من أشباه خطاب الوضع ترجع إلى ترتب المسببات على أسبابها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p521/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p521/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p521/r6.claim: The verse alludes to the Torah's account: after leaving Sinai/Horeb for Paran in year two and traveling toward Hebron, Israelites remembered free fish and produce in Egypt, complained about manna, and wept; God was angered, Moses sought pardon, and God sent quail, which they stored for a month.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p521/r6.anchor: وقد أشارت الآية إلى قصة ذكرتها التوراة مجملة منتثرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522/r1.claim: The emphatic negator لن conveys the Israelites’ extreme vexation by making their refusal seem to extend through all time.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522/r1.anchor: والتعبير بلن المفيدة لتأبيد النفي في اللغة العربية لأداء معنى كلامهم المحكي هنا في شدة الضجر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522/r2.claim: They call manna and quail one food because it recurred every day, although it consisted of two things.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522/r2.anchor: ووصفوا الطعام بواحد وإن كان هو شيئين المن والسلوى لأن المراد أنه متكرر كل يوم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522/r3.claim: The jussive يخرج replaces an expected أن يخرج, presenting the result as certain if Moses asks and pressing him to act for their benefit.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522/r3.anchor: فعدل عن ذلك إلى الإتيان بفعل مجزوم في صورة جواب طلبهم إيماء إلى أنهم واثقون بأنه إن دعا ربه أجابه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522/r4.claim: إخراج means bringing forth from the earth; من is partitive, explanatory, or partitive twice, and من بقلها may be circumstantial or an apposition to ما تنبت.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522/r4.anchor: والإخراج : الإبراز من الأرض ، و ( من ) الأولى تبعيضية والثانية بيانية أو الثانية أيضا تبعيضية لأنهم لا يطلبون جميع البقل بل بعضه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522/r5.speaker: الحسن
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522/r5.claim: Al-Hasan says the Israelites were agricultural people who yearned for their former habits.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522/r5.anchor: وعن الحسن : كانوا قوما فلاحة فنزعوا إلى عكرهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522/r6.claim: Fūm most likely means garlic: exchanging ث for ف is common in Arabic, and garlic fits the accompanying produce and the Torah’s list.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522/r6.anchor: وقد اختلف في الفوم فقيل : هو الثوم بالمثلثة وإبدال الثاء فاء شائع في كلام العرب كما قالوا : جدث وجدف وثلغ وفلغ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522/r7.speaker: الزجاج
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522/r7.claim: Al-Zajjāj cites a poem by Uḥayḥa b. al-Jallāḥ as evidence that fūm means wheat.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522/r7.anchor: وقيل الفوم الحنطة وأنشد الزجاج لأحيحة بن الجلاح

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522#2/r1.claim: The cited poem mentions fields of fūm, which the adjacent parenthetical gloss identifies as wheat.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522#2/r2.speaker: قيل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522#2/r2.claim: Another reported interpretation takes fūm to mean chickpeas in the dialect of the people of Syria.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522#2/r2.anchor: وقيل الفوم الحمص بلغة أهل الشام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522#2/r3.speaker: موسى
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522#2/r3.claim: One attribution makes the rebuke beginning أتستبدلون Moses’s speech.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522#2/r3.anchor: هو من كلام موسى وقيل من كلام الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
