IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522#2/r4.speaker: الله
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522#2/r4.claim: Another attribution makes the rebuke beginning أتستبدلون God's speech.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522#2/r4.anchor: وقيل من كلام الله وهو توبيخ شديد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522#2/r5.claim: The question is a severe rebuke, stripped of persuasion and warning, and expresses astonishment at their foolish choice.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522#2/r5.anchor: واقتصر على الاستفهام المقصود منه التعجب فالتوبيخ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522#2/r6.claim: The s and t in استبدل intensify the action rather than request it, as in استغنى, استجاب, and استكبر.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522#2/r6.anchor: السين والتاء فيه لتأكيد الحدث وليس للطلب فهو كقوله : { واستغنى الله } ( التغابن : 6 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522#2/r7.claim: استبدل derives from بدل; Arabic uses several augmented derivatives, while a simple unaugmented verb is unattested.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522#2/r7.anchor: وفعل استبدل مشتق من البدل بالتحريك مثل شبه ، ويقال بكسر الباء وسكون الدال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522#2/r8.claim: The بدل family means putting one thing or quality in place of another, or compensating one thing with another.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522#2/r8.anchor: وجميع أفعال مادة البدل تدل على جعل شيء مكان شيء آخر من الذوات أو الصفات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522#2/r9.claim: In the common construction with باء, the direct object is what is taken and the باء phrase what is given; here the lesser food is taken for the better food.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522#2/r9.anchor: فالمنصوب هو المأخوذ والمجرور هو المبذول نحو قوله هنا : { أتستبدلون الذي هو أدنى بالذي هو خير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522#2/r10.claim: The second complement can also take من with the sense of the exchange باء, as in the construction cited with the verse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p522#2/r10.anchor: وقد يجر المعمول الثاني بمن التي هي بمعنى باء البدلية كقول أبي الشيص

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p524/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p524/r1.speaker: أبو الشيص
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p524/r1.claim: Abū al-Shayṣ’s verse illustrates بدل taking من for the thing exchanged away.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p524/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p524/r2.speaker: الكشاف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p524/r2.claim: Al-Kashshāf treats بدل as having a باء construction in which the given and taken items are reversed from تبدل and استبدل; Qutb and al-Taftāzānī develop variants of this analysis.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p524/r2.anchor: ووقع في ( الكشاف ) عند قوله تعالى : { ولا تتبدلوا الخبيث بالطيب } ما يقتضي أن فعل بدل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p524/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p524/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p524/r3.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr sees no difference among بدل, تبدل, and استبدل in this construction; he finds al-Kashshāf’s account unsupported by lexicographers or its own al-Asās.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p524/r3.anchor: والأظهر عندي أن لا فرق بين بدل وتبدل واستبدل وأن كلام ( الكشاف ) مشكل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p524/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p524/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p524/r4.claim: اهبطوا is permission colored by rebuke: if this is what they want, they may descend to any Egyptian town, though no nearby town was then reachable.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p524/r4.anchor: فالأمر في قوله : { اهبطوا } للإباحة المشوبة بالتوبيخ أي إن كان هذا همكم فاهبطوا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p524/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p524/r5.speaker: قيل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p524/r5.claim: An alternative reads مصر as Egypt, the country they left; the impossible command to return is pure reproach and a threat recalling their old hardship.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p524/r5.anchor: وقيل : أراد اهبطوا مصر أي بلد مصر بلد القبط أي ارجعوا إلى مصر التي خرجتم منها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p524/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p524/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p524/r6.claim: If مصر means the country, it may be diptote as a feminine place-name or triptote as a place-name or a feminine three-letter name with a still middle consonant.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p524/r6.anchor: واعلم أن مصر على هذا المعنى يجوز منعه من الصرف على تأويله بالبقعة فيكون فيه العلمية والتأنيث

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p524/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p524/r7.speaker: ابن عطية
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p524/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya notes مصر without nunation in Ibn Masʿūd’s reading and without alif in Ubayy’s codex and some ʿUthmānic codices.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p524/r7.anchor: في قراءة ابن مسعود بدون تنوين وأنه في مصحف أبي بن كعب بدون ألف وأنه ثبت بدون ألف في بعض مصاحف عثمان قاله ابن عطية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p524/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p524/r8.speaker: مالك
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p524/r8.claim: Ashhab reports Mālik’s view that مصر here means their own town, the dwelling place of Pharaoh.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p524/r8.anchor: وذكر أن أشهب قال قال لي مالك : هي عندي مصر قريتك مسكن فرعون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p524/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p524/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p524/r9.claim: The wording اهبطوا rather than لنَهْبِط signals that Moses does not include himself; the threat recalls their desire for their former humiliating life.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p524/r9.anchor: وربما كان قوله : { اهبطوا } دون لنهبط مؤذنا بذلك لأنه لا يريد إدخال نفسه في هذا الأمر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p525/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p525/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p525/r1.claim: The فاء in فإن لكم ما سألتم marks sequence: they obtain what they requested upon descending, rather than giving a reason for the command.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p525/r1.anchor: الظاهر أن الفاء للتعقيب عطفت جملة { إن لكم ما سألتم } على جملة { اهبطوا } للدلالة على حصول سؤلهم بمجرد هبوطهم مصر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p525/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p525/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p525/r2.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr invokes ʿAbd al-Qāhir’s point that إن can itself link and motivate a clause; adding فاء therefore signals simple coordination and sequence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p525/r2.anchor: واعلم أن من شأن إن إذا جاءت على هذا الوجه أي الذي في قول بشار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p525/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p525/r3.speaker: أبو الطيب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p525/r3.claim: Abū al-Ṭayyib’s couplet offers a parallel reproach: if this year pleases you, return to Homs next year.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p525/r3.anchor: فإن كان أعجبكم عامكم فعودوا إلى حمص في القابل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p526/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p526/r1.speaker: أبو حيان
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p526/r1.claim: Abū Ḥayyān reads فإن لكم ما سألتم as the answer to the command, allowing a nominal sentence to answer an imperative.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p526/r1.anchor: وجعل أبو حيان في ( البحر المحيط ) جملة { فإن لكم ما سألتم } جوابا للأمر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p526/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p526/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p526/r2.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr rejects both a causal explanation and a command-answer reading: Moses is angry, not encouraging or persuading them to descend.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p526/r2.anchor: لا يخفى أن كلا المعنيين ضعيف ههنا لعدم قصد الترغيب في هذا الهبوط حتى يعلل أو يعلق ، وإنما هو كلام غضب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p526/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p526/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p526/r3.claim: The emphatic إن treats them as doubters because their request is long delayed and their longing makes them suspect they may not obtain it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p526/r3.anchor: واقتران الجملة بإن المؤكدة لتنزيلهم منزلة من يشك لبعد عهدهم بما سألوه حتى يشكون هل يجدونه من شدة شوقهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p526/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p526/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p526/r4.claim: The humiliation clause is a result of the earlier blessings of liberation and a land to inhabit, which they failed to value when they yearned for Egypt and shrank from entering the town.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p526/r4.anchor: فلأن هاته الجملة لها مزيد الارتباط بالجمل قبلها إذ كانت في معنى النتيجة والأثر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p526/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p526/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p526/r5.claim: The واء rather than فاء makes the punishment an independently asserted report of what their ingratitude merited, not merely a consequence attached to Moses’s rebuke.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p526/r5.anchor: وأما كونه بالواو دون الفاء فليكون خبرا مقصودا بذاته وليس متفرعا على قول موسى لهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p526/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p526/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p526/r6.claim: Gratitude means displaying a blessing’s intended effects; failing to do so merits its removal and replacement with its opposite.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p526/r6.anchor: فإن شكر النعمة هو إظهار آثارها المقصودة منها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p527/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p527/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p527/r1.claim: The pronoun in وضربت عليهم ... وباءوا refers to all Israelites, including later generations; the addressed Israelites are included by implication through inherited ancestral traits.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p527/r1.anchor: فالضمير في قوله : { وضربت عليهم . . . وباءوا } إلخ عائدة إلى جميع بني إسرائيل لا إلى خصوص الذين أبوا دخول القرية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p527/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p527/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p527/r2.claim: The third-person pronoun follows the apparent sense because these later Israelites are not the addressees; this is not التفات.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p527/r2.anchor: فالإتيان بضمير الغيبة هنا جار على مقتضى الظاهر لأنهم غير المخاطبين فليس هو من الالتفات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p527/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p527/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p527/r3.claim: ضرب originally means forceful contact between surfaces; related idioms extend it to strong attachment, such as fixing a tent or house to the ground.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p527/r3.anchor: والضرب في كلام العرب يرجع إلى معنى التقاء ظاهر جسم بظاهر جسم آخر بشدة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p527/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p527/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p527/r4.claim: Verses by ʿAbda b. al-Ṭabīb and Ziyād al-Aʿjam attest ضرب بيتا and قبة ضربت for firmly setting up a dwelling.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p527/r4.anchor: قال عبدة بن الطبيب : إن التي ضربت بيتا مهاجرة وقال زياد الأعجم : في قبة ضربت على ابن الحشرج

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p527/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p527/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p527/r5.claim: The phrase may be a concealed metaphor: humiliation and poverty are pictured as a tent or house fixed around them, with ضرب as an imaginative metaphor.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p527/r5.anchor: فقوله : { وضربت عليهم الذلة والمسكنة } استعارة مكنية إذ شبهت الذلة والمسكنة في الإحاطة بهم واللزوم بالبيت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p527/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p527/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p527/r6.claim: Another analysis makes ضربت a dependent metaphor for humiliation adhering like clay to a wall, without a concealed metaphor.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p527/r6.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون ضربت استعارة تبعية وليس ثمة مكنية بأن شبه لزوم الذلة لهم ولصوقها بلصوق الطين بالحائط

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p527/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p527/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p527/r7.claim: Al-Ṭībī takes the dependent-metaphor path, while al-Taftāzānī also treats the striking as a dependent metaphor and allows tent or clay as the comparison.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p527/r7.anchor: وهي طريقة في الآية سلكها الطيبي في { شرح الكشاف } وخالفه التفتزاني وجعل الضرب استعارة تبعية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p528/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p528/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p528/r1.claim: The verse’s tent is only a figurative comparison, whereas the tent in Ziyād’s poem may be real; the verse is an explicit metaphor and the poem can be literal with an allusion.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p528/r1.anchor: لأن القبة في الآية مشبه بها وليست بموجودة والقبة في البيت يمكن أن تكون حقيقة فالآية استعارة وتصريح والبيت حقيقة وكناية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p528/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p528/r2.speaker: الطيبي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p528/r2.claim: Al-Ṭībī emphasizes that the metaphor in the verse differs from Ziyād’s potentially literal tent.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p528/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p528/r3.speaker: التفتزاني
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p528/r3.claim: Al-Taftāzānī reads either metaphorical analysis as an allusion to the Jews’ humiliation; Ibn ʿĀshūr says these rhetorical insights can coexist.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p528/r3.anchor: وجعل التفتزاني الآية على الاحتمالين في الاستعارة كناية عن كون اليهود أذلاء متصاغرين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p528/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p528/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p528/r4.claim: ذلة means disgrace or abasement, is pronounced with kasra only, and opposes honor; al-Samawʾal or al-Ḥārithī contrasts the two in a verse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p528/r4.anchor: وما ضرنا أنا قليل وجارنا عزيز وجار الأكثرين ذليل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p528/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p528/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p528/r5.claim: مسكنة means poverty, from stillness because poverty reduces a person’s movement; it also means weakness, and مسكين denotes a poor person.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p528/r5.anchor: والمسكنة الفقر مشتقة من السكون لأن الفقر يقلل حركة صاحبه . وتطلق على الضعف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p528/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p528/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p528/r6.claim: Their humiliation means they lost courage and displayed need despite abundant blessings; weariness made those blessings seem worthless, and greed persisted in their descendants.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p528/r6.anchor: ومعنى لزوم الذلة والمسكنة لليهود أنهم فقدوا البأس والشجاعة وبدا عليهم سيما الفقر والحاجة مع وفرة ما أنعم الله عليهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p528/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p528/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p528/r7.claim: باءوا means return, metaphorically describing a reversal from a state pleasing to God into His anger.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p528/r7.anchor: والبوء الرجوع وهو هنا مستعار لانقلاب الحالة مما يرضى الله إلى غضبه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p529/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p529/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p529/r1.claim: The singular demonstrative ذالك summarizes the preceding statement as one mentioned matter; the punishment terms themselves are unseen and are not pointed to as objects.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p529/r1.anchor: وأفرد اسم الإشارة لتأويل المشار إليه بالمذكور وهو أولى بجواز الإفراد من إفراد الضمير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p529/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p529/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p529/r2.claim: Abū ʿUbayda challenged Ruʾba’s singular كأنه when the poet had named plural lines, and Ruʾba replied that he meant ذلك, the whole matter.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p529/r2.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة لرؤبة : إن أردت الخطوط فقل كأنها وإن أردت السواد والبياض فقل كأنهما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p529/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p529/r3.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p529/r3.claim: Al-Kashshāf explains singular demonstrative and relative forms by saying their grammatical number and gender are not literal.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p529/r3.anchor: وقال صاحب ( الكشاف ) ( والذي حسن ذلك أن أسماء الإشارة ليست تثنيتها وجمعها وتأنيثها على الحقيقة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p529/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p529/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p529/r4.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr finds that explanation of little value because it still relies on interpretation or metaphor, with no special advantage for these forms.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p529/r4.anchor: وهو قليل الجدوى لأن المدار على التأويل والمجاز سواء كان في استعمال لفظ في معنى آخر أو في استعمال صيغة في معنى أخرى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p529/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p529/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p529/r5.claim: He suggests al-Kashshāf may mean that ذا and الذي denote a genus, while their dual and plural forms are separate words rather than inflections of a singular.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p529/r5.anchor: فلعله أراد أن ذا موضوع لجنس ما يشار إليه . والذي موضوع لجنس ما عرف بصلة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p529#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p529#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p529#2/r1.claim: The باء is causal: disbelief and the related acts caused worldly humiliation and poverty and God’s anger, warning against repeating them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p529#2/r1.anchor: والباء في قوله : { بأنهم كانوا يكفرون } سببية أي إن كفرهم وما معه كان سببا لعقابهم في الدنيا بالذلة والمسكنة وفي الآخرة بغضب الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p529#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p529#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p529#2/r2.claim: The charge of killing prophets covers Jewish generations who killed, ordered, or silently failed to defend them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p529#2/r2.anchor: خاص بأجيال اليهود الذين اجترموا هذه الجريمة العظيمة سواء في ذلك من باشر القتل وأمر به ومن سكت عنه ولم ينصر الأنبياء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p529#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p529#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p529#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr says Isaiah son of Amoz, alive in the mid-eighth century BCE, was sawn on a tree by King Manasseh around 700 BCE.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p529#2/r3.anchor: قتله الملك منسى ملك اليهود سنة 700 قبل المسيح نشر نشرا على جذع شجرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p529#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p529#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p529#2/r4.claim: Jeremiah was stoned after repeatedly rebuking and advising the Jews; Ibn ʿĀshūr notes disagreement about this account.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p529#2/r4.anchor: فرجموه بالحجارة حتى قتلوه وفي ذلك خلاف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p529#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p529#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p529#2/r5.claim: Zechariah, John’s father, was killed by Herod while trying to save his son from execution during Jesus’s prophethood.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p529#2/r5.anchor: وزكرياء الأخير أبا يحيى قتله هيرودس العبراني ملك اليهود من قبل الرومان لأن زكرياء حاول تخليص ابنه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p529#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p529#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p529#2/r6.claim: Herod killed John son of Zechariah because Herod’s niece was angry with John.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p529#2/r6.anchor: ويحيى بن زكرياء قتله هيرودس لغضب ابنة أخت هيرودس على يحيى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p530/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p530/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p530/r1.claim: بغير الحق means without a valid ground in their own law; this indicts them by their scripture, although killing prophets can never be justified.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p530/r1.anchor: أي بدون وجه معتبر في شريعتهم فإن فيها : { أنه من قتل نفسا بغير نفس أو فساد في الأرض فكأنما قتل الناس جميعا }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p530/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p530/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p530/r2.claim: The text says prophets rather than messengers because enemies cannot overcome messengers without undermining the purpose of revelation; the claim that Jews killed Jesus conflicts with that wisdom, since God ended his mission after its aim was achieved.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p530/r2.anchor: وإنما قال ( الأنبياء ) لأن الرسل لا تسلط عليهم أعداؤهم لأنه مناف لحكمة الرسالة التي هي التبليغ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p530/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p530/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p530/r3.claim: The second ذالك may repeat the first reference to punishment, adding disobedience and transgression as further causes; repetition can serve instead of conjunction.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p530/r3.anchor: يحتمل أن تكون الإشارة فيه إلى نفس المشار إليه بذلك الأولى فيكون تكريرا للإشارة لزيادة تمييز المشار إليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p530/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p530/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p530/r4.claim: Alternatively, the second ذالك may refer to disbelief and killing the prophets, which caused the punishment; persistent small sins lead into greater ones.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p530/r4.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المشار إليه بذلك الثاني هو الكفر بآيات الله وقتلهم النبيئين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p530/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p530/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p530/r5.claim: On either reading, both باءs are causal; Ibn ʿĀshūr rejects making one mean مع, since repetition can replace conjunction without the strained reading in al-Kashshāf and al-Ṭībī.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p530/r5.anchor: ولا حاجة إلى جعل إحدى الباءين بمعنى مع على تقدير جعل اسم الإشارة الثاني تكريرا للأول

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153/r1.claim: The Israelites spoke in the wilderness after tiring of manna and quail and recalling their former life in Egypt; the two foods are called one food because they ate them together and repeatedly received the same pair.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153/r1.anchor: كان هذا القول منهم في التيه حين ملوا المن والسلوى، وتذكروا عيشهم الأول بمصر، وكنى عن المن والسلوى ب طعام واحد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153/r2.claim: In the dialect of Banu Amir, the ʿayn of فادع is pronounced with kasra.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153/r2.anchor: وهما طعامان، لأنهما كانا يؤكلان في وقت واحد، ولتكرارهما سواء أبدا قيل لهما طعام واحد، ولغة بني عامر «فادع» بكسر العين.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153/r3.claim: يخرج is jussive through the conditional sense implicit in the command; Abu Umar al-Jarmi instead makes the command itself govern it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153/r3.anchor: ويخرج: جزم بما تضمنه الأمر من معنى الجزاء، وبنفس الأمر على مذهب أبي عمر الجرمي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153/r4.claim: Sibawayh supplies an omitted object for يخرج, estimated as مأكولا مما تنبت الأرض.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153/r4.anchor: والمفعول على مذهب سيبويه مضمر تقديره مأكولا مما تنبت الأرض

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153/r5.speaker: الأخفش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153/r5.claim: Al-Akhfash regards من in مما as extra and ما as the object; Sibawayh rejects extra من outside negation, as in ما رأيت من أحد.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153/r5.anchor: وقال الأخفش: «من» في قوله: مما زائدة «وما» مفعولة، وأبى سيبويه أن تكون «من» ملغاة في غير النفي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153/r6.claim: The من in من بقلها marks kind, and بقلها is an apposition repeating the preposition; baql includes all plants the earth grows, and qithāʾ is plural of qithʾa.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153/r6.anchor: ومن في قوله: من بقلها لبيان الجنس، وبقلها بدل بإعادة الحرف، والبقل كل ما تنبته الأرض من النجم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153/r7.speaker: طلحة بن مصرف ويحيى بن وثاب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153/r7.claim: Talha ibn Musarrif and Yahya ibn Waththab read قثائها with a damma on the qaf.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153/r7.anchor: وقرأ طلحة بن مصرف ويحيى بن وثاب: «قثائها» ، بضم القاف.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153/r8.speaker: ابن عباس وأكثر المفسرين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas and most exegetes say fūm means wheat.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وأكثر المفسرين: «الفوم الحنطة» .

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153/r10.speaker: عطاء وقتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153/r10.claim: Ata and Qatada define fūm as grains suitable for baking, including wheat, fava beans, and lentils.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153/r10.anchor: وقال عطاء وقتادة: «الفوم جميع الحبوب التي يمكن أن تختبز كالحنطة والفول والعدس ونحوه» .

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153/r11.speaker: الضحاك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153/r11.claim: Al-Dahhak says fūm means garlic, supported by Ubayy ibn Kaʿb's reading with thāʾ and a report from Ibn Abbas; Ibn Atiyya prefers wheat because consonant substitution is not analogically productive.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153/r11.anchor: وقال الضحاك: «الفوم الثوم» ، وهي قراءة عبد الله بن مسعود بالثاء، وروي ذلك عن ابن عباس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153/r12.claim: Ibn Atiyya prefers the wheat interpretation; Ibn Abbas's poetic citation supports it by using fūm for wheat.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153/r12.anchor: والأول أصح: أنها الحنطة، وأنشد ابن عباس قول أحيحة بن الجلاح

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153/r13.claim: Ibn Abbas cites Uhayha ibn al-Jallah's poem as evidence that fūm means wheat.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153/r13.anchor: وأنشد ابن عباس قول أحيحة بن الجلاح: [الطويل] قد كنت أغنى الناس شخصا واجدا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153/r14.speaker: ابن دريد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153/r14.claim: Ibn Durayd says fūm means either crops or wheat, and the Azd of al-Sarat call ears of grain fūm.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153/r14.anchor: قال ابن دريد: «الفوم الزرع أو الحنطة» ، وأزد السراة يسمون السنبل فوما

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153/r15.claim: Istibdāl means seeking to put one thing in another's place; al-Zajjaj derives أدنى from nearness in value.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153/r15.anchor: والاستبدال طلب وضع الشيء موضع الآخر، وأدنى مأخوذ عند أبي إسحاق الزجاج من الدنو أي القرب في القيمة.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153#2/r1.speaker: علي بن سليمان
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153#2/r1.claim: Ali ibn Sulayman derives أدنى, with eased hamza, from danīʾ, meaning plainly base or inferior.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153#2/r1.anchor: وقال علي بن سليمان: «هو مهموز من الدنيء البين الدناءة، بمعنى الأخس، إلا أنه خففت همزته» .

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153#2/r2.speaker: غيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153#2/r2.claim: Another derives it from dūn, lower: its original form أدون is reshaped to أفلع, with final wāw changing to alif.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153#2/r2.anchor: وقال غيره: «هو مأخوذ من الدون أي الأحط، فأصله أدون أفعل، قلب فجاء أفلع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153#2/r4.claim: The verse asks whether the Israelites would exchange the inferior herbs, cucumbers, fūm, lentils, and onions for the better manna and quail.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153#2/r4.anchor: أتستبدلون البقل والقثاء والفوم والعدس والبصل التي هي أدنى بالمن والسلوى الذي هو خير؟

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153#2/r5.speaker: الزجاج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153#2/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj says manna and quail are superior in value, since the requested vegetables have little worth.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153#2/r5.anchor: وهذا قول الزجاج، ويحتمل أن يفضل المن والسلوى لأنه الطعام الذي من الله به

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153#2/r6.claim: Manna and quail are better because God supplied and commanded them, so continuing to obey and thank Him earns a reward stored for the afterlife; the requested food lacks these qualities.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153#2/r6.anchor: وفي استدامة أمر الله تعالى وشكر نعمته أجر وذخر في الآخرة، والذي طلبوا عار من هذه الخصال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153#2/r7.claim: Manna and quail may be better in taste and pleasure, since vegetables are inferior in this respect.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153#2/r7.anchor: ويحتمل أن يفضل في الطيب واللذة به، فالبقول لا محالة أدنى من هذا الوجه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153#2/r8.claim: They may be superior as nourishment and benefit.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153#2/r8.anchor: ويحتمل أن يفضل في حسن الغذاء ونفعه، فالمن والسلوى خير لا محالة في هذا الوجه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153#2/r9.claim: They require no labor, whereas the requested crops require cultivation and toil.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153#2/r9.anchor: ويحتمل أن يفضل من جهة أنه لا كلفة فيه ولا تعب، والذي طلبوا لا يجيء إلا بالحرث والزراعة والتعب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153#2/r10.claim: Their divine origin makes their lawfulness certain, whereas produce acquired through commerce or usurpation can involve doubtful status.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153#2/r10.anchor: ويحتمل أن يفضل في أنه لا مرية في حله وخلوصه لنزوله من عند الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153#2/r11.claim: Ibn Atiyya says all of these grounds together establish the superiority of manna and quail.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153#2/r11.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد رحمه الله: ويترتب الفضل للمن والسلوى بهذه الوجوه كلها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153#2/r12.claim: The verse omits the intervening events: Moses prayed to his Lord, received an answer, and then told them to descend.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153#2/r12.anchor: وفي الكلام حذف، تقديره: فدعا موسى ربه فأجابه، فقال لهم: اهبطوا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153#2/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153#2/r13.claim: Most readers inflect مصر with tanwin, in agreement with the codex, though some Uthmani codices are reported otherwise.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153#2/r13.anchor: وجمهور الناس يقرؤون «مصرا» بالتنوين وهو خط المصحف، إلا ما حكي عن بعض مصاحف عثمان رضي الله عنه.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153#2/r14.speaker: مجاهد وغيره ممن صرفها
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153#2/r14.claim: Mujahid and others who inflect مصر take it as an unspecified town, citing the command to enter a town and reports that the Israelites settled Syria after the wilderness.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p153#2/r14.anchor: وقال مجاهد وغيره ممن صرفها: «أراد مصرا من الأمصار غير معين» ، واستدلوا بما اقتضاه القرآن من أمرهم بدخول القرية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r1.speaker: طائفة ممن صرفها
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r1.claim: Some who inflect مصر still identify it as Pharaoh's Egypt, citing the Quran's account that Israel inherited Pharaoh's lands and traces; they allow its inflection.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r1.anchor: وقالت طائفة ممن صرفها: أراد مصر فرعون بعينها، واستدلوا بما في القرآن من أن الله تعالى أورث بني إسرائيل ديار آل فرعون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r2.speaker: الأخفش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r2.claim: Al-Akhfash permits inflecting the name because of its lightness and resemblance to Hind and Daʿd; Sibawayh does not permit this.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r2.anchor: قال الأخفش: «لخفتها وشبهها بهند ودعد» . وسيبويه لا يجيز هذا.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r3.speaker: غير الأخفش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r3.claim: Another explanation says the word is inflected because it denotes a place.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r4.speaker: الحسن وأبان بن تغلب وغيرهما
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r4.claim: Al-Hasan, Aban ibn Taghlib, and others read مصر without inflection, as does Ubayy's codex, and mean Pharaoh's Egypt.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r4.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وأبان بن تغلب وغيرهما: «اهبطوا مصر» بترك الصرف، وكذلك هي في مصحف أبي بن كعب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r5.speaker: الأعمش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r5.claim: Al-Aʿmash identifies it as the Egypt over which Salih ibn Ali presides.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r5.anchor: قال الأعمش: «هي مصر التي عليها صالح بن علي» .

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r6.speaker: أشهب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r6.claim: Ashhab reports Malik's view that it is Malik's own Egypt, the town where Pharaoh resided.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r6.anchor: وقال أشهب: «قال لي مالك: هي عندي مصر قريتك مسكن فرعون» .

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r7.claim: The statement فإن لكم ما سألتم implies that God left them to their own devices.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r7.anchor: وقوله تعالى: فإن لكم ما سألتم يقتضي أنه وكلهم إلى أنفسهم.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r8.speaker: النخعي وابن وثاب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r8.claim: Al-Nakhaʿi and Ibn Waththab read سألتم with kasra on the sīn, a dialectal form.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r8.anchor: وقرأ النخعي وابن وثاب «سألتم» بكسر السين وهي لغة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r9.claim: The humiliation and poverty were imposed and decreed for them; ضرب is used in idioms for imposing or binding an obligation, and the verbal noun is annexed semantically to its object.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r9.anchor: وضربت عليهم الذلة والمسكنة معناه ألزموها وقضي عليهم بها، كما يقال ضرب الأمير البعث

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r10.claim: ذلة is a state or condition derived from ذل.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r10.anchor: والذلة فعلة من الذل كأنها الهيئة والحال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r11.speaker: الزجاج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r11.claim: Al-Zajjaj derives maskana from stillness and says it is the appearance of poverty and subjection, which even a wealthy Jew retains.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r11.anchor: قال الزجاج: «هي مأخوذة من السكون وهي هنا: زي الفقر وخضوعه، وإن وجد يهودي غني فلا يخلو من زي الفقر ومهانته» .

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r12.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r12.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada interpret maskana as the poll tax, jizya.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r12.anchor: قال الحسن وقتادة: «المسكنة الخراج أي الجزية» .

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r13.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r13.claim: Abu al-Aliya interprets maskana as poverty and need.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r14.claim: They bore God's wrath: baʾtu means to bear something, illustrated by Muhalhil's address to Yahya ibn al-Harith ibn ʿAbbad.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r14.anchor: وباؤ بغضب من الله معناه: مروا متحملين له، تقول: بؤت بكذا إذا تحملته

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r15.claim: Wrath meaning will is an essential attribute, while wrath displayed through punishment is an attribute of action.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r15.anchor: والغضب بمعنى الإرادة صفة ذات، وبمعنى إظهاره على العبد بالمعاقبة صفة فعل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r16.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r16.claim: ذلك points to the imposition of humiliation and what follows; the bāʾ in بأنهم marks cause.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r16.anchor: والإشارة بذلك إلى ضرب الذلة وما بعده، والباء في بأنهم باء السبب.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r17.speaker: المهدوي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r17.claim: Al-Mahdawi says bāʾ means lām, yielding the sense 'because they'.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r17.anchor: وقال المهدوي: «إن الباء بمعنى اللام» والمعنى: لأنهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r18.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r18.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r18.claim: آيات may mean the nine signs and other extraordinary signs proving the truth of the messenger, or the signs of the Torah analogous to Quranic signs.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p154/r18.anchor: والآيات هنا تحتمل أن يراد بها التسع وغيرها مما يخرق العادة، وهو علامة لصدق الآية به

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p155/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p155/r1.speaker: الحسن بن أبي الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p155/r1.claim: Al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan reads وتقتلون in the second person, returning to direct address; a third-person reading is also reported from him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p155/r1.anchor: وقرأ الحسن بن أبي الحسن: «وتقتلون» بالتاء على الرجوع إلى خطابهم، وروي عنه أيضا بالياء.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p155/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p155/r2.speaker: نافع
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p155/r2.claim: Nafiʿ hamzates النبيئين wherever it occurs except the two Ahzab passages, 33:50 and 33:53, where he omits lengthening and hamza; the remaining readers omit hamza throughout.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p155/r2.anchor: وقرأ نافع: بهمز «النبيئين» ، وكذلك حيث وقع في القرآن، إلا في موضعين: في سورة الأحزاب:

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p155/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p155/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p155/r3.claim: Hamzating derives nabīʾ from anbaʾa, 'to inform': nabīʾ means an informer, like samīʿ meaning one who makes heard; the plural nabāʾ supports the derivation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p155/r3.anchor: فأما من همز فهو عنده من «أنبأ» إذا أخبر، واسم فاعله منبىء فقيل نبيء، بمعنى منبىء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p155/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p155/r4.speaker: الشاعر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p155/r4.claim: A poetic line addressed to the Seal of the Prophets uses النبآء as a plural form supporting the hamzated derivation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p155/r4.anchor: يا خاتم النبآء إنك مرسل ... بالحق كل هدى الإله هداكا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p155/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p155/r5.speaker: أبو علي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p155/r5.claim: Abu Ali cites Sibawayh's نبيئة in a construction with نبوته and the universal use of تنبأ to argue that the root's final radical is hamza.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p155/r5.anchor: قال أبو علي: «زعم سيبويه أنهم يقولون في تحقير النبوة: كان مسيلمة نبوته نبيئة سوء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p155/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p155/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p155/r6.claim: Those who do not hamzate differ: some derive nabī from hamza but ease the hamza, while others derive it from naba yanbū, meaning to appear; the prophet guides to the manifest path of guidance and salvation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p155/r6.anchor: واختلف القائلون بترك الهمز في نبيء، فمنهم من اشتق النبي من همز ثم سهل الهمز، ومنهم من قال: هو مشتق من نبا ينبوا إذا ظهر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p155/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p155/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p155/r7.claim: The dominant plural أنبياء resembles defective forms such as walī/awliyāʾ and ṣafī/aṣfiyāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p155/r7.anchor: واستدلوا بأن الأغلب في جمع أنبياء كفعيل في المعتل، نحو ولي وأولياء وصفي وأصفياء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p155/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p155/r8.speaker: الزهراوي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p155/r8.claim: Al-Zahrawi records نبوء for 'appeared', making a conspicuous road نبيء with hamza.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p155/r8.anchor: وحكى الزهراوي أنه يقال نبوء إذا ظهر فهو نبيء، والطريق الظاهر نبيء بالهمز

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p155/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p155/r9.speaker: رجل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p155/r9.claim: A report says a man greeted the Prophet as 'Nabīʾ of God' with hamza; the Prophet answered that he was God's prophet without hamza.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p155/r9.anchor: وروي أن رجلا قال للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: السلام عليك يا نبيء الله، وهمز، فقال له النبي عليه السلام: لست بنبيء الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p155/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p155/r10.speaker: أبو علي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p155/r10.claim: Abu Ali calls the greeting report's chain weak; he says the Prophet's silence when praised as خاتم النبآء strengthens its weakness, since the plural and singular follow the same pattern.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p155/r10.anchor: قال أبو علي: «ضعف سند هذا الحديث، ومما يقوي ضعفه أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم، قد أنشده المادح يا خاتم النبآء ولم يؤثر في ذلك إنكار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p156/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p156/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p156/r1.claim: بغير الحق intensifies the atrocity and sin: although no prophet could rightly be killed, the phrase rules out a conceivable excuse; no prophet committed a crime warranting execution, and God allowed some to be killed as an honor raising their rank, like martyrs among believers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p156/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى: بغير الحق تعظيم للشنعة والذنب الذي أتوه، ومعلوم أنه لا يقتل نبي بحق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p156/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p156/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p156/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas and others say only prophets not commanded to fight were killed; every prophet commanded to fight was victorious.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p156/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس وغيره: «لم يقتل قط من الأنبياء إلا من لم يؤمر بقتال، وكل من أمر بقتال نصر» .

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p156/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p156/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p156/r3.claim: ذلك refers back to the earlier indication and reinforces it; the bāʾ in بما expresses cause.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p156/r3.anchor: وقوله تعالى: ذلك رد على الأول وتأكيد للإشارة إليه، والباء في بما باء السبب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p156/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p156/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p156/r4.claim: يعتدون means transgressing limits; transgression applies broadly to crossing boundaries and is conventionally used for injustice and sins.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p156/r4.anchor: ويعتدون معناه: يتجاوزون الحدود، والاعتداء تجاوز الحد في كل شيء، وعرفه في الظلم والمعاصي.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p51/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p51/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p51/r1.claim: Fūm is said to mean wheat and bread.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p51/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p51/r2.speaker: الفراء
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p51/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says fūm is an old dialect word in the command fūmū, meaning bake bread.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p51/r2.anchor: قال الفراء (1) هي لغة قديمة يقول أهلها: فوموا، أي: اختبزوا.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p51/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p51/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p51/r3.claim: Another reported interpretation takes fūm to mean grains.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p51/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p51/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p51/r4.claim: Ibn Qutayba prefers garlic, supported by the reading thūmihā in the codex of ʿAbd Allāh.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p51/r4.anchor: وهذا أعجب الأقاويل إلي؛ لأنها في مصحف عبد الله: "وثومها"

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p51/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p51/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p51/r5.claim: The garlic reading is linguistically supported by Arabic interchange of thāʾ and fāʾ, as in jadath/jadaf and mughāthīr/mughāfīr.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p51/r5.anchor: والعرب تبدل الثاء بالفاء فيقولون جدث وجدف. والمغاثير والمغافير

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p51/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p51/r6.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p51/r6.claim: Bāʾū means they returned; the verb is used as bǔtu bi-kadhā and abūʾu bihi, not bāʾa bi-l-shayʾ.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p51/r6.anchor: أي رجعوا. يقال: بؤت بكذا فأنا أبوء به. ولا يقال: باء بالشيء.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p88/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p88/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p88/r1.claim: The Israelites said this while in the wilderness; by one food they meant manna and quail.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p88/r1.anchor: هذا قولهم في التيه وعنوا بالطعام الواحد المن والسلوى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p88/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p88/r2.speaker: محمد بن القاسم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p88/r2.claim: They counted manna and quail as one food because the manna was eaten with quail and the quail with manna.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p88/r2.anchor: كان المن يؤكل بالسلوى والسلوى بالمن فلذلك كانا طعاما واحدا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p88/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p88/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p88/r3.claim: Baql is a collective noun; they meant vegetables.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p88/r3.anchor: والبقل هاهنا اسم جنس وعنوا به البقول

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p88/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p88/r4.speaker: أبو منصور اللغوي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p88/r4.claim: Against a popular narrow usage, baql means herbage and spring growth eaten by both people and animals.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p88/r4.anchor: إنما البقل العشب وما ينبت الربيع مما يأكله الناس والبهائم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p88/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p88/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p88/r5.claim: Baqalat and abqalat are both eloquent forms for land sprouting vegetation; ibtaqalat describes camels grazing.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p88/r5.anchor: يقال بقلت الأرض وأبقلت لغتان فصيحتان إذا أنبت البقل وابتقلت الإبل إذا رعت

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p88/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p88/r6.speaker: أبو النجم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p88/r6.claim: Abu al-Najm’s poem uses tabaqqalat for camels grazing at the first sprouting of vegetation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p88/r6.anchor: تبقلت في أول التبقل وبين رماحي مالك ونهشل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p88/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p88/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p88/r7.claim: Qiththāʾ has both kasra and damma on its first consonant; the kasra is better and is the majority reading.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p88/r7.anchor: وفي القثاء لغتان كسر القاف وضمها والكسر أجود وبه قرأ الجمهور

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p88/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p88/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود، أبو رجاء، قتادة، طلحة بن مصرف، الأعمش
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p88/r8.claim: These readers pronounce qiththāʾ with damma on the qāf.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p88/r8.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود و أبو رجاء وقتادة وطلحة بن مصرف والأعمش بضم القاف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p88/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p88/r9.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p88/r9.claim: The kasra pronunciation is Hijazi; the damma pronunciation belongs to Tamim and some of Banu Asad.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p88/r9.anchor: الكسر لغة أهل الحجاز والضم لغة تميم وبعض بني أسد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p88/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p88/r10.speaker: ابن عباس، السدي عن أشياخه، الحسن، أبو مالك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p88/r10.claim: One interpretation of fūm is wheat.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p88/r10.anchor: أنه الحنطة قاله ابن عباس والسدي عن أشياخه والحسن وأبو مالك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p88/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p88/r11.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p88/r11.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says fūm is an old dialect in the request fūmū lanā, meaning bake bread for us.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p88/r11.anchor: هي لغة قديمة يقول أهلها فوموا لنا أي اختبزوا لنا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p88/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p88/r12.speaker: الفراء، مجاهد، الربيع بن أنس، مقاتل، الكسائي، النضر بن شميل، ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p88/r12.claim: A second view identifies fūm as garlic, supported by the variant thūmuhā and its pairing with similar foods.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p88/r12.anchor: أنه الثوم وهو قراءة عبد الله وأبي وثومها واختاره الفراء وعلل بأنه ذكر مع ما يشاكله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p88/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p88/r13.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p88/r13.claim: The garlic reading is explained by the Arabic interchange of fāʾ and thāʾ, as in several paired word forms.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p88/r13.anchor: والفاء تبدل من الثاء كما تقول العرب الجدث والجدف للقبر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p89/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p89/r1.speaker: ابن قتيبة، الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p89/r1.claim: A third interpretation says fūm means grains.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p89/r1.anchor: والثالث أنه الحبوب ذكره ابن قتيبة و الزجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p89/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p89/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p89/r2.claim: Adnā means lower or worse, while khayr means higher; manna and quail were better than what the people requested.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p89/r2.anchor: أي أرادأ بالذي هو خير أي أعلى يريد أن المن والسلوى اعلى ما طلبتم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p89/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p89/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود، ابن عباس، قتادة، ابن زيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p89/r3.claim: One view takes miṣran as any unspecified Egyptian city, since the requested produce was available in towns.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p89/r3.anchor: أنه اسم لمصر من الأمصار غير معين قاله ابن مسعود و ابن عباس وقتادة وابن زيد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p89/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p89/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p89/r4.claim: This interpretation explains the order to descend to a city by the availability there of the requested foods.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p89/r4.anchor: وإنما أمروا بالمصر لأن الذي طلبوه في الأمصار

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p89/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p89/r5.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس، أبو العالية، الضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p89/r5.claim: A second view identifies Miṣr as the specific land of Egypt, Pharaoh’s Egypt according to Ibn Abbas.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p89/r5.anchor: قال أبو صاح عن ابن عباس أراد مصر فرعون وهذا قول أبوالعالية والضحاك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p89/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p89/r6.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p89/r6.claim: Al-Farrāʾ prefers the specific Egypt interpretation and cites the non-tanwīn reading of Miṣr as evidence.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p89/r6.anchor: واختاره الفراء واحتج بقراءة عبد الله قال وسئل عنها الأعمش

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p89/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p89/r7.speaker: الأعمش
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p89/r7.claim: When asked about the reading, al-Aʿmash said it means the Egypt ruled by Ṣāliḥ ibn ʿAlī.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p89/r7.anchor: وسئل عنها الأعمش فقال هى مصر التي عليها صالح بن على

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p89/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p89/r8.speaker: مفضل الضبي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p89/r8.claim: Al-Mufaḍḍal al-Ḍabbī explains Egypt’s name as the boundary between the eastern and western limits.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p89/r8.anchor: سميت مصرا لأنها أخر حدود المشرق وأول حدود المغرب فهى حد بينهما والمصر الحد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p89/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p89/r9.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p89/r9.claim: In Hajar usage, miṣr means a place’s boundaries, as in a deed describing a house with its borders.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p89/r9.anchor: وأهل هجر يكتبون في عهدهم اشترى فلان الدار بمصورها أي بحدودها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p89/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p89/r10.speaker: عدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p89/r10.claim: ʿAdī’s verse uses miṣran to mean a boundary or limit between day and night.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p89/r10.anchor: وجاعل الشمس مصرا لاخفاء به بين النهار وبين الليل قد فصلا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p89/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p89/r11.speaker: ابن فارس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p89/r11.claim: Some explain the name Miṣr by people’s intent toward it, like maṣartu al-shāh for milking a sheep because people flock there and rarely leave.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p89/r11.anchor: حكى ابن فارس ان قوما قالوا سميت بذلك لقصد الناس إياها كقولهم مصرت الشاة إذا حلبتها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p90/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p90/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p90/r1.claim: Being struck with humiliation means being made to bear it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p90/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى ﴿ وضربت عليهم الذلة ﴾ أي ألزموها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p90/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p90/r2.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p90/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ treats dhilla and dhull as synonyms.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p90/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p90/r3.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p90/r3.claim: Al-Hasan interprets the imposed humiliation as the jizya tax.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p90/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p90/r4.speaker: أبو العالية، السدي، أبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p90/r4.claim: One interpretation of maskana is poverty and destitution.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p90/r4.anchor: انها الفقر والفاقة قاله أبوالعالية والسدي وابو عبيدة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p90/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p90/r5.speaker: السدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p90/r5.claim: Al-Suddī also transmits an interpretation of maskana as poverty of the soul.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p90/r5.anchor: وروي عن السدي قال هي فقر النفس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p90/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p90/r6.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p90/r6.claim: Another interpretation of maskana is submissiveness.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p90/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p90/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p90/r8.claim: The demonstrative that refers either to God’s wrath alone or to all that was imposed on them, including humiliation and poverty.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p90/r8.anchor: إشارة إلى الغضب وقيل إلى جميع ما ألزموه من الذلة والمسكنة وغيرها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p90/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p90/r9.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p90/r9.claim: Nāfiʿ uses hamza in nabiyyīn and related forms except in two places in al-Aḥzāb, where two successive same-kind kasra hamzas meet.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p90/r9.anchor: وقوله تعالى ﴿ ذلك ﴾ إشارة إلى الغضب وقيل إلى جميع ما ألزموه من الذلة والمسكنة وغيرها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p90/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p90/r10.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p90/r10.claim: Al-Zajjāj considers leaving the hamza the better form; nabi may derive from informing or from rising in rank.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p90/r10.anchor: قال الزجاج الأجود ترك الهمز واشتقاق النبي من نبأ وأنبأ أي أخبر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p90/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p90/r11.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p90/r11.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports that Israelites killed three hundred prophets in one day, then opened their vegetable market that evening.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p90/r11.anchor: كانت بنو اسرائيل تقتل في اليوم ثلاثمائة نبي ثم يقيمون سوق بقلهم في آخر النهار

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p90#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p90#2/r1.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p90#2/r1.claim: Bi-ghayri l-ḥaqq can mean without any crime or offense.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p90#2/r1.anchor: أن معناه بغير جرم قاله ابن الانباري

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p90#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p90#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p90#2/r2.claim: A second view treats bi-ghayri l-ḥaqq as emphatic, as in the statement that hearts in breasts grow blind.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p90#2/r2.anchor: أنه توكيد كقوله تعالى ﴿ ولكن تعمى القلوب التي في الصدور ﴾

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p90#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p90#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p90#2/r3.claim: A third view describes their killing as unjust, just as God’s judgment is described as right without implying He judges otherwise.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p90#2/r3.anchor: خارج مخرج الصفة لقتلهم أنه ظلم فهو كقوله تعالى ﴿ رب احكم بالحق ﴾

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p90#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p90#2/r5.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p90#2/r5.claim: Al-Zajjāj defines transgression as exceeding the proper measure in anything.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p90#2/r5.anchor: الاعتداء مجاوزة القدر في كل شئ

MAJAZ:v1p42/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p42/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p42/r2.claim: Al-maskana is the verbal noun of miskīn; an example calls the poorer of two men the more miskīn.

MAJAZ:v1p42/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p42/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p42/r3.claim: Bāʾū bi-ghaḍab means that they bore or took on the anger.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p280/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p280/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p280/r1.claim: God reminds Israel of the pleasant, nourishing, easy provision of manna and quails, then rebukes their weariness and request to replace it with inferior produce.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p280/r1.anchor: واذكروا نعمتي عليكم في إنزالي عليكم المن والسلوى، طعاما طيبا نافعا هنيئا سهلا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p280/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p280/r2.speaker: الحسن البصري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p280/r2.claim: Al-Hasan says they showed ingratitude, would not endure the provision, and recalled the diet they had lived on before.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p280/r2.anchor: وقال الحسن البصري رحمه الله: فبطروا ذلك ولم يصبروا عليه، وذكروا عيشهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p280/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p280/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p280/r3.claim: Ibn Masud's reading has thūm, with thāʾ, where the standard text has fūm.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p280/r3.anchor: وقع في قراءة ابن مسعود "وثومها" بالثاء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p280/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p280/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p280/r4.claim: Mujahid, in a report through Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, interprets fūm as garlic; al-Rabi ibn Anas and Saʿid ibn Jubayr agree.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p280/r4.anchor: وكذلك فسره مجاهد في رواية ليث بن أبي سليم، عنه، بالثوم. وكذا الربيع بن أنس، وسعيد بن جبير

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p280/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p280/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p280/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas is reported by al-Hasan as interpreting fūm as garlic.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p280/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p280/r6.speaker: اللغة القديمة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p280/r6.claim: An older Arabic usage takes fūmū lanā to mean bake bread for us.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p280/r6.anchor: وفي اللغة القديمة: فوموا لنا بمعنى: اختبزوا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p280/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p280/r7.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p280/r7.claim: If the baking gloss is correct, Ibn Jarir says fūm is a letter substitution: fāʾ and thāʾ may exchange because their articulation points are close.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p280/r7.anchor: فإن كان ذلك صحيحا، فإنه من الحروف المبدلة كقولهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p280/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p280/r8.speaker: آخرون
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p280/r8.claim: Another group interprets fūm as wheat, the grain from which bread is made.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p280/r8.anchor: وقال آخرون: الفوم الحنطة، وهو البر الذي يعمل منه الخبز

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p280/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p280/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p280/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas says fūm means wheat and cites the poet Ahiha ibn al-Jallah, whose use of the word fūm supports wheat as a cultivated grain.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p280/r9.anchor: قول أحيحة بن الجلاح وهو يقول: قد كنت أغنى الناس شخصا واحدا … ورد المدينة عن زراعة فوم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p280/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p280/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p280/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas also explains fūm as wheat in the dialect of Banu Hashim.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p280/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قول الله تعالى: {وفومها} قال: الفوم الحنطة بلسان بني هاشم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281/r1.claim: Ali ibn Abi Talha, al-Dahhak, and Ikrima transmit from Ibn Abbas that fūm means wheat.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281/r1.anchor: وعكرمة عن ابن عباس أن الفوم: الحنطة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281/r2.claim: Mujahid and Ata interpret fūm as bread.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281/r3.speaker: أبو مالك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281/r3.claim: Hasan and Abu Malik are reported to interpret fūm as wheat.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281/r3.anchor: عن الحسن، وحصين، عن أبي مالك: {وفومها} قال: الحنطة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281/r4.speaker: عكرمة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281/r4.claim: Ikrima, al-Suddi, al-Hasan al-Basri, Qatada, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam also take fūm to mean wheat.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281/r4.anchor: وهو قول عكرمة، والسدي، والحسن البصري، وقتادة، وعبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281/r5.speaker: البخاري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281/r5.claim: Al-Bukhari reports a view that fūm means all grains people eat.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281/r5.anchor: وقال البخاري: وقال بعضهم: الحبوب التي تؤكل كلها فوم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281/r6.claim: Moses rebukes the Israelites for seeking lowly foods while they enjoyed abundant, pleasant, beneficial provision.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281/r6.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {قال أتستبدلون الذي هو أدنى بالذي هو خير} فيه تقريع لهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281#2/r1.claim: The written and majority reading is Miṣran, declined with tanwin and written with an alif in the Uthmanic codices.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281#2/r1.anchor: هكذا هو منون مصروف مكتوب بالألف في المصاحف الأئمة العثمانية، وهو قراءة الجمهور بالصرف

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281#2/r2.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281#2/r2.claim: Ibn Jarir refuses a reading without declension because the codices unanimously use the declined form.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets Miṣran as any one of the cities, as transmitted by Ibn Abi Hatim through Ikrima.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281#2/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: {اهبطوا مصرا} قال: مصرا من الأمصار

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281#2/r4.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281#2/r4.claim: Al-Suddi, Qatada, and al-Rabi ibn Anas are reported to give the same interpretation as Ibn Abbas: a city among cities.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281#2/r4.anchor: وروي عن السدي، وقتادة، والربيع بن أنس نحو ذلك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281#2/r5.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281#2/r5.claim: The readings of Ubayy ibn Kab and Ibn Masud have Miṣr without declension.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281#2/r5.anchor: وقع في قراءة أبي بن كعب وابن مسعود: "اهبطوا مصر" من غير إجراء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281#2/r6.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281#2/r6.claim: Abu al-Aliyah and al-Rabi ibn Anas explain the non-declined reading as Egypt of Pharaoh; Ibn Abi Hatim also transmits this from al-Aliyah and al-Aʿmash.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281#2/r6.anchor: عن أبي العالية، والربيع بن أنس أنهما فسرا ذلك بمصر فرعون

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281#2/r7.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281#2/r7.claim: Ibn Jarir allows Egypt of Pharaoh even with declension, treating the spelling as following the codex, like 76:15–16, but leaves the intended place unresolved.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281#2/r7.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون المراد مصر فرعون على قراءة الإجراء أيضا. ويكون ذلك من باب الاتباع لكتابة المصحف

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281#2/r8.claim: Ibn Kathir rejects Ibn Jarir's hesitation and prefers a generic city, as reported from Ibn Abbas and others.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281#2/r8.anchor: وهذا الذي قاله فيه نظر، والحق أن المراد مصر من الأمصار كما روي عن ابن عباس وغيره

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281#2/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281#2/r9.claim: Moses' point is that the requested produce is common in any city, so it is too lowly and plentiful to warrant asking God for it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281#2/r9.anchor: هذا الذي سألتم ليس بأمر عزيز، بل هو كثير في أي بلد دخلتموه وجدتموه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281#2/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281#2/r10.claim: Because their request came from arrogance and excess rather than need, they were not granted it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p281#2/r10.anchor: ولا ضرورة فيه، لم يجابوا إليه، والله أعلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282/r1.claim: Humiliation and poverty were imposed on them by divine decree and law; they remain subdued and are humiliated by whoever gains power over them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282/r1.anchor: وضعت عليهم وألزموا بها شرعا وقدرا، أي: لا يزالون مستذلين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282/r2.speaker: الضحاك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak transmits from Ibn Abbas that the people described are holders of jizya obligations.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282/r2.anchor: قال الضحاك عن ابن عباس في قوله: {وضربت عليهم الذلة والمسكنة} قال: هم أصحاب النيالات

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282/r3.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282/r3.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada explain the imposed humiliation as paying jizya by hand while subdued.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282/r3.anchor: عن الحسن وقتادة، في قوله تعالى: {وضربت عليهم} قال: يعطون الجزية عن يد وهم صاغرون

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282/r4.speaker: الضحاك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282/r4.anchor: وقال الضحاك: {وضربت عليهم الذلة} قال: الذل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282/r5.speaker: الحسن
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282/r5.claim: Al-Hasan says God left them without protection and beneath Muslims' feet; this community encountered them while Magians collected jizya from them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282/r5.anchor: أذلهم الله فلا منعة لهم، وجعلهم الله تحت أقدام المسلمين. ولقد أدركتهم هذه الأمة وإن المجوس لتجبيهم الجزية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282/r6.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282/r6.claim: Abu al-Aliyah, al-Rabi ibn Anas, and al-Suddi interpret miskinah as poverty.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282/r6.anchor: وقال أبو العالية والربيع بن أنس والسدي: المسكنة الفاقة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282/r7.speaker: عطية العوفي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282/r7.claim: Atiyya al-Awfi interprets miskinah as a tax or land levy.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282/r8.speaker: الضحاك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282/r8.claim: Al-Dahhak also glosses miskinah as jizya.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282#2/r1.speaker: الضحاك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282#2/r1.claim: Al-Dahhak says they incurred God's anger.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282#2/r1.anchor: قال الضحاك: استحقوا الغضب من الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282#2/r2.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282#2/r2.claim: Al-Rabi ibn Anas says anger from God was brought down upon them; Saʿid ibn Jubayr says they deserved divine displeasure.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282#2/r2.anchor: وقال الربيع بن أنس: فحدث عليهم غضب من الله. وقال سعيد بن جبير: {وباءوا بغضب من الله} يقول: استوجبوا سخطا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282#2/r3.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282#2/r3.claim: Ibn Jarir explains bāʾū as returning while carrying something; here they returned burdened with God's anger, paralleling 5:29.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282#2/r3.anchor: يعني بقوله: {وباءوا بغضب من الله} انصرفوا ورجعوا، ولا يقال: باؤوا إلا موصولا إما بخير وإما بشر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282#2/r4.claim: Their humiliation and anger followed their arrogance against truth, disbelief in God's signs, and dishonoring prophets and their followers until they killed prophets.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282#2/r4.anchor: وكفرهم بآيات الله، وإهانتهم حملة الشرع وهم الأنبياء وأتباعهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282#2/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282#2/r5.claim: The Prophet defines arrogance as rejecting truth and despising people; Ibn Kathir uses this to characterize Israel's rejection and violence.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282#2/r5.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "الكبر بطر الحق، وغمط الناس"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282#2/r6.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282#2/r6.claim: Ibn Masud reports Malik ibn Marara asking whether his good looks and wish no one surpass him by two sandal straps count as arrogance; the Prophet says arrogance is rejecting truth and belittling people.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282#2/r6.anchor: قال ابن مسعود: كنت لا أحجب عن النجوى، ولا عن كذا ولا عن كذا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282#2/r7.claim: Israel's disbelief and killing of prophets brought God's irresistible punishment and disgrace in this world, joined to disgrace in the next as fitting recompense.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p282#2/r7.anchor: أحل الله بهم بأسه الذي لا يرد، وكساهم ذلا في الدنيا موصولا بذل الآخرة جزاء وفاقا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p283/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p283/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p283/r1.claim: Ibn Masud reports that Israelites killed three hundred prophets in one day, then sold vegetables in the market at day's end.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p283/r1.anchor: عن أبي معمر، عن عبد الله بن مسعود، قال: كانت بنو إسرائيل في اليوم تقتل ثلاثمائة نبي، ثم يقيمون سوق بقلهم في آخر النهار

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p283/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p283/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p283/r2.claim: The Prophet says the most severely punished at the Resurrection include someone killed by a prophet or who killed a prophet, a deviant leader, and an image-maker.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p283/r2.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "أشد الناس عذابا يوم القيامة رجل قتله نبي، أو قتل نبيا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p283/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p283/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p283/r3.claim: Disobedience means doing what is forbidden; transgression means exceeding the limits of what is permitted or commanded, and this is an additional cause of their punishment.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p283/r3.anchor: أنهم كانوا يعصون ويعتدون، فالعصيان فعل المناهي، والاعتداء المجاوزة في حد المأذون فيه أو المأمور به

NAHHAS:v1p231/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p231/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p231/r1.claim: يا موسى is a singular vocative; لن makes نصبر subjunctive, على makes طعام genitive, and واحد is its adjective.
NAHHAS:v1p231/r1.anchor: ( يا موسى ) نداء مفرد ( لن نصبر ) نصب بلن ( على طعام ) خفض بعلى ( واحد ) من نعته

NAHHAS:v1p231/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p231/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p231/r2.claim: فادع is a request functioning like an imperative, so its wāw is dropped; Banū ʿĀmir pronounce its ʿayn with kasra at the consonant junction.
NAHHAS:v1p231/r2.anchor: ( فادع ) سؤال بمنزلة الأمر فلذلك حذفت منه الواو ولغة بني عامر فادع لنا بكسر العين

NAHHAS:v1p231/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p231/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p231/r3.claim: يخرج لنا is jussive as the response to a command with conditional force.
NAHHAS:v1p231/r3.anchor: ( يخرج لنا ) جزم لأنه جواب الأمر وفيه معنى المجازاة

NAHHAS:v1p231/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p231/r4.speaker: الأخفش
NAHHAS:v1p231/r4.claim: Akhfash calls من extra so ما can serve as the object of يخرج; Nahhas rejects this under Sibawayh's rule that من is not extra in affirmative clauses, supplying an omitted object: edible produce.
NAHHAS:v1p231/r4.anchor: قال الأخفش من زائدة قال أبو جعفر هذا خطأ على قول سيبويه

NAHHAS:v1p231/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p231/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p231/r5.claim: من بقلها is appositional with a repeated preposition; وقثائها is coordinated with it.
NAHHAS:v1p231/r5.anchor: ( من بقلها ) بدل بإعادة الحروف ( وقثائها ) عطف

NAHHAS:v1p231/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p231/r6.speaker: طلحة ويحيى بن وثاب
NAHHAS:v1p231/r6.claim: They read وقثائها with ḍamma on qāf.
NAHHAS:v1p231/r6.anchor: وقرأ طلحة ويحيى بن وثاب ( وقثائها ) بضم القاف

NAHHAS:v1p231/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p231/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p231/r7.claim: The plural of قثاء is قثائي, like علباء/علابي; قثاء belongs to hamza-root words, as shown by أقثأت القوم.
NAHHAS:v1p231/r7.anchor: وتقول في جمعها قثائي مثل علباء وعلابي إلا أن قثاء من ذوات الهمزة

NAHHAS:v1p231/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p231/r8.speaker: علي بن سليمان
NAHHAS:v1p231/r8.claim: He says أدنى can only derive from hamzated دنيء, with hamza substituted.
NAHHAS:v1p231/r8.anchor: قال أبو جعفر سمعت علي بن سليمان يقول لا يصح عندي في ( أتستبدلون الذي هو أدنى )

NAHHAS:v1p231/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p231/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p231/r9.claim: Deriving أدنى from دنيء is allowable only in poetry, not prose, and so cannot explain the Qurʾānic wording.
NAHHAS:v1p231/r9.anchor: قال أبو جعفر هذا الذي ذكرنا إنما يجوز في الشعر ولا يجوز في الكلام

NAHHAS:v1p231#2/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p231#2/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p231#2/r6.claim: Though some derive أدنى as inferior or nearer, the best meaning is what is closer in worldly life compared with what is better in the afterlife because of its reward.
NAHHAS:v1p231#2/r6.anchor: وأجود من هذين القولين أن يكون المعنى والله أعلم أتستبدلون الذي هو أقرب إليكم في الدنيا

NAHHAS:v1p231#2/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p231#2/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p231#2/r7.claim: مصرا is best read as indefinite, matching the written alif; taking مصر as a proper name is possible but less apt because it is called a town, not a land or country.
NAHHAS:v1p231#2/r7.anchor: ( اهبطوا مصرا ) نكرة هذا أجود الوجوه لأنها في السواد بألف

NAHHAS:v1p231#2/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p231#2/r8.speaker: الكسائي
NAHHAS:v1p231#2/r8.claim: Al-Kisāʾī allows declension of مصر even as a definite name because it is light like هند; Nahhas rejects this under the rules of Khalil, Sibawayh, and Farraʾ.
NAHHAS:v1p231#2/r8.anchor: قال الكسائي يجوز أن تصرف مصر وهي معرفة لخفتها يريد أنها مثل هند

NAHHAS:v1p231#2/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p231#2/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p231#2/r9.claim: The argument is wrong: a woman named زيد would remain diptote under Khalil, Sibawayh, and Farraʾ; the claim that Arabs freely decline all diptotes is also rejected.
NAHHAS:v1p231#2/r9.anchor: وهذا خطأ على قول الخليل وسيبويه والفراء لأنك لو سميت امرأة بزيد لم تصرف

NAHHAS:v1p231#2/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p231#2/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p231#2/r10.claim: ما is accusative as the noun of فإن لكم ما سألتم; الذلة is the passive subject of ضربت, and المسكنة is coordinated with it.
NAHHAS:v1p231#2/r10.anchor: ( فإن لكم ما سألتم ) ما نصب بان ( وضربت عليهم الذلة ) اسم ما لم يسم فاعلة

NAHHAS:v1p231#2/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p231#2/r11.speaker: الأخفش
NAHHAS:v1p231#2/r11.claim: He interprets بما عصوا as ‘because of their disobedience’; كانوا يعتدون is coordinated with عصوا.
NAHHAS:v1p231#2/r11.anchor: ( ذلك بما عصوا ) قال الأخفش أي بعصيانهم ( وكانوا يعتدون ) عطف عليه

JISHUMI:v1p405/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p405/r1.speaker: نافع
JISHUMI:v1p405/r1.claim: Nāfiʿ reads nabiyīn and nabiyūn with hamza, restoring the original form; the other readers omit hamza, the lighter and more widespread reading.
JISHUMI:v1p405/r1.anchor: قرأ نافع: النبيئين والنبيئون بالهمز رده إلى الأصل، والباقون بغير همز، وهو الاختيار

JISHUMI:v1p405/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p405/r2.speaker: رسول الله
JISHUMI:v1p405/r2.claim: A report says a man addressed the Prophet with nabīʾ, with hamza, and he instructed him to say nabī without hamza.
JISHUMI:v1p405/r2.anchor: وروي أن رجلا قال: يا نبيء الله - بالهمز، فقال: لا تقل نبيء الله بالهمز، ولكن قل: نبي الله

JISHUMI:v1p405/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p405/r3.speaker: الكسائي
JISHUMI:v1p405/r3.claim: One etymology derives nabī from nabwa, an elevated place; al-Kisāʾī gives “path” as another derivation, since people are guided by a prophet.
JISHUMI:v1p405/r3.anchor: وقيل: إنه مأخوذ من النبوة، وهو الرفعة في المكان، يقال للمكان المرتفع: نبوة، وقيل: هو الطريق عن الكسائي

JISHUMI:v1p405/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p405/r4.speaker: قراءة العامة
JISHUMI:v1p405/r4.claim: The common reading has qiththā with kasra on qāf; Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb uses ḍamma, a Tamīm dialect.
JISHUMI:v1p405/r4.anchor: وقراءة العامة قثائها بكسر القاف وهي اللغة المشهورة، وعن يحيى بن وثاب بضم القاف، وهي لغة تميم

JISHUMI:v1p405/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p405/r5.speaker: قراءة العامة
JISHUMI:v1p405/r5.claim: The common tanwīn on miṣran means any city; al-Ḥasan omits tanwīn to mean Egypt specifically, and Ibn Masʿūd’s codex lacks alif and tanwīn.
JISHUMI:v1p405/r5.anchor: وقراءة العامة مصرا بالتنوين، والمراد مصر من الأمصار، وعن الحسن بغير تنوين، أراد مصر بعينه

JISHUMI:v1p405/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p405/r6.speaker: السلمي
JISHUMI:v1p405/r6.claim: The common reading has light yaqtulūn; al-Sulamī reads it with an intensified consonant.
JISHUMI:v1p405/r6.anchor: وقراءة العامة يقتلون بالتخفيف، وعن السلمي بالتشديد من التثقيل

JISHUMI:v1p405/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p405/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p405/r7.claim: Ṣabr is restraint of the self from what it desires, opposite to panic; the cited poem contrasts patience with panic.
JISHUMI:v1p405/r7.anchor: الصبر: أصله الحبس، ونقيضه الجزع، وهو حبس النفس عن الشيء

JISHUMI:v1p405/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p405/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p405/r8.claim: Ṭaʿām means food or nourishment; ṭaʿm with ḍamma means eating, ṭaʿm also means taste, and food can denote nourishing substance.
JISHUMI:v1p405/r8.anchor: والطعام: ما يتغذى به، والطعم بضم الطاء: الأكل، والطعم: عرض يدرك بحاسة الذوق

JISHUMI:v1p405/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p405/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p405/r9.claim: Wāḥid can mean one, the first number, or what cannot be divided; God is one through uniqueness in His praiseworthy attributes.
JISHUMI:v1p405/r9.anchor: والواحد: الفرد، والواحد: أول عدد الحساب، وحده ما لا يتجزأ، والله واحد لتفرده بصفاته الحسنى

JISHUMI:v1p405/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p405/r10.speaker: ابن السراج
JISHUMI:v1p405/r10.claim: Duʿāʾ may derive from calling out; its essential form is a request from someone lower to someone above, unlike a command, which reflects rank.
JISHUMI:v1p405/r10.anchor: الدعاء: قيل: أصله النداء عن ابن السراج، فكأن من يدعو ربه يناديه

JISHUMI:v1p407/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p407/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p407/r1.claim: They call it one food because their daily diet did not change; alternatively Arabic can use the singular for a pair and vice versa, as in the verse about pearls and coral.
JISHUMI:v1p407/r1.anchor: لما كان غذاؤهم في كل يوم لا يتغير قيل: طعام واحد، كما يقال: لمن داوم على الصوم والصلاة أمره أمر واحد

JISHUMI:v1p407/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p407/r2.speaker: الحسن
JISHUMI:v1p407/r2.claim: Though they valued manna and quail, their taste had been formed by onions and lentils, so they longed for familiar food.
JISHUMI:v1p407/r2.anchor: كانوا أهل بصل وعدس، قد ألفوه، فاشتاقت طباعهم إلى ما جرت به عاداتهم، فسألوا ذلك، عن الحسن

JISHUMI:v1p407/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p407/r3.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v1p407/r3.claim: Another explanation says they had grown tired of the wilderness and were too ashamed to state that plainly, so they hinted at it indirectly.
JISHUMI:v1p407/r3.anchor: وقيل: تبرموا بالمفاوز، واحتشموا أن يظهروا ذلك، فعرضوا بهذا القول

JISHUMI:v1p407/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p407/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p407/r4.claim: Baql means any plant without a stalk, and qiththā is a kind of cucumber.
JISHUMI:v1p407/r4.anchor: يخرج لنا مما تنبت الأرض من بقلها كل نبت لا ساق له وقثائها نوع من الخيار

JISHUMI:v1p407/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p407/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v1p407/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets fūm as bread.
JISHUMI:v1p407/r5.anchor: فومها قيل: هو الخبز، عن ابن عباس

JISHUMI:v1p407/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p407/r6.speaker: القتبي
JISHUMI:v1p407/r6.claim: Al-Qutaybī interprets fūm as all grains.

JISHUMI:v1p407/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p407/r7.speaker: الكلبي والنضر بن شميل
JISHUMI:v1p407/r7.claim: Al-Kalbī and al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl interpret fūm as garlic and explain the reading through interchange of fāʾ and thāʾ.
JISHUMI:v1p407/r7.anchor: وقيل: هو الثوم، عن الكلبي والنضر بن شميل، والثاء تبدل من الفاء

JISHUMI:v1p407/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p407/r8.speaker: الكسائي وأبو عبيدة
JISHUMI:v1p407/r8.claim: Al-Kisāʾī and Abū ʿUbayda cite the interchangeable forms jadath and jadaf; ʿAbd Allāh’s codex has thūm, “garlic.”
JISHUMI:v1p407/r8.anchor: وهو قول الكسائي وأبي عبيدة، وقيل: إنه في مصحف عبد الله، وثومها

JISHUMI:v1p407/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p407/r9.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وعطاء ومجاهد
JISHUMI:v1p407/r9.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Qatāda, ʿAṭāʾ, and Mujāhid interpret fūm as wheat; al-Mubarrad also prefers this meaning.
JISHUMI:v1p407/r9.anchor: قيل: هو الحنطة، عن الحسن وقتادة وعطاء ومجاهد، واختيار المبرد

JISHUMI:v1p407/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p407/r10.speaker: موسى
JISHUMI:v1p407/r10.claim: One report says Moses spoke the rebuke about exchanging the better food for the lower; another says God spoke it.
JISHUMI:v1p407/r10.anchor: قال يعني موسى، وقيل: الله قال لهم ذلك

JISHUMI:v1p407/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p407/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p407/r11.claim: One interpretation says they were leaving better food for worse; another says they rejected God’s choice for their own, making the rhetorical question a prohibition.
JISHUMI:v1p407/r11.anchor: قيل: أتتركون من الطعام ما هو خير، وتطلبون ما هو شر، وقيل: أتتركون ما اختار الله لكم

JISHUMI:v1p407/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p407/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p407/r12.claim: Other readings explain adnā as “closer” in ease of access, or say they exchanged inferior food for tastier food.
