JISHUMI:v1p407/r12.anchor: وقيل: هو من الدنو أي تتركون ما هو أقرب مأخذا، وتختارون ما هو أبعد، وقيل: بدلوا الأخبث بالألذ

JISHUMI:v1p407/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p407/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p407/r13.claim: Some say the request was not sinful because both foods were permitted; others say it was sinful because they resented God’s choice, which the author regards as stronger.
JISHUMI:v1p407/r13.anchor: قيل: لا؛ لأن الأول كان مباحا، فسألوا مباحا آخر، وقيل: كان معصية؛ لأنهم لم يرضوا بما اختاره الله لهم

JISHUMI:v1p407/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p407/r14.speaker: قتادة والسدي ومجاهد وأبو علي
JISHUMI:v1p407/r14.claim: Miṣran may mean any city; Abū ʿAlī argues it cannot mean Egypt because they were told to enter Jerusalem.
JISHUMI:v1p407/r14.anchor: قيل: مصرا من الأمصار، عن قتادة والسدي ومجاهد وأبي علي، قال أبو علي: لا يجوز أن يريد المصر المعروفة

JISHUMI:v1p407/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p407/r15.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v1p407/r15.claim: Abū Muslim says the command does not entail entry into Egypt.
JISHUMI:v1p407/r15.anchor: قال أبو مسلم: الأمر بذلك لا يقتضي دخول مصر

JISHUMI:v1p407/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p407/r16.speaker: الحسن وأبو العالية والربيع والأعمش
JISHUMI:v1p407/r16.claim: Another view identifies the destination as Pharaoh’s Egypt; another identifies it as Jerusalem, where they could obtain the plants they wanted.
JISHUMI:v1p407/r16.anchor: وقيل: يعني مصر فرعون، عن الحسن وأبي العالية والربيع والأعمش

JISHUMI:v1p407/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p407/r17.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p407/r17.claim: The promised provision is the plant food they had asked for; being struck with humiliation means being bound to disgrace, or being charged jizya, as in the tribute verse.
JISHUMI:v1p407/r17.anchor: قيل: ألزموا الذلة، وهو الذل والهوان، وقيل: الجزية، لقوله: (حتى يعطوا الجزية عن يد وهم صاغرون)

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p173#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p173#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p173#2/r1.claim: The people had been farmers; returning to their old habits made them weary of their blessing and desirous of misery.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p173#2/r1.anchor: كانوا فلاحة فنزعوا إلى عكرهم فاجموا ما كانوا فيه من النعمة وطلبت انفسهم الشقاء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p173#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p173#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p173#2/r2.claim: The single food means manna and quails, called one because they did not vary; even a varied daily menu could be called one food if unchanged.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p173#2/r2.anchor: أرادوا ما رزقوا في التيه من المن والسلوى فإن قلت هما طعامان فما لهم قالوا على طعام واحد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p173#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p173#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p173#2/r3.claim: Alternatively, the two foods were one kind because both belonged to luxurious eating, while the farming people wanted their familiar varied grains and vegetables.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p173#2/r3.anchor: ويجوز ان يريدوا انهما ضرب واحد لأنهما معا من طعام اهل التلذذ والتترف

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p173#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p173#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p173#2/r4.claim: The verb 'bring forth' means to make appear and produce.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p173#2/r4.anchor: يظهر لنا ويوجد والبقل ما أنبتته الأرض من الخضر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p173#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p173#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p173#2/r5.claim: The requested greens are choice vegetables eaten by people, such as mint, celery and leek.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p173#2/r5.anchor: والمراد به اطايب البقول التى يأكلها الناس كالنعناع والكرفس والكراث وأشباهها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p173#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p173#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p173#2/r6.claim: A variant reading vocalizes the word for cucumbers with a damma.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p173#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p173#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p173#2/r7.claim: Fūm means wheat, supported by the idiom 'bring us wheat' meaning bake bread.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p173#2/r7.anchor: والفوم الحنطة ومنه فوموا لنا أي اخبزوا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p173#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p173#2/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p173#2/r8.claim: Another view takes fūm to mean garlic; Ibn Masud's reading 'and its garlic' supports it and better pairs it with lentils and onions.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p173#2/r8.anchor: ويدل عليه قراءة إبن مسعود ( وثومها ) وهو للعدس والبصل اوفق

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p174/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p174/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p174/r1.claim: Adnā means lower in rank and smaller in value; nearness and distance can metaphorically indicate low and high worth.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p174/r1.anchor: الذي هو أقرب منزلة وأدون مقدارا والدنو والقرب يعبر بهما عن قلة المقدار

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p174/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p174/r2.speaker: زهير الفرقبي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p174/r2.claim: Zuhayr al-Farqabī reads adnaʾ with hamza, deriving it from meanness.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p174/r2.anchor: وقرأ زهير الفرقبي ( أدنأ ) بالهمزة من الدناءة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p174/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p174/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p174/r3.claim: The reading with a damma means descend to the place from the wilderness; h-b-ṭ can mean entering a valley or leaving it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p174/r3.anchor: وقرىء ( اهبطوا ) بالضم أي انحدروا اليه من التيه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p174/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p174/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p174/r4.claim: The wilderness extended from Jerusalem to Qinnasrin, twelve farsakhs by eight.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p174/r4.anchor: وبلاد التيه ما بين بيت المقدس إلى قنسرين وهي إثنا عشر فرسخا في ثمانية فراسخ

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p174/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p174/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p174/r5.claim: Miṣran may be the proper name of Egypt; it is declined despite properness and femininity because its middle consonant is quiescent, like Noah and Lot.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p174/r5.anchor: ويحتمل أن يريد العلم وإنما صرفه مع اجتماع السببين فيه وهما التعريف والتأنيث لسكون وسطه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p174/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p174/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p174/r6.claim: If it means the country, it has only one of the two causes of indeclinability; if it means any city, it is indefinite, while Abdullah's codex and al-Aʿmash read the city name without tanwin.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p174/r6.anchor: وإن أريد به البلد فما فيه الا سبب واحد وان يريد مصرا من الأمصار وفي مصحف عبد الله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p174#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p174#2/r1.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p174#2/r1.claim: One view identifies Egypt with Miṣrāyim, an Arabized form.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p174#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p174#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p174#2/r2.claim: Humiliation surrounds them like a tent, or sticks to them like plaster; Jews are lowly and destitute either in reality or by feigning poverty to avoid a higher poll tax.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p174#2/r2.anchor: جعلت الذلة محيطة بهم مشتملة عليهم فهم فيها كما يكون في القبة من ضربت عليه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p174#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p174#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p174#2/r3.claim: To incur God's wrath means to become deserving of it, like someone who merits being killed in retaliation for an equal victim.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p174#2/r3.anchor: من قولك باء فلان بفلان اذا كان حقيقا بان يقتل به لمساواته له

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p174#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p174#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p174#2/r4.claim: The demonstrative refers to humiliation, indigence and incurring wrath, caused by disbelief and killing prophets; the Jews killed Isaiah, Zechariah, John and others.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p174#2/r4.anchor: إشارة إلى ما تقدم من ضرب الذلة والمسكنة والخلاقة بالغضب أي ذلك بسبب كفرهم وقتلهم الأنبياء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p174#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p174#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p174#2/r5.claim: Although prophet-killing is inherently unjust, 'without right' means even by their own standards the prophets had committed no offense deserving death; they only advised them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p174#2/r5.anchor: معناه انهم قتلوهم بغير الحق عندهم لأنهم لم يقتلوا ولا أفسدوا في الأرض

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p174#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p174#2/r6.speaker: علي رضي الله عنه
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p174#2/r6.claim: Ali reads the verb with gemination, emphasizing repeated killing.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p174#2/r6.anchor: وقرأ علي رضي الله عنه ( ويقتلون ) بالتشديد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p175/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p175/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p175/r1.claim: The repeated demonstrative reiterates the previous reference.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p175/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p175/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p175/r2.claim: Their disobedience means committing many sins and transgressing God's limits in every matter, alongside disbelief and prophet-killing.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p175/r2.anchor: بسبب إرتكابهم أنواع المعاصي وإعتدائهم حدود الله في كل شيء مع كفرهم بآيات الله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p175/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p175/r3.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p175/r3.claim: Another view specifies their transgression as violating the Sabbath.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p175/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p175/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p175/r4.claim: The demonstrative may point back to disbelief and killing as the result of persistent disobedience and transgression, which hardened hearts until they dared deny signs and kill prophets.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p175/r4.anchor: ويجوز أن يشار بذلك إلى الكفر وقتل الأنبياء على معنى أن ذلك بسبب عصيانهم واعتدائهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p175/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p175/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p175/r5.claim: Alternatively, it may refer to the disbelief and killing together with their other disobedience.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p175/r5.anchor: أو ذلك الكفر والقتل مع ما عصوا

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p128#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p128#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p128#2/r1.claim: Fūm means wheat, according to Ibn Abbas, Qatada, and al-Suddi; Ibn Abbas cites Uhayha ibn al-Jallah's poem as evidence for the word.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p128#2/r1.anchor: وهو قول ابن عباس , وقتادة , والسدي , وأنشد ابن عباس من سأله عن الفوم , وأنه الحنطة قول أحيحة بن الجلاح

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p128#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p128#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p128#2/r2.claim: Mujahid, Ibn Zayd, and ʿAtaʾ say fūm means bread.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p128#2/r2.anchor: والثاني : أنه الخبز , وهو قول مجاهد , وابن زيد , وعطاء

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p128#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p128#2/r3.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p128#2/r3.claim: Al-Rabi ibn Anas and al-Kisaʾi take fūm as thūm, garlic, as explicitly reflected in Ibn Masud's reading with thāʾ.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p128#2/r3.anchor: والثالث : أنه الثوم بالثاء , وذلك صريح في قراءة ابن مسعود , وهو قول الربيع بن أنس والكسائي

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p128#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p128#2/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p128#2/r4.claim: Most reciters read miṣran with tanwīn; some read it without tanwīn, and Ibn Masud's reading omits the alif.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p128#2/r4.anchor: قرأ عامة القراء بالتنوين , وقرأ بعضهم بغير تنوين , وهي كذلك , وقراءة ابن مسعود بغير ألف

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p128#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p128#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p128#2/r5.claim: Qatada, al-Suddi, Mujahid, and Ibn Zayd say miṣran means any city, since the requested produce is available only in towns.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p128#2/r5.anchor: أحدهما : أنه أراد أي مصر , أرادوا من غير تعيين ؛ لأن ما سألوا من البقل والقثاء والفوم , لا يكون إلا في الأمصار

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p128#2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p128#2/r6.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p128#2/r6.claim: Al-Hasan, Abu al-ʿAliya, and al-Rabi say the verse means the specific Egypt from which the Israelites left, Pharaoh's Egypt.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p128#2/r6.anchor: والثاني : أنه أراد مصر فرعون , الذي خرجوا منه , وهذا قول الحسن , وأبي العالية والربيع

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p128#2/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p128#2/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p128#2/r7.claim: Some derive miṣr from cutting off, as the city is bounded off by its built-up area.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p128#2/r7.anchor: فمنهم من قال : إنه مشتق من القطع , لانقطاعه بالعمارة

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p128#2/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p128#2/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p128#2/r8.claim: Others derive miṣr from separating one thing from another.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p128#2/r8.anchor: ومنهم من قال : إنه مشتق من الفصل بينه وبين غيره

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p128#2/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p128#2/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p128#2/r9.claim: A line by ʿAdi ibn Zayd uses miṣran for what separates day and night, as lexical evidence.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p128#2/r9.anchor: قال عدي بن زيد : وجاعل الشمس مصرا لا خفاء به بين النهار وبين الليل قد فصلا

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p128#2/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p128#2/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p128#2/r10.claim: Al-dhilla can mean humiliation and abasement, or the imposition of jizya, the latter according to al-Hasan and Qatada.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p128#2/r10.anchor: وفي قوله تعالى : { وضربت عليهم الذلة } تأويلان : أحدهما : أنه من الذلة والصغار . والثاني : أنه فرض الجزية عليهم , وهذا قول الحسن وقتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p128#2/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p128#2/r11.speaker: أبي العالية
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p128#2/r11.claim: Maskana may mean need, according to Abu al-ʿAliya, or poverty, according to al-Suddi.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p128#2/r11.anchor: وفي ( المسكنة ) تأويلان : أحدهما : أنها الفاقة , وهو قول أبي العالية . والثاني : أنه الفقر , وهو قول السدي

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p128#2/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p128#2/r12.speaker: أبو العباس المبرد
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p128#2/r12.claim: Al-Mubarrad derives bāʾū from station or position: they came to occupy a station of God's wrath; a retaliation report says the killer becomes equivalent to the slain brother's killer.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p128#2/r12.anchor: أحدها : وهو قول أبي العباس المبرد : أن أصل ذلك : المنزلة , ومعناه أنهم نزلوا بمنزلة غضب الله

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p128#2/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p128#2/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p128#2/r13.claim: A report describes a man bringing his brother's killer to the Prophet, who says “he is equivalent to him,” meaning the killer takes the victim-killer's place.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p128#2/r13.anchor: وروي : أن رجلا جاء برجل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم , فقال : هذا قاتل أخي , قال ( فهو بواء به ) أي أنه مقتول

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p130/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p130/r1.speaker: أبو إسحاق الزجاج
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p130/r1.claim: Al-Zajjaj derives bāʾū from equality: they were made equal in wrath.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p130/r1.anchor: والثاني : وهو قول أبي إسحاق الزجاج : أن أصل ذلك التسوية , ومعناه : أنهم تساووا بغضب من الله

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p130/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p130/r2.speaker: عبادة بن الصامت
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p130/r2.claim: A report from ʿUbada ibn al-Samit says the Prophet distributed spoils among them on an equal basis, illustrating bawāʾ as equality.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p130/r2.anchor: ومنه ما يروى عن عبادة بن الصامت قال : ( جعل الله الأنفال إلى نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم , فقسمها بينهم على بواء ) , أي على سواء بينهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p130/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p130/r3.speaker: الكسائي
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p130/r3.claim: Al-Kisaʾi says bāʾū means they returned with God's wrath; return must be accompanied by something good or evil.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p130/r3.anchor: والثالث : وهو قول الكسائي , أن معناه أنهم رجعوا بغضب من الله , قال : البواء : الرجوع

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p130/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p130/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p130/r4.claim: One theological explanation is that God allowed unbelievers to kill some prophets so they could attain otherwise unreachable high ranks; this was not abandonment by God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p130/r4.anchor: أحدهما : أن الله عز وجل ؛ إنما جاز أن يخلي بين الكفار وقتل الأنبياء , لينالوا من رفيع المنازل ما لا ينالونه بغيره , وليس ذلك بخذلان لهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p130/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p130/r5.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p130/r5.claim: Al-Hasan says God never ordered a prophet to wage war and then let him be killed; He allowed unbelievers to kill prophets who had not been commanded to fight.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p130/r5.anchor: والثاني : وهو قول الحسن , أن الله عز وجل , ما أمر نبيا بالحر

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p130/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p130/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p130/r6.claim: Nabī has the plural form nabāʾ, used by Abbas ibn Mirdas in a verse praising the Prophet.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p130/r6.anchor: وقد جاء في جمع ( نبي ) : ( نباء ) , قال العباس ابن مرداس السلمي , يمدح النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p130/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p130/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p130/r7.claim: The common reading leaves nabī unhamzated; Nafiʿ alone reads al-anbiyāʾ and al-nabiyyīn with hamza.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p130/r7.anchor: وهو غير مهموز في قراءة الجمهور إلا نافعا , فإنه قرأ الأنبياء , والنبيئين بالهمز

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p130/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p130/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p130/r8.claim: One etymology derives nabī from nabaʾ, report, because a prophet reports from God; the source links this root to the verse about what was reported in Moses' scriptures.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p130/r8.anchor: أحدها : أنه مأخوذ من النبأ , وهو الخبر , لأنه ينبئ عن الله , أي يخبر

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p130/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p130/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p130/r9.claim: A second etymology takes nabī from “path”; the Prophet is called nabī because it is the way to him, supported by al-Qutami's line.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p130/r9.anchor: والثاني : أن أصل النبي هو الطريق , قال القطامي : لما وردنا نبيا واستتب لنا

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p130/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p130/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p130/r10.claim: A third etymology derives nabī from elevation because prophets hold a high rank.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p130/r10.anchor: والثالث : أنه مأخوذ من النبوة ؛ لأن منزلة الأنبياء رفيعة

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p130/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p130/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p130/r11.claim: Layla al-Akhyaliyya's verse uses bawāʾ for equivalence between slain parties, supporting the interpretation of bāʾū.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p130/r11.anchor: فإن يكن القتلى بواء فإنكم فتى ما قتلتم آل عوف بن عامر

MUJAHID:v1p77#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p77#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p77#2/r1.claim: The word fūm refers to bread.
MUJAHID:v1p77#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد قال الفوم الخبز

MUQATIL:2:60-61/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:60-61/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:60-61/r5.claim: When asked about clothing, God made the Israelites' garments grow with their children, remain on adults, and neither tear, wear out, nor become dirty; a pillar of light illuminated their journeys at night without moonlight.
MUQATIL:2:60-61/r5.anchor: فجعلت الثياب تطول مع أولادهم، وتبقى على كبارهم، ولا تمزق ولا تبلى ولا تدنس،

MUQATIL:2:60-61/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:60-61/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:60-61/r6.claim: After tiring of manna and quails, the Israelites asked Moses for earth's produce; “fūm” means garlic.

MUQATIL:2:60-61/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:60-61/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:60-61/r7.claim: Moses rebuked them for exchanging the inferior produce of the earth for the better manna and quails, and told them to go down to a city where they could obtain what they requested.
MUQATIL:2:60-61/r7.anchor: يقول: الذى هو دون المن والسلوى من نبات الأرض { بالذي هو خير } ،

MUQATIL:2:60-61/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:60-61/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:60-61/r8.claim: Humiliation imposed on the Jews means the jizya, and neediness means poverty; they incurred God's anger.
MUQATIL:2:60-61/r8.anchor: يعنى على اليهود الذلة، وهى الجزية، { والمسكنة } ، يعنى الفقر،

MUQATIL:2:60-61/r9.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:60-61/r9.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:60-61/r9.claim: The signs of God they disbelieved in mean the Qur'an; they killed prophets unjustly because they disobeyed and transgressed in their religion.
MUQATIL:2:60-61/r9.anchor: بأنهم كانوا يكفرون بآيات الله } ، يعنى القرآن، { ويقتلون النبيين بغير الحق

NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r1.claim: The one food was manna and quail; it was called one because it did not change, as a person may call a daily unchanging menu one food despite its variety.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r1.anchor: هو ما رزقوا في التيه من المن والسلوى

NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, they considered manna and quail one kind because both were refined foods, while they wanted the vegetables and grains familiar to an agricultural people.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r2.anchor: أو أرادوا أنهما ضرب واحد لأنهما معا من طعام أهل التلذد والتترف

NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r3.claim: They ask Moses to ask God to bring forth food; the verbs mean to ask and to manifest or produce.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r4.claim: The requested greens are the earth's vegetables, especially choice herbs such as mint, celery and leek.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r4.anchor: هو ما أنبتته الأرض من الخضر والمراد به أطايب البقول كالنعناع والكرفس والكراث

NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r6.claim: Fum means either wheat or garlic; Ibn Masud's reading has thum, garlic.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r7.claim: Adna means lower in rank and lesser in value, while what is better is higher and nobler.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r7.anchor: أقرب منزلة وأدون مقدارا والدنو والقرب يعبر بهما عن قلة المقدار

NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r8.claim: Misr may mean any city, to which they descend from the wilderness, located between Jerusalem and Qinnasrin; the wilderness is twelve by eight farsakhs.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r8.anchor: من الأمصار أى انحدروا إليه من التيه وبلاد التيه ما بين بيت المقدس

NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r9.claim: Alternatively, Misr means Pharaoh's Egypt; it is declined despite feminine and proper-name features because it means a town or has a quiescent middle consonant, like Noah and Lot.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r9.anchor: صرفه مع وجود السببين وهما التأنيث والتعريف لارادة البلد أو لسكون وسطه كنوح ولوط

NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r10.claim: The things they requested are available in cities, not in the wilderness.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r10.anchor: فإن الذى سألتم يكون فى الأمصار لا فى التيه

NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r11.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r11.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r11.claim: Humiliation and poverty surround and cling to them; Jews are subdued and poor either literally or by displaying poverty out of fear of an increased poll tax.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r11.anchor: أى الهوان والفقر يعنى جعلت الذلة محيطة بهم مشتملة عليهم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r12.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r12.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r12.claim: They may be poor in fact or display poverty and humility from fear that the jizya will be doubled.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r12.anchor: إما على الحقيقة و إما لتصاغرهم وتفاقرهم خيفة أن تضاعف عليهم الجزية

NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r13.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r13.speaker: حمزة وعلى
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r13.claim: Hamzah and al-Kisa'i have a distinct vocalization of the pronoun in عليهم; Abu Amr kasras both hā and mīm, while the other readers kasra the hā and damma the mīm.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r13.anchor: عليهم الذلة حمزة وعلى وكذا كل ما كان قبل الهاء ياء ساكنة وبكسر الهاء والميم أبو عمرو

NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r14.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r14.speaker: أبو عمرو
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r14.claim: Abu Amr reads the pronoun with kasra on both hā and mīm; the remaining readers kasra hā and damma mīm.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r14.anchor: وبكسر الهاء والميم أبو عمرو وبكسر الهاء وضم الميم غيرهم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r15.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r15.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r15.claim: To incur God's anger means to become deserving of it, by analogy with one who is liable to be killed in return for an equal victim.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r15.anchor: من قولك باء فلان بفلان إذا كان حقيقيا بأن يقتل به لمساواته له أى صاروا أحقاء بغضبه

NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r16.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r16.speaker: الكسائي
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r16.claim: Al-Kisa'i is reported to read the following word as حفوا.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r17.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r17.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r17.claim: The first that refers to the imposed humiliation, poverty and deserved anger.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r17.anchor: إشارة إلى ما تقدم من ضرب الذلة والمسكنة والخلاقة بالغضب

NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r18.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r18.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r18.claim: Their unbelief and killing of prophets caused their punishment; the prophets killed by the Jews included Isaiah, Zechariah and John.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r18.anchor: وقد قتلت اليهود شعياء وزكريا ويحيا صلوات الله عليهم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r19.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r19.speaker: نافع
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r19.claim: Nafi' pronounces the word for prophets with a hamza, as in its related forms.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r20.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r20.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r20.claim: Nabī may derive from informing, as one who tells from God, or from rising; nubuwwa is an elevated place.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r20.anchor: والنبي من النبأ لأنه يخبر عن الله تعالى فعيل بمعنى مفعل

NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r21.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r21.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r21.claim: Killing them without right means even by their own standard; the Torah did not warrant their killing, and the phrase is a circumstantial accusative describing wrongful killing.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r22.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r22.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r22.claim: The repeated that may refer to sins generally, or specifically to Sabbath transgression; alternatively unbelief and killing arose from persistent disobedience and excess that hardened their hearts.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p46#2/r22.anchor: وقيل هو اعتداؤهم في السبت ويجوز أن يشار بذلك إلى الكفر وقتل الأنبياء

NASAFI-FULL:v1p48/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p48/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p48/r1.claim: The final that may point to unbelief and killing prophets together with the other acts of disobedience.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p48/r1.anchor: أو ذلك الكفر والقتل مع ما عصوا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61/r1.claim: The request occurred during the wandering, after they tired of manna and quail and remembered their former life in Egypt.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61/r1.anchor: كان هذا القول منهم في التيه حين ملوا المن والسلوى، وتذكروا عيشهم الأول بمصر.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61/r2.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan says they were people accustomed to leeks, onions, and lentils, and their appetites returned to their bad old habits.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61/r2.anchor: قال الحسن: كانوا نتانى أهل كراث وأبصال وأعداس، فنزعوا إلى عكرهم عكر السوء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61/r3.claim: They called manna and quail one food though they were two because they ate one together with the other.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61/r3.anchor: وكنوا عن المن والسلوى بطعام واحد وهما اثنان لأنهم يأكلون أحدهما بالآخر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61/r4.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61/r4.claim: Another view says the two foods repeated daily, so they were called one regular fare, like a person constant in one practice.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61/r4.anchor: لتكرارهما في كل يوم غذاء كما تقول لمن يداوم على الصوم والصلاة والقراءة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61/r5.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61/r5.claim: Another interpretation is that they could not bear universal prosperity, which left no one needing help; the passage says they were the first to use slaves and servants.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61/r5.anchor: لن نصبر على الغنى فيكون جميعنا أغنياء فلا يقدر بعضنا على الاستعانة ببعض

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61/r6.claim: Ṭaʿām can mean anything eaten or drunk; Qur'anic 'taste' can include drinking wine, and honey as salwā would also be a drink.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61/r6.anchor: الطعام يطلق على ما يطعم ويشرب قال الله تعالى: ومن لم يطعمه فإنه مني

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61/r7.claim: Food can conventionally mean grain or dates specifically; Abū Saʿīd's report on zakāt al-fiṭr contrasts a measure of food with barley.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61/r7.anchor: صاعا من طعام أو صاعا من شعير

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61/r8.claim: In ordinary usage, a food market means the place where food is sold, not every place selling something edible or drinkable.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61/r8.anchor: والعرف جار بأن القائل: ذهبت إلى سوق الطعام، فليس يفهم منه إلا موضع بيعه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61/r9.claim: With fatḥah, ṭaʿm can mean what taste conveys or something desirable; with ḍammah it means food.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61/r9.anchor: والطعم بالفتح: هو ما يؤديه الذوق يقال: طعمه مر. والطعم أيضا: ما يشتهى منه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61/r10.speaker: أبو خراش
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61/r10.claim: Abū Khirāsh's poetry uses ṭaʿm first for food and then for its savor or desirability.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61/r10.anchor: قال أبو خراش: أرد شجاع البطن لو تعلمينه وأوثر غيري من عيالك بالطعم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61/r11.claim: The verb ṭaʿima means to eat or taste; it means 'taste' in 2:249 and 'eat' in 33:53.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61/r11.anchor: وقد طعم يطعم فهو طاعم إذا أكل وذاق ومنه قوله تعالى: «ومن لم يطعمه فإنه مني»

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r1.speaker: النبي محمد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r1.claim: The Prophet described Zamzam as nourishment for the hungry and a cure for illness.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r1.anchor: وقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في زمزم: «إنها طعام طعم وشفاء سقم»

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r2.claim: Asking someone to feed one a report means asking them to tell it; an imam's being asked to be fed means prompting him when he loses his recitation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r2.anchor: يقول: إذا استفتح فافتحوا عليه. وفلان ما يطعم النوم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r3.claim: An unnamed poet describes ostriches at Wajrah as tasting sleep only while fasting, illustrating the idiom.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r3.anchor: وقال الشاعر: نعاما بوجرة صفر الخدو د ما تطعم النوم إلا صياما

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r4.claim: Banū ʿĀmir pronounce fa-dʿu with kasrah on ʿayn at the consonant meeting, treating the defective verb like a sound verb.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r4.anchor: لغة بني عامر «فادع» بكسر العين لالتقاء الساكنين يجرون المعتل مجرى الصحيح

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r5.claim: Yukh'rij is jussive as though the command says, 'Ask Him and say: bring forth'; al-Zajjāj weakens the alternative that supplies a deleted lām.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r5.anchor: و «يخرج» مجزوم على معنى سله وقل له: أخرج، يخرج.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r6.speaker: الأخفش
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r6.claim: Al-Akhfash regards min in mimmā as extra, while Sībawayh treats it as non-extra because the clause is affirmative.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r6.anchor: و «من»، في قوله «مما» زائدة في قول الأخفش، وغير زائدة في قول سيبويه لأن الكلام موجب.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r7.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r7.claim: Al-Naḥḥās says al-Akhfash sought an object for yukh'rij by treating mā as that object.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r7.anchor: قال النحاس: وإنما دعا الأخفش إلى هذا لأنه لم يجد مفعولا ل «يخرج»

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r8.claim: Al-Qurṭubī prefers an omitted object inferred as edible food; the first min is partitive and the second specifies.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r8.anchor: والأولى أن يكون المفعول محذوفا دل عليه سائر الكلام

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r9.claim: Min bāqlihā is an appositive for mā with the preposition repeated; qiththāʾ and the remaining foods are coordinated with it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r9.anchor: بدل من «ما» بإعادة الحرف. { وقثآئها } عطف عليه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r10.claim: Baql is any plant without a stem, while a tree has one; qiththāʾ is cucumber, and Yaḥyā b. Waththāb and Ṭalḥah read its qāf with ḍamma, a less common variant.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r10.anchor: والبقل معروف، وهو كل نبات ليس له ساق. والشجر: ما له ساق.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r11.claim: Qithāʾ can form qithāʾī, is a wāw-root, and aqthaʾa can mean to feed people it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r11.anchor: إلا أن قثاء من ذوات الواو تقول: أقثأت القوم أي أطعمتهم ذلك.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r12.speaker: الجعدي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r12.claim: Al-Jaʿdī's poetry uses nafthāʾ for calming a boiling pot by adding water, illustrating the root's sense of calming.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r12.anchor: قال الجعدي: تفور علينا قدرهم فنديمها ونفثؤها عنا إذا حميها غلا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r13.claim: The f-th-ʾ root also means calming anger, tiring from running, or heat subsiding; the proverb says sour curdled milk calms anger.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r14.claim: Rathīʾah is milk curdled by milking it onto sour milk; irtathaʾa means the milk thickened.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r14.anchor: الرثيئة: اللبن المحلوب على الحامض ليخثر.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r15.speaker: عائشة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r15.claim: ʿĀʾishah says her mother succeeded in fattening her for introduction to the Prophet only after feeding her cucumber with fresh dates; al-Qurṭubī grades the chain sound.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r15.anchor: عن عائشة قالت: «كانت أمي تعالجني للسمنة، تريد أن تدخلني على رسول الله

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r16.speaker: جويبر عن الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r16.claim: Juwaybir reports from al-Ḍaḥḥāk that fūm means garlic because it pairs with onion; this view invokes interchange of fāʾ and thāʾ.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r16.anchor: فقيل: هو الثوم، لأنه المشاكل للبصل. رواه جويبر عن الضحاك.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r17.speaker: ابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r17.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reads thūmihā with thāʾ; the same reading is also related from Ibn ʿAbbās.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#2/r17.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود «ثومها» بالثاء المثلثة وروي ذلك عن ابن عباس.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#3/r1.speaker: أمية بن أبي الصلت
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#3/r1.claim: Umayyah b. Abī al-Ṣalt's line listing gardens and al-fūm supports interpreting fūm as garlic.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#3/r1.anchor: كانت منازلهم إذ ذاك ظاهرة فيها الفراديس والفومان والبصل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#3/r2.speaker: حسان
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#3/r2.claim: Ḥassān pairs fūm with onion as food, supporting the garlic view adopted by al-Kisāʾī and al-Naḍr b. Shumayl.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#3/r2.anchor: وقال حسان: وأنتم أناس لئام الأصول طعامكم الفوم والحوقل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#3/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#3/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and most exegetes identify fūm as wheat; al-Naḥḥās prefers this view because its support is stronger and its chains sound.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#3/r3.anchor: وقيل: الفوم الحنطة روي عن ابن عباس أيضا وأكثر المفسرين واختاره النحاس

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#3/r4.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#3/r4.claim: Al-Naḥḥās rejects the garlic view despite al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ: interchange cannot be extended by analogy and is uncommon in Arabic.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#3/r4.anchor: والإبدال لا يقاس عليه وليس ذلك بكثير في كلام العرب.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#3/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#3/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās answered a questioner who said fūm means wheat by citing a line of Uḥayḥah b. al-Jallāḥ about wheat cultivation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#3/r5.anchor: وأنشد ابن عباس لمن سأله عن الفوم وأنه الحنطة، قول أحيحة بن الجلاح

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#3/r6.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#3/r6.claim: Al-Zajjāj argues that the people would not request food without grain, the foundation of nourishment.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#3/r6.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق الزجاج: وكيف يطلب القوم طعاما لا بر فيه، والبر أصل الغذاء!

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#3/r7.speaker: الجوهري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#3/r7.claim: Al-Jawharī defines fūm as wheat and al-Akhfash cites a supporting wheat-cultivation poem.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#3/r7.anchor: وقال الجوهري أبو نصر: الفوم الحنطة. وأنشد الأخفش

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#3/r8.speaker: ابن دريد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#3/r8.claim: Ibn Durayd says fūmah means an ear of wheat and cites a line describing ears in a scout's hand.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#3/r8.anchor: وقال ابن دريد: الفومة السنبلة وأنشد

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#3/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#3/r9.claim: Other dialectal explanations make fūm chickpeas in Syrian speech; fāmī is an altered nisbah of fūmī, and fūmū lanā means bake for us.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#3/r9.anchor: وقال بعضهم: الفوم: الحمص لغة شامية. وبائعه فامي، مغير عن فومي

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#3/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#3/r10.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#3/r10.claim: Al-Farrāʾ calls fūmū lanā an old dialect for 'bake for us'; ʿAṭāʾ and Qatādah define fūm as any grain made into bread.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#3/r10.anchor: قال الفراء: هي لغة قديمة. وقال عطاء وقتادة: الفوم كل حب يختبز.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#3/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#3/r11.speaker: جمهور العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#3/r11.claim: Most scholars permit eating onions, garlic, and other foul-smelling greens because sound reports establish their permissibility.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#3/r11.anchor: فذهب جمهور العلماء إلى إباحة ذلك للأحاديث الثابتة في ذلك.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#3/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#3/r12.speaker: طائفة من أهل الظاهر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#3/r12.claim: Some literalists who hold congregational prayer obligatory prohibit these foods, arguing that deliberately doing what prevents an obligation is forbidden and the Prophet called them foul.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#3/r12.anchor: وذهبت طائفة من أهل الظاهر القائلين بوجوب الصلاة في الجماعة فرضا إلى المنع

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#3/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#3/r13.speaker: جابر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#3/r13.claim: Jābir reports that the Prophet told a companion to eat greens after finding them in a pot, explaining that he privately converses with one the companion does not; Muslim and Abū Dāwūd transmit it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#3/r13.anchor: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أتي ببدر فيه خضرات من بقول فوجد لها ريحا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#4/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#4/r1.claim: Al-Qurṭubī takes Jābir's report to show the restriction was particular to the Prophet, while others may eat these foods.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#4/r1.anchor: أخرجه مسلم وأبو داود. فهذا بين في الخصوص له والإباحة لغيره.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#4/r2.speaker: أبو أيوب
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#4/r2.claim: Abū Ayyūb served the Prophet food with garlic; asked whether it was forbidden, the Prophet said no, but that he disliked it. Muslim records the report.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#4/r2.anchor: فقال: أحرام هو؟ قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «لا ولكني أكرهه»

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#4/r3.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#4/r3.claim: Abū Saʿīd reports the Prophet saying at Khaybar that he does not prohibit what God made lawful but dislikes the smell of garlic.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#4/r3.anchor: أيها الناس إنه ليس لي تحريم ما أحل الله ولكنها شجرة أكره ريحها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#4/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#4/r4.claim: These reports suggest a personal restriction because the Prophet alone was singled out for conversation with the angel.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#4/r4.anchor: فهذه الأحاديث تشعر بأن الحكم خاص به، إذ هو المخصوص بمناجاة الملك.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#4/r5.speaker: جابر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#4/r5.claim: Jābir's report establishes the shared rule: anyone eating garlic, onion, or leek must not approach the mosque because angels are harmed by what harms people.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#4/r5.anchor: فلا يقربن مسجدنا فإن الملائكة تتأذى مما يتأذى منه بنو آدم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#4/r6.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#4/r6.claim: In a report transmitted by Muslim, ʿUmar says the Prophet removed people smelling of onion or garlic from the mosque to al-Baqīʿ and ordered eaters to cook them thoroughly.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#4/r6.anchor: إذا وجد ريحهما من الرجل في المسجد أمر به فأخرج إلى البقيع، فمن أكلهما فليمتهما طبخا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#5/r1.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#5/r1.claim: A report attributed to ʿAlī from the Prophet calls lentils blessed and sanctified, softening the heart and increasing tears, and says seventy prophets including Jesus blessed them.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#5/r1.anchor: عليكم بالعدس فإنه مبارك مقدس وإنه يرق القلب ويكثر الدمعة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#5/r2.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#5/r2.claim: ʿUmar b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz alternated bread with oil, meat, and lentils on successive days.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#5/r2.anchor: وكان عمر بن عبد العزيز يأكل يوما خبزا بزيت، ويوما بلحم، ويوما بعدس.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#5/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#5/r3.speaker: الحليمي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#5/r3.claim: Al-Ḥalīmī calls lentils and olive oil food of the righteous; their connection with Abraham's hospitality is itself a virtue, and lentils ease worship without stirring desire like meat.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#5/r3.anchor: قال الحليمي: والعدس والزيت طعام الصالحين ولو لم يكن له فضيلة إلا أنه ضيافة إبراهيم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#5/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#5/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#5/r4.claim: Wheat is the soundest identification of fūm, barley was close and fed Medina, and lentils were food in Abraham's town, linking the grains to the two prophets.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#5/r4.anchor: والحنطة من جملة الحبوب وهي الفوم على الصحيح، والشعير قريب منها وكان طعام أهل المدينة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#5/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#5/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#5/r5.claim: A report says the Prophet and his household never ate their fill of wheat bread for three consecutive days from his arrival in Medina until his death.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#5/r5.anchor: لم يشبع هو وأهله من خبز بر ثلاثة أيام متتابعة منذ قدم المدينة إلى أن توفاه الله

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#6/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#6/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#6/r1.claim: Istibdāl means putting one thing in place of another, as with badal.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#6/r1.anchor: الاستبدال: وضع الشيء موضع الآخر ومنه البدل، وقد تقدم.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#6/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#6/r2.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#6/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj derives adnā from d-n-w, closeness in value: a comparable garment is cheap.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#6/r2.anchor: مأخوذ عند الزجاج من الدنو أي القرب في القيمة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#6/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#6/r3.speaker: علي بن سليمان
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#6/r3.claim: ʿAlī b. Sulaymān derives adnā from the base dāniʾ, low or vile, with the hamzah softened.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#6/r3.anchor: هو مهموز من الدنيء البين الدناءة بمعنى الأخس، إلا أنه خفف همزته.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#6/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#6/r4.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#6/r4.claim: Another derivation takes adnā from dūn, inferior: its form began as adwan, underwent metathesis, and changed final wāw to alif.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#6/r4.anchor: هو مأخوذ من الدون أي الأحط فأصله أدون

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#6/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#6/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#6/r5.claim: A noncanonical reading is adnaʾ, with hamzah.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#6/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#6/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#6/r6.claim: The verse asks whether they exchange inferior herbs, cucumbers, grain, lentils, and onions for the better manna and quail.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#6/r6.anchor: ومعنى الآية: أتستبدلون البقل والقثاء والفوم والعدس والبصل الذي هو أدنى

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#6/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#6/r7.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#6/r7.claim: First, al-Zajjāj says manna and quail are better because the requested vegetables have little worth by comparison.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#6/r7.anchor: الأول: أن البقول لما كانت لا خطر لها بالنسبة إلى المن والسلوى كانا أفضل قاله الزجاج.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#6/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#6/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#6/r8.claim: Second, God's gift came with a command to eat it, so continuing in obedience and gratitude brought afterlife reward, unlike their request.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#6/r8.anchor: في استدامة أمر الله وشكر نعمته أجر وذخر في الآخرة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#6/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#6/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#6/r9.claim: Third, what God gave them was more delicious than what they requested.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#6/r9.anchor: لما كان ما من الله به عليهم أطيب وألذ من الذي سألوه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#6/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#6/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#6/r10.claim: Fourth, God's food came without effort, while their requested food required cultivation, agriculture, and toil.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#6/r10.anchor: والذي طلبوه لا يجيء إلا بالحرث والزراعة والتعب

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#6/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#6/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#6/r11.claim: Fifth, manna and quail were certainly lawful as gifts from God, whereas dealings in crops could involve usurpation and doubt.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#6/r11.anchor: لما كان ما ينزل عليهم لا مرية في حله وخلوصه لنزوله من عند الله

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#6/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#6/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#6/r12.claim: The verse permits eating wholesome, pleasurable foods; the Prophet liked sweets and honey and drank cool, fresh water.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#6/r12.anchor: في هذه الآية دليل على جواز أكل الطيبات والمطاعم المستلذات

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#6/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#6/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#6/r13.claim: The command to go down to a town was a challenge incapacitating them, as in the command to become stone or iron.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#6/r13.anchor: وهذا أمر معناه التعجيز كقوله تعالى: قل كونوا حجارة أو حديدا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#7/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#7/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#7/r1.claim: Their being commanded to descend while in the wandering was a punishment.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#7/r1.anchor: لأنهم كانوا في التيه وهذا عقوبة لهم.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#7/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#7/r2.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#7/r2.claim: An alternative report says they were given the food they asked for.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#7/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#7/r3.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#7/r3.claim: Mujāhid and others take tanwīn miṣran as an indefinite town among the towns.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#7/r3.anchor: قال مجاهد وغيره: فمن صرفها أراد مصرا من الأمصار غير معين.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#7/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#7/r4.speaker: عكرمة عن ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#7/r4.claim: ʿIkrimah transmits Ibn ʿAbbās's explanation: a town among these towns.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#7/r4.anchor: وروى عكرمة عن ابن عباس في قوله: «اهبطوا مصرا» قال: مصرا من هذه الأمصار.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#7/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#7/r5.speaker: طائفة ممن صرفها
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#7/r5.claim: Other grammarians who read the word with tanwīn still identify it as Egypt itself.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#7/r5.anchor: وقالت طائفة ممن صرفها أيضا: أراد مصر فرعون بعينها.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#7/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#7/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#7/r6.claim: The indefinite-town view cites the apparent order to enter a town and reports that they lived in Syria after the wandering; the Egypt view cites their inheritance of Pharaoh's lands.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#7/r6.anchor: استدل الأولون بما اقتضاه ظاهر القرآن من أمرهم دخول القرية

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#7/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#7/r7.speaker: الأخفش والكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#7/r7.claim: Al-Akhfash and al-Kisāʾī permit tanwīn because the name is light like Hind and Daʿd, citing a poem that uses both case forms.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#7/r7.anchor: قال الأخفش والكسائي: لخفتها وشبهها بهند ودعد وأنشد

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#7/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#7/r8.speaker: سيبويه والخليل والفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#7/r8.claim: Sībawayh, al-Khalīl, and al-Farrāʾ reject that declension, reasoning that Zayd would not take tanwīn as a woman's name.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#7/r8.anchor: وسيبويه والخليل والفراء لا يجيزون هذا لأنك لو سميت امرأة بزيد لم تصرف.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#7/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#7/r9.speaker: غير الأخفش
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#7/r9.claim: Another grammarian explains the tanwīn by saying the word means a place, making it declinable.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#7/r9.anchor: وقال غير الأخفش: أراد المكان فصرف.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#7/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#7/r10.speaker: الحسن وأبان بن تغلب وطلحة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#7/r10.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Abān b. Taghlib, and Ṭalḥah read Miṣr without tanwīn; the Ubayy codex and Ibn Masʿūd likewise identify Pharaoh's Egypt.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#7/r10.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وأبان بن تغلب وطلحة: «مصر» بترك الصرف.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#7/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#7/r11.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#7/r11.claim: Mālik told Ashhab that this is Egypt, his own town and Pharaoh's residence, as quoted by Ibn ʿAṭiyyah.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#7/r11.anchor: قال أشهب قال لي مالك: هي عندي مصر قريتك مسكن فرعون

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#7/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#7/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#7/r12.claim: Miṣr originally means boundary; miṣr al-dār is the house's limit, and Ibn Fāris says people of Hajar used the term for property boundaries.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#7/r12.anchor: والمصر أصله في اللغة الحد. ومصر الدار: حدودها.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#7/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#7/r13.speaker: عدي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#7/r13.claim: ʿAdī's line calls the sun a clear boundary dividing day from night, illustrating the root meaning.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#7/r13.anchor: قال عدي: وجاعل الشمس مصرا لا خفاء به بين النهار وبين الليل قد فصلا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r1.claim: Mā is the object governed by inna in 'you have what you asked for.'

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r2.speaker: ابن وثاب والنخعي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r2.claim: Ibn Waththāb and al-Nakhaʿī read saʾaltum with kasrah on sīn; saʾalta and salta are both used, and yatasāwalan shows the wāw root.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن وثاب والنخعي «سألتم» بكسر السين يقال: سألت وسلت بغير همز.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r3.claim: Ḍuribat ʿalayhim means humiliation and poverty were imposed and decreed, an image compared to pitching tents; the verb can mean a judge imposed a penalty.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r3.anchor: أي ألزموهما وقضي عليهم بهما مأخوذ من ضرب القباب

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r4.speaker: الفرزدق
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r4.claim: Al-Farazdaq's line to Jarīr uses ḍuribat for an affliction imposed and sealed by scripture.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r4.anchor: قال الفرزدق في جرير: ضربت عليك العنكبوت بنسجها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r5.claim: Al-Qurṭubī glosses dhillah as abasement and maskanah as poverty, claiming that even a rich Jew displays poverty's dress, submission, and humiliation.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r6.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Qatādah explain dhillah as the obligation of paying jizyah.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r6.anchor: وقيل: الذلة فرض الجزية عن الحسن وقتادة.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r7.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r7.claim: Al-Zajjāj takes maskanah as submissiveness, deriving it from stillness because poverty reduces movement.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r7.anchor: والمسكنة الخضوع، وهي مأخوذة من السكون أي قلل الفقر حركته قاله الزجاج.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r8.speaker: أبو عبيدة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r8.claim: Abū ʿUbaydah glosses dhillah as lowliness; maskanah is the verbal noun of miskīn.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r8.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: الذلة الصغار. والمسكنة مصدر المسكين.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r9.speaker: الضحاك بن مزاحم عن ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r9.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk transmits Ibn ʿAbbās's explanation of the people struck by humiliation and poverty as holders of tax-farming contracts.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r9.anchor: وروى الضحاك بن مزاحم عن ابن عباس: { وضربت عليهم الذلة والمسكنة }

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r10.claim: Bāʾū means they returned and remained bound to the consequence; the root means return, including the prayer acknowledging and binding oneself to God's blessing.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r10.anchor: { وبآءوا } أي انقلبوا ورجعوا أي لزمهم ذلك.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r11.claim: Bawāʾ can mean returning retribution for blood or equal status in a matter, as poetry also describes return with captives and spoils.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r11.anchor: والبواء: الرجوع بالقود. وهم في هذا الأمر بواء أي سواء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r12.claim: Al-Qurṭubī says the meaning of divine anger has already been treated in the Fātiḥah.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r12.anchor: وقد تقدم معنى الغضب في الفاتحة.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r13.claim: Dhālika explains the cause: they disbelieved in God's book and prophets' miracles, including those of Jesus, John, Zechariah, and Muhammad, and killed prophets.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r13.anchor: { بأنهم كانوا يكفرون } أي يكذبون { بآيات الله } أي بكتابه ومعجزات أنبيائه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r14.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r14.claim: Al-Ḥasan has a variant reading of yaqtulūn; another transmission from him matches the common reading.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r14.anchor: وروي عن الحسن «يقتلون» وعنه أيضا كالجماعة.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r15.speaker: نافع
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r15.claim: Nāfiʿ reads al-nabiyyīn with hamzah throughout the Qur'an except two verses in al-Aḥzāb, where he leaves it unlengthened and unhamzated; the other readers omit hamzah throughout.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#8/r15.anchor: وقرأ نافع «النبيئين» بالهمز حيث وقع في القرآن إلا في موضعين: في سورة الأحزاب:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#9/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#9/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#9/r1.claim: The two exceptions to Nāfiʿ's hamzated reading are 33:50 and 33:53, where he reads without lengthening or hamzah because two kasrah hamzahs meet; other readers omit hamzah everywhere.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#9/r1.anchor: إن وهبت نفسها للنبي إن أراد [الأحزاب: 50]. لا تدخلوا بيوت النبي إلا [الأحزاب: 53]

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#9/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#9/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#9/r2.claim: The hamzated form derives from anbaʾa, 'inform': nabīʾ is an active participle, plural anbiyāʾ, with nabāʾ also attested as a plural.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#9/r2.anchor: فأما من همز فهو عنده من أنبأ إذا أخبر واسم فاعله منبىء.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#9/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#9/r3.speaker: العباس بن مرداس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#9/r3.claim: Al-ʿAbbās b. Mirdās's praise of the Prophet as the seal of nabāʾ supports the hamzated form.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#9/r3.anchor: قال العباس بن مرداس السلمي يمدح النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: يا خاتم النبآء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#9/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#9/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#9/r4.claim: Those omitting hamzah either derive the word from the same root with a softened hamzah or from nabā yanbū, 'to rise'; nabwah is elevation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#9/r4.anchor: فمنهم من اشتق اشتقاق من همز، ثم سهل الهمز. ومنهم من قال: هو مشتق من نبا ينبو

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#9/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#9/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#9/r5.claim: Without hamzah, nabī can mean a path; a messenger is called nabī because people are guided by him as by a road.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#9/r5.anchor: والنبي بترك الهمز أيضا الطريق، فسمي الرسول نبيا لاهتداء الخلق به كالطريق

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#9/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#9/r6.speaker: شاعر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#9/r6.claim: An unnamed poet uses nabī for a path on the ground, supporting the unhamzated lexical sense.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#9/r6.anchor: قال الشاعر: لأصبح رتما دقاق الحصى مكان النبي من الكاثب

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#9/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#9/r7.speaker: أبو علي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#9/r7.claim: A report where the Prophet rejects nabīʾ with hamzah and accepts nabī without it has a weak chain, according to Abū ʿAlī; the Prophet's uncorrected hearing of a hamzated poem also weakens it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#9/r7.anchor: قال أبو علي: ضعف سند هذا الحديث ومما يقوي ضعفه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#9/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#9/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#9/r8.claim: 'Without right' magnifies the enormity of the killing; it does not imply any prophet could deserve execution, since none did an act requiring it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#9/r8.anchor: فكان هذا تعظيما للشنعة عليهم ومعلوم أنه لا يقتل نبي بحق، ولكن يقتل على الحق

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#9/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#9/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#9/r9.claim: God's allowing disbelievers to kill prophets honors them and raises their rank, as with believers slain in God's cause; it is not abandonment.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#9/r9.anchor: ذلك كرامة لهم وزيادة في منازلهم كمثل من يقتل في سبيل الله من المؤمنين

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#9/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#9/r10.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#9/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥasan say prophets not commanded to fight could be killed, while every prophet commanded to fight was victorious.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#9/r10.anchor: قال ابن عباس والحسن: لم يقتل نبي قط من الأنبياء إلا من لم يؤمر بقتال

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#9/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#9/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#9/r11.claim: The second dhālika points back to and reinforces the first; bi in bimā marks cause, and al-Akhfash glosses it as 'because of their disobedience.'
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#9/r11.anchor: «ذلك» رد على الأول وتأكيد للإشارة إليه. والباء في «بما» باء السبب.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#9/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#9/r12.speaker: الأخفش
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#9/r12.claim: Al-Akhfash interprets bimā as 'because of their disobedience'; disobedience opposes obedience, while transgression exceeds limits, especially in injustice and sins.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:61#9/r12.anchor: قال الأخفش: أي بعصيانهم. والعصيان: خلاف الطاعة.

SAMIN-DURR:2:61/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61/r1.claim: لن نصبر على طعام واحد is a subject–predicate clause, and the whole clause is an object of the verb of saying.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61/r1.anchor: ناصب ومنصوب، والجملة في محل نصب بالقول

SAMIN-DURR:2:61/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61/r2.claim: Although manna and quails are two foods, واحد can mean one unchanging, nonvarying kind.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61/r2.anchor: وإنما كانا طعامين وهما المن والسلوى؛ لأن المراد بالواحد ما لا يختلف ولا يتبدل

SAMIN-DURR:2:61/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61/r3.speaker: قيل
SAMIN-DURR:2:61/r3.claim: They may call the two items one because both are luxury foods, whereas they wanted their familiar varied crops.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61/r3.anchor: وقت واحد، وقيل: كنوا بذلك عن الغنى، فكأنهم

SAMIN-DURR:2:61/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61/r4.speaker: قيل
SAMIN-DURR:2:61/r4.claim: Another explanation is that they ate one food together with the other, or ate both at the same time.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61/r4.anchor: وقت واحد، وقيل: كنوا بذلك عن الغنى، فكأنهم

SAMIN-DURR:2:61/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61/r5.speaker: قيل
SAMIN-DURR:2:61/r5.claim: Calling it one food may allude to shared wealth: they did not want everyone to share one thing, since that would leave no one serving another; they were said to be the first to use servants and slaves.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61/r5.anchor: وقيل: كنوا بذلك عن الغنى، فكأنهم قالوا: لن نرضى أن نكون كلنا مشتركين في شيء واحد فلا يخدم بعضنا بعضا

SAMIN-DURR:2:61/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61/r6.claim: طعام can mean anything eaten or drunk, as in 2:249, but sometimes refers specifically to certain foods such as grain or dates; a charity hadith distinguishes a measure of food from barley.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61/r6.anchor:
والطعام: اسم لكل ما يطعم من مأكول ومشروب، ومنه
ومن لم يطعمه

SAMIN-DURR:2:61/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61/r7.claim: طعم with fatḥa can mean the verbal noun, something desired as food, or what taste perceives, as in sweet and bitter taste.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61/r7.anchor: والطعم بفتح الطاء المصدر أو ما يشتهى من الطعام أو ما يؤديه الذوق، تقول: طعمه حلو وطعمه مر

SAMIN-DURR:2:61/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61/r8.claim: طعم with ḍamma means the tasted food; Abu Khirash's poem uses الطعم first for the food itself and then for its desirability.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61/r8.anchor:
وبضمها الشيء المطعوم كالأكل والأكل، قال أبو خراش:
496 أرد شجاع البطن لو تعلمينه
وأوثر غيري من عيالك بالطعم

SAMIN-DURR:2:61/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61/r9.claim: طعم can also mean giving; the prophetic report إذا استطعمكم الإمام فأطعموه means prompt the imam when he asks for a cue.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61/r9.anchor:
وقد يعبر به عن الإعطاء، قال عليه السلام:
" إذا استطعمكم الإمام فأطعموه "
أي: إذا استفتح فافتحوا عليه

SAMIN-DURR:2:61/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61/r10.claim: The phrase ما يطعم النوم means does not sleep; a poem uses it for ostriches that sleep only standing.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61/r10.anchor:
وفلان ما يطعم النوم إلا قائما، قال:
497 نعاما بوجرة صفر

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#2/r1.claim: The standard imperative is ادع with ḍamma; Banu Amir use ادع with kasra.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#2/r1.anchor: اللغة الفصيحة " ادع " بضم العين من دعا يدعو، ولغة بني عامر: فادع بكسر العين

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#2/r2.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#2/r2.claim: Abu al-Baqa explains the kasra as resolving two adjacent sukuns while treating the weak verb like a sound verb; the author objects that normally the first, not second, of two sukuns is vowelled.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#2/r2.anchor: قال أبو البقاء: " لالتقاء الساكنين، يجرون المعتل مجرى الصحيح، ولا يراعون المحذوف

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#2/r3.claim: The dialect may instead reflect a verb pattern دعى يدعي like رمى يرمي.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#2/r3.anchor: فيجوز أن يكون [من لغتهم] دعى يدعي مثل رمى يرمي

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#2/r4.claim: دعاء here means asking, but can also mean naming or calling, as in the quoted poem دعتني أخاها.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#2/r4.anchor:
والدعاء هنا السؤال، ويكون بمعنى التسمية كقوله:
498 دعتني أخاها أم عمرو

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#2/r5.claim: لنا attaches to ادع, and its lām expresses purpose.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#2/r5.anchor:
و " لنا " متعلق به، واللام للعلة.
قوله " يخرج

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#2/r6.claim: يخرج is jussive as the response to the imperative.

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#2/r7.speaker: بعضهم
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#2/r7.claim: Some grammarians posit an omitted command lām, understanding ليخرج; al-Zajjaj weakens that analysis.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#2/r7.anchor: وقال بعضهم: " مجزوم بلام الأمر مقدرة، أي: ليخرج، وضعفه الزجاج

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#3/r1.speaker: سيبويه
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#3/r1.claim: Sibawayh supplies an omitted object for يخرج: مأكولا or شيئا from what the earth grows.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#3/r1.anchor: مفعول " يخرج " محذوف عند سيبويه تقديره: مأكولا [مما] أو شيئا مما تنبت الأرض

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#3/r2.claim: The preposition من may attach to the verb and mark the point of origin.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#3/r2.anchor: والجار يجوز أن يتعلق بالفعل قبله، وتكون " من " لابتداء الغاية

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#3/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#3/r3.claim: Alternatively, من may qualify the omitted object as something from what the earth grows, with من partitive.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#3/r3.anchor: وأن يكون صفة لذلك المفعول المحذوف، فيتعلق بمضمر أي: مأكولا كائنا مما تنبته الأرض

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#3/r4.speaker: الأخفش
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#3/r4.claim: Al-Akhfash treats من as an extra marker in the object, yielding يخرج ما تنبته الأرض; he does not require a special condition for its being extra.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#3/r4.anchor: ومذهب الأخفش أن " من " زائدة في المفعول، والتقدير: يخرج ما تنبته الأرض، لأنه لا يشترط في زيادتها شيئا

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#3/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#3/r5.claim: ما may be a relative noun or an indefinite noun with an adjective, with its resumptive omitted; it cannot be a verbal noun because the object produced is a concrete substance, not cultivation as an action, under either analysis.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#3/r5.anchor: يجوز أن تكون موصولة اسمية أو نكرة موصوفة والعائد محذوف، أي: من الذي تنبته

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r1.claim: من بقلها may be an appositive to ما with the preposition repeated, where من explains the kind.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r1.anchor: من بقلها } يجوز فيه وجهان: أحدهما: أن يكون بدلا من " ما " بإعادة العامل

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r2.claim: Alternatively it may be an accusative circumstantial phrase describing the omitted pronoun returning to ما; من remains explanatory.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r2.anchor: والثاني: أن يكون في محل نصب على الحال من الضمير المحذوف العائد على " ما

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r3.claim: بقل is all plant growth without a stem, and its plural is بقول.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r3.anchor: والبقل كل ما تنبته الأرض من النجم أي: مما لا ساق له، وجمعه: بقول

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r4.claim: قثاء is the familiar cucumber; its singular is قثاءة, following the قمح/قمحة pattern.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r4.anchor: والقثاء معروف، الواحد: قثاءة، فهو من باب قمح وقمحة

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r5.speaker: قرئ
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r5.claim: The usual pronunciation of قثاء has kasra on qāf, and another reading uses ḍamma.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r5.anchor: وفيها لغتان: المشهورة كسر القاف، وقرئ بضمها

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r6.claim: The hamza in قثاء is original, as in أقثأت الأرض when cucumbers become abundant; its pattern is فعال.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r6.anchor: والهمزة أصل بنفسها في قولهم: أقثأت الأرض أي: كثر قثاؤها ووزنها فعال

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r7.claim: قثاء may have the plural قثائي, like علباء and علابي.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r7.anchor: ويقال في جمعها قثائي مثل علباء وعلابي

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r8.speaker: بعضهم
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r8.claim: Some derive قثاء from a waw-root and cite أقثأت القوم and فثأت القدر; the author calls this a gross error because the expected forms would instead preserve the waw-derived pattern, with yāʾ substitution in the four-letter verb.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r8.anchor: قال بعضهم: " إلا أن قثاء من ذوات الواو، تقول: أقثأت القوم،: أي أطعمتهم ذلك، وفثأت القدر

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r9.claim: The author rejects that waw-root argument: it should produce أقثيت from أقثوت and فثوت القدر, and the poem should say نفثوها, not نفثؤها.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r9.anchor: وهم فاحش، لأنه لما جعلها من ذوات الواو كيف يستدل عليها بقولهم: " أقثأت القوم

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r10.claim: المقثأة and المقثؤة, with fatḥa or ḍamma on tāʾ, name a place where cucumbers grow.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r10.anchor: والمقثأة والمقثؤة بفتح التاء وضمها: موضع القثاء

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r11.claim: الفوم means garlic; fāʾ may irregularly replace thāʾ, as in جدف/جدث, عاثور/عافور, and معاثير/معافير.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r11.anchor: والفوم: الثوم، والفاء تبدل من الثاء، قالوا: جدف وجدث، وعاثور وعافور

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r12.claim: A second interpretation of الفوم is wheat, supported by a verse of poetry Ibn Abbas recited about farming فوم.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r12.anchor:
وقيل الحنطة، وأنشد ابن عباس:
500 قد كنت أغنى الناس شخصا واحدا
نزل المدينة عن زراعة فوم

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r13.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r13.speaker: أبو إسحاق الزجاج
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r13.claim: Al-Zajjaj says أدنى derives from دنو, nearness; it can be lower in value and baseness, or nearer to them in this world, while the better food brings afterlife benefit through patience.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r13.anchor: قول أبي إسحاق الزجاج أن أصله: أدنو من

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r14.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r14.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r14.claim: On the near-in-this-world interpretation, the superior food's benefit is obtained in the afterlife through patience.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r14.anchor: والثاني: أنه أقرب لكم لأنه في الدنيا بخلاف الذي هو خير، فإنه بالصبر عليه يحصل نفعه في الآخرة

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r15.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r15.speaker: علي بن سليمان الأخفش
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r15.claim: Al-Akhfash derives أدنى from أدنأ, the lowly or base thing, with hamza softened; the poem is cited as a witness.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#4/r15.anchor:
الحنطة، وأنشد ابن عباس:
500 قد كنت أغنى الناس

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#5/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#5/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#5/r1.claim: The poem fragment is cited with al-Akhfash's proposal that أدنى originated as أدنأ with hamza and underwent hamza easing.

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#5/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#5/r2.speaker: زهير الفرقبي
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#5/r2.claim: Zuhayr al-Firqabi reads أدنأ with hamza, supporting the derivation from دنأ and dناءة.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#5/r2.anchor: ويدل عليه قراءة زهير الفرقبي: " أدنأ " بالهمز

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#5/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#5/r3.speaker: قيل
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#5/r3.claim: A third etymology takes أدنى from أدون, the bad or inferior thing; the middle radical is moved after the final radical, producing أَدْنَو, then undergoes weak-letter change, on pattern أفلع.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#5/r3.anchor: خط المصحف، فقيل: إنهم أمروا بهبوط مصر من

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#5/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#5/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#5/r4.claim: أدنى is the predicate of هو, while هو خير is likewise a relative clause with a resumptive element.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#5/r4.anchor: وأدنى خبر عن " هو " والجملة صلة وعائد، وكذلك " هو خير " أيضا صلة وعائد

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#5/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#5/r5.speaker: قرأ الجمهور
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#5/r5.claim: The majority read مصر with nunation, matching the written muṣḥaf; one explanation is that they were sent to any Egyptian city, so the word is declinable.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#5/r5.anchor: مصرا " قرأه الجمهور منونا، وهو خط المصحف، فقيل

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#5/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#5/r6.speaker: قيل
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#5/r6.claim: They may instead have been sent to Egypt itself, which is declinable because its middle consonant is silent and the name is light like هند and دعد; a poem illustrates the forms, or the declension may reflect treating it as a place name.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#5/r6.anchor: وقيل: أمروا بمصر بعينه وإنما صرف لخفته، لسكون وسطه كهند ودعد، وأنشد

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#5/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#5/r7.speaker: الحسن وغيره
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#5/r7.claim: Al-Hasan and others read مصر without nunation; the same form occurs in some Uthman and Ubayy codices, as if a particular place were intended.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#5/r7.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وغيره: " مصر " وكذلك هي في بعض مصاحف عثمان ومصحف أبي، كأنهم عنوا مكانا بعينه

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#5/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#5/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#5/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the name is an Arabicized Persian form of مصرائيم; if it names a specific place, its foreignness means it should be indeclinable, like ماه and جور and حمص.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#5/r8.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: " إنه معرب من لسان العجم، فإن أصله مصرائيم، فعرب " ، وعلى هذا إذا قيل بأنه علم لمكان بعينه فلا

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#5/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#5/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#5/r9.claim: The majority unanimously prevent declension for مصر in يوسف 12:99.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#5/r9.anchor:
ولذلك أجمع الجمهور على منعه في قوله
ادخلوا مصر

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#5/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#5/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#5/r10.claim: In the basic language, المصر is the boundary between two things; people of Hajar used مصورها to mean a property's boundaries, and a poem calls the sun a boundary between day and night.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#5/r10.anchor: والمصر في أصل اللغة: " الحد الفاصل بين الشيئين " وحكي عن أهل هجر أنهم إذا كتبوا بيع دار قالوا: اشترى فلان

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#6/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#6/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#6/r1.claim: ما is an accusative noun of إن, whose predicate is لكم; it means that which, with its resumptive pronoun omitted: الذي سألتموه.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#6/r1.anchor: ما " في محل نصب اسما لإن، والخبر في الجار قبله

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#6/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#6/r2.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#6/r2.claim: Abu al-Baqa regards the indefinite-relative analysis as weak because the request refers to a specific thing, not an unspecified one.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#6/r2.anchor: قال أبو البقاء: " ويضعف أن يكون نكرة موصوفة " يعني أن الذي سألوه شيء معين

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#6/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#6/r3.speaker: قرئ
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#6/r3.claim: A reading سلتم, like بعتم, is derived from the long-alif verb سال.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#6/r3.anchor: وقرئ: " سلتم " مثل بعتم، وهي مأخوذة من سال بالألف

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#6/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#6/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#6/r4.claim: Hassan's poem سالت هذيل رسول الله witnesses the long-alif form; the origin of its alif is disputed as yāʾ, waw, or hamza, with details deferred to 70:1.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#6/r4.anchor:
قال حسان رضي الله عنه :
504 سالت هذيل رسول الله فاحشة
ضلت هذيل بما سالت ولم تصب

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#6/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#6/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#6/r5.claim: ضربت is passive, with الذلة as its نائب الفاعل.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#6/r5.anchor: مبني للمفعول، " الذلة " قائم مقام الفاعل

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#6/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#6/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#6/r6.claim: ضربت means imposed or decreed upon them, by analogy with erecting tents; al-Farazdaq's poem to Jarir uses ضربت عليك.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#6/r6.anchor:
ومعنى " ضربت " أي: ألزموها وقضي عليهم بها، من ضرب القباب، قال الفرزدق لجرير:
505 ضربت عليك العنكبوت

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#6/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#6/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#6/r7.claim: الذلة means humiliation; ذل with ḍamma is subjection imposed by coercion, while ذل with kasra follows resistance without coercion, as al-Raghib says.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#6/r7.anchor: والذلة: الصغار، والذل بالضم ما كان عن قهر، وبالكسر ما كان بعد شماس من غير قهر، قاله الرغب

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#6/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#6/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#6/r8.claim: مسكنة is on the pattern مفعلة from stillness, since poverty leaves a person with little movement; مسكين follows مفعيل.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#6/r8.anchor: والمسكنة: مفعلة من السكون، لأن المسكين قليل الحركة والنهوض، لما به من الفقر، والمسكين مفعيل منه

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#6/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#6/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#6/r9.claim: The mīm recurs in تمسكن and متمسكن, but this does not make it a root letter: derivation shows it is extra, as with تمندل and تمذرع.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#6/r9.anchor: قالوا: تمسكن يتمسكن فهو متمسكن، وذلك كما تثبت ميم تمندل وتمدرع من الندل والدرع

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#6/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#6/r10.speaker: الراغب
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#6/r10.claim: Al-Raghib says the mīm in مسكنة is extra in the stronger view; citing the dispute also suggests the nūn is extra and the root is مسك.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#6/r10.anchor: وقال الراغب: { وضربت عليهم الذلة والمسكنة } فالميم في ذلك زائدة في أصح القولين " وإيراد هذا الخلاف يؤذن بأن النون زائدة

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#6/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#6/r11.speaker: author
