SAMIN-DURR:2:61#6/r11.claim: The alif in باء is from wāw, as shown by باء يبوء and the pattern قال يقول; باء means to return, and the prophetic wording أبوء بنعمتك علي illustrates it.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#6/r11.anchor:
ألف " باء بكذا " منقلبة عن واو لقولهم: " باء يبوء " مثل: قال يقول:، قال عليه الصلاة والسلام
" أبوء بنعمتك علي

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#6/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#6/r12.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#6/r12.claim: A poem's آبوا is wrongly offered as evidence for باء: it belongs to آَبَ يَؤوب, with radicals hamza-waw-bāʾ, unlike باء يبوء; reversing the roots is unattested.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#6/r12.anchor: وهذا وهم، لأن هذا البيت من مادة آب يؤوب فمادته من همزة وواو وباء

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#7/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#7/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#7/r1.claim: البواء can mean return in retaliation, and people may be بواء, equal in a matter; the poem لا يبوء الدم بالدم means blood is not repaid with blood in retribution.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#7/r1.anchor:
والبواء: الرجوع بالقود، وهم في هذا الأمر بواء أي: سواء، قال:
507 ألا تنتهي عنا ملوك وتتقي
محارمنا لا

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#7/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#7/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#7/r2.claim: باء بكذا can also mean acknowledge or admit; the cited prophetic report means accepting the favor and binding oneself to it, and poetry uses بؤت بحقها.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#7/r2.anchor:
وباء بكذا أقر أيضا، ومنه الحديث المتقدم، أي أقر بها [وألزمها نفسي]، وقال:
508 أنكرت باطلها وبؤت بحقها

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#7/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#7/r3.speaker: الراغب
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#7/r3.claim: Al-Raghib says البواء originally means equal parts sharing one place, contrasted with النبوة, the parts' incompatibility.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#7/r3.anchor: وقال الراغب: " أصل البواء مساواة الأجزاء في المكان خلاف النبوة الذي هو منافاة الأجزاء

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#7/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#7/r4.speaker: الراغب
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#7/r4.claim: Al-Raghib explains باؤوا بغضب as settling in a place with wrath; باء signals that their fitting place carries God's anger, and he compares the ironic announcement in 3:21.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#7/r4.anchor:
بحقها
...................................
وقال الراغب: " أصل البواء مساواة الأجزاء في

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#7/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#7/r5.speaker: الراغب
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#7/r5.claim: Al-Raghib says interpreting بؤت بحقها as I admitted its right does not follow the word's lexical implication.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#7/r5.anchor:
بحقها
...................................
وقال الراغب: " أصل البواء مساواة الأجزاء في

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#7/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#7/r6.speaker: خلف الأحمر
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#7/r6.claim: Khalaf al-Ahmar says حياك الله وبياك originally was بوأك and changed for sound-pattern matching.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#7/r6.anchor: وقولهم: حياك الله وبياك " أصله: بوأك وإنما غير للمشاكلة، قاله خلف الأحمر

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#7/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#7/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#7/r7.claim: بغضب is a circumstantial phrase describing those who returned: they returned under wrath, not with wrath as a direct object.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#7/r7.anchor: بغضب " في موضع الحال من فاعل " باؤوا ": أي: رجعوا مغضوبا عليهم، وليس مفعولا به

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#7/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#7/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#7/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reads باء فلان بفلان as deserving to be killed in retaliation for him, hence becoming deserving God's wrath; this makes the bāʾ phrase unlike a circumstantial phrase.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#7/r8.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: " هو من قولك: باء فلان بفلان إذا كان حقيقا بأن يقتل به لمساواته له ومكافأته

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#7/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#7/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#7/r9.claim: من الله most naturally modifies غضب as an adjective, with an implied كائن; من marks metaphorical origin.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#7/r9.anchor: الظاهر أنه في محل جر صفة لغضب، فيتعلق بمحذوف أي: بغضب كائن من الله

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#7/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#7/r10.speaker: قيل
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#7/r10.claim: An alternative attaches من الله directly to the verb, understanding رجعوا من الله بغضب; the author considers this weak.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#7/r10.anchor: وقيل: هو متعلق بالفعل نفسه أي: رجعوا من الله بغضب، وليس بقوي

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#8/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#8/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#8/r1.claim: The demonstrative ذلك points back to the humiliation, poverty, and incurring of wrath; the clause بأنهم is its predicate and explains the cause of that fate.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#8/r1.anchor: مبتدأ أشير به إلى ما تقدم من ضرب الذلة والمسكنة والخلافة بالغضب. و " بأنهم " الخبر. والباء للسببية

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#8/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#8/r2.speaker: المهدوي
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#8/r2.claim: Al-Mahdawi takes the preposition باء as equivalent to لام, but the author says causal باء already expresses the reason without that substitution.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#8/r2.anchor: وقال المهدوي: " الباء بمعنى اللام أي: لأنهم " ولا حاجة إلى هذا

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#8/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#8/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#8/r3.claim: يكفرون is the accusative predicate of كان; كان and its clause predicate أن, while the أن-clause is governed by باء and that phrase predicates ذلك.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#8/r3.anchor: و " يكفرون " في محل نصب خبرا لكان، وكان وما في حيزها في محل رفع خبرا لأن

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#8/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#8/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#8/r4.claim: The phrase بآيات الله attaches to يكفرون, and its باء marks transitivity.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#8/r4.anchor: قوله " بآيات الله " متعلق بيكفرون، والباء للتعدية

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#8/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#8/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#8/r5.claim: ويقتلون is coordinated in the accusative with كان's predicate; one reading shifts to direct address, while gemination in يقتّلون marks repeated killing.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#8/r5.anchor: قوله " ويقتلون " في محل نصب عطفا على خبر كان، وقرئ: " تقتلون " بالخطاب

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#8/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#8/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#8/r6.claim: Most readers leave the hamza out of النبي and its derivatives; Nafi of Medina pronounces it throughout except two places in al-Ahzab, with Qalun reported to omit it in connected reading there.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#8/r6.anchor: والقراء على ترك الهمز في النبوة وما تصرف منها، ونافع المدني على الهمز في الجميع إلا موضعين: في سورة الأحزاب

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#8/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#8/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#8/r7.claim: With hamza, النبي derives from نَبَأ (news): it means one who informs about God or one informed by God; its plural نبآء supports this derivation, as in al-Abbas ibn Mirdas's verse.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#8/r7.anchor: فأما من همز فإنه جعله مشتقا من النبأ وهو الخبر، فالنبي فعيل بمعنى فاعل

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#8/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#8/r8.speaker: العباس ابن مرداس
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#8/r8.claim: Al-Abbas ibn Mirdas's line uses نبآء with the hamza visible, supporting derivation of النبي from نبأ.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#8/r8.anchor: واستدلوا على ذلك بجمعه على نبآء، كظريف وظرفاء، قال العباس ابن مرداس:

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#8/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#8/r9.speaker: أبو علي
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#8/r9.claim: Abu Ali cites Sibawayh calling the verified pronunciation of نبيا and برية poor, since the usual Arabic practice is to ease the hamza.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#8/r9.anchor: قال أبو علي: " قال سيبويه: " بلغنا أن قوما من أهل التحقيق يحققون نبيا وبرية، قال: وهو رديء

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#8/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#8/r10.speaker: أبو عبيد
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#8/r10.claim: Abu Ubayd says nearly all readers, ordinary speakers, and most Arabs omit the hamza, and relates a report in which the Prophet corrects a man who says يا نبيء الله.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#8/r10.anchor: وقال أبو عبيد: " الجمهور الأعظم من القراء والعوام على إسقاط الهمز من النبي والأنبياء، وكذلك أكثر العرب

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#8/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#8/r11.speaker: أبو عبيدة
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#8/r11.claim: Abu Ubayda says Arabs replace hamza in النبي، البرية، and الخابية; he adds الذرية from ذرأ, while Sibawayh's تنبأ مسيلمة shows that the hamza is original.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#8/r11.anchor: وقال لي أبو عبيدة: العرب تبدل الهمز في ثلاثة أحرف: النبي والبرية والخابية

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#8/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#8/r12.speaker: الحاكم
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#8/r12.claim: Al-Hakim grades the correction report authentic according to the conditions of the two Ṣaḥīḥ collections, though neither collection includes it.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#8/r12.anchor: ذكره الحاكم في المستدرك، وقال: هو صحيح على شرط الشيخين، ولم يخرجاه

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#8/r13.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#8/r13.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#8/r13.claim: Ibn Atiyya argues the report is weak because the Prophet did not object when al-Abbas recited يا خاتم النبآء, and the singular should not differ from the plural.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#8/r13.anchor: قال ابن عطية: " مما يقوي ضعفه أنه لما أنشده العباس: " يا خاتم النبآء " لم ينكره

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#8/r14.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#8/r14.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#8/r14.claim: The author will not reject Nafi's canonical reading on the basis of a speculative report; if the report is sound, يا نبيء الله may have been stopped because it suggested an expelled person, not because hamza itself was wrong.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#8/r14.anchor: وبهذا لا ينبغي أن ترد به قراءة هذا الإمام الكبير. أما الحديث فقد ضعفوه

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#9/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#9/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#9/r1.claim: The Prophet's ban on saying راعنا is analogous: the Jews could exploit that word as an insult in their language; alternatively, it encouraged choosing the most eloquent language.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#9/r1.anchor: ونظير ذلك نهيه للمؤمنين عن قولهم: " راعنا " ، لما وجدت اليهود بذلك طريقا إلى السب به في لغتهم

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#9/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#9/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#9/r2.claim: For readers without hamza, the preferred account is that they ease an underlying hamza, matching the hamzated reading and forms such as تنبأ مسيلمة.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#9/r2.anchor: وأما من لم يهمز فإنه يحتمل وجهين، أحدهما: أنه من المهموز ولكن خفف، وهذا أولى

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#9/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#9/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#9/r3.claim: A second derivation for the non-hamzated form takes it from نبا ينبو, to rise or appear; the Prophet's rank is elevated and his position manifest.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#9/r3.anchor: والثاني: أنه أصل آخر بنفسه مشتق من نبا ينبو إذا ظهر وارتفع

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#9/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#9/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#9/r4.claim: On the نبا derivation, النبي can be an active participle meaning elevated or a passive participle meaning God raised him above creation; its sound changes yield أنبياء.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#9/r4.anchor: فهو فعيل بمعنى فاعل أي: ظاهر مرتفع، أو بمعنى مفعول أي: رفعه الله على خلقه

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#9/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#9/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#9/r5.claim: A further etymology derives النبي from الطريق, since a prophet is God's path to creation through whom people learn their Creator; the first cited poem uses نبيا to mean a road.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#9/r5.anchor: أو يكون مأخوذا من النبي الذي هو الطريق، وذلك أن النبي طريق الله إلى خلقه

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#9/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#9/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#9/r6.claim: The second cited poetic use places a النبي at a mountain, while نبيئة is reported as a disparaging diminutive for Musaylima; أنبياء follows the regular plural pattern of weak فعيل nouns.

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#9/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#9/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#9/r7.claim: Qalun's omission of hamza in the two al-Ahzab positions follows his treatment of two adjacent hamzas: a preceding long vowel triggers substitution and assimilation, as in بالسوء إلا.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#9/r7.anchor: وأما قالون فإنما ترك الهمز في الموضعين المذكورين لمدرك آخر، وهو أنه من أصله في اجتماع الهمزتين

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#9/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#9/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#9/r8.claim: Qalun has no reported disagreement at these النبي positions; the hamza remains underlying and is omitted only in connected reading, returning at a pause.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#9/r8.anchor: ففي التحقيق لم يترك همز " النبي " بل همزه ولما همزه أداه قياس تخفيفه إلى ذلك

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#10/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#10/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#10/r1.claim: بغير الحق is either a circumstantial phrase describing the killers as acting wrongly, or an adjective to an omitted verbal noun meaning an unlawful killing.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#10/r1.anchor: في محل نصب على الحال من فاعل " يقتلون " تقديره: يقتلونهم مبطلين، ويجوز أن يكون نعتا لمصدر محذوف

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#10/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#10/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#10/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari asks why the verse adds بغير الحق when prophets could only be killed unlawfully; he answers that the killers themselves had no justifying case against them.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#10/r2.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " قتل الأنبياء لا يكون إلا بغير الحق، فما فائدة ذكره؟

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#10/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#10/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#10/r3.claim: Another explanation treats بغير الحق as a description of the killing's injustice to the prophets, intensifying the condemnation of the crime.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#10/r3.anchor: وقيل: إنما خرج وصفهم بذلك مخرج الصفة لقتلهم بأنه ظلم في حقهم لاحق

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#10/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#10/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#10/r4.claim: The repeated demonstrative ذلك either emphasizes the earlier reference or, with al-Zamakhshari, points specifically to disbelief and killing the prophets as caused by persistent disobedience and transgression.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#10/r4.anchor: وفي تكرير اسم الإشارة قولان، أحدهما: أنه مشار به إلى ما أشير بالأول إليه على سبيل التأكيد

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#10/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#10/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#10/r5.claim: ما is a verbal noun particle and باء is causal, so the clause means because of their disobedience; عصوا is a relative clause with no syntactic case.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#10/r5.anchor: و " ما " مصدرية والباء للسببية، أي بسبب عصيانهم، فلا محل ل " عصوا " لوقوعه صلة

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#10/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#10/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#10/r6.claim: عصوا derives from عصيوا: the ياء took fatḥa after a vowel change, then was deleted as the first of two quiescent letters, leaving the pattern فعوا.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#10/r6.anchor: وأصل عصوا عصيوا، تحركت الياء وانفتح ما قبلها، قلبت ألفا

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#10/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#10/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#10/r7.claim: كانوا يعتدون is an accusative predicate of كان, and that clause coordinates with the relative clause of ما.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#10/r7.anchor: " وكانوا يعتدون " في محل نصب خبرا ل " كان " ، وكان وما بعدها عطف على صلة " ما " المصدرية

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#10/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#10/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#10/r8.claim: عصيان originally denotes firmness, while اعتداء is تجاوز derived from عدا يعدو; the verse leaves both verbs' objects unstated to include every form of disobedience and transgression.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#10/r8.anchor: وأصل العصيان: الشدة، اعتصت النواة، اشتدت، والاعتداء على المجاوز من عدا يعدو

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#10/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#10/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#10/r9.claim: يعتدون originates as يعتديون and undergoes the same deletion and sound change as يتقون, yielding the pattern يفتعون.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#10/r9.anchor: وأصل " يعتدون " يعتديون، ففعل به ما فعل ب

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#10/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#10/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#10/r10.claim: The final و of عصوا assimilates into the following و because the preceding vowel is fatḥa, with no lengthened vowel to block assimilation; اهتدوا وإن تولوا illustrates the same pattern.
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#10/r10.anchor: والواو من " عصوا " واجبة الإدغام في الواو بعدها لانفتاح ما قبلها

SAMIN-DURR:2:61#11/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#11/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:61#11/r1.claim: When a damma before و creates a long vowel, that length blocks assimilation between identical following sounds, so the letters remain distinct, as in آمنوا وعملوا and الذي يوسوس.

RAZI-FULL:v3p91#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p91#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p91#2/r1.claim: The recognized reading has yukh'rij with yaḍamma and ra kasra, and tanbut with taḍamma and ta kasra.
RAZI-FULL:v3p91#2/r1.anchor: القراءة المعروفة يخرج لنا بضم الياء وكسر الراء

RAZI-FULL:v3p91#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p91#2/r2.speaker: زيد بن علي
RAZI-FULL:v3p91#2/r2.claim: Zayd b. ʿAlī reads yukh'rij with ya fatḥa and ra ḍamma, and tanbut with ta fatḥa and ba ḍamma.
RAZI-FULL:v3p91#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي بفتح الياء وضم الراء

RAZI-FULL:v3p91#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p91#2/r3.speaker: الظاهريون من المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v3p91#2/r3.claim: Most literalist commentators hold that the request for another kind of food was sinful, but Razi rejects this view.
RAZI-FULL:v3p91#2/r3.anchor: أكثر الظاهريين من المفسرين زعموا أن ذلك السؤال كان معصية

RAZI-FULL:v3p91#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p91#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p91#2/r4.claim: Razi argues that manna and quail had been permitted rather than commanded, so asking for another food was permissible, including asking through Moses because that seemed likelier to be answered.

RAZI-FULL:v3p92/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p92/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p92/r1.claim: They may have tired of eating one kind of food for forty years and wanted something different.
RAZI-FULL:v3p92/r1.anchor: لما تناولوا ذلك النوع الواحد أربعين سنة ملوه فاشتهوا غيره

RAZI-FULL:v3p92/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p92/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p92/r2.claim: People may prefer food familiar from their upbringing, even if inferior, to unfamiliar food that is more excellent.
RAZI-FULL:v3p92/r2.anchor: لعلهم في أصل الخلقة ما تعودوا ذلك النوع وإنما تعودوا سائر الأنواع

RAZI-FULL:v3p92/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p92/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p92/r3.claim: Their request may have been driven by weariness with the wilderness and a desire to reach settled lands, rather than by the foods themselves.
RAZI-FULL:v3p92/r3.anchor: ملوا من البقاء في التيه فسألوا هذه الأطعمة التي لا توجد إلا في البلاد

RAZI-FULL:v3p92/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p92/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p92/r4.claim: A monotonous diet can weaken appetite and digestion; variety can strengthen appetite and increase pleasure, making a change of food reasonable.
RAZI-FULL:v3p92/r4.anchor: المواظبة على الطعام الواحد سبب لنقصان الشهوة وضعف الهضم وقلة الرغبة والاستكثار من الأنواع

RAZI-FULL:v3p92/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p92/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p92/r5.claim: Nothing in the Quran says they were forbidden to request a different food, and the response granting what they asked for indicates the request was permissible; otherwise answering it would entail prophetic sin.
RAZI-FULL:v3p92/r5.anchor: ولو كانوا عاصين في ذلك السؤال لكانت الإجابة إليه معصية وهي غير جائزة على الأنبياء

RAZI-FULL:v3p92/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p92/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p92/r6.claim: An objection says God gave them an immediate worldly request after they rejected what He chose, as in 42:20; Razi answers that this departs from the apparent meaning.

RAZI-FULL:v3p92/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p92/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p92/r7.claim: An objection reads their inability to endure one food as proof they disliked the manna and quail, making the request sinful.
RAZI-FULL:v3p92/r7.anchor: كرهوا إنزال المن والسلوى وتلك الكراهة معصية

RAZI-FULL:v3p92/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p92/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p92/r8.claim: Razi replies that they expressed desire for another food, not dissatisfaction with what they had; the future negation in lan does not establish resentment toward the present food.
RAZI-FULL:v3p92/r8.anchor: دلالة على أنهم ما كانوا راضين به فقط

RAZI-FULL:v3p92/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p92/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p92/r9.claim: An objection takes Moses' question about replacing better with inferior food as an explicit condemnation proving the request sinful.

RAZI-FULL:v3p92/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p92/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p92/r10.claim: Razi says the rhetorical rebuke may concern losing a greater worldly benefit or a greater afterlife benefit, rather than sin in the request itself.
RAZI-FULL:v3p92/r10.anchor: استفهام على سبيل الإنكار ، وذلك يدل على كونه معصية

RAZI-FULL:v3p92/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p92/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p92/r11.claim: Razi concludes that the request was permissible, so the humiliation and divine anger were caused by the subsequent disbelief and killing of prophets, not by asking for other food.
RAZI-FULL:v3p92/r11.anchor: فثبت بما ذكرنا أن ذلك السؤال ما كان معصية بل كان سؤالا مباحا

RAZI-FULL:v3p93/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p93/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p93/r1.claim: One food means a single unchanging menu or manner of eating, not a single food species.
RAZI-FULL:v3p93/r1.anchor: ليس المراد أنه واحد في النوع بل أنه واحد في النهج

RAZI-FULL:v3p93/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p93/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p93/r2.claim: The usual reading has qithāʾihā with qaf kasra; al-Aʿmash and Talha read it with qaf ḍamma.
RAZI-FULL:v3p93/r2.anchor: قرأ الأعمش وطلحة وقثائها بضم القاف

RAZI-FULL:v3p93/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p93/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p93/r3.claim: The usual reading is fumihā with fa; a reading attributed to Ibn Masʿud and Ibn ʿAbbas has thumihā, which some consider more fitting beside onions.
RAZI-FULL:v3p93/r3.anchor: وعن علقمة عن ابن مسعود وثومها

RAZI-FULL:v3p93/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p93/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v3p93/r4.claim: One report from Ibn ʿAbbas interprets fum as wheat.

RAZI-FULL:v3p93/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p93/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v3p93/r5.claim: Another report from Ibn ʿAbbas interprets fum as bread; this is also transmitted from Mujahid, ʿAta, and Ibn Zayd, and Arabic usage includes fumū lanā meaning bake for us.
RAZI-FULL:v3p93/r5.anchor: وعنه أيضا أن الفوم هو الخبز

RAZI-FULL:v3p93/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p93/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v3p93/r6.claim: Another view, also transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbas and Mujahid, interprets fum as garlic; al-Kisaʾi selects this view.
RAZI-FULL:v3p93/r6.anchor: وقيل هو الثوم وهو مروي أيضا عن ابن عباس ومجاهد واختيار الكسائي

RAZI-FULL:v3p93/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p93/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p93/r7.claim: Supporters of the garlic interpretation cite the Ibn Masʿud reading thumihā, argue that wheat could not be inferior to manna and quail, and note garlic's fit with lentils and onions.
RAZI-FULL:v3p93/r7.anchor: أنه في حرف عبد الله بن مسعود وثومها

RAZI-FULL:v3p93/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p93/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p93/r8.claim: The usual reading is atastabdilūna; Ubayy b. Kaʿb's codex has atubaddilūna with bāʾ quiescent.
RAZI-FULL:v3p93/r8.anchor: وفي حرف أبي بن كعب : ( أتبدلون ) بإسكان الباء

RAZI-FULL:v3p93/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p93/r9.speaker: زهير الفرقبي
RAZI-FULL:v3p93/r9.claim: Zuhayr al-Farqabi reads adnaʾ with hamza, from the word for baseness.

RAZI-FULL:v3p93/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p93/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p93/r10.claim: Adnā does not mean inferior in religious benefit, since God granted the request; it refers to worldly benefit.
RAZI-FULL:v3p93/r10.anchor: والأول غير مراد لأن الذي كانوا عليه لو كان أنفع في باب الدين

RAZI-FULL:v3p93/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p93/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p93/r11.claim: The comparison does not rank the foods' taste universally, since a food delightful to one people may be inferior to another; it concerns the certainty and effortless availability of manna and quail versus the requested foods.
RAZI-FULL:v3p93/r11.anchor: الطعام الذي يكون ألذ الأطعمة عند قوم قد يكون أخسها عند آخرين

RAZI-FULL:v3p93/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p93/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p93/r12.claim: A counterargument says guaranteed food disliked by their tastes was harder to consume than desired food obtained with effort; Razi answers that certain present benefit still outweighs uncertain distant benefit.
RAZI-FULL:v3p93/r12.anchor: هب أنه وقع التعارض من هذه الجهة لكنه وقع الترجيح بما أن الحاضر المتيقن

RAZI-FULL:v3p93#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p93#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p93#2/r1.claim: The usual reading of ihbiṭū is with bāʾ kasra; another reading has bāʾ ḍamma.

RAZI-FULL:v3p93#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p93#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p93#2/r2.claim: The well-known reading gives Miṣran tanwin despite the two factors of definiteness and feminine gender because its middle consonant is quiescent, as with Nuh and Lut; if common noun, it has only one factor.
RAZI-FULL:v3p93#2/r2.anchor: بالتنوين وإنما صرفه مع اجتماع السببين فيه وهما التعريف والتأنيث

RAZI-FULL:v3p93#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p93#2/r3.speaker: عبد الله
RAZI-FULL:v3p93#2/r3.claim: The codex of ʿAbd Allah and al-Aʿmash's reading have Miṣr without tanwin.
RAZI-FULL:v3p93#2/r3.anchor: وفي مصحف عبد الله وقرأ به الأعمش

RAZI-FULL:v3p93#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p93#2/r4.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v3p93#2/r4.claim: Al-Hasan says the final alif in miṣran was added by a scribe, making the word definite and referring specifically to Pharaoh's Egypt; this is also transmitted from Abu al-ʿAliya and al-Rabiʿ.
RAZI-FULL:v3p93#2/r4.anchor: الألف في مصرا زيادة من الكاتب

RAZI-FULL:v3p93#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p93#2/r5.speaker: مفسرون
RAZI-FULL:v3p93#2/r5.claim: Among those accepting tanwin, some take Egypt to mean Pharaoh's country, while others understand it as any town where the requested foods could be found.
RAZI-FULL:v3p93#2/r5.anchor: المراد البلد الذي كان فيه فرعون

RAZI-FULL:v3p93#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p93#2/r6.speaker: كثير من المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v3p93#2/r6.claim: Many commentators deny that Miṣr means Pharaoh's Egypt, citing the command to enter the Holy Land, the grant of that land, the ban on turning back, and the forty-year exclusion before entry.
RAZI-FULL:v3p93#2/r6.anchor: أن يكون هو البلد الذي كانوا فيه مع فرعون

RAZI-FULL:v3p93#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p93#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p93#2/r7.claim: An objection says the command to enter the Holy Land may be recommendatory and therefore need not bar entry into Egypt; Razi invokes the principle that an imperative is presumptively obligatory.
RAZI-FULL:v3p93#2/r7.anchor: أمر والأمر للندب فلعلهم ندبوا إلى دخول الأرض المقدسة

RAZI-FULL:v3p94/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p94/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p94/r1.claim: Even if entering the Holy Land were only recommended, allowing the prophets to abandon a recommended duty would be improper.
RAZI-FULL:v3p94/r1.anchor: فهب أنه للندب ولكن الإذن في تركه يكون إذنا في ترك المندوب

RAZI-FULL:v3p94/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p94/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p94/r2.claim: A reply says do not turn back can mean do not disobey the command or deny the Holy Land's superiority, or the prohibition may apply only for a specified time; Razi finds that limitation contrary to the apparent sense.
RAZI-FULL:v3p94/r2.anchor: فلا نسلم أن معناه ولا ترجعوا إلى مصر بل فيه وجهان آخران

RAZI-FULL:v3p94/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p94/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p94/r3.claim: Razi says the context makes do not turn back refer to the immediately preceding order to enter the Holy Land, while restricting the prohibition to a particular time departs from its apparent meaning.
RAZI-FULL:v3p94/r3.anchor: تبادر إلى الفهم أن هذا النهي يرجع إلى ما تعلق به ذلك الأمر

RAZI-FULL:v3p94/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p94/r4.speaker: أبو مسلم الأصفهاني
RAZI-FULL:v3p94/r4.claim: Abu Muslim allows Pharaoh's Egypt: without tanwin, Miṣr must be a proper name and that is the only city with this name; with tanwin, it could remain a proper name or mean any city, allowing a choice among cities.
RAZI-FULL:v3p94/r4.anchor: أما أبو مسلم الأصفهاني فإنه جوز أن يكون المراد مصر فرعون

RAZI-FULL:v3p94/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p94/r5.speaker: أبو مسلم الأصفهاني
RAZI-FULL:v3p94/r5.claim: Abu Muslim argues that God bequeathed Egypt to the Israelites, so they could not be forbidden from entering it; he cites the report that God made them inherit it.
RAZI-FULL:v3p94/r5.anchor: أن الله تعالى ورث بني إسرائيل أرض مصر

RAZI-FULL:v3p94/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p94/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p94/r6.claim: An objection says owning a house does not always permit entry, as when a person observing mosque retreat owns a home; perhaps Israel's inheritance meant authority while the Holy Land command barred entry.
RAZI-FULL:v3p94/r6.anchor: الرجل قد يكون مالكا للدار وإن كان ممنوعا عن دخولها بوجه آخر

RAZI-FULL:v3p94/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p94/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p94/r7.claim: Abu Muslim's side answers that ownership normally entails unrestricted use, and barring entry contradicts that default without evidence.
RAZI-FULL:v3p94/r7.anchor: قلنا الأصل أن الملك مطلق للتصرف والمنع من التصرف خلاف الدليل

RAZI-FULL:v3p94/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p94/r8.speaker: الفريق الأول
RAZI-FULL:v3p94/r8.claim: The first group answers Abu Muslim that the standard reading is with tanwin and that the apparent general choice can be restricted to this specific city by their earlier evidence.
RAZI-FULL:v3p94/r8.anchor: نتمسك بالقراءة المشهورة وهي التي فيها التنوين

RAZI-FULL:v3p95/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p95/r1.speaker: الفريق الأول
RAZI-FULL:v3p95/r1.claim: The first group replies to Abu Muslim that property may be limited, as with pledged and leased property, so prior evidence overrides the default that ownership permits unrestricted use.
RAZI-FULL:v3p95/r1.anchor: أنا لا ننازع في أن الملك مطلق للتصرف ولكن

RAZI-FULL:v3p95/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p95/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p95/r2.claim: Humiliation was made to surround and adhere to them, like someone inside a tent or clay stuck to a wall; the more likely meaning is deserved humiliation.
RAZI-FULL:v3p95/r2.anchor: جعلت الذلة محيطة بهم حتى مشتملة عليهم فهم فيها كمن يكون في القبة المضروبة

RAZI-FULL:v3p95/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p95/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p95/r3.claim: The view that humiliation means specifically the jizya is unlikely because jizya was not imposed on them from the beginning.
RAZI-FULL:v3p95/r3.anchor: فقوله بعيد لأن الجزية ما كانت مضروبة عليهم من أول الأمر

RAZI-FULL:v3p95/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p95/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p95/r4.claim: Al-maskana means poverty, need, and intensified hardship; this kind of suffering can function as punishment.
RAZI-FULL:v3p95/r4.anchor: فالمراد به الفقر والفاقة وتشديد المحنة

RAZI-FULL:v3p95/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p95/r5.speaker: بعض العلماء
RAZI-FULL:v3p95/r5.claim: Some scholars regard the prediction of their humiliation and poverty as a miracle because the Prophet foretold it and it occurred, revealing unseen knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v3p95/r5.anchor: ومن العلماء من عد هذا من باب المعجزات لأنه عليه السلام أخبر عن ضرب الذلة والمسكنة عليهم

RAZI-FULL:v3p95/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p95/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p95/r6.claim: The word bāʾū can mean they returned, and it is only used with evil; al-Zajjaj gives another view that it means God's anger was made equal to them.
RAZI-FULL:v3p95/r6.anchor: أي رجعوا وانصرفوا بذلك ولا يقال باء إلا بشر

RAZI-FULL:v3p95/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p95/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p95/r7.claim: A third interpretation of bāʾū is that they deserved the anger, as in 5:29, where tabūʾ means to incur or deserve the two sins.

RAZI-FULL:v3p95/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p95/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p95/r8.claim: God's anger means His will to exact punishment.
RAZI-FULL:v3p95/r8.anchor: وأما غضب الله فهو إرادة الانتقام

RAZI-FULL:v3p95/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p95/r9.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v3p95/r9.claim: The Muʿtazilites argue that if God creates disbelief just as He creates humiliation and poverty, there is no reason to make one the recompense for the other rather than the reverse.
RAZI-FULL:v3p95/r9.anchor: لو كان الكفر حصل فيهم بخلق الله تعالى كما حصلت الذلة والمسكنة فيهم بخلقه

RAZI-FULL:v3p95/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p95/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p95/r10.claim: Razi answers the Muʿtazilite objection by counterarguing with knowledge and motive; he says the nature of disbelief was discussed earlier.
RAZI-FULL:v3p95/r10.anchor: وجوابه المعارضة بالعلم والداعي / وأما حقيقة الكفر

RAZI-FULL:v3p95#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p95#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p95#2/r1.claim: Their killing of prophets also makes them deserve the preceding punishment; disbelief in God's signs means ignorance and denial and does not itself include killing prophets.
RAZI-FULL:v3p95#2/r1.anchor: وذلك هو الجهل والجحد بآياته فلا يدخل تحته قتل الأنبياء

RAZI-FULL:v3p95#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p95#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p95#2/r2.claim: One answer to why the text says without right is that people may commit a wrong act believing it justified through a doubt, but these people knew their killing was wrong and did it anyway.
RAZI-FULL:v3p95#2/r2.anchor: أن الإتيان بالباطل قد يكون حقا لأن الآتي به اعتقده حقا لشبهة وقعت في قلبه

RAZI-FULL:v3p95#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p95#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p95#2/r3.claim: A second answer is emphatic repetition, as in 23:117, whose wording that an idol has no proof makes the added denial rhetorically emphatic.
RAZI-FULL:v3p95#2/r3.anchor: أن هذا التكرير لأجل التأكيد كقوله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v3p95#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p95#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p95#2/r4.claim: A third answer distinguishes God's just taking of life from people killing without right, forestalling the objection that God also kills.
RAZI-FULL:v3p95#2/r4.anchor: القتل الصادر من الله قتل بحق ومن غير الله قتل بغير حق

RAZI-FULL:v3p95#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p95#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p95#2/r5.claim: The definite phrase without the right refers to the recognized legal grounds for killing among Muslims, as in the Prophetic report listing three cases in which Muslim blood is lawful.
RAZI-FULL:v3p95#2/r5.anchor: لا يحل دم امرىء مسلم إلا بإحدى معان ثلاث

RAZI-FULL:v3p95#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p95#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p95#2/r6.claim: By contrast, the indefinite phrase without any right denies that there was any justification of any kind.
RAZI-FULL:v3p95#2/r6.anchor: وأما الحق المنكر فالمراد به تأكيد العموم أي لم يكن هناك حق

RAZI-FULL:v3p95#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p95#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p95#2/r7.claim: The phrase that was because they disobeyed restates the cause in different words, like a master listing a servant's past offenses with varied rebukes.
RAZI-FULL:v3p95#2/r7.anchor: فهو تأكيد بتكرير الشيء بغير اللفظ الأول وهو بمنزلة أن يقول الرجل لعبده

RAZI-FULL:v3p95#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p95#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p95#2/r8.claim: They transgressed means they acted unjustly, crossing from right into falsehood.
RAZI-FULL:v3p95#2/r8.anchor: المراد منه الظلم : أي تجاوزوا الحق إلى الباطل

RAZI-FULL:v3p95#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p95#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p95#2/r9.claim: The punishment's causes are ordered excellently: first offenses against God through ignorance and denial, then killing prophets, then personal sins, and finally sins against others through aggression.
RAZI-FULL:v3p95#2/r9.anchor: فبدأ أولا بما فعلوه في حق الله تعالى وهو جهلهم به وجحدهم لنعمه

STUDYQURAN:2:61/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:61/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:61/r1.claim: Numbers 11:4–5 parallels Israel's craving for foods remembered from Egypt, including cucumbers, onions, and garlic.
STUDYQURAN:2:61/r1.anchor: A Biblical parallel to this verse’s content is found in Numbers 11:4–5, where the Israelites crave meat and wish for the “fish . . . the cucumbers, the

STUDYQURAN:2:61/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:61/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:61/r2.claim: Numbers 11:31–35 says quails were given, but those who craved them were struck down for greed toward God's provision.
STUDYQURAN:2:61/r2.anchor: In Numbers 11:31–35, they are given quails, only to have those who craved them struck down for their greediness in relation to God’s provision.

STUDYQURAN:2:61/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:61/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:61/r3.claim: The word fūm, rendered garlic, may instead mean wheat.
STUDYQURAN:2:61/r3.anchor: Here garlic ( fūm ) may also mean “wheat.”

STUDYQURAN:2:61/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:61/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:61/r4.claim: Habaṭa, “go down,” need not describe a change in elevation; English similarly uses “descend” for arriving at a place or moving into or out of a valley.
STUDYQURAN:2:61/r4.anchor: need not be a change in elevation; analogously, in English one might say that one “descends” upon a place;

STUDYQURAN:2:61/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:61/r5.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:2:61/r5.claim: The better food refers to manna and quails, while the lesser food means the items the Israelites requested.
STUDYQURAN:2:61/r5.anchor: Better is usually understood here to refer to the manna and quails, while the lesser refers to the other foods they were requesting.

STUDYQURAN:2:61/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:61/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:61/r6.claim: Miṣr can mean a town or city; as a proper name or foreign word, it means Egypt.
STUDYQURAN:2:61/r6.anchor: A town renders miṣr, which can also mean a city, and used as a proper name or foreign word it means “Egypt.”

STUDYQURAN:2:61/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:61/r7.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:2:61/r7.claim: The orthography requires miṣran rather than miṣra and therefore excludes Egypt itself; some early commentators nevertheless understood it as Pharaoh's miṣr.
STUDYQURAN:2:61/r7.anchor: though some mention is made of early commentators understanding this to be the “miṣr of Pharaoh.”

STUDYQURAN:2:61/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:61/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:61/r8.claim: The killing of prophets recurs in Qurʾānic passages and has parallels in Luke, Matthew, Romans, 1 Thessalonians, and 1 Kings.
STUDYQURAN:2:61/r8.anchor: The killing of the prophets (2:61, 87, 91; 3:21, 112, 181; 4:155; 5:70) is also mentioned several times in the Bible (Luke 13:34; Matthew 23:37; Romans 11:3; 1 Thessalonians 2:14–15; 1 Kings 19:10).

TAB-FULL:v2p11#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p11#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p11#2/r1.claim: Al-Tabari recalls that patience means restraining and holding the self back, and interprets the Israelites as saying they could not endure one food.
TAB-FULL:v2p11#2/r1.anchor: قد دللنا فيما مضى قبل على معنى الصبر، وأنه كف النفس وحبسها عن الشيء.

TAB-FULL:v2p11#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p11#2/r2.speaker: بعض أهل التأويل
TAB-FULL:v2p11#2/r2.claim: Some commentators identify the single food God provided in the wilderness as quail.
TAB-FULL:v2p11#2/r2.anchor: وهو السلوى في قول بعض أهل التأويل

TAB-FULL:v2p11#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p11#2/r3.speaker: وهب بن منبه
TAB-FULL:v2p11#2/r3.claim: Wahb ibn Munabbih instead says the single food was fine bread with meat.
TAB-FULL:v2p11#2/r3.anchor: وفي قول وهب بن منبه هو الخبز النقي مع اللحم

TAB-FULL:v2p11#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p11#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v2p11#2/r4.claim: Qatada says a cloud shaded the Israelites in the wilderness when they received manna and quail.
TAB-FULL:v2p11#2/r4.anchor: عن قتادة: " قوله: {وإذ قلتم يا موسى لن نصبر على طعام واحد} [البقرة: 61] قال: كان القوم في البرية قد ظلل عليهم

TAB-FULL:v2p11#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p11#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v2p11#2/r5.claim: Qatada says they tired of their food and recalled the way of life they had before, which prompted their request for produce.
TAB-FULL:v2p11#2/r5.anchor: عن قتادة: " في قوله: {لن نصبر على طعام واحد} [البقرة: 61] قال: ملوا طعامهم، وذكروا عيشهم الذي كانوا فيه قبل ذلك

TAB-FULL:v2p11#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p11#2/r6.speaker: أبو العالية
TAB-FULL:v2p11#2/r6.claim: Abu al-Aliya says their food was quail and their drink manna, and they asked for the produce listed in the verse.
TAB-FULL:v2p11#2/r6.anchor: عن أبي العالية: " في قوله: {وإذ قلتم يا موسى لن نصبر على طعام واحد} [البقرة: 61] قال: كان طعامهم السلوى، وشرابهم المن

TAB-FULL:v2p11#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p11#2/r7.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v2p11#2/r7.claim: In another report, Qatada says that after reaching Syria they lacked their former foods and asked Moses for crops.
TAB-FULL:v2p11#2/r7.anchor: وقال قتادة: إنهم لما قدموا الشأم فقدوا أطعمتهم التي كانوا يأكلونها

TAB-FULL:v2p14/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p14/r1.speaker: ابن أبي نجيح
TAB-FULL:v2p14/r1.claim: Ibn Abi Najih says their one food was manna and quail, which they sought to replace with vegetables and the other listed crops.
TAB-FULL:v2p14/r1.anchor: سمعت ابن أبي نجيح: " في قوله عز وجل: {لن نصبر على طعام واحد} [البقرة: 61] المن والسلوى، فاستبدلوا به البقل

TAB-FULL:v2p14/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p14/r2.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v2p14/r2.claim: Al-Suddi says the Israelites had been given provisions in the wilderness but tired of them and asked for crops.
TAB-FULL:v2p14/r2.anchor: عن السدي: " أعطوا في التيه ما أعطوا، فملوا ذلك وقالوا: {يا موسى لن نصبر على طعام واحد

TAB-FULL:v2p14/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p14/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v2p14/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd says manna was honey sent from heaven and quail was their food; they knew no bread and asked for plants.
TAB-FULL:v2p14/r3.anchor: ابن زيد، قال: " كان طعام بني إسرائيل في التيه واحدا، وشرابهم واحدا، كان شرابهم عسلا ينزل لهم من السماء يقال له المن

TAB-FULL:v2p14/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p14/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p14/r4.claim: Al-Tabari reads min as partitive: the Israelites asked for some of what the earth produces, so the particle itself supplies the partitive sense.
TAB-FULL:v2p14/r4.anchor: لأن من تأتي بمعنى التبعيض لما بعدها، فاكتفي بها عن ذكر التبعيض

TAB-FULL:v2p14/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p14/r5.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v2p14/r5.claim: An alternative grammatical view takes min as redundant, yielding the sense of what the earth grows; its proponents cite Arabic usage and Qur'an 2:271.
TAB-FULL:v2p14/r5.anchor: وقد قال بعضهم: من ههنا بمعنى الإلغاء والإسقاط، كأن معنى الكلام عنده: يخرج لنا ما تنبت الأرض

TAB-FULL:v2p14/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p14/r6.speaker: جماعة من أهل العربية
TAB-FULL:v2p14/r6.claim: A group of Arabic grammarians denies that min can be redundant, arguing that it always signals that the speaker intends some of what follows.
TAB-FULL:v2p14/r6.anchor: وقد أنكر من أهل العربية جماعة أن تكون من بمعنى الإلغاء في شيء من الكلام

TAB-FULL:v2p14/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p14/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p14/r7.claim: Al-Tabari prefers the partitive reading: they asked for some of the earth's produce; he also says the listed plants, gourds, lentils, and onions were familiar crops and seeds.
TAB-FULL:v2p14/r7.anchor: فتأويل الكلام إذا على ما وصفنا من أمر من ذكرنا: فادع لنا ربك يخرج لنا بعض ما تنبت الأرض

TAB-FULL:v2p14/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p14/r8.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v2p14/r8.claim: Some commentators say fūm means wheat and bread.

TAB-FULL:v2p18/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p18/r1.speaker: عطاء ومجاهد
TAB-FULL:v2p18/r1.claim: ʿAṭāʾ and Mujahid interpret fūm as bread.
TAB-FULL:v2p18/r1.anchor: عن ابن جريج، عن عطاء، ومجاهد: " قوله: {وفومها} [البقرة: 61] قالا: خبزها "

TAB-FULL:v2p18/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p18/r2.speaker: قتادة والحسن
TAB-FULL:v2p18/r2.claim: Qatada and al-Hasan say fūm is the grain from which people make bread.
TAB-FULL:v2p18/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، والحسن: " الفوم: هو الحب الذي يختبزه الناس "

TAB-FULL:v2p18/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p18/r3.speaker: أبو مالك
TAB-FULL:v2p18/r3.claim: Abu Malik identifies fūm as wheat.
TAB-FULL:v2p18/r3.anchor: عن أبي مالك: " في قوله: {وفومها} [البقرة: 61] قال: الحنطة "

TAB-FULL:v2p18/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p18/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v2p18/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies fūm as bread.
TAB-FULL:v2p18/r5.anchor: قال لي ابن زيد: " الفوم: الخبز "

TAB-FULL:v2p18/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p18/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v2p18/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says fūm means wheat and bread.
TAB-FULL:v2p18/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس: " في قوله: {وفومها} [البقرة: 61] يقول: الحنطة والخبز "

TAB-FULL:v2p18/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p18/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v2p18/r7.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas through al-Dahhak identifies fūm specifically as wheat.
TAB-FULL:v2p18/r7.anchor: عن الضحاك، عن ابن عباس: " في قوله: {وفومها} [البقرة: 61] قال: هو البر بعينه الحنطة "

TAB-FULL:v2p18#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p18#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v2p18#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says fūm means wheat in the language of Banu Hashim.
TAB-FULL:v2p18#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس: " في قول الله عز وجل: {وفومها} [البقرة: 61] قال: الفوم: الحنطة بلسان بني هاشم "

TAB-FULL:v2p18#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p18#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v2p18#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas also identifies fūm as wheat and cites Aḥīḥa ibn al-Jallāḥ's poem mentioning fūm cultivation.
TAB-FULL:v2p18#2/r2.anchor: أن عبد الله بن عباس: سئل عن قول الله: {وفومها} [البقرة: 61] قال: " الحنطة أما سمعت قول أحيحة بن الجلاح

TAB-FULL:v2p18#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p18#2/r4.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v2p18#2/r4.claim: Al-Rabiʿ says fūm is garlic and notes that one reading has thūm in its place.
TAB-FULL:v2p18#2/r4.anchor: عن الربيع، قال: " الفوم: الثوم «وهو في بعض القراءات» وثومها "

TAB-FULL:v2p18#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p18#2/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p18#2/r5.claim: Al-Tabari says wheat and bread were called fūm in an older Arabic usage, quoting the expression fūmū lanā, meaning bake for us.
TAB-FULL:v2p18#2/r5.anchor: وقد ذكر أن تسمية الحنطة والخبز جميعا فوما من اللغة القديمة، حكي سماعا من أهل هذه اللغة: فوموا لنا، بمعنى اختبزوا لنا

TAB-FULL:v2p18#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p18#2/r6.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v2p18#2/r6.claim: Al-Tabari records Ibn Masʿud's reading thūmuhā, with thāʾ, instead of fūmuhā.
TAB-FULL:v2p18#2/r6.anchor: وذكر أن ذلك قراءة عبد الله بن مسعود «وثومها» بالثاء

TAB-FULL:v2p18#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p18#2/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p18#2/r7.claim: If the variant is authentic, al-Tabari explains the f/thāʾ difference as letter substitution caused by nearby articulation points, citing Arabic word pairs.
TAB-FULL:v2p18#2/r7.anchor: فإن كان ذلك صحيحا فإنه من الحروف المبدلة، كقولهم: وقعوا في عاثور شر وعافور شر

TAB-FULL:v2p18#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p18#2/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p18#2/r8.claim: Al-Tabari explains maghāfīr as a sweet substance resembling honey that descends from the sky and settles on trees.
TAB-FULL:v2p18#2/r8.anchor: والمغافير شبيه بالشيء الحلو يشبه بالعسل ينزل من السماء حلوا يقع على الشجر

TAB-FULL:v2p19/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p19/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p19/r1.claim: Al-Tabari defines substitution as leaving one thing for another and glosses adnā as lower, meaner, and less valuable.
TAB-FULL:v2p19/r1.anchor: الاستبدال: هو ترك شيء لآخر غيره مكان المتروك. ومعنى قوله: {أدنى} [البقرة: 61] أخس وأوضع وأصغر قدرا وخطرا

TAB-FULL:v2p19/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p19/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p19/r2.claim: Al-Tabari glosses adnā as lower, meaner, and less valuable, connecting it with d-n-ʾ words for low or base things.
TAB-FULL:v2p19/r2.anchor: أخس وأوضع وأصغر قدرا وخطرا، وأصله من قولهم: هذا رجل دني بين الدناءة

TAB-FULL:v2p19/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p19/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p19/r3.claim: Al-Tabari notes an Arabic form without hamza and a hamzated form in which people say dāniʾ for mean or vile.
TAB-FULL:v2p19/r3.anchor: وإنه ليدني في الأمور بغير همز إذا كان يتتبع خسيسها

TAB-FULL:v2p19/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p19/r4.speaker: الأعشى
TAB-FULL:v2p19/r4.claim: A line by al-Aʿshā uses hamzated dāniʾ, evidence for the hamzated Arabic form.
TAB-FULL:v2p19/r4.anchor: بيت الأعشى: [البحر السريع] باسلة الوقع سرابيلها … بيض إلى دانئها الظاهر

TAB-FULL:v2p19/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p19/r5.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v2p19/r5.claim: Some interpret adnā as nearer, deriving it from d-n-w, nearness.
TAB-FULL:v2p19/r5.anchor: وقد تأول بعضهم قوله: {الذي هو أدنى} [البقرة: 61] بمعنى الذي هو أقرب

TAB-FULL:v2p19/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p19/r6.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v2p19/r6.claim: Qatada glosses the requested food as worse than the food God had given them.
TAB-FULL:v2p19/r6.anchor: عن قتادة، قال: " {أتستبدلون الذي هو أدنى بالذي هو خير} [البقرة: 61] يقول: أتستبدلون الذي هو شر

TAB-FULL:v2p19/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p19/r7.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v2p19/r7.claim: Mujahid glosses adnā as more inferior or worse.
TAB-FULL:v2p19/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: " {الذي هو أدنى} [البقرة: 61] قال: أردأ "

TAB-FULL:v2p21/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p21/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p21/r1.claim: Al-Tabari supplies the omitted event: Moses prayed, God answered him, and gave the Israelites what they had asked for.
TAB-FULL:v2p21/r1.anchor: فدعا لهم موسى ربه أن يعطيهم ما سألوه، فاستجاب الله له دعاءه، فأعطاهم ما طلبوا

TAB-FULL:v2p21/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p21/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p21/r2.claim: Al-Tabari says the requested produce is found in settled towns and villages, so they must leave the wilderness for a place where it grows.
TAB-FULL:v2p21/r2.anchor: لأنكم في البدو، والذي طلبتم لا يكون في البوادي والفيافي، وإنما يكون في القرى والأمصار

TAB-FULL:v2p21/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p21/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p21/r3.claim: Most reciters pronounce miṣran with tanwīn; on this reading it means any town, since the requested crops are found in settled places rather than wilderness.
TAB-FULL:v2p21/r3.anchor: فقرأه عامة القراء: {مصرا} [البقرة: 61] بتنوين المصر وإجرائه

TAB-FULL:v2p21/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p21/r4.speaker: بعض من قرأ بالإجراء والتنوين
TAB-FULL:v2p21/r4.claim: Al-Tabari allows that a reader who adds tanwīn might still intend the proper name Egypt, following the written form of the codex.
TAB-FULL:v2p21/r4.anchor: بعض من قرأ ذلك بالإجراء والتنوين، كان تأويل الكلام عنده: اهبطوا مصرا البلدة التي تعرف بهذا الاسم

TAB-FULL:v2p21/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p21/r5.speaker: الذي لم ينون مصر
TAB-FULL:v2p21/r5.claim: The reading without tanwīn and the alif clearly means the specific, well-known Egypt.
TAB-FULL:v2p21/r5.anchor: وأما الذي لم ينون مصر فإنه لا شك أنه عنى مصر التي تعرف بهذا الاسم بعينها دون سائر البلدان غيرها

TAB-FULL:v2p23/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p23/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v2p23/r1.claim: Qatada takes miṣran to mean one of the cities or towns.
TAB-FULL:v2p23/r1.anchor: عن قتادة: " في قوله: {اهبطوا مصرا} [البقرة: 61] قال: يعني مصرا من الأمصار "

TAB-FULL:v2p23/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p23/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v2p23/r2.claim: Mujahid says it means a city, and reports that the Israelites did not return to Egypt.
TAB-FULL:v2p23/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد: " {اهبطوا مصرا} [البقرة: 61] قال: مصرا من الأمصار، زعموا أنهم لم يرجعوا إلى مصر "

TAB-FULL:v2p23/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p23/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v2p23/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd says the command means a town; he takes it to be the holy land God assigned to Israel, citing 5:21.
TAB-FULL:v2p23/r3.anchor: قال ابن زيد: " {اهبطوا مصرا} [البقرة: 61] قال: مصرا من الأمصار. ومصر لا تجري في الكلام، فقيل: أي مصر؟ فقال: الأرض المقدسة التي كتب الله

TAB-FULL:v2p23/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p23/r4.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v2p23/r4.claim: Other commentators say the command means the Egypt where Pharaoh lived.
TAB-FULL:v2p23/r4.anchor: وقال آخرون: هي مصر التي كان فيها فرعون

TAB-FULL:v2p24/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p24/r1.speaker: أبو العالية
TAB-FULL:v2p24/r1.claim: Abu al-Aliya identifies miṣran with Pharaoh's Egypt.
TAB-FULL:v2p24/r1.anchor: عن أبي العالية: " في قوله: {اهبطوا مصرا} [البقرة: 61] قال: يعني به مصر فرعون "

TAB-FULL:v2p24/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p24/r2.speaker: من قال إنها مصرا من الأمصار
TAB-FULL:v2p24/r2.claim: Proponents of the generic-city reading argue that the Israelites were settled in Syria after leaving Egypt; the holy land was assigned to them, and their descendants entered it under Joshua after the forty years of wandering, with no text saying they returned to Egypt.
TAB-FULL:v2p24/r2.anchor: ومن حجة من قال: إن الله جل ثناؤه إنما عنى بقوله: {اهبطوا مصرا} [البقرة: 61] مصرا من الأمصار دون مصر فرعون بعينها

TAB-FULL:v2p24/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p24/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p24/r3.claim: Al-Tabari answers that Israel's inheritance of Egypt's property made them its owners but did not mean they returned there; their homes were in Syria.
TAB-FULL:v2p24/r3.anchor: قيل لهم: فإن الله جل ثناؤه إنما أورثهم ذلك فملكهم إياها ولم يردهم إليها، وجعل مساكنهم الشأم.

TAB-FULL:v2p24/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p24/r4.speaker: من قال إنها مصر فرعون
TAB-FULL:v2p24/r4.claim: Those arguing for Pharaoh's Egypt cite the statement that Israel inherited Egypt's gardens and goods, reasoning that inheritance would be of no benefit unless some Israelites went there.
TAB-FULL:v2p24/r4.anchor: قالوا: فأخبر الله، جل ثناؤه أنه قد ورثهم ذلك وجعلها لهم، فلم يكونوا يرثونها ثم لا ينتفعون بها.

TAB-FULL:v2p24/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p24/r5.speaker: أبي بن كعب وعبد الله بن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v2p24/r5.claim: The pro-Egypt argument also cites Ubayy ibn Kaʿb's and Ibn Masʿud's reading without an alif, which they take to mean Egypt itself.
TAB-FULL:v2p24/r5.anchor: في قراءة أبي بن كعب وعبد الله بن مسعود: (اهبطوا مصر) بغير ألف

TAB-FULL:v2p24/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p24/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p24/r6.claim: Al-Tabari says neither the Qur'an nor a decisive prophetic report settles which interpretation is correct, and exegetes disagree.
TAB-FULL:v2p24/r6.anchor: والذي نقول به في ذلك أنه لا دلالة في كتاب الله على الصواب من هذين التأويلين، ولا خبر به عن الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم

TAB-FULL:v2p24/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p24/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p24/r7.claim: Al-Tabari concludes that God gave them a settled, cultivated place where they could obtain the crops they requested; it could have been Egypt or Syria.
TAB-FULL:v2p24/r7.anchor: فأولى الأقوال في ذلك عندنا بالصواب أن يقال: إن موسى سأل ربه أن يعطي قومه ما سألوه من نبات الأرض

TAB-FULL:v2p24/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p24/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p24/r8.claim: Al-Tabari accepts the reading with alif and tanwīn because it agrees with Muslim codices and the widespread recitation; he rejects the opposing reading as non-authoritative.
TAB-FULL:v2p24/r8.anchor: فأما القراءة فإنها بالألف والتنوين: {اهبطوا مصرا} [البقرة: 61] وهي القراءة التي لا يجوز عندي غيرها لاجتماع خطوط مصاحف المسلمين

TAB-FULL:v2p26/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p26/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p26/r1.claim: Ḍuribat means imposed and made binding, as when an authority imposes tribute, tax, or conscription.
TAB-FULL:v2p26/r1.anchor: قال أبو جعفر: يعني بقوله: {وضربت} [البقرة: 61] أي فرضت. ووضعت عليهم الذلة وألزموها

TAB-FULL:v2p26/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p26/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p26/r2.claim: Al-dhilla is abasement and humiliation, the state of subjection imposed on them.
TAB-FULL:v2p26/r2.anchor: وأما الذلة، فهي الفعلة من قول القائل: ذل فلان يذل ذلا وذلة. كالصغرة من صغر الأمر

TAB-FULL:v2p26/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p26/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p26/r3.claim: The abasement is linked to the rule that protection under continued unbelief is withheld unless the People of the Book pay jizya in submission.
TAB-FULL:v2p26/r3.anchor: حتى يعطوا الجزية عن يد وهم صاغرون} [التوبة: 29]

TAB-FULL:v2p26/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p26/r4.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
TAB-FULL:v2p26/r4.claim: They explain the imposed humiliation as paying the jizya while subdued.
TAB-FULL:v2p26/r4.anchor: عن الحسن، وقتادة: " في قوله: {وضربت عليهم الذلة} [البقرة: 61] قالا: يعطون الجزية عن يد

TAB-FULL:v2p26/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p26/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p26/r5.claim: Al-maskana is the verbal noun of miskīn; Arabic also uses forms such as tamaskana and tamaskunan.
TAB-FULL:v2p26/r5.anchor: وأما المسكنة، فإنها مصدر المسكين، يقال: ما فيهم أسكن من فلان وما كان مسكينا ولقد تمسكن مسكنة

TAB-FULL:v2p26/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p26/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p26/r6.claim: Here al-maskana means the humility and abasement that accompany want and poverty.
TAB-FULL:v2p26/r6.anchor: والمسكنة في هذا الموضع مسكنة الفاقة والحاجة، وهي خشوعها وذلها

TAB-FULL:v2p26/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p26/r7.speaker: أبو العالية
TAB-FULL:v2p26/r7.claim: Abu al-Aliya glosses al-maskana as need or destitution.
TAB-FULL:v2p26/r7.anchor: عن أبي العالية: " في قوله: {والمسكنة} [البقرة: 61] قال: الفاقة

TAB-FULL:v2p26/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p26/r8.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v2p26/r8.claim: Al-Suddi glosses the imposed maskana as poverty.
TAB-FULL:v2p26/r8.anchor: عن السدي: " قوله: {وضربت عليهم الذلة والمسكنة} [البقرة: 61] قال: الفقر

TAB-FULL:v2p26/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p26/r9.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v2p26/r9.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies the people punished here as the Israelite Jews, explicitly distinguishing them from Egypt’s Copts.
TAB-FULL:v2p26/r9.anchor: قال ابن زيد: " في قوله: {وضربت عليهم الذلة والمسكنة} [البقرة: 61] قال هؤلاء يهود بني إسرائيل

TAB-FULL:v2p26/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p26/r10.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v2p26/r10.claim: Ibn Zayd says God replaced their honor with humiliation, blessing with hardship, and favor with anger for disbelief, killing prophets, wrongful aggression, and disobedience.
TAB-FULL:v2p26/r10.anchor: فأخبرهم الله جل ثناؤه أنه يبدلهم بالعز ذلا، وبالنعمة بؤسا، وبالرضا عنهم غضبا

TAB-FULL:v2p28/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p28/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p28/r1.claim: Bāʾū means they turned back bearing something; the verb is joined to either good or evil, as in the verse about bearing another’s sin.
TAB-FULL:v2p28/r1.anchor: باء فلان بذنبه يبوء به بوءا وبواء. ومنه قول الله عز وجل {إني أريد أن تبوء بإثمي وإثمك} [المائدة: 29]

TAB-FULL:v2p28/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p28/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p28/r2.claim: They returned carrying God’s anger, which had settled on them and made them liable to His displeasure.
TAB-FULL:v2p28/r2.anchor: ورجعوا منصرفين متحملين غضب الله، قد صار عليهم من الله غضب، ووجب عليهم منه سخط

TAB-FULL:v2p28/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p28/r3.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v2p28/r3.claim: Al-Rabiʿ says that anger from God befell them.
TAB-FULL:v2p28/r3.anchor: عن أبيه، عن الربيع: " في قوله: {وباءوا بغضب من الله} فحدث عليهم غضب من الله

TAB-FULL:v2p28/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p28/r4.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v2p28/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak says they deserved God’s anger.
TAB-FULL:v2p28/r4.anchor: عن الضحاك: " في قوله: {وباءوا بغضب من الله} قال: استحقوا الغضب من الله

TAB-FULL:v2p28#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p28#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p28#2/r1.claim: The demonstrative dhālika gathers the multiple punishments just described: humiliation, poverty, and God’s anger.

TAB-FULL:v2p28#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p28#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p28#2/r2.claim: The phrase bima means ‘because of’: their punishment was for disbelief in God’s signs and killing prophets unjustly.
TAB-FULL:v2p28#2/r2.anchor: ويعني بقوله: {بأنهم كانوا يكفرون} [البقرة: 61] من أجل أنهم كانوا يكفرون

TAB-FULL:v2p28#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p28#2/r3.speaker: أعشى بني ثعلبة
TAB-FULL:v2p28#2/r3.claim: Al-Tabari cites al-Aʿsha’s use of بما as evidence that it expresses the cause or reason for an event.
TAB-FULL:v2p28#2/r3.anchor: قال أعشى بني ثعلبة: [البحر المتقارب] مليكية جاورت بالحجا … ز قوما عداة وأرضا شطيرا

TAB-FULL:v2p28#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p28#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p28#2/r4.claim: Kufr is covering or concealing; God’s signs are His proofs, evidences, and indications of His oneness and His messengers’ truthfulness.
TAB-FULL:v2p28#2/r4.anchor: معنى الكفر: تغطية الشيء وستره، وأن آيات الله: حججه وأعلامه وأدلته على توحيده وصدق رسله

TAB-FULL:v2p28#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p28#2/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p28#2/r5.claim: The charge means they denied God’s proofs of His oneness and the messengers’ truth, rejected their force, and called them lies.
TAB-FULL:v2p28#2/r5.anchor: يجحدون حجج الله على توحيده، وتصديق رسله ويدفعون حقيتها، ويكذبون بها

TAB-FULL:v2p28#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p28#2/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p28#2/r6.claim: The prophets are God’s messengers, sent to convey what He commissioned them to tell their audiences.
TAB-FULL:v2p28#2/r6.anchor: ويعني بقوله: {ويقتلون النبيين بغير الحق} [البقرة: 61] ويقتلون رسل الله الذين ابتعثهم لإنباء ما أرسلهم به عنه

TAB-FULL:v2p28#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p28#2/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p28#2/r7.claim: Nabī is originally hamzated from anbaʾa, ‘to inform’; the form munbiʾ shifted to nabī by changing hamza to yāʾ, like samīʿ and baṣīr from their corresponding forms.
TAB-FULL:v2p28#2/r7.anchor: وأصله الهمز، لأنه من أنبأ عن الله، فهو ينبئ عنه إنباء، وإنما الاسم منه منبئ ولكنه صرف وهو مفعل إلى فعيل

TAB-FULL:v2p31/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p31/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p31/r1.claim: Al-Tabari cites Abbas ibn Mirdas’s line, whose form khatim al-naba supports a hamzated singular nabi.
TAB-FULL:v2p31/r1.anchor: يا خاتم النبآء إنك مرسل … بالخير كل هدى السبيل هداكا

TAB-FULL:v2p31/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p31/r2.speaker: some scholars
TAB-FULL:v2p31/r2.claim: Some derive nabī and nubuwwa without hamza from nabwa, an elevated place, and say the original sense is a visible, raised road; they report not hearing the word hamzated.
TAB-FULL:v2p31/r2.anchor: وقد قال بعضهم: النبي والنبوة غير مهموز. لأنهما مأخوذان من النبوة، وهي مثل النجوة، وهو المكان المرتفع

TAB-FULL:v2p31/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p31/r3.speaker: القطامي
TAB-FULL:v2p31/r3.claim: Al-Qutami’s line uses nabiyan for a road, cited by the unhamzated etymology as evidence that nabī means a manifest road.
TAB-FULL:v2p31/r3.anchor: ويستشهد على ذلك ببيت القطامي: [البحر البسيط] لما وردن نبيا واستتب بها

TAB-FULL:v2p31/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p31/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p31/r4.claim: Killing prophets without right means killing God’s messengers without His authorization, while denying their missions and prophethood.
TAB-FULL:v2p31/r4.anchor: أنهم كانوا يقتلون رسل الله بغير إذن الله لهم بقتلهم منكرين رسالتهم جاحدين نبوتهم

TAB-FULL:v2p32/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p32/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p32/r1.claim: Tabari explains that the punishment came because of their disobedience, unbelief, and transgression.
TAB-FULL:v2p32/r1.anchor: ثناؤه: {ذلك بما عصوا} [البقرة: 61] والمعنى: ذلك بعصيانهم وكفرهم معتدين.

TAB-FULL:v2p32/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p32/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p32/r2.claim: Transgression is crossing a boundary God set for His servants and passing beyond it.
TAB-FULL:v2p32/r2.anchor: والاعتداء: تجاوز الحد الذي حده الله لعباده إلى غيره، وكل متجاوز حد شيء إلى غيره فقد تعداه

TAB-FULL:v2p32/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p32/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p32/r3.claim: The punishment followed their disobedience to God’s command and crossing the limits into what He prohibited.
TAB-FULL:v2p32/r3.anchor: فعلت بهم ما فعلت من ذلك بما عصوا أمري، وتجاوزوا حدي إلى ما نهيتهم عنه

ZAJJAJ:v1p141#2/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p141#2/r3.speaker: بعض النحويين
ZAJJAJ:v1p141#2/r3.claim: Some grammarians supply an implied request: ask God and say, “Bring it out for us,” and then He brings it out for them.
ZAJJAJ:v1p141#2/r3.anchor: قال بعض النحويين المعنى سله وقل له أخرج لنا يخرج لنا هو

ZAJJAJ:v1p141#2/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p141#2/r4.speaker: قوم
ZAJJAJ:v1p141#2/r4.claim: Others treat “yukhriǧ lanā” as a supplication, equivalent to the direct request “Bring it out for us.”
ZAJJAJ:v1p141#2/r4.anchor: وقال قوم: معنى (يخرج لنا) معنى الدعاء كأنه قال: أخرج لنا.

ZAJJAJ:v1p141#2/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p141#2/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p141#2/r5.claim: He prefers construing the following verb as the response to an imperative, as with “tell My servants to establish prayer”; Qur’anic imperatives without a jussive particle are otherwise indicative.
ZAJJAJ:v1p141#2/r5.anchor: وكلا القولين مذهب، ولكنه على الجواب أجود لأن ما في القرآن من لفظ الأمر الذي، ليس معه جازم - مرفوع

ZAJJAJ:v1p143/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p143/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p143/r1.claim: Al-qithāʾ has two dialectal forms; some readers pronounce its possessive form with ḍamma, while the more common and better reading has kasra.
ZAJJAJ:v1p143/r1.anchor: في القثاء لغتان، يقال القثاء والقثاء (يا هذا) و (قد) قرأ بعضهم قثائها بالضم، والأجود الأكثر

ZAJJAJ:v1p143/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p143/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p143/r2.claim: “Fūm” means wheat, and more broadly baked grains; the proposed meaning “garlic” is unknown in Arabic and ill-suited to a request for staple food, since wheat is food’s foundation. “Fūmū lanā” means bake bread for us.
ZAJJAJ:v1p143/r2.anchor: وفومها: الفوم الحنطة، ويقال الحبوب وقال بعض النحويين إنه يجوز عنده الفوم ههنا الثوم، وهذا ما لا يعرف

ZAJJAJ:v1p143/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p143/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p143/r3.claim: The unhamzated reading “adnā” is preferred in transmission and means nearer or lower in value; the hamzated “adnaʾ” is also possible and denotes something base or vile.
ZAJJAJ:v1p143/r3.anchor: و (أدنى) القراءة فيه بغير الهمز وقد قرأ بعضهم " أدنأ " بالذي هو خير، وكلاهما له وجه في اللغة

ZAJJAJ:v1p144/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p144/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p144/r1.claim: Most readers include final alif in “miṣran”; it can mean any town, appropriate to their wilderness setting, or Egypt as a masculine proper name and is then declinable.

ZAJJAJ:v1p144/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p144/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p144/r2.claim: A reading without alif can refer to Egypt: the place name is treated as masculine but named after a feminine city, so it is indeclinable, as in the cited verse.
ZAJJAJ:v1p144/r2.anchor: وجائز أن يكون مصر بغير ألف على أنه يريد مصرا كما قال عز وجل: (ادخلوا مصر إن شاء الله آمنين)

ZAJJAJ:v1p144/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p144/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p144/r3.claim: “Dhilla” is abasement and “maskana” is submission or humility; the latter derives from stillness, since poverty reduces a poor person’s movement.
ZAJJAJ:v1p144/r3.anchor: (الذلة): الصغار، (المسكنة): الخضوع، واشتقاقه: من السكون. إنما يقال مسكين للذي أسكنه الفقر، أي قلل حركته.

ZAJJAJ:v1p144/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p144/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p144/r4.claim: The expression “bāʾū bi-ghaḍab” means that they bore or incurred the wrath.
ZAJJAJ:v1p144/r4.anchor: يقال بؤت بكذا وكذا أي احتملته.

ZAJJAJ:v1p144/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p144/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p144/r5.claim: “That” refers to the wrath that came upon them because they disbelieved in God’s signs.
ZAJJAJ:v1p144/r5.anchor: معنى ذلك والله أعلم الغضب حل بهم بكفرهم.

ZAJJAJ:v1p145/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p145/r1.speaker: أهل المدينة
ZAJJAJ:v1p145/r1.claim: The agreed reading of “nabiyyīn,” “anbiyāʾ,” and “barīʾa” drops hamza; a group of Medinan readers pronounce hamza in these forms throughout the Qur’an.
ZAJJAJ:v1p145/r1.anchor: القراءة المجمع عليها في النبيين والأنبياء والبرئة طرح لهمزة، وجماعة من أهل المدينة يهمزون جميع ما في القرآن

ZAJJAJ:v1p145/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p145/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p145/r2.claim: Dropping hamza is better: hamzated faʿīl forms usually pluralize as faʿlāʾ, whereas weak-root forms take afʿilāʾ; the latter pattern is possible with sound roots but rare.
ZAJJAJ:v1p145/r2.anchor: والأجود ترك الهمزة، لأن الاستعمال يوجب أن ما كان مهموزا من فعيل فجمعه فعلاء، مثل ظريف وظرفاء ونبيء ونبآء.

ZAJJAJ:v1p145/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p145/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p145/r3.claim: “Nabī” may derive from “anbaʾa,” with hamza dropped through frequent use, or from a verb meaning to rise, giving the sense of high rank.
ZAJJAJ:v1p145/r3.anchor: فيجوز أن يكون نبي من أنبأت مما ترك همزه لكثرة الاستعمال، ويجوز أن يكون من نبأ ينبوء إذا ارتفع

TABRISI:2:61/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61/r1.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:2:61/r1.claim: Abu Ali argues that the hamzated form of nabiʾ preserves the word's original hamza, supported by Hijazi speakers who pronounce it.
TABRISI:2:61/r1.anchor: الحجة لمن همز النبيء أن يقول هو أصل الكلمة ألا ترى أن ناسا من أهل الحجاز حققوا الهمزة

TABRISI:2:61/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABRISI:2:61/r2.claim: A report has the Prophet answer a man who called him nabīʾ Allah by saying he is nabī Allah.
TABRISI:2:61/r2.anchor: فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم: " لست نبيء

TABRISI:2:61/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:61/r3.claim: The author suspects some transmitters judged the report's chain weak.
TABRISI:2:61/r3.anchor: فأظن أن من أهل النقل من ضعف إسناد هذا الحديث

TABRISI:2:61/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:61/r4.claim: As evidence against rejecting hamza, the author says a poet praised the Prophet with the plural and no known objection; a fault in the singular would also affect the plural.
TABRISI:2:61/r4.anchor: ولو كان في واحده نكير لكان الجمع كالواحد

TABRISI:2:61/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:61/r5.claim: Those who read without hamza cite the Quranic plural anbiyaʾ, whose pattern commonly comes from weak-final nouns, as evidence that the singular's hamza was replaced.
TABRISI:2:61/r5.anchor: وحجة من أبدل ولم يحقق مجيء الجمع في التنزيل على أنبياء

TABRISI:2:61/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61/r6.speaker: سيبويه
TABRISI:2:61/r6.claim: Sibawayh's report that all Arabs say tanabbaʾa with hamza supports deriving nabiʾ from the hamzated root and rules out nabāwa.
TABRISI:2:61/r6.anchor: سيبويه حكى أن جميع العرب يقولون تنبأ مسيلمة بالهمزة

TABRISI:2:61/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61/r7.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:2:61/r7.claim: Al-Zajjaj allows nabi to derive either from anbaʾa with hamza dropped through frequent use or from nabā, to rise.
TABRISI:2:61/r7.anchor: وقال الزجاج يجوز أن يكون نبي من أنبأت فترك همزته لكثرة الاستعمال

TABRISI:2:61/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:61/r8.claim: Ṭabrisī defines food as nourishment, ṭaʿm as eating, and food also as a physical substance perceived by taste.
TABRISI:2:61/r8.anchor: الطعام ما يتغذى به والطعم بضم الطاء الأكل والطعام عرض يدرك بحاسة الذوق

TABRISI:2:61/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:61/r9.claim: Wāḥid is the first number; God is one because He is distinguished by His most beautiful attributes.
TABRISI:2:61/r9.anchor: والله تعالى واحد لتفرده بصفاته الحسنى

TABRISI:2:61/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61/r10.speaker: ابن السراج
TABRISI:2:61/r10.claim: Ibn al-Sarraj derives duʿāʾ, supplication, from nidāʾ, calling.
TABRISI:2:61/r10.anchor: والدعاء أصله النداء عن ابن السراج

TABRISI:2:61/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:61/r11.claim: Supplication is a request addressed by a speaker to someone above him; its distinction from a command lies in the speakers' rank.
TABRISI:2:61/r11.anchor: وحقيقة الدعاء قول القائل لمن فوقه افعل والفرق بينه وبين الأمر يظهر بالرتبة

TABRISI:2:61/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:61/r12.claim: Inbāt means bringing forth plants and derives from the sense of appearing.
TABRISI:2:61/r12.anchor: والإنبات إخراج النبات وأصله من الظهور

TABRISI:2:61/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:61/r13.claim: Baql is spring growth and, more specifically, any plant without a stem; both baqalat and abqalat are eloquent forms for the earth's producing it.
TABRISI:2:61/r13.anchor: فالبقل كل نبات ليس له ساق

TABRISI:2:61/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:61/r14.claim: Qiththa has two pronunciations, with kasra on qaf preferred and identified as Quranic usage.
TABRISI:2:61/r14.anchor: وفي القثاء لغتان ضم القاف وكسرها والكسر أجود وهي لغة القرآن

TABRISI:2:61/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61/r15.speaker: عيسى الثقفي
TABRISI:2:61/r15.claim: Isa al-Thaqafi is reported to have the anomalous reading with damma on qaf in qiththa.
TABRISI:2:61/r15.anchor: روي عن عيسى الثقفي في الشواذ بالضم

TABRISI:2:61#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:61#2/r1.claim: The cited verse depicts fūm as a crop cultivated in Medina.
TABRISI:2:61#2/r1.anchor: قد كنت أغنى الناس شخصا واحدا ورد المدينة عن زراعة فوم

TABRISI:2:61#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#2/r2.speaker: الفراء والأزهري
TABRISI:2:61#2/r2.claim: Al-Farra and al-Azhari say fūm means wheat or bread; Arabs use it to mean bake bread.
TABRISI:2:61#2/r2.anchor: وقال الفراء والأزهري: هو الحنطة والخبز.

TABRISI:2:61#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#2/r3.speaker: قوم
TABRISI:2:61#2/r3.claim: Some identify fūm as grains from which bread is baked.
TABRISI:2:61#2/r3.anchor: وقال قوم هو الحبوب التي تخبز

TABRISI:2:61#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#2/r4.speaker: الكسائي
TABRISI:2:61#2/r4.claim: Al-Kisaʾi says fūm means garlic, with fāʾ replacing thāʾ as in the words hadath and jadaf.
TABRISI:2:61#2/r4.anchor: وقال الكسائي: هو الثوم أبدل من الثاء فاء كما قالوا حدث وجدف.

TABRISI:2:61#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#2/r5.speaker: الفراء
TABRISI:2:61#2/r5.claim: Al-Farra considers the garlic reading more fitting because onion follows fūm in the verse.
TABRISI:2:61#2/r5.anchor: قال الفراء: وهذا أشبه بما ذكره بعده من البصل

TABRISI:2:61#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#2/r6.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:2:61#2/r6.claim: Al-Zajjaj rejects garlic as an implausible meaning because people would not ask for garlic without bread, the staple.
TABRISI:2:61#2/r6.anchor: قال الزجاج: وهذا بعيد لأنه لا يعرف الثوم بمعنى الفوم

TABRISI:2:61#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:61#2/r7.claim: Ṭabrisī calls that objection weak because anomalous readings attributed to Ibn Masud and Ibn Abbas read thūm, garlic, with thāʾ.
TABRISI:2:61#2/r7.anchor: وهذا ضعيف لأنه قد روي في الشواذ عن ابن مسعود وابن عباس وثومها بالثاء

TABRISI:2:61#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#2/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:61#2/r8.claim: ʿAdas means the familiar lentil grain.

TABRISI:2:61#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#2/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:61#2/r9.claim: Adnā can mean nearer or lower, as in something close or inferior.
TABRISI:2:61#2/r9.anchor: وقوله أدنى أي أقرب وأدون كما تقول هذا شيء مقارب أو دون

TABRISI:2:61#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#2/r10.speaker: الفراء
TABRISI:2:61#2/r10.claim: Al-Farra prefers deriving adnā from baseness, with hamza omitted.
TABRISI:2:61#2/r10.anchor: فتركت همزتها وهو اختيار الفراء وحكى الأزهري

TABRISI:2:61#2/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#2/r11.speaker: ابن زيد
TABRISI:2:61#2/r11.claim: Ibn Zayd distinguishes al-danī without hamza, meaning vile, from al-danīʾ with hamza, meaning lewd.
TABRISI:2:61#2/r11.anchor: عن ابن زيد الدني بلا همز الخسيس والدنيء بالهمزة الماجن

TABRISI:2:61#2/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#2/r12.speaker: بعضهم
TABRISI:2:61#2/r12.claim: One etymology derives Miṣr from being cut off from its surroundings by cultivation.
TABRISI:2:61#2/r12.anchor: فقال بعضهم هو من القطع لانقطاعه بالعمارة عما سواه

TABRISI:2:61#2/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#2/r13.speaker: آخرون
TABRISI:2:61#2/r13.claim: Another etymology derives Miṣr from its separation from other places.
TABRISI:2:61#2/r13.anchor: ومنهم من قال هو مشتق من الفصل بينه وبين غيره

TABRISI:2:61#2/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#2/r14.speaker: عدي بن زيد
TABRISI:2:61#2/r14.claim: Adi ibn Zayd's verse depicts the sun making Egypt a clear division between day and night, supporting the separation etymology.
TABRISI:2:61#2/r14.anchor:
وقال عدي بن زيد:
وجاعل الشمس مصرا لا خفاء به

TABRISI:2:61#2/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#2/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:61#2/r15.claim: Ḍuribat ʿalayhim al-dhilla means humiliation was imposed on them, by analogy with a ruler imposing a tax.
TABRISI:2:61#2/r15.anchor: وضربت عليهم الذلة أي فرضت ووضعت عليهم الذلة وألزموها

TABRISI:2:61#2/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#2/r16.speaker: قوم
TABRISI:2:61#2/r16.claim: Another explanation says they settled in the abode of humiliation, using the idiom of pitching tents.
TABRISI:2:61#2/r16.anchor: وقيل ضربت عليهم الذلة أي حلوا بمنزل الذل والمسكنة مأخوذ من ضرب القباب

TABRISI:2:61#2/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#2/r17.speaker: الفرزدق
TABRISI:2:61#2/r17.claim: Al-Farazdaq's image of a spider's web spread over someone illustrates the idiom of something being laid upon them.
TABRISI:2:61#2/r17.anchor:
قال الفرزدق:
ضربت عليك العنكبوت بنسجها

TABRISI:2:61#2/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#2/r18.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:61#2/r18.claim: Dhilla derives from the verb meaning to be humbled or low.
TABRISI:2:61#2/r18.anchor: وأما الذلة فمشتقة من قولهم ذل فلان يذل ذلا وذلة

TABRISI:2:61#2/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#2/r19.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:61#2/r19.claim: Maskana derives from miskīn; here it means the humility and lowliness of poverty and need, with forms tamaskana and taskana also used.

TABRISI:2:61#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#3/r1.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:2:61#3/r1.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the root sense of bāʾū is equalization.

TABRISI:2:61#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#3/r2.speaker: عبادة بن الصامت
TABRISI:2:61#3/r2.claim: Ubada ibn al-Samit reports that the Prophet distributed the spoils equally among the recipients, illustrating bāʾūʾan as equal shares.
