TABRISI:2:61#3/r2.anchor: روي عن عبادة بن الصامت قال جعل الله تعالى الأنفال إلى نبيه فقسمها بينهم على بواء أي على سواء

TABRISI:2:61#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#3/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:61#3/r3.claim: A line of poetry uses bawāʾ for an equal or balanced exchange, while noting that blood is not measured out like goods.
TABRISI:2:61#3/r3.anchor: فيقتل جبرا بامرىء لم يكن له بواأ ولكن لا تكايل بالدم

TABRISI:2:61#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#3/r4.speaker: قوم
TABRISI:2:61#3/r4.claim: Some say bāʾū means they confessed what incurred God's wrath; an anonymous verse uses the verb for admitting fault and sin.
TABRISI:2:61#3/r4.anchor: وقال قوم هو الاعتراف ومعناه أنهم اعترفوا بما يوجب غضب الله

TABRISI:2:61#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#3/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:61#3/r5.claim: Anger means the will to inflict harm; when attributed to God it means His will to punish the one under wrath.
TABRISI:2:61#3/r5.anchor: والغضب إرادة إيصال الضرر إلى من غضب عليه فإذا أضيف إلى الله تعالى

TABRISI:2:61#3/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#3/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:61#3/r6.claim: Nabi derives from nabaʾ, news, because a prophet reports from God.
TABRISI:2:61#3/r6.anchor: والنبي اشتقاقه من النبأ الذي هو الخبر لأنه المخبر عن الله سبحانه

TABRISI:2:61#3/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#3/r7.speaker: سيبويه
TABRISI:2:61#3/r7.claim: Sibawayh's evidence that Arabs say nabīʾat suʾ and tanabbaʾa supports the hamzated root and excludes derivation from nabāwa.
TABRISI:2:61#3/r7.anchor: سيبويه زعم أنهم يقولون في تحقير النبوة كان مسيلمة نبيئة سوء

TABRISI:2:61#3/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#3/r8.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:2:61#3/r8.claim: Abu Ali says nabāwa means elevation, which is not necessarily prophethood, whereas a messenger from God is precisely described by nabaʾ, news.
TABRISI:2:61#3/r8.anchor: قال أبو علي: ومما يقوي أنه من النبأ الذي هو الخبر

TABRISI:2:61#3/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#3/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:61#3/r9.claim: Iʿtidāʾ is crossing the limit God set for His servants, or any limit of one thing into another.
TABRISI:2:61#3/r9.anchor: والاعتداء تجاوز الحد الذي حده الله لعباده إلى غيره

TABRISI:2:61#3/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#3/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:61#3/r10.claim: Yukh’rij is jussive as the answer to an omitted command, understood as asking God and telling Him to bring forth the requested food; the implied conditional is indicated by context.
TABRISI:2:61#3/r10.anchor: قوله يخرج لنا مجزوم لأنه جواب أمر محذوف لأن تقديره أدع لنا ربك وقل له أخرج لنا

TABRISI:2:61#3/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#3/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:61#3/r11.claim: Another parse makes yukh’rij jussive after an implicit command lām, as in the cited verse from Ibrahim 14:31.
TABRISI:2:61#3/r11.anchor: وقيل أن تقديره أن يكون يخرج مجزوما بإضمار اللام

TABRISI:2:61#4/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#4/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:61#4/r1.claim: Min in mimmā is partitive because they sought some of what the earth produces, not everything; the alternative treats it as redundant, but min is added only in negation.
TABRISI:2:61#4/r1.anchor: وقوله مما تنبت الأرض من هنا للتبعيض لأن المراد يخرج لنا بعض ما تنبته الأرض

TABRISI:2:61#4/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#4/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:61#4/r2.claim: All canonical readers give Miṣr tanwīn, taking it as an unspecified city since the Israelites were in the wilderness; it may instead mean Egypt proper, a masculine name.
TABRISI:2:61#4/r2.anchor: ونون جميع القراء مصرا لأنه أراد مصرا من الأمصار بغير تعيين

TABRISI:2:61#4/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#4/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
TABRISI:2:61#4/r3.claim: Ibn Masud is reported to read Miṣr without the alif; it may mean Egypt proper as in Yusuf 12:99, whose name is masculine despite denoting a city, or reflect the written muṣḥaf.
TABRISI:2:61#4/r3.anchor: وروي عن ابن مسعود أنه قرأ بغير ألف

TABRISI:2:61#4/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#4/r4.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:2:61#4/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains that the wrath came upon them because of their disbelief in God's signs.
TABRISI:2:61#4/r4.anchor: قال الزجاج معناه والله أعلم الغضب حل بهم بكفرهم

TABRISI:2:61#4/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#4/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:61#4/r5.claim: Ṭabrisī says dhālika points back to the wrath in bāʾū bi-ghaḍab; the causal phrase is governed by the predicate, and the deleted clause is understood from what follows.
TABRISI:2:61#4/r5.anchor: ذلك إشارة إلى الغضب في قوله وباؤوا بغضب

TABRISI:2:61#4/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#4/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:61#4/r6.claim: He applies the same parsing to dhālika bimā ʿaṣaw, with mā and its clause interpreted as a verbal noun.
TABRISI:2:61#4/r6.anchor: وكذلك قوله { ذلك بما عصوا } فإن ما مع صلته في تأويل المصدر

TABRISI:2:61#4/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#4/r7.speaker: أبو زيد
TABRISI:2:61#4/r7.claim: Abu Zayd cites poetry with yaqūm jussive without the command lām as evidence for its omission.
TABRISI:2:61#4/r7.anchor:
وأنشد أبو زيد:
فيضحي صريعا ما يقوم لحاجة

TABRISI:2:61#4/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#4/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:61#4/r8.claim: Another poetic example has adʿu coordinated with udʿu after omission of the command lām.
TABRISI:2:61#4/r8.anchor:
وأنشد غيره:
فقلت ادعي وأدع فإن أندى

TABRISI:2:61#4/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#4/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:61#4/r9.claim: A further poetic example makes tafdi jussive with the implied sense li-tafdi.
TABRISI:2:61#4/r9.anchor:
وقال آخر:
محمد تفد نفسك كل نفس

TABRISI:2:61#4/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#4/r10.speaker: الفراء
TABRISI:2:61#4/r10.claim: Al-Farra states that deleting the command lām is allowed only in poetry, where meter forces it.
TABRISI:2:61#4/r10.anchor: في حلقة الفراء فسمعته يقول لأصحابه لا يجوز حذف لام الأمر إلا في الشعر

TABRISI:2:61#4/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#4/r11.speaker: المازني
TABRISI:2:61#4/r11.claim: Al-Mazini challenges al-Farra's claim that deletion is poetic necessity because the line could instead say fa-lyadun minni.
TABRISI:2:61#4/r11.anchor: المازني قال جلست في حلقة الفراء فسمعته يقول لأصحابه لا يجوز حذف لام الأمر إلا في الشعر

TABRISI:2:61#5/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#5/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:61#5/r1.claim: After listing God's favors to the Israelites, the passage recounts their ingratitude and disobedient choice.
TABRISI:2:61#5/r1.anchor: لما عدد سبحانه فيما قبل ما أسداه إليهم من النعم والإحسان ذكر ما قابلوا به تلك النعم

TABRISI:2:61#5/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#5/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:61#5/r2.claim: The addressees of the recollection are the Israelites' forebears.
TABRISI:2:61#5/r2.anchor: أي قال أسلافكم من بني إسرائيل

TABRISI:2:61#5/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#5/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:61#5/r3.claim: They say they cannot endure one food: manna and quails are called one because the same daily food repeated from day to day, even if it offered varieties.
TABRISI:2:61#5/r3.anchor: وإنما قال على طعام واحد وإن كان طعامهم المن والسلوى وهما شيئان

TABRISI:2:61#5/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#5/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:61#5/r4.claim: An alternative account says only manna first descended; they tired of it and then quails were sent.
TABRISI:2:61#5/r4.anchor: وقيل إنه كان ينزل عليهم المن وحده فملوه فقالوا ذلك فأنزل عليهم السلوى من بعد ذلك

TABRISI:2:61#5/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#5/r5.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:2:61#5/r5.claim: Qatada says the people were shaded by clouds and given manna and quails in the wilderness, tired of them, recalled life in Egypt, and asked Moses for its produce.
TABRISI:2:61#5/r5.anchor: ما رواه قتادة قال كان القوم في البرية قد ظلل عليهم الغمام وأنزل عليهم المن والسلوى

TABRISI:2:61#5/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#5/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:61#5/r6.claim: Another explanation says they sought produce so the poor could assist the rich, rather than having everyone equally rich and independent.
TABRISI:2:61#5/r6.anchor: وقيل إنهم قالوا لا نصبر على الغنى بأن يكون جميعنا أغنياء

TABRISI:2:61#5/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#5/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:61#5/r7.claim: One view makes Moses ask whether they exchange the better food God chose for what is lower and worse; another makes God say it.
TABRISI:2:61#5/r7.anchor: معناه قال لهم موسى وقيل بل قال الله لهم أتتركون ما اختار الله لكم

TABRISI:2:61#5/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#5/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:61#5/r8.claim: A further interpretation contrasts farmed and crafted food with manna and quails given freely.
TABRISI:2:61#5/r8.anchor: وقيل إنه أراد أتستبدلون ما تتبذلون في زراعته وصناعته بما أعطاه الله إياكم عفوا

TABRISI:2:61#5/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#5/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:61#5/r9.claim: Another reading of adnā is the lower-priced choice in place of the more valuable, tasty one.
TABRISI:2:61#5/r9.anchor: وقيل المراد تختارون الذي هو أقرب أي أقل قيمة على الذي هو أكثر قيمته وألذ

TABRISI:2:61#5/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#5/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:61#5/r10.claim: One view says their request was no sin because they asked for another permissible food; Ṭabrisī prefers the view that it was sinful because they rejected God's choice and were reproached.
TABRISI:2:61#5/r10.anchor: واختلف في سؤالهم هذا هل كان معصية فقيل لم يكن معصية لأن الأول كان مباحا

TABRISI:2:61#5/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#5/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:61#5/r11.claim: The more apt view is that the request was sinful because they were reproached for refusing what God chose.

TABRISI:2:61#5/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#5/r12.speaker: الحسن والربيع
TABRISI:2:61#5/r12.claim: Al-Hasan and al-Rabiʿ say the requested Egypt is Pharaoh's Egypt from which the Israelites departed.
TABRISI:2:61#5/r12.anchor: فقال الحسن والربيع أراد مصر فرعون الذين خرجوا منه

TABRISI:2:61#5/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#5/r13.speaker: أبو مسلم وابن زيد
TABRISI:2:61#5/r13.claim: Abu Muslim, with a report also attributed to Ibn Zayd, identifies Egypt as Jerusalem.
TABRISI:2:61#5/r13.anchor: وقال أبو مسلم أراد بيت المقدس وروي ذلك عن ابن زيد

TABRISI:2:61#5/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#5/r14.speaker: قتادة والسدي ومجاهد
TABRISI:2:61#5/r14.claim: Qatada, al-Suddi, and Mujahid take miṣr as any city: the requested crops are found in towns, not in the wilderness.
TABRISI:2:61#5/r14.anchor: وقال قتادة والسدي ومجاهد أراد مصرا من الأمصار

TABRISI:2:61#5/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#5/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:61#5/r15.claim: On this reading, the speech ends with the promise that the produce they requested would be available in a settled city; the verse then begins a new account of Sabbath violators and prophet-killers.
TABRISI:2:61#5/r15.anchor: وقد تم الكلام ها هنا ثم استأنف حكم الذين اعتدوا في السبت ومن قتل الأنبياء

TABRISI:2:61#6/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#6/r1.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
TABRISI:2:61#6/r1.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada interpret the humiliation as the subjection expressed in paying jizya under Quran 9:29.

TABRISI:2:61#6/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#6/r2.speaker: عطاء
TABRISI:2:61#6/r2.claim: Ata says the humiliation refers to the Jewish kistīj, a distinctive belt and dress.
TABRISI:2:61#6/r2.anchor: وقيل هو الكستيج وزي اليهود عن عطاء

TABRISI:2:61#6/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#6/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:61#6/r3.claim: Maskana means the appearance of poverty; even their wealthy people feign destitution lest the tax be doubled.
TABRISI:2:61#6/r3.anchor: يعني زي الفقر فترى المثري منهم يتباءس مخافة أن يضاعف عليه الجزية

TABRISI:2:61#6/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#6/r4.speaker: قوم
TABRISI:2:61#6/r4.claim: Some argue this verse shows wealth's merit because it condemns poverty.
TABRISI:2:61#6/r4.anchor: وقال قوم هذه الآية تدل على فضل الغنى

TABRISI:2:61#6/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#6/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:61#6/r5.claim: Ṭabrisī says that is not the right interpretation: the blame is for poverty of heart, since Jews can be materially wealthy yet spiritually needy; the Prophet says true wealth is of the soul.

TABRISI:2:61#6/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#6/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABRISI:2:61#6/r6.claim: The Prophet is reported to say that true wealth is wealth of the soul.

TABRISI:2:61#6/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#6/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
TABRISI:2:61#6/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd says God exchanged the Jews' honor for humiliation, prosperity for misery, and approval for anger, as requital for disbelief and unjust killing of prophets.
TABRISI:2:61#6/r7.anchor: أبدل الله اليهود بالعز ذلا وبالنعمة بؤسا وبالرضا عنهم غضبا

TABRISI:2:61#6/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#6/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:61#6/r8.claim: They returned bearing God's anger, which was due upon them and had overtaken them.
TABRISI:2:61#6/r8.anchor: أي رجعوا منصرفين متحملين غضب الله قد وجب عليهم من الله الغضب

TABRISI:2:61#6/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#6/r9.speaker: قوم
TABRISI:2:61#6/r9.claim: Some explain the wrath as worldly affliction and retribution replacing ease and blessing.
TABRISI:2:61#6/r9.anchor: وقال قوم: الغضب هو ما حل بهم في الدنيا من البلاء والنقمة

TABRISI:2:61#6/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#6/r10.speaker: آخرون
TABRISI:2:61#6/r10.claim: Others take the wrath as punishment for their sins in the afterlife.
TABRISI:2:61#6/r10.anchor: وقال آخرون هو ما ينالهم في الآخرة من العقاب على معاصيهم

TABRISI:2:61#6/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#6/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:61#6/r11.claim: Dhālika points back to the wrath, humiliation, and poverty already mentioned as caused by their disbelief in God's signs.
TABRISI:2:61#6/r11.anchor: فقال { ذلك } أي ذلك الغضب وضرب الذلة والمسكنة حل بهم لأجل

TABRISI:2:61#6/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#6/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:61#6/r12.claim: One explanation takes God's signs to mean the Gospel and Quran, making the first wrath for rejecting Jesus and the Gospel and a second for rejecting Muhammad and the Quran; another takes them as Muhammad's attributes.
TABRISI:2:61#6/r12.anchor: وقيل أراد بآيات الله الإنجيل والقرآن ولذلك قال فباءوا بغضب على غضب

TABRISI:2:61#6/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#6/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:61#6/r13.claim: Killing the prophets without right means without any offense, as in the killings of Zechariah and John.
TABRISI:2:61#6/r13.anchor: أي بغير جرم كزكريا ويحيى وغيرهما

TABRISI:2:61#6/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#6/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:61#6/r14.claim: The qualifier 'without right' does not imply that prophets could ever be killed justly; it emphasizes that their killing was sheer injustice, like the cited Quranic and poetic examples.
TABRISI:2:61#6/r14.anchor: لا يدل على أنه قد يصح أن يقتل النبيون بحق لأن هذا خرج مخرج الصفة لقتلهم

TABRISI:2:61#6/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#6/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:61#6/r15.claim: Dhālika bimā ʿaṣaw refers to their Sabbath violation and killing prophets, or to breaking the covenant and assaulting prophets; God acted against them for disobedience and transgression.
TABRISI:2:61#6/r15.anchor: ذلك إشارة إلى ما تقدم أيضا بعصيانهم في قتل الأنبياء وعدوهم السبت

TABRISI:2:61#6/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#6/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:61#6/r16.claim: God allowed prophets to be killed so they could attain ranks unavailable otherwise; allowing murder of believers and righteous people likewise does not mean God has abandoned them.
TABRISI:2:61#6/r16.anchor: إنما جاز ذلك لتنال أنبياء الله سبحانه من رفع المنازل والدرجات ما لا ينالونه بغير القتل

TABRISI:2:61#6/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#6/r17.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:2:61#6/r17.claim: Al-Hasan says God never ordered a prophet to fight and then be killed in battle; those killed were killed outside combat.
TABRISI:2:61#6/r17.anchor: إن الله تعالى لم يأمر نبيا بالقتال فقتل فيه

TABRISI:2:61#6/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#6/r18.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:61#6/r18.claim: Ṭabrisī's preferred view is that God may not allow a prophet's death before he completes his assigned revelation, since that would undermine the obligations and their benefits; once he has delivered it, God may allow his killers and need not prevent it.
TABRISI:2:61#6/r18.anchor: والصحيح أن النبي إن كان لم يؤد الشرع الذي أمر بتأديته لم يجز أن يمكن الله سبحانه من قتله

TABRISI:2:61#7/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:61#7/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABRISI:2:61#7/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet saying that Israelites divided 500 years after Moses, when captive-born offspring had become numerous, and divided again 200 years after Jesus.
TABRISI:2:61#7/r1.anchor: اختلفت بنو إسرائيل بعد موسى بخمسمائة سنة حتى كثر فيهم أولاد السبايا

THALABI:v1p204/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p204/r5.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v1p204/r5.claim: The Israelites were people accustomed to leeks, onions, and lentils; they reverted to their bad former habits and craved familiar foods, so they rejected manna and quails.
THALABI:v1p204/r5.anchor: قال الحسن: كانوا نتانى أهل كراث وأبصال وأعداس فنزعوا إلى عكرهم عكر السوء

THALABI:v1p204/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p204/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p204/r6.claim: Although manna and quail are two foods, the Arabs can describe two things with the singular “one”; he cites the pearls and coral verse, although they come only from the salt sea.
THALABI:v1p204/r6.anchor: وإنما قالوا (واحد) وهما اثنان لأن العرب تعبر عن اثنين بلفظ الواحد

THALABI:v1p204/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p204/r7.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
THALABI:v1p204/r7.claim: They kneaded manna and quail together, making one food that they ate.
THALABI:v1p204/r7.anchor: قال عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم: كانوا يعجنون المن والسلوى فيصير طعاما واحدا

THALABI:v1p204/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p204/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p204/r8.claim: Fa-dʿu means “ask,” and lanā means “for us.”
THALABI:v1p204/r8.anchor: فادع فسأل وادع. لنا لأجلنا. ربك يخرج لنا مما تنبت الأرض

THALABI:v1p204/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p204/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p204/r9.claim: The common reading has qiththāʾihā with kasra on qāf.

THALABI:v1p204/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p204/r10.speaker: يحيى بن وثاب، وطلحة بن مصرف، والأشيب العقيلي
THALABI:v1p204/r10.claim: These readers pronounce qiththāʾihā with ḍamma on qāf, a Tamim dialect.
THALABI:v1p204/r10.anchor: وقرأ يحيى بن وثاب، وطلحة بن مصرف، والأشيب العقيلي: وقثائها بضم القاف

THALABI:v1p204/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p204/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v1p204/r11.claim: Fūm means bread; the Arabs say fūmū lanā to mean “bake for us.”
THALABI:v1p204/r11.anchor: قال ابن عباس: الفوم: الخبز، تقول العرب: فوموا لنا، أي اختبزوا لنا

THALABI:v1p204/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p204/r12.speaker: عطاء وأبو مالك
THALABI:v1p204/r12.claim: Fūm means wheat in an old language; the cited poem uses fūm in the context of farming.
THALABI:v1p204/r12.anchor: عطاء وأبو مالك: هو الحنطة وهي لغة قديمة، قال الشاعر

THALABI:v1p204/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p204/r13.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p204/r13.claim: An unnamed view takes fūm to mean all grains.
THALABI:v1p204/r13.anchor: هو الحبوب كلها. الكلبي والنضر بن شميل

THALABI:v1p204/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p204/r14.speaker: الكلبي والنضر بن شميل والكسائي والمعرج
THALABI:v1p204/r14.claim: These authorities take fūm to mean garlic; al-Muʿarrij cites a line by Ḥassān in which fūm is paired with ḥawqal as food.
THALABI:v1p204/r14.anchor: الكلبي والنضر بن شميل والكسائي والمعرج: هو الثوم، وأنشد المعرج لحسان

THALABI:v1p205/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p205/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p205/r1.claim: On the garlic interpretation, Arabs interchange fāʾ and thāʾ, as in alternate words for gum and a grave; ʿAbd Allāh’s codex reads “and its garlic.”
THALABI:v1p205/r1.anchor: فالعرب تعاقب بين الفاء والثاء فتقول للصمغ العرفط: مغاثير ومغافير

THALABI:v1p205/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p205/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v1p205/r2.claim: A report from ʿAlī praises lentils as blessed and purifying, softening the heart and increasing tears; it says seventy prophets blessed them, with Jesus the last.
THALABI:v1p205/r2.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «عليكم بالعدس فإنه مبارك مقدس وإنه يرقق القلب

THALABI:v1p205/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p205/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p205/r3.claim: Ubayy’s codex reads atubaddilūn in place of atastabdilūn.
THALABI:v1p205/r3.anchor: فقال لهم موسى عند ذلك: أتستبدلون وفي مصحف أبي: أتبدلون

THALABI:v1p205/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p205/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p205/r4.claim: Adnā means lower, baser, and worse; khayr means nobler and better, so the rebuke asks why they exchange good for evil.
THALABI:v1p205/r4.anchor: بالذي هو خير أشرف وأفضل، ومعناه: أتتركون الذي هو خير

THALABI:v1p205/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p205/r5.speaker: الفراء عن زهير العرقي
THALABI:v1p205/r5.claim: Zuhayr al-ʿAriqī is reported to read adnāʾ with hamza; the common reading omits hamza.
THALABI:v1p205/r5.anchor: حكى الفراء عن زهير العرقي: إنه قرأ (أدناء) بالهمزة، والعامة على ترك الهمزة

THALABI:v1p205/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p205/r6.speaker: some grammarians
THALABI:v1p205/r6.claim: Some grammarians derive adnā from adwan by moving the nūn and changing wāw to yāʾ, as in awlā min al-wayl.
THALABI:v1p205/r6.anchor: وقال بعض النحاة: هو أدون فقدمت النون وحولت الواو ياء

THALABI:v1p205/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p205/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p205/r7.claim: The good and evil may refer to kinds of food, or to God’s choice for them as against their own choices.
THALABI:v1p205/r7.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون هذا الخير والشر منصرفين إلى أجناس الطعام وأنواعه

THALABI:v1p205/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p205/r8.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v1p205/r8.claim: Miṣr means any one of the cities: had the verse meant the particular Egypt, it would be uninflected, as in the command to enter Egypt in Joseph’s story.
THALABI:v1p205/r8.anchor: ولو أراد مصر بعينها لقال: (مصر) ولم يصرفه كقوله ادخلوا مصر إن شاء الله

THALABI:v1p205/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p205/r9.speaker: الضحاك
THALABI:v1p205/r9.claim: Miṣr means the Egypt of Moses and Pharaoh.

THALABI:v1p205/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p205/r10.speaker: الأعمش
THALABI:v1p205/r10.claim: Miṣr means the Egypt ruled by Ṣāliḥ b. ʿAlī; the uninflected reading of al-Ḥasan and Ṭalḥa and the codices of ʿAbd Allāh and Ubayy support its being a proper name, though inflected for shortness.
THALABI:v1p205/r10.anchor: وقال الأعمش: هي مصر التي عليها صالح بن علي ودليل هذا القول: قراءة الحسن وطلحة

THALABI:v1p205/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p205/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p205/r11.claim: The requested items are the plants of the earth.
THALABI:v1p205/r11.anchor: فإن لكم ما سألتم من نبات الأرض

THALABI:v1p205/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p205/r12.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p205/r12.claim: Ḍuribat means “was imposed” or “made binding”; al-dhilla is abasement and humiliation, explained as the jizya, with a supporting verse.
THALABI:v1p205/r12.anchor: وضربت جعلت. عليهم وألزموا. الذلة الذل والهوان. قالوا: بالجزية، يدل عليه قوله: حتى يعطوا الجزية

THALABI:v1p205/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p205/r13.speaker: unidentified speaker
THALABI:v1p205/r13.claim: An unidentified gloss identifies the term with al-kastibinj, a Jewish weight.

THALABI:v1p205/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p205/r14.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p205/r14.claim: Miskana means possessing poverty; people may look poor while wealthy. It can also mean humiliation and poverty of heart; miskīn derives from stillness and few movements.
THALABI:v1p205/r14.anchor: والمسكنة يعني ذي الفقر. [فتراهم] كأنهم فقراء وأن كانوا مياسير

THALABI:v1p206/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p206/r1.speaker: الكسائي وغيره
THALABI:v1p206/r1.anchor: وباؤ بغضب من الله أي رجعوا في قول الكسائي وغيره

THALABI:v1p206/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p206/r2.speaker: أبو روق
THALABI:v1p206/r2.claim: Abū Rawq glosses the phrase as “deserved”; he considers the bāʾ an extra particle.

THALABI:v1p206/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p206/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة
THALABI:v1p206/r3.claim: Abū ʿUbayda says the phrase means they bore and acknowledged it, comparing it to the prophetic supplication “I acknowledge Your favor upon me and my sin”; God’s anger means blame, threat, and punishment, and likewise hatred and wrath.
THALABI:v1p206/r3.anchor: أبو عبيدة: احتملوا وأقروا به، ومنه الدعاء المأثور: (أبوء بنعمتك علي وأبوء بذنبي

THALABI:v1p206/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p206/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p206/r4.claim: Their unbelief in God’s signs concerns the description of Muḥammad as merciful in the Torah, Gospel, and Qurʾān.
THALABI:v1p206/r4.anchor: ذلك بأنهم كانوا يكفرون بآيات الله بصفة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وإنه الرحيم في التوراة والإنجيل والفرقان

THALABI:v1p206/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p206/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p206/r5.claim: The common reading has yaqtulūn with light consonants; al-Sulamī reads it with shadda, expressing intensive killing.
THALABI:v1p206/r5.anchor: ويقتلون قراءة العامة بالتخفيف من القتل، وقرأ السلمي بالتشديد من التقتيل

THALABI:v1p206/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p206/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p206/r6.claim: The famous reading has al-nabiyyīn with shadda and no hamza; Nāfiʿ alone uses hamza and lengthens it.
THALABI:v1p206/r6.anchor: النبيين القراءة المشهورة بالتشديد من غيرهم، وتفرد نافع بهمز النبيئين

THALABI:v1p206/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p206/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p206/r7.claim: With hamza, nabīʾ means “informer,” from the Arabic root n-b-ʾ, illustrated by the verse “when she informed him of it.”
THALABI:v1p206/r7.anchor: فمن همز معناه: المخبر، من قول العرب: أنبأ النبي إنباءا، ونبأ ينبئ تنبئة

THALABI:v1p206/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p206/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p206/r8.claim: Without hamza, the word may reflect deletion of hamza for ease because it is frequent, or mean elevated, from nabūʾa, as in the cited line about a side lifted from the bed.
THALABI:v1p206/r8.anchor: ومن حذف الهمز فله وجهان: أحدهما: إنه أراد الهمز فحذفه طلبا للخفة لكثرة استعمالها

THALABI:v1p206/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p206/r9.speaker: الكسائي
THALABI:v1p206/r9.claim: Al-Kisāʾī says nabī without hamza means “road”; a messenger is named for guiding people, and a poem uses nabī in this sense.
THALABI:v1p206/r9.anchor: قال الكسائي: النبي بغير همز: الطريق، فسمي الرسول نبيا، وإنما دقائق الحصا

THALABI:v1p206/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p206/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p206/r10.claim: The prophets killed unjustly include Isaiah, Zechariah, John, and the other prophets killed by the Jews.
THALABI:v1p206/r10.anchor: بغير الحق مثل أشعيا وزكريا ويحيى وسائر من قتل اليهود من الأنبياء

THALABI:v1p206/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p206/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p206/r11.claim: A report says the Jews killed seventy prophets in one hour early in the day; 112 Israelite worshippers ordered right and forbade wrong, and were all killed by day’s end.
THALABI:v1p206/r11.anchor: وفي الخبر: إن اليهود قتلوا سبعين نبيا من أول النهار

THALABI:v1p206/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p206/r12.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p206/r12.claim: “That was because they disobeyed and transgressed” means they went beyond God’s command and committed His prohibitions.
THALABI:v1p206/r12.anchor: ذلك بما عصوا وكانوا يعتدون يتجاوزون أمري ويرتكبون محارمي

ASAD-NOTES:2:61#n46/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:61#n46/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:61#n46/r1.claim: Moses asks whether they would trade freedom for the meager comforts of Egyptian captivity; in Sinai they longed for Egypt's comparative security, as Numbers 11 and Moses' next sentence indicate.
ASAD-NOTES:2:61#n46/r1.anchor: exchange your freedom for the paltry comforts which you enjoyed in your Egyptian captivity

ASAD-NOTES:2:61#n47/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:61#n47/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:61#n47/r1.claim: Habata literally means descending a slope and figuratively falling in dignity; since Moses' exclamation is not literal, Asad combines both senses as returning to Egypt in shame.
ASAD-NOTES:2:61#n47/r1.anchor: used figuratively in the sense of falling from dignity and becoming mean and abject

ASAD-NOTES:2:61#n48/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:61#n48/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:61#n48/r1.claim: The passage concerns a later phase of Jewish history; Asad cites John the Baptist and Gospel accusations by Jesus, plus accounts of Zachariah's murder, as evidence that Jews killed prophets.
ASAD-NOTES:2:61#n48/r1.anchor: This passage obviously refers to a later phase of Jewish history.

ASAD-NOTES:2:61#n48/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:61#n48/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:61#n48/r2.claim: The auxiliary kanu signals continuity or repeated persistence in their wrongdoing.
ASAD-NOTES:2:61#n48/r2.anchor: implication of continuity in, or persistent repetition of, their wrongdoing transpires from the use of the auxiliary verb kanu

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p579/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p579/r1.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p579/r1.claim: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib says the people had grown tired of their way of life.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p579/r1.anchor: قال # سعيد بن المسيب: ملوا عيشهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p579/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p579/r2.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p579/r2.claim: Qatada says they remembered their former Egyptian food and asked Moses to pray for it; ta'am is a generic term for what is eaten.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p579/r2.anchor: وقال قتادة: ذكر القوم عيشا كان لهم بمصر، فقالوا لموسى:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p579/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p579/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p579/r3.claim: They called it one food because manna with quail was eaten together like one dish and presented as one color, although made from different ingredients.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p579/r3.anchor: وإنما قالوا: طعام واحد، وكان طعامهم المن والسلوى، لأنهم كانوا يأكلون المن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p579/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p579/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p579/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says manna was their food and quail their drink, but the two were combined when eaten and therefore counted as one food.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p579/r4.anchor: قال ابن زيد: كان (¬5) طعامهم المن، وشرابهم السلوى،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p579/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p579/r5.speaker: أصحاب المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p579/r5.claim: Some linguists say food was called one because their daily nourishment never changed, like someone described as following one regular course by keeping to fasting and prayer.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p579/r5.anchor: وقال أصحاب المعاني: لما كان غذاؤهم في كل يوم لا يتغير، قيل: طعام واحد،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p581/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p581/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p581/r1.claim: Dua means asking one who can grant benefit or harm; it is named for the call used by a petitioner.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p581/r1.anchor: معنى الدعاء: الطلب (¬1) ممن يملك النفع والضر.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p581/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p581/r2.speaker: ابن السراج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p581/r2.claim: Ibn al-Sarraj says dua originally means calling; a request is called dua because the petitioner says Lord and calls upon God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p581/r2.anchor: وقال ابن السراج: أصله النداء وإنما قال للمسألة: دعاء؛ لأن السائل يقول: يا رب، فينادي ربه عز وجل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p581/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p581/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p581/r3.claim: The petition is expressed in the past tense as an optimistic expression that it has already happened.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p581/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p581/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p581/r4.claim: Yukhrij means asking God to bring something out; the following imperfect serves as the response to the preceding command, as in two cited verses.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p581/r4.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {يخرج لنا} المعنى سله وقل له: أخرج (¬6) يخرج، وكذلك قوله: {وقل لعبادي يقولوا التي هي أحسن}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p581/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p581/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p581/r5.claim: Baql is any plant that does not retain a stalk after livestock graze it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p581/r5.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {من بقلها} البقل: كل نبات لا يبقى له ساق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p581/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p581/r6.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p581/r6.claim: Al-Farra says fawm is an old word for wheat and bread; some Arabs also say fummu lana to mean bake bread for us, as in a verse by Ahihah ibn al-Jallah about sowing fawm.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p581/r6.anchor: فقال الفراء: الفوم فيما يذكرون لغة قديمة، وهي الحنطة والخبز جميعا قد ذكرا، قال: وقال بعضهم: سمحت العرب من أهل اللغة يقولون:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p581/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p581/r7.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p581/r7.claim: Al-Farra prefers reading fawm as thum, garlic: Abdullah's reading with thā fits the neighboring lentils and onions, supported by dialectal interchange of fā' and thā.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p581/r7.anchor: قال الفراء: وهي في قراءة عبد الله: (وثومها) بالثاء، وكأنه أشبه المعنيين بالصواب؛

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p581/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p581/r8.speaker: الكسائي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p581/r8.claim: Al-Kisa'i also chooses the interpretation of fawm as garlic.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p581/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p581/r9.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p581/r9.claim: Al-Zajjaj says fawm means wheat, or grain generally, and rejects garlic as unknown and implausible because the people sought staple food containing grain.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p581/r9.anchor: وقال الزجاج: الفوم: الحنطة، ويقال: الحبوب، لا اختلاف بين أهل اللغة أن الفوم: الحنطة.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p583/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p583/r1.speaker: اللحياني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p583/r1.claim: Al-Lihyani says fum and thum both refer to wheat.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p583/r1.anchor: وقال اللحياني: هو الفوم والثوم (¬5)، للحنطة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p583/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p583/r2.speaker: ابن دريد، المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p583/r2.claim: Ibn Durayd says the Azd of al-Sarat call the wheat ear fawm; al-Mubarrad chooses this explanation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p583/r2.anchor: وقال ابن دريد: أزد السراة يسمون السنبل فوما (¬8). وهذا القول اختيار # المبرد.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p583/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p583/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p583/r3.claim: The object of yukhrij is omitted and understood as something from the earth's plants; the same kind of omitted object occurs in the verse about Abraham's descendants.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p583/r3.anchor: ومفعول (يخرج) محذوف من الكلام، تقديره: يخرج لنا مما تنبت الأرض من بقلها شيئا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p583/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p583/r4.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p583/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj prefers adna from nearness: the people would exchange a readily available, ordinary food for the noble provision specially granted them over others.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p583/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p583/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p583/r5.claim: Another reading takes adna as nearer in value, meaning of lesser worth, or as less tasty and pleasurable than what was better.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p583/r5.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون معنى الدنو في قرب القيمة (¬5)، يقول: أتستبدلون الذي هو أقرب في القيمة (¬6)،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p583/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p583/r6.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p583/r6.claim: Al-Farra also derives adna from baseness, with Zuhayr al-Farqabi reportedly reading it adna'a with hamza.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p583/r6.anchor: على أنه قد حكى الفراء (¬1) عن زهير الفرقبي (¬2) أنه يقرأ (أدنأ) بالهمز

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p583/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p583/r7.speaker: بعض النحويين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p583/r7.claim: Some grammarians explain adna as adwan, meaning lower or meaner, by swapping n and w; the author rejects this because dun meaning inferior does not yield a verb.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p583/r7.anchor: وقال بعض النحويين: (أدنى) هاهنا بمعنى أدون، أي: أوضع وأخس، فقدمت النون وحولت الواو ألفا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p586/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p586/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p586/r1.claim: The command to descend to Misr may be spoken by Moses, or by God after an omitted prayer and response.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p586/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: {اهبطوا مصرا} جائز أن يكون هذا من كلام موسى لهم (¬2)، وجائز أن يكون من قول الله تعالى لهم،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p586/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p586/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p586/r2.claim: With tanwin, Misran can mean any city, since the requested produce was available in towns and cities.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p586/r2.anchor: فإن الذي سألتم لا يكون إلا في القرى والأمصار، ولهذا نون مصر،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p586/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p586/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p586/r3.claim: Misr may instead mean Egypt specifically; it could then take declension because the name is light and short.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p586/r3.anchor: وجائز أن يكون أراد مصر بعينها، وصرفها لخفتها وقلة حروفها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p586/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p586/r4.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p586/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the name is declined because it is masculine and was given to a masculine place-name, like other short names.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p586/r4.anchor: قال الزجاج: صرف؛ لأنه مذكر سمي به مذكر (¬6)، فهو مثل جمل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p586/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p586/r5.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p586/r5.claim: Al-Farra prefers leaving Misr undeclined; unlike common feminine names of three letters with a still middle letter, a place-name is rarely used as a personal name, and its written alif marks pause.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p586/r5.anchor: والفراء يختار ترك الإجراء، ويفرق بين هذا وبين أسماء النساء،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p586/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p586/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p586/r6.claim: The noninflected reading is described as rare; the author favors inflection because the name is light and short.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p586/r6.anchor: ويختار قراءة من قرأ مصر بغير تنوين (¬8)، وهي قرآءة مهجورة (¬9)، # والوجه ما ذكرنا قبل، أنه صرف لخفته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p586/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p586/r7.speaker: الكسائي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p586/r7.claim: Al-Kisa'i says eloquent Arabs freely decline words normally treated as indeclinable, including in poetry; only comparatives on af'al are never heard declined.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p586/r7.anchor: وقال الكسائي: العرب الفصحاء (¬2) لا يبالون أن يجروا مالا يجري،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p586/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p586/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p586/r8.claim: Misr means a boundary; Adi ibn Zayd's verse makes the sun a boundary between day and night, and the word also means a house's limits or cultivated land separated from wilderness.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p586/r8.anchor: والمصر في اللغة: الحاجز بين الشيئين (¬4).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p589/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p589/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p589/r1.claim: ‘They were struck with humiliation’ means it was imposed on them so firmly that it did not leave them; the image is of one thing affixed to another, like a nail driven in.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p589/r1.anchor: أي: ألزموها إلزاما لا تبرح عنهم، يقال: ضرب عليه (¬2) كذا، إذا ألزمه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p589/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p589/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p589/r2.claim: The expression ‘struck upon’ extends to imposing an obligation, as in a levy imposed on a servant or merchants.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p589/r2.anchor: وأصله من ضرب الشيء على الشيء، كما يضرب المسمار على الشيء فيلزمه، فيقال (¬3) لكل من ألزم شيئا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p589/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p589/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p589/r3.claim: The phrase ‘a lasting blow’ describes something enduring, and al-Nābigha uses it of evil that people do not think temporary.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p589/r3.anchor: ويقال للشيء الدائم: ضربة لازم ولازب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p589/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p589/r4.speaker: أبو عبيد عن الكسائي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p589/r4.claim: ذلة means abasement: a docile horse is the opposite of a difficult one, while a man is described as ذليل or ذلة.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p589/r4.anchor: أبو عبيد عن الكسائي: فرس ذلول بين (¬1) الذل، وهو ضد الصعوبة، ورجل ذليل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p589/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p589/r5.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p589/r5.claim: He derives مسكنة from سکون and defines it as the verbal noun of the poor person; its verb is تمسكن, ‘became poor.’
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p589/r5.anchor: قال الليث: المسكنة مصدر فعل المسكين، وإذا اشتقوا منه فعلا قالوا: تمسكن إذا صار مسكينا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p589/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p589/r6.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p589/r6.claim: He explains مسكنة as conditions that still and restrain a person; مسكين was then understood as if its initial mīm belonged to the root, by analogy with other formations.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p589/r6.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري: المسكنة الأمور التي تسكن صاحبها وتمنعه من الحركة ومن هذا أخذ المسكين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p589/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p589/r7.speaker: جماعة من المفسرين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p589/r7.claim: One reported interpretation takes the humiliation as referring to the people living in Moses’ time; another takes it as referring to people in the Prophet’s time.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p589/r7.anchor: فأما معنى الآية، فإن جماعة من المفسرين قالوا: في هذا ما دل على أن قوله: {وضربت عليهم الذلة}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p589/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p589/r8.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p589/r8.claim: Many exegetes, including al-Kalbī, say humiliation and poverty began then as signs of hardship because God knew they would kill prophets, and their descendants inherited them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p589/r8.anchor: قال كثير من المفسرين: ضربت عليهم يومئذ الذلة والمسكنة، وهو أثر البؤس وزي الفقر، وذلك لعلم الله فيهم أنهم سيقتلون النبيين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p589/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p589/r9.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p589/r9.claim: He favors the interpretation that humiliation followed their descent into Egypt: the omitted connective sense is that they descended, acted corruptly, and were then struck with humiliation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p589/r9.anchor: وإلى هذا القول مال ابن الأنباري، لأنه قال: قوله: {وضربت عليهم الذلة} (¬2) منسوق على محذوف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p589/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p589/r10.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p589/r10.claim: They interpret the humiliation as paying the jizya while subdued.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p589/r10.anchor: وقال الحسن وقتادة: {وضربت عليهم الذلة} يعطون الجزية عن يد وهم صاغرون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p591/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p591/r1.speaker: عطاء بن السائب
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p591/r1.claim: He identifies the humiliation with the Jewish distinguishing badge and clothing, and poverty with a poor appearance; even a wealthy Jew appeared impoverished for fear of increased jizya.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p591/r1.anchor: وقال عطاء بن السائب (¬4): هو [الكستيج] (¬5) وزي اليهودية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p591/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p591/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p591/r2.claim: This points to a later application: before Islam they paid no jizya and were not marked by distinctive clothing.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p591/r2.anchor: وهذا يدل على أن هذا الضرب وهذا الأثر حصل على المتأخرين منهم، لأنهم قبل الإسلام لم يعطوا الجزية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p591/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p591/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p591/r3.claim: The apparent objection that wealthy Jews cannot be poor is answered by taking humiliation as jizya and poverty as inward poverty of heart and soul, whose effects need not show outwardly.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p591/r3.anchor: قيل: الذلة الجزية، والمسكنة فقر القلب والنفس، وغير ظاهر آثارهما

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p591/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p591/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p591/r4.claim: Alternatively, the general wording may intend only a particular subset of people.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p591/r4.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون هذا من العموم الذي أريد به الخصوص

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p591/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p591/r5.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p591/r5.claim: He glosses باءوا بغضب as ‘they returned.’

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p591/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p591/r6.speaker: الكسائي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p591/r6.claim: He glosses باءوا as ‘they departed with it’ and says the verb always takes something good or bad, not bare departure.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p591/r6.anchor: وقال الكسائي: انصرفوا به (¬1)، ولا يكون أبدا باؤوا إلا بشيء إما بخير وإما بشر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p591/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p591/r7.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p591/r7.claim: He cites the report ‘Ṭalḥa returned with Paradise’ to illustrate باء as returning with something.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p591/r7.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري: وجاء في الحديث: "باء طلحة بالجنة" (¬4) أي: انصرف بها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p591/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p591/r8.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p591/r8.claim: He explains باؤوا بغضب as bearing it; al-Zajjāj gives the same lexical gloss for the related wording in 2:90 and for 5:29.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p591/r8.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: باؤوا بغضب: احتملوه (¬5)، ونحو ذلك قال الزجاج في قوله: {فباءوا بغضب على غضب} [البقرة: 90].

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p591/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p591/r9.speaker: أبو العباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p591/r9.claim: He derives the root from dwelling or a dwelling place: to bear a sin is to come to occupy the position of the guilty, and the other senses of carrying, returning, and acknowledging converge on settling in a place.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p591/r9.anchor: فمذهب أبي العباس أنه من الباءة والمباءة، وهو منزل القوم حيث (¬1) يتبوؤون (¬2).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p594/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p594/r1.speaker: الفرزدق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p594/r1.claim: His line to Muʿāwiya uses بؤت to mean ‘I would have acknowledged it,’ as if taking the place of one who confesses it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p594/r1.anchor: فلو كان هذا الأمر في جاهلية ... لبؤت به أوغص بالماء شاربه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p594/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p594/r2.speaker: لبيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p594/r2.claim: Labīd’s line likewise uses بؤت بحقها for accepting or acknowledging its due right.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p594/r2.anchor: أنكرت باطلها وبؤت بحقها ... عندي ولم تفخر على كرامها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p594/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p594/r4.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p594/r4.claim: He derives the root from equality: people are بواء when equal, a spear is aligned toward a horseman, and bloods are equal; bearing a sin is carrying it evenly.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p594/r4.anchor: وعند الزجاج أن أصل هذا الحرف من التسوية (¬5). تقول العرب: هم في هذا الأمر بواء، أي: سواء.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p594/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p594/r5.speaker: عبادة بن الصامت
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p594/r5.claim: A report from him says the Prophet divided spoils equally among the people; عن بواء means on an equal basis.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p594/r5.anchor: وفي حديث عبادة بن الصامت قال: (جعل الله الأنفال إلى نبيه - صلى الله عليه وسلم - فقسمها بينهم عن بواء) (¬3) أي (¬4) عن سواء بينهم في القسم.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p594/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p594/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p594/r6.claim: Thus the wrath is pictured as settled equally upon them; God’s wrath means His condemnation and punishment, not a human-like emotional state.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p594/r6.anchor: فمعنى {وباءوا بغضب من الله} كأنهم استوى عليهم الغضب من الله (¬5). ومعنى غضب الله: ذمه إياهم وإنزال العقوبة بهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p596/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p596/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p596/r1.claim: ‘That’ points back to the humiliation, poverty, and wrath just mentioned.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p596/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {ذلك بأنهم} (ذلك) إشارة إلى ضرب الذلة (¬7) والمسكنة والغضب (¬8)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p596/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p596/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p596/r2.claim: He says the signs of God they disbelieved in refer to the wisdom sent down to Muhammad.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p596/r2.anchor: ومعنى {يكفرون بآيات الله} قال ابن عباس: يريد الحكمة التي أنزلت على محمد - صلى الله عليه وسلم - (¬9).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p596/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p596/r3.speaker: غيره
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p596/r3.claim: Another exegetical view identifies the signs as Muhammad’s description and the stoning verse.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p596/r3.anchor: وقال غيره: أي بصفة محمد - صلى الله عليه وسلم - وآية الرجم (¬1).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p596/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p596/r4.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p596/r4.claim: Although Jews in Muhammad’s time did not personally kill the prophets, God calls them killers because they supported the earlier killers; the same collective attribution occurs in 5:81.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p596/r4.anchor: قال الفراء: إنما ألزمهم الله القتل ولم يقتلوا، لأن الذين كانوا في زمن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - من اليهود تولوا أولئك الذين قتلوا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p596/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p596/r5.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p596/r5.claim: The prophets meant include Zakariyyā, Yaḥyā, and Isaiah, along with the other prophets the Jews killed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p596/r5.anchor: ويعني بالنبيين من قتلهم اليهود مثل: زكريا ويحيى وشعيا، وسائر من قتلوا من الأنبياء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p597/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p597/r1.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p597/r1.claim: The phrase بغير الحق grammatically modifies the killing and means that the killing was unjust.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p597/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {بغير الحق} هو صفة للقتل، كأنه قيل: قتلا بغير حق، يعني بالظلم (¬4).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p597/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p597/r2.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p597/r2.claim: The prophets had committed no offense that could warrant their blood or expel them from prophethood; a prophet can never lawfully be killed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p597/r2.anchor: معناه: ويقتلون النبيين من غير جرم وذنوب أتوها توجب دماءهم، وتلزمهم أن يمحوا من ديوان النبوة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p597/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p597/r3.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p597/r3.claim: Another view treats بغير الحق as emphatic, since killing a prophet could only be unlawful; the text gives ‘hearts that are in the chests’ as a parallel.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p597/r3.anchor: وقيل: قوله: {بغير الحق} تأكيد، لأن قتل النبي لا يكون إلا بغير حق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p597/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p597/r4.speaker: الأخفش
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p597/r4.claim: He parses ما with the verb as a verbal noun: the disbelief and killing occurred through disobedience, abandonment of commands, and failure to obey.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p597/r4.anchor: قال الأخفش: ما والفعل بمنزلة المصدر، أي: ذلك الكفر والقتل بعصيانهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p597/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p597/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p597/r5.claim: Here disbelief and disobedience coincide and each entails the other, though disobedience is not disbelief in every context; alternatively, an omitted noun makes it the ill effect of their disobedience.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p597/r5.anchor: لأن نفس الكفر والقتل هو العصيان، فالعصيان هو الكفر، والكفر هو العصيان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p597/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p597/r6.speaker: كثير من المفسرين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p597/r6.claim: Many exegetes restrict the disobedience and transgression to violating the Sabbath; others take them generally as sins, exceeding God’s commands, and violating His prohibitions.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p597/r6.anchor: وعلى هذا التأويل يتوجه قول من خص العصيان والاعتداء بعصيانهم الله في السبت، واعتدائهم فيه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p597/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p597/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p597/r7.claim: The accusations do not apply to every Jew across all generations: some died earlier, some had only some traits, and those who approved or followed the perpetrators share their guilt; collective attribution can target only offenders and their supporters, as in 9:30.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p597/r7.anchor: ولكن الله تعالى أضاف هذه الأوصاف إلى اليهود، وهو يريد الجانين والذين تولوهم كقوله تعالى: {وقالت اليهود عزير ابن الله} [التوبة: 30]

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p597/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p597/r8.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p597/r8.claim: Most Arabs omit the hamza in النبي; he says the Arabs likewise omit it in four words whose original forms contain hamza.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p597/r8.anchor: قال (¬7) أبو عبيدة: اجتمعت العرب على حذف الهمزة من أربعة أحرف من النبي والذرية والخابية والبرية

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:61/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:61/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:61/r1.claim: The one food was manna and quail together; baql means plants without lasting stems, qiththa a kind of vegetable, and fūm wheat.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:61/r1.anchor: يعني: المن الذي كانوا يأكلونه والسلوى، فكانا طعاما واحدا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:61/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:61/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:61/r2.claim: Moses calls the requested food lower and worse than the higher, better food they had.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:61/r2.anchor: أي: أخس وأوضع { بالذي هو خير } أي: أرفع وأجل؟

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:61/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:61/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:61/r3.claim: Their requested produce is available only in towns and cities.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:61/r3.anchor: أي: فإن] الذي سألتم لا يكون إلا في القرى والأمصار

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:61/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:61/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:61/r4.claim: The humiliation applies to Jews in the Prophet's era: it means the jizya and Jewish dress, imposed so they cannot escape; poverty is shown by its garb and visible misery.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:61/r4.anchor: أي: على اليهود الذين كانوا في عصر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم { الذلة } يعني: الجزية وزي اليهودية،

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:61/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:61/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:61/r5.claim: To incur or return bearing something is the meaning of باؤوا; they incurred God's anger because they disbelieved signs sent to Muhammad.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:61/r5.anchor: احتملوا وانصرفوا { بغضب من الله ذلك } أي: ذلك الضرب والغضب

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:61/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:61/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:61/r6.claim: The charge of killing the prophets refers to siding with those who committed the killings; killing them without right means killing them unjustly.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:61/r6.anchor: أي: يتولون أولئك الذين فعلوا ذلك { بغير حق } أي: قتلا بغير حق، يعني: بالظلم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:61/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:61/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:61/r7.claim: Their disbelief and killing resulted from the evil consequence of committing sins and transgressing God's command.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:61/r7.anchor: الكفر والقتل بشؤم ركوبهم المعاصي وتجاوزهم أمر الله تعالى.

SIBAWAYH:فالبدلأنتقولضربعبداللهظهرهوبطنه.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فالبدلأنتقولضربعبداللهظهرهوبطنه.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:فالبدلأنتقولضربعبداللهظهرهوبطنه.claim: In expressions such as back and belly or plain and mountain, the second noun may be nominative as apposition or emphasis, or accusative in an expanded construction.
SIBAWAYH:فالبدلأنتقولضربعبداللهظهرهوبطنه.anchor: فالبدل أن تقول ضرب عبد الله ظهره وبطنه وضرب زيد الظهر والبطن

SIBAWAYH:فالبدلأنتقولضربعبداللهظهرهوبطنه.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فالبدلأنتقولضربعبداللهظهرهوبطنه.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:فالبدلأنتقولضربعبداللهظهرهوبطنه.claim: The implied sense is on the back and belly or in the plain and mountain; this is not ordinary adverbial syntax and is restricted to established pairs.

SIBAWAYH:فالبدلأنتقولضربعبداللهظهرهوبطنه.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فالبدلأنتقولضربعبداللهظهرهوبطنه.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:فالبدلأنتقولضربعبداللهظهرهوبطنه.claim: Khalīl reports the idiom مطرنا الزرع والضرع; Sībawayh allows its second nouns to be parsed as apposition, emphasis, or accusative.
SIBAWAYH:فالبدلأنتقولضربعبداللهظهرهوبطنه.anchor: وزعم الخليل ~~رحمه الله أنهم يقولون مطرنا الزرع والضرع

SIBAWAYH:فالبدلأنتقولضربعبداللهظهرهوبطنه.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فالبدلأنتقولضربعبداللهظهرهوبطنه.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:فالبدلأنتقولضربعبداللهظهرهوبطنه.claim: Nominative forms such as night and day can be understood as apposition or as broad usage in which the time is treated as part of the expression.
SIBAWAYH:فالبدلأنتقولضربعبداللهظهرهوبطنه.anchor: كما قال صيد عليه الليل والنهار وهو نهاره

SIBAWAYH:فالبدلأنتقولضربعبداللهظهرهوبطنه.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فالبدلأنتقولضربعبداللهظهرهوبطنه.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:فالبدلأنتقولضربعبداللهظهرهوبطنه.claim: Jarīr's verse treats night as a named part of the expression, supporting Sībawayh's broad nominative construction.
SIBAWAYH:فالبدلأنتقولضربعبداللهظهرهوبطنه.anchor: فى كل هذا جعل الليل بعض الاسم

SIBAWAYH:فالبدلأنتقولضربعبداللهظهرهوبطنه.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فالبدلأنتقولضربعبداللهظهرهوبطنه.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:فالبدلأنتقولضربعبداللهظهرهوبطنه.claim: In the conditional examples, accusative follows one analysis, while nominative is possible when the clause means that truth or falsehood occurs or is present.
SIBAWAYH:فالبدلأنتقولضربعبداللهظهرهوبطنه.anchor: والنصب فيه جيد بالغ على التفسير الأول والرفع على قوله وإن وقع صبر

SIBAWAYH:فالبدلأنتقولضربعبداللهظهرهوبطنه.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فالبدلأنتقولضربعبداللهظهرهوبطنه.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:فالبدلأنتقولضربعبداللهظهرهوبطنه.claim: A pronoun may be clarified by an explicit body-part noun, as in the phrase about turning a back and belly; the poetry supplies parallel replacements.
SIBAWAYH:فالبدلأنتقولضربعبداللهظهرهوبطنه.anchor: قلت ضرب عبد الله ظهره ومطر قومك سهلهم

SIBAWAYH:فالبدلأنتقولضربعبداللهظهرهوبطنه.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فالبدلأنتقولضربعبداللهظهرهوبطنه.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:فالبدلأنتقولضربعبداللهظهرهوبطنه.claim: Al-Jaʿdī's line permits أهلها to replace the implied people associated with Ḥimyar.

SIBAWAYH:فالبدلأنتقولضربعبداللهظهرهوبطنه.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فالبدلأنتقولضربعبداللهظهرهوبطنه.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:فالبدلأنتقولضربعبداللهظهرهوبطنه.claim: Sībawayh distinguishes verbal-noun or direction expressions such as forward and back from place names, which instead involve an omitted preposition.
SIBAWAYH:فالبدلأنتقولضربعبداللهظهرهوبطنه.anchor: فإنما خبر أن الذهاب كان على هذه الحال

SIBAWAYH:فالبدلأنتقولضربعبداللهظهرهوبطنه.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فالبدلأنتقولضربعبداللهظهرهوبطنه.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:فالبدلأنتقولضربعبداللهظهرهوبطنه.claim: ʿĀmir ibn al-Ṭufayl's line uses place names; the intended sense includes the preposition bi, unlike the verbal-noun examples.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p347/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p347/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p347/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses fūm as wheat; Abu Mihjan's line about cultivating fūm is cited as Arabic evidence for that sense.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p347/r1.anchor: وسأله عن قول الله - عز وجل -: {وَفُومِهَا} ما الفوم؟ قال: الحنطة. أما سمعت قول أبي محجن الثقفي

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p347/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p347/r2.speaker: الفراء
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p347/r2.claim: Al-Farra says fūm in an old dialect can mean both wheat and bread; Arabs also used fawwimū lanā to mean bake for us.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p347/r2.anchor: وقال الفراء إن الفوم فيما ذُكِرَ لغة قديمة وهي الحنطة والخبز جميعاً

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p347/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p347/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p347/r3.claim: The reading attributed to Abdullah, thūmihā with thāʾ, means garlic and better fits lentils and onions; Arabic speakers can interchange fāʾ and thāʾ.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p347/r3.anchor: وهي في قراءة عبد الله: "وثومِها" بالثاء، فكأنه أشبه المعنيين بالصواب لأنه مع ما يشاكله من العدس والبصل

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p492/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p492/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p492/r6.claim: Bint al-Shati notes that in substitution constructions the preposition bi enters the thing relinquished, as in exchanging the lower for the better.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p492/r6.anchor: والقاعدة في الاستبدال، أن الباء تدخل على المتروك

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p762/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p762/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p762/r1.claim: When a sound masculine plural appears alongside a broken plural of abundance, he says it indicates paucity; without that pairing it can denote either few or many.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p762/r1.anchor: جمع المذكر السالم إذا كان معه جمع كثرة فإنه يفيد القلة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p762/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p762/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p762/r2.claim: He observes that accounts of the Children of Israel’s sins use the prophets term, contrasting النبيين in al-Baqara with الأنبياء in Āl ʿImrān.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p762/r2.anchor: عندما يذكر معاصي بني إسرائيل يذكر الأنبياء

NASHR:v2p214/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p214/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p214/r6.claim: The author points back to the earlier discussion of reading the hāʾ and mīm in عليهم الذلة with either ḍamma or kasra.
NASHR:v2p214/r6.anchor: وتقدم اختلافهم في ضم الهاء والميم وكسرهما من نحو عليهم الذلة

NASHR:v2p214/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p214/r7.speaker: نافع
NASHR:v2p214/r7.claim: Nāfiʿ’s hamza treatment of النبياء, النبيئين, النبيء and النبوة is referred to the separate hamza chapter.
NASHR:v2p214/r7.anchor: وتقدم مذهب نافع في همز الأنبياء والنبيئين والنبيء والنبوءة

NASHR:v2p214/r13.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p214/r13.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p214/r13.claim: The passage notes a disagreement over sukūn versus ḍamma on ʿayn in a catalogue of words, but this excerpt supplies no reader assignments.
NASHR:v2p214/r13.anchor: إسكان العين وضمها منهما ومما كان على وزنهما، أو في حكمهما

NASHR:v2p104#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p104#2/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p104#2/r1.claim: A final rāʾ that is open, including نصبر, is stopped on with sukūn only; the author sets out parallel categories for still, transferred-kasra and other final rāʾs.
NASHR:v2p104#2/r1.anchor: أو كانت مفتوحة نحو أمر، وليفجر، ولن نصبر، والسحر، والخير

NASHR:v2p104#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p104#2/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p104#2/r2.claim: When final rāʾ has a permanent lexical or inflectional kasra, pause permits rawm or sukūn; a nominative ending permits rawm, ishāmām, or sukūn.
NASHR:v2p104#2/r2.anchor: جاز في الوقف عليها الروم والسكون كما سيأتي في بابه. وإن كانت مرفوعة نحو قضي الأمر

NASHR:v2p104#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p104#2/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p104#2/r3.claim: At pause with sukūn or ishāmām, tarqīq is the established rule when the preceding sound is kasra, sukūn after kasra, silent yāʾ, imāla, or a soft rāʾ; otherwise the rāʾ is tafkhīm.

NASHR:v2p104#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p104#2/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p104#2/r4.claim: Some soften a rāʾ with its own kasra at pause on the ground that pause makes the preceding state temporary; the author notes a possible distinction between temporary and permanent kasra.
NASHR:v2p104#2/r4.anchor: وذهب بعضهم إلى الوقف عليها بالترقيق إن كانت مكسورة لعروض الوقف

NASHR:v2p104#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p104#2/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p104#2/r5.claim: With rawm, a kasra softens rāʾ for all; a ḍamma is softened only by Warsh through al-Azraq after specified triggers, while other cases are tafkhīm, with some distinction for a kasra ending.
NASHR:v2p104#2/r5.anchor: فإن كانت كسرة رققتها للكل وإن كانت ضمة نظرت إلى ما قبلها

NASHR:v2p95/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p95/r1.speaker: طاهر بن غلبون
NASHR:v2p95/r1.claim: Some authorities, including Ṭāhir b. Ghalbūn, soften every tanwīn rāʾ without exception; al-Dānī read this from him. The readers exclude مصرا, إصرا, قطرا, وزرا, وقرا because of an emphatic consonant.
NASHR:v2p95/r1.anchor: وذهب آخرون إلى ترقيق كل منون، ولم يستثنوا ذكرا وبابه فمنهم أبو الحسن طاهر بن غلبون

NASHR:v2p95/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p95/r2.speaker: أبو شامة
NASHR:v2p95/r2.claim: Abū Shāma sees no difference between a fatḥa and ḍamma tanwīn rāʾ and says the ḍamma should more strongly favor tafkhīm; the author says al-Jaʿbarī adopted this and wrongly faulted al-Shāṭibī.
NASHR:v2p95/r2.anchor: ولا يظهر لي فرق بين كون الراء في ذلك مفتوحة، أو مضمومة، بل المضمومة أولى بالتفخيم

NASHR:v2p95/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p95/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو الداني
NASHR:v2p95/r3.claim: Al-Dānī, Abū al-Fatḥ and Ibn Khāqān, Ibn Bulayma, Ibn al-Faḥḥām and al-Shāṭibī soften tanwīn rāʾ in both environments, including after silent yāʾ or adjacent kasra.
NASHR:v2p95/r3.anchor: وهذا مذهب أبي عمرو الداني وشيخيه أبي الفتح وابن خاقان، وبه قرأ عليهما

NASHR:v2p95/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p95/r4.speaker: ابن سفيان
NASHR:v2p95/r4.claim: Ibn Sufyān and al-Mahdawī instead use tafkhīm in connected recitation because of tanwīn, then tarqīq at pause; this is a second face in al-Kāfī.
NASHR:v2p95/r4.anchor: وذهب الآخرون إلى تفخيم ذلك وصلا من أجل التنوين والوقف عليه بالترقيق كابن سفيان، والمهدوي

NASHR:v2p95/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p95/r5.speaker: صاحب التبصرة
NASHR:v2p95/r5.claim: Al-Tabṣira uniquely reports a second view: a tanwīn rāʾ on the faʿīl pattern is softened at pause but emphatic in connection, attributed to Abū al-Ṭayyib.
NASHR:v2p95/r5.anchor: وانفرد صاحب التبصرة في الوجه الثاني بترقيق ما كان وزنه فعيلا في الوقف وتفخيمه في الوصل

NASHR:v2p201/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p201/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p201/r1.claim: Combining by word repeats each word with a foundational or word-specific variant, stopping when possible or joining to the last face; for two-word differences, the reader stops after the second word and completes the options.
NASHR:v2p201/r1.anchor: الجمع بالحرف، وهو أن يشرع القارئ في القراءة فإذا مر بكلمة فيها خلف أصولي، أو فرشي أعاد تلك الكلمة بمفردها

NASHR:v2p201/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p201/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p201/r2.claim: The Egyptian word-by-word method is more reliable for exhausting variants and easier to learn, but it detracts from the flow and beauty of recitation.
NASHR:v2p201/r2.anchor: وهذا مذهب المصريين، وهو أوثق في استيفاء أوجه الخلاف وأسهل في الأخذ وأحضر

NASHR:v2p201/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p201/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p201/r3.claim: The Syrian method reads one transmitter’s face to a permissible stop, then repeats to that stop with the next reader; the author learned both methods and combines them, prioritizing the next reader most compatible with the first and observing good performance.
NASHR:v2p201/r3.anchor: والمذهب الثاني الجمع بالوقف، وهو إذا شرع القارئ بقراءة من قدمه لا يزال بذلك الوجه حتى ينتهي إلى وقف يسوغ الابتداء مما بعده

IBNHISHAM:v1p535/r1.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p535/r1.speaker: ابن هشام
IBNHISHAM:v1p535/r1.claim: Manna was a sweet substance falling on the Israelites’ trees at dawn; they gathered and ate or drank it like honey.
IBNHISHAM:v1p535/r1.anchor: قال ابن هشام: المن: شيء كان يسقط في السحر على شجرهم، فيجتنونه حلوا مثل العسل

IBNHISHAM:v1p535/r2.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p535/r2.speaker: أعشى بني قيس بن ثعلبة
IBNHISHAM:v1p535/r2.claim: Al-Aʿshā invokes manna and salwā as satisfying provisions, supporting their place as foods in the Israelites’ account.
IBNHISHAM:v1p535/r2.anchor: قال أعشى بني قيس بن ثعلبة: لو أطعموا المن والسلوى مكانهم ... ما أبصر الناس طعما فيهم نجعا

IBNHISHAM:v1p535/r3.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p535/r3.speaker: ابن هشام
IBNHISHAM:v1p535/r3.claim: Salwā is described as a bird, with singular salwāt; one reported identification is the quail.
IBNHISHAM:v1p535/r3.anchor: والسلوى: طير، واحدتها: سلواة، ويقال: إنها السماني

IBNHISHAM:v1p535/r4.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p535/r4.speaker: خالد بن زهير الهذلي
IBNHISHAM:v1p535/r4.claim: Ibn Hishām also reports that salwā can mean honey, citing a line by Khālid ibn Zuhayr al-Hudhalī.

IBNHISHAM:v1p535/r8.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p535/r8.speaker: ابن هشام
IBNHISHAM:v1p535/r8.claim: Ibn Hishām glosses fūm as wheat and cites Umayya ibn Abī al-Ṣalt’s poem as evidence.
IBNHISHAM:v1p535/r8.anchor: قال ابن هشام: الفوم: الحنطة. قال أمية بن أبي الصلت الثقفي

IBNHISHAM:v1p536/r1.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p536/r1.speaker: ابن هشام
IBNHISHAM:v1p536/r1.claim: In the cited poem, al-wudhayl means pieces of silver; fūm means wheat, whose singular is fūma.
IBNHISHAM:v1p536/r1.anchor: قال ابن هشام: الوذيل: قطع الفضة (والفوم: القمح) ، واحدته: فومة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p28/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28/r1.claim: The passage lists apparent differences in Qur'anic statements, including denial that people will ask one another alongside a later description of them asking, and two formulations limiting what prevents belief.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28/r1.anchor: فلا أنساب بينهم يومئذ ولا يتساءلون

ALUSI-FULL:v1p28/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28/r2.claim: Examples of verbal variation include wool described once as ṣūf and once as ʿihn, and the ordering of poverty and humiliation in the cited phrase.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28/r2.anchor: وأما الختلاف فكقوله تعالى ( كالصوف المنفوش )

ALUSI-FULL:v1p28/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28/r3.claim: Further alleged inconsistencies include calling the Prophet a father, varying the material from which Adam was created, repetitions in wording and meaning, and explaining that three plus seven days equals ten complete.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28/r3.anchor: وقوله تعالى ( النبي أولى بالمؤمنين من أنفسهم وأزواجه أمهاتهم ) وهو أب لهم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p28/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28/r4.speaker: عثمان
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28/r4.claim: Uthman is reported to have said that the Qur'an contains grammatical irregularities that the Arabs will set right with their tongues.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28/r4.anchor: وقال عثمان : إن في القرآن لحنا ستقيمه العرب بالسنتها

ALUSI-FULL:v1p28/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28/r5.claim: An objection argues that even freedom from all such defects would not establish inimitability, since sermons and poetry show the same feature and the claim scales to short surahs.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28/r5.anchor: أنا لو سلمنا السلامة من جميع ذلك لكنه ليس بأعجاز إذ هو موجود في كثير من الخطب

ALUSI-FULL:v1p28/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28/r6.claim: A proposed criterion makes the Qur'an miraculous through agreement with reason and subtle meaning; the author rejects it as common among eloquent speech and says it also applies to non-miraculous prophetic speech and the Torah and Gospel.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28/r6.anchor: وقيل هو موافقته لقضية العقل ودقيق المعنى ورد بأنه معتاد في أكثر كلام البلغاء

ALUSI-FULL:v1p28/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28/r7.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28/r7.claim: Another view locates inimitability in the Qur'an's pre-eternity; the author objects that this would make all divine attributes miraculous and that an unobservable eternal speech cannot be the object of a challenge.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28/r7.anchor: وقيل إعجازه قدمه وأعترض بأنه يستدعي أن يكون كل من صفاته تعالى كذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v1p28/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28/r8.speaker: الأستاذ أبو إسحاق الأسفراييني والنظام
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28/r8.claim: Abu Ishaq al-Isfarayini and al-Nazzam say the miracle is that God diverted eloquent Arabs' motives from attempting a rival; al-Murtada instead says their necessary knowledge for competing was removed.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28/r8.anchor: إعجازه بصرف دواعي بلغاء العرب عن معارضته

ALUSI-FULL:v1p28/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28/r9.claim: The author objects that the diversion theory makes the miracle the act of diversion rather than the Qur'an itself, contrary to the Muslims' prior consensus.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28/r9.anchor: أنه يستلزم أن يكون المعجز الصرفة لا القرآن وهو خلاف ما عليه إجماع المسلمين

ALUSI-FULL:v1p28/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28/r10.claim: He further argues that if each Arab was diverted individually, producing a like text would be customary for each; ordinary speech is not eloquent, so the theory wrongly entails that the Qur'an itself is not eloquent.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28/r10.anchor: فلو كان الإعجاز بالصرفة لكانت على خلاف المتعاد بالنسبة إلى كل واحد

BURHAN:v1p126/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p126/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p126/r3.claim: The same accusation appears with the definite phrase in al-Baqara and without the article in Al Imran, illustrating variation in definiteness.
BURHAN:v1p126/r3.anchor: الرابع بالتعريف والتنكير كقوله فى البقرة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p576/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p576/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p576/r1.claim: Min is a genitive preposition used for partitive meaning, beginning point, and explanation of a kind; context also licenses figurative uses.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p576/r1.anchor: ' من ' حرف من حروف الخفض يرد للتبعيض . تقول : هذا الذراع من هذا الثوب . ويرد لابتداء الغاية

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p576/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p576/r9.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p576/r9.claim: Min explains the kind meant: the Israelites ask for vegetables and cucumbers among what the earth grows.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p576/r9.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن ' من ' في القرآن على ثمانية أوجه

BURHAN:v3p164/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p164/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p164/r4.claim: In “ask your Lord to bring forth for us,” the omitted object is “something.”

BURHAN:v4p169/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p169/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p169/r7.claim: When context supplies the comparison, an elative used predicatively often omits the less-preferred object of comparison.
BURHAN:v4p169/r7.anchor: الخامسة يكثر حذف المفضول إذا دل عليه دليل وكان أفعل خبرا

BURHAN:v3p217/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p217/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p217/r6.claim: Al Imran uses indefinite حق in a generic conditional statement; al-Baqara's definite الحق concerns a familiar rationale used by the people being described.
BURHAN:v3p217/r6.anchor: والحكمة فيه أن الجملة في آل عمران خرجت مخرج الشرط وهو عام فناسب أن يكون النفي بصيغة التنكير

BURHAN:v2p346/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p346/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p346/r4.claim: Al-Zarkashi says this contradicts the rhetoricians’ consensus: the cited questions refer to past actions; no evidence supports future reference, and the grammar of أتقتلون does not determine the intended time.
BURHAN:v2p346/r4.anchor: وهذا الذي قاله مخالف لاجماع البيانيين ولادليل فيما ذكره بل الاستفهام في الآيتين عن ماض

BURHAN:v2p346/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p346/r5.speaker: ابن جني
BURHAN:v2p346/r5.claim: Ibn Jinni notes that grammatical inflection can differ from the meaning; the future-subjunctive أن in “that he says” does not make the condemnatory question’s event future in sense.
BURHAN:v2p346/r5.anchor: وقد ذكر ابن جني في التنبيه ( 3 ) أن الإعراب قد يرد خلاف ما عليه المعنى

BURHAN:v2p346/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p346/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p346/r6.claim: For rhetorical questions used in negative forms, the interrogative may disappear entirely, remain alongside another sense, or allow either reading; context decides.
BURHAN:v2p346/r6.anchor: بالكلية لاينبغي ان يطلق أحد الامرين بل منه ما تجرد كما في التسوية ومنه ما يبقى

BURHAN:v2p346/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p346/r7.speaker: النحاة والبيانيون
BURHAN:v2p346/r7.claim: Grammarians and rhetoricians differ over whether an affirmative question used for acknowledgment asserts a fact or seeks the addressee’s admission despite the speaker already knowing it.
BURHAN:v2p346/r7.anchor: وفي كلام النحاة والبيانيين كل من القولين

ITQAN:v2p352/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p352/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p352/r1.claim: Fum means wheat; Abu Mihjan al-Thaqafi’s poem uses the word in a line about farming wheat as evidence for its Arabic usage.
ITQAN:v2p352/r1.anchor: ﴿ وفومها ﴾ قال الحنطة قال وهل تعرف العرب ذلك قال نعم أما سمعت قول أبي محجن الثقفي

RUMMANI:v1p91/r1.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p91/r1.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p91/r1.claim: The metaphor of striking humiliation upon them makes its imposition perceptible and suggests degradation, intensifying the rebuke and aversion from their condition.
RUMMANI:v1p91/r1.anchor: عليهم من الذلة كما يثبت الشيء بالضرب لأن التمكين به محسوس

DAMGHANI:v1p175/r5.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p175/r5.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p175/r5.claim: Adnā means inferior or lesser: the Israelites are asking to exchange food inferior to manna and quail for what is better.
DAMGHANI:v1p175/r5.anchor: الرابع : أدنى يعني دون فذلك قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p267/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p267/r12.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p267/r12.claim: Ḥaqq can mean a crime or offense in the phrase “without right.”
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p267/r12.anchor: والسابع عشر : الجرم . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة :

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p119/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p119/r9.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p119/r9.claim: Adnā can mean lower or inferior.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p119/r9.anchor: والرابع : بمعنى أدون . ومنه قوله تعالى ' في البقرة ' :

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p348/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p348/r1.speaker: الكسائي
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p348/r1.claim: One reported reading takes al-fūm to mean garlic; al-Kisāʾī and al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl are named for this view, and al-Farrāʾ also chooses it by analogy with fāʾ replacing thāʾ.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p348/r1.anchor: ونقل في الفوم بمعنى الثوم، أنه قول الكسائي والنضر بن شميل

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p348/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p348/r2.speaker: النحاس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p348/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and most exegetes read al-fūm as wheat; al-Naḥḥās prefers this interpretation as more apt.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p348/r2.anchor: وقيل: الفوم الحنطة، روي عن ابن عباس أيضاً، وأكثر المفسرين، واختاره النحاس وقال: هو أولى

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p348/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p348/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p348/r3.claim: Bint al-Shāṭiʾ rejects letter substitution as a general proof for garlic, since replacing thāʾ with fāʾ is not a rule that can be analogically extended.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p348/r3.anchor: وإن كان الكسائي والفراء اختارا القول الأول لإبدال العرب الفاء من الثاء، والإبدال لا يقاس عليه

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#4/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#4/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#4/r1.claim: The author reads indefinite ḥaqq in 3:112 as killing the prophets without any right or cause whatsoever, intensifying the condemnation; definite al-ḥaqq in 2:61 refers to the recognized category of right.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#4/r1.anchor: فكلمة (حق) ههنا نكرة عامة، وكلمة (الحق) معرّفة معلومة

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#4/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#4/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#4/r2.claim: The denunciation is stronger in Āl ʿImrān: it universalizes humiliation with “wherever they are found” and repeats the verb and preposition before poverty; al-Baqara simply joins humiliation and poverty.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#4/r2.anchor: فأعاد الفعل وحرف الجر للزيادة في التوكيد

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#4/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#4/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#4/r3.claim: The author treats al-nabiyyīn in al-Baqara as a plural of paucity and al-anbiyāʾ in Āl ʿImrān as a plural of abundance, underscoring the latter’s greater condemnation.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#4/r3.anchor: ذكر الجمع في آية البقرة بصورة القلة فقال: (ويقتلون النبيين) وذكره في آية آل عمران بصورة الكثرة

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#3/r22.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#3/r22.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#3/r22.claim: The definite الحق in 2:61 means the known right that could authorize killing; the passage introduces its contrast with indefinite حق in 3:112 without yet explaining that form.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#3/r22.anchor: كلمة (الحق) المعرّفة في آية البقرة تدل على أنهم كانوا يقتلون الأنبياء بغير الحق الذي يدعو إلى القتل
